Lagerland Redesign Board
Lagerland Redesign Board 0 of 21 pages picked

Three styles for every page. You pick one.

The studio site and each of the 20 app pages get their own world. Every app becomes a standalone microsite with its own navigation, type and page structure; only a thin footer strip links back to Lagerland. Every style keeps the permalinks, the seo/schema/quick_answer structure and the App Store elements (official badge, Smart App Banner, desktop QR, sticky bar, price).

  1. Read the three style cards for a page. Each preview shows the style's typefaces and colours; "Full style card" has the first-viewport layout, page sequence and signature move.
  2. Pick one with its button. You can change a pick at any time. Use the note box to steer it, for example "style B, but with A's navigation".
  3. Picks save automatically. Claude reads them before the first build phase starts. Nothing is built until you approve the plan at the bottom.

Connecting to the shared store…

Specimens, not sketches

Each preview sets the page's real headline in the style's real typefaces and colours. Full HTML sketches were stopped to save session credits; they get built only for the styles you pick, in that page's phase.

How the three were chosen

For each page, seven directions were drawn from the audience's own world and ranked. A dice roll chose style A from that list, B is the top-ranked direction, and C comes from a second roll. The roll service was unreachable here, so the roll ran without its catalogue of outside challengers.

Kept on every page

Content stays visible without JavaScript. Reduced-motion is respected. Text meets WCAG AA contrast. Fonts are open-license and self-hosted, with no third-party font host. Nothing is invented: no ratings, quotes or numbers beyond what the site already states.

Fixes already queued

Three critics reviewed all 63 styles for collisions between apps, invented claims and buildability. Their fixes are listed under each style and get applied before anything is built. One applies everywhere: each page's three styles must differ in section order, not only in the hero.

Retired

Paper & Ink, the cream ground, Newsreader + Inter, and the one template shared by every app page. Light or dark is now chosen per world from where people use the app, not forced on every page.

Lagerland Apps (studio site)

Homepage, all-apps index, journal, guides, audience pages, comparisons index, transparency, about, support, 404

What the page must prove: In one viewport: this is one person's independent catalogue of distinct private apps, here is the fastest route to the one you need, and the privacy claim is a public per-app record (0 tracking domains, 0 ad SDKs, audited 11 Jun 2026), not a slogan.

The default page this refuses: Indie studio homepage: serif or grotesk headline beside floating device mockups, a trust-stat row, then 2- or 3-column grids of equal app cards (icon, name, tagline, pills) per category, journal cards, FAQ, footer: exactly the incumbent v3 Paper & Ink.

Today's page, for comparison
Picked
Lagerland Apps (studio site)Big Shoulders Stencil Display

Private software for iPhone, iPad, Watch and Mac

One developer in Finland. No tracking, no ads, no accounts.

THE ROLL

The Open Depot

Open-storage art depots, where a whole collection is kept in view on racks and every object is located and labelled: Schaulager, Basel (Herzog & de Meuron, 2003) and Depot Boijmans Van Beuningen, Rotterdam (MVRDV, 2021). Crossed with Nordic warehouse wayfinding: pallet-rack beam labels with aisle-bin codes, stencil aisle signs and stocktake cards. The name's literal reading (lager = stock, store) is spent here once and lifted from warehouse to open store.

The catalogue is an open store, not a showroom. Every app sits in view at a fixed aisle-bin location with its declared contents on the label (tracking domains, SDKs, account). It refuses the hero-plus-icon-card grid by making the homepage the depot's location index, read aisle by aisle and picked by hand.

  • #E6E8E5
  • #FFFFFF
  • #14191F
  • #E2560F
  • #1E3E8C

Type
Big Shoulders Stencil Display 800 and 500 (Fontsource, 14 KB per weight) with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400, 700 and 400 italic (Fontsource, 12-14 KB each), Martian Mono 400 and 600, only for real data: location codes, declared values, dates, counts (Fontsource, 10 KB each)
Light
A visitor reads bin labels on a phone at midday, as if standing in a white-painted open depot under even 5000K high-bay light, with orange beams, blue uprights and labels legible at arm's length. Scheme: light.
Signature
Pick. Tap, click or press Enter on a ledger row and its box slides out of the bin: a drawer opens with the app's box front at large scale (app ground colour, 120px squircle icon, first screenshot 240px tall), the orange 'Go to <App> · code' ticket, the official badge and, on wide screens, the QR. Technique: each row is a <details> whose summary is the full ledger row; CSS transitions grid-template-rows from 0fr to 1fr, and the box lifts 6px with a soft 0 8px 24px shadow. On hover the box only nudges 3px as a preview; about 10 lines of JS close the previously opened drawer. No JS: <details> works natively, and every word (name, job, platforms, price, declared values, link) sits in the always-visible summary, so the drawer adds only image, badge and QR. Reduced motion: the drawer opens instantly with no lift.
Remembered as
The Lagerland site was an open warehouse: huge stencil aisle signs, orange shelf beams, and every app on a labelled bin saying what's inside (0 trackers, 0 ad SDKs). I pulled one out and its box showed me the app.
Risk
It is the name's literal reading. A depot can read cold and industrial against 'calm', and a dense ledger can feel like a spreadsheet to a casual shopper if row rhythm and box fronts are not generous. Orange-and-blue racking also nears generic stock-photo industry. Stencil tires below 40px, so it never sets running text.

App Store route

Routing comes first. The aisle beam (seven jump labels) and the ledger rows are the action, and every row's app name links straight to /apps/<slug>/. The Pick drawer adds an orange pick-ticket button ('Go to Observa · 1-02') and the official App Store badge (Apple artwork untouched, 40px). On screens 1024px and wider it also shows assets/qr/<slug>.svg in a white label, 'Scan to install on iPhone'; Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly show the badge only. The price statement is price.value verbatim on every row. The sticky bar: once the aisle beam scrolls away, a 44px orange beam with the seven aisle labels sticks to the top. Smart App Banner: none on studio pages, except journal posts and guides with exactly one mentioned app. Icons are squircle-masked at 1.06 overscale (cropping baked white corners) on a box front painted in the app's own world ground (studio_swatch from its chosen microsite). The bin label stays in constant studio type; the box belongs to the app.

Page sequence

  1. Beam masthead: nav as white beam labels on the orange beam
  2. Level one: stencil H1 and lede (the about-strip text, AI-canonical), then the stocktake strip (computed proof from transparency.yml)
  3. Aisle beam: seven aisle labels (the 7 need clusters) as jump links
  4. Location index: per aisle, a stencil sign plus the cluster lead line, then ledger rows (aisle-bin code, box front, name, tagline, platforms, price.value, declared tracking/SDK/account); each row opens a Pick drawer with screenshot, Go-to ticket, badge and QR
  5. Goods in: the newest arrival (computed from release.first_release, now Xiangqiful) on the receiving bay: large box front, first screenshot, real arrival date
  6. Swap shelf: four comparisons as transfer tickets ('From Strong → GymLogger X') plus the computed comparison count → /alternatives/
  7. Delivery notes: the latest two journal posts (date in mono, title, lede)
  8. Ledger extract: the 6-app transparency sample (orange header row, mono values) → /transparency/
  9. Service counter: six FAQ <details> tags (first open), plus a founder line (Antti Aittamaa, one developer, Finland, since 2025) and email
  10. Close: the aisle labels again, 'Pick something'
  11. Footer: the depot floor plan, with aisles as outlined rectangles listing every app, plus studio links, privacy, support and 'Made on a MacBook at 63°N'

Navigation

The orange beam is the masthead on every studio page: the mark plus LAGERLAND label, then beam labels for Apps, Journal, Transparency, Alternatives and About, with Guides, For and Support in the 'Index' directory sheet (a <details> panel that works without JS). The current page's label is printed on blue with white text. Breadcrumbs are set as a location path in Martian ('LAGERLAND / JOURNAL / streaks-are-a-debt'). /apps/ is the full location index with each aisle's lead copy. /for/ pages are pick lists: the audience's stack as location rows, each with why it is on the list.

Motion

Mechanical and short: things move along rails and never float or fade. Pick drawer 180ms ease-out; box lift 6px; aisle jumps use smooth scroll (instant under reduced motion); the sticky aisle beam drops in over 120ms. No reveal-on-scroll, no parallax, no count-up: stocktake values are static text.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Journal posts, guides, /for/ pages, transparency, the alternatives index, about, support and 404 keep the orange beam masthead and one blue upright as the left rail. On desktop the 28px upright's punched slots mark each H2, and the current section's slot fills orange: a working table of contents. On mobile the upright is 6px and an 'On this shelf' <details> holds the contents. The title is stencil 800 in sentence case at 56-72px; the meta line (date, read time, last updated) is Martian 14px. The column sits on a white label-stock sheet over concrete: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 18/1.6 at 68ch in #14191F, with H2s in Atkinson 700 at 26px. The Quick Answer is a bin label: a white panel with a 12px orange top band, titled 'Quick answer', the answer at 19px (speakable). Tables are ledgers: orange header row, black text, Martian figures, concrete zebra rows; plist keys are in Martian on concrete. Mentioned apps close the post as their ledger rows, with the Pick drawer. The journal index is a delivery-notes ledger: date, title, read time, and the location codes of mentioned apps. Guides are problem tickets that resolve to bins. /transparency/ is the full stock ledger, one bin label per app with every field in a dl and the source status printed as label text (Source-verified / App Store-declared / Manifest pending). The alternatives index is a ledger grouped by our app under stencil signs. 404 reads 'BIN EMPTY' above the aisle directory.

Materials

flat painted-concrete ground (#E6E8E5, no texture) · pallet-rack uprights with punched teardrop slots (CSS mask pattern) · orange box-section beams carrying white beam labels · white self-adhesive bin labels with aisle-bin codes (e.g. 1-02) · stencil-sprayed aisle signs · stocktake strip and stock ledger · app box fronts painted in each app's own ground colour · orange pick tickets

Colour strategy

Committed: beam orange carries about 30% of the surface as masthead, aisle beams and ledger header rows; blue uprights frame both page edges; concrete grey is the ground; each app's own colour appears only on its box front. · light

Type rationale

Depots and crates are marked with sprayed stencil, and the condensed stencil fits a seven-aisle directory on one beam; it is kept at 40px and above. Atkinson was drawn by the Braille Institute for legibility at distance and for low vision, which is the label-reading job and also a calm reading face. Martian's wide mono reads like label-printer output and is never used for running text. Total about 86 KB.

New assets needed

A clean vector studio mark: an SVG redraw of the stone star and block ring, because the PNG has a baked checkerboard. Data, not art: a per-app studio_swatch {ground, ink} in front matter, sampled from icons now and replaced by each chosen microsite's ground later. Racks, beams and labels are CSS. Optional later: per-app SVG wordmarks from each microsite's face for the box fronts. Everything else runs on the existing icons, screenshots and QR SVGs.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

The Back Catalogue

Independent record labels as identity systems. Factory Records' catalogue numbering under Peter Saville: every artefact numbered, every sleeve its own design. The yellow-label principle of Deutsche Grammophon: one constant cartouche on radically different covers (principle only, none of its trade dress). And the record shop's browser shelf, with spines filed by genre behind black plastic divider cards.

The studio is a small label. Each app is a record filed spine-out by genre in its own colours, and the label appears only as a catalogue number and one constant cartouche. It refuses the hero-plus-icon-card grid by making the catalogue a shelf you browse and pull a record from.

  • #F2B21B
  • #141414
  • #FFFFFF
  • #4A3F22
  • #5C5C5C
Type
Krona One 400 (Fontsource, 10 KB) with Familjen Grotesk 400, 600 and 400 italic (Fontsource, 11-12 KB each), none: catalogue numbers, dates and prices are set in Familjen Grotesk 600 with tabular figures
Light
A browser at the new-releases shelf of a small record shop on a bright afternoon, the wall painted the label's cloudberry yellow, spines lit flat and even. Scheme: light, drenched.
Signature
Face-out. Hovering or focusing a spine on desktop turns that record face-out: its flex-basis grows from 42px to 400px over 220ms and the sleeve face appears, while the previous face-out record turns back to its spine. On touch, a tap toggles it through a <button aria-expanded> in each spine, and the app name stays a plain link. Technique: a flex row with :hover, :focus-within and :has() collapses the default record while another is hovered; a .is-out class is kept by about 20 lines of JS; every sleeve face is server-rendered. No JS: the newest release is server-rendered face-out, every spine name is a link, and the back-cover discography directly below lists every tagline, so nothing is reachable only by interaction. Reduced motion: the swap is instant.
Remembered as
A yellow record-shop wall with a shelf of nineteen spines in different colours. Every Lagerland app was a record; I touched one and it turned to face me, with sleeve, price sticker and a QR where the barcode goes.
Risk
Familiar: 'studio as record label' is a known indie trope, and the pick lands near where many studio redesigns go. Nineteen app colours on a yellow wall can turn noisy unless the swatch data is tuned. Vertical spine text scans slower than a list (the back-cover discography and mobile stack carry that load). Cloudberry plus black can read as a warning sign if the shelf is not the clear focus.

390x844, cloudberry. Masthead 56px: a 32px roundel, LAGERLAND in Krona One 17px, and a black 'Catalogue' tab on the right that opens the genre and page sheet. App Store route

The shelf is the routing: every spine name links to /apps/<slug>/. The face-out sleeve carries a black 'Open <App> →' button, the price sticker (price.value verbatim), the official App Store badge (unaltered, 40px) and, on desktop, the app's QR printed where a sleeve's barcode sits, 'Scan to install on iPhone'; Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly show the badge only. The back-cover discography repeats every route as text. The sticky bar: after the shelf leaves the viewport, a 48px black divider strip sticks to the top with the seven genre labels in yellow, jumping back into the shelf. Smart App Banner: only on journal posts and guides with exactly one mentioned app. Icons and names: the spine and sleeve wear the app's own world colours (studio_swatch from its microsite, interim sampled from the icon), with the icon squircle-masked at 1.06. The label adds only the cartouche and catalogue number, never its own colour, to an app's sleeve.

Page sequence

  1. Masthead: centre-label roundel, LAGERLAND, divider-card tabs
  2. Statement: Krona H1 and lede (the about-strip text, AI-canonical) with the credits link
  3. The shelf: seven genre dividers, eighteen spines, the newest release face-out (the routing core; badge, QR and price on the face-out sleeve)
  4. Back cover: the full discography as a tracklist (LGL no. · app · tagline · formats · released · price.value), the shelf's text twin with every job line visible
  5. Credits: the 6-app transparency sample set as album credits (tracking domains 0, third-party SDKs, account, analytics), plus 'Full credits for all 19 →' (computed)
  6. Versus: four comparisons as split-single sleeves (our app's colour half, the competitor half in plain black type) plus the computed count → /alternatives/
  7. Liner notes: the latest two journal posts as inner-sleeve excerpts
  8. Pressed by one person: founder block (Antti Aittamaa, Finland, since 2025), then six FAQ <details> 'from the counter' (first open)
  9. Close: 'Back to the shelf' plus email
  10. Footer: the label discography (all LGL numbers and names), studio links, privacy, support, 'Made on a MacBook at 63°N'

Navigation

Black divider-card tabs across the yellow masthead (Apps, Journal, Transparency, Alternatives, About; the current card is raised); Guides, For and Support sit in the footer and the mobile 'Catalogue' sheet (<details>, works without JS). /apps/ is the whole shelf plus the back-cover discography with genre notes. /for/ pages are compilations: each audience's stack as a tracklist with why each app is on it. /guides/ is a row of staff-pick shelf-talker cards that open into each guide. Catalogue numbers are computed in first_release order, so new apps append and old numbers never change.

Motion

Records slide and nothing fades. Face-out 220ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1). On load the newest record rises 12px and settles once over 300ms (skipped under reduced motion). Divider cards never move; no scroll reveals; the sticky divider strip simply docks.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Liner notes. A 120px cloudberry masthead band holds the roundel, the post's date and read time (Familjen 600 15px) and the title in Krona One at 40-48px, black, three lines at most at 1100px. Below sits the inner sleeve: a white sheet with the column in Familjen Grotesk 18/1.62 at 66ch, #141414, H2s in Familjen 600 at 26px, links underlined in black. The Quick Answer is the shrink-wrap sticker: a black panel titled 'Quick answer' in yellow, with the white 18px answer at the top of the sheet. Tables are back-cover tracklists: tabular figures, 1px black rules, no fills. Mentioned apps close the post face-out (sleeve with 'Open →'); on desktop their spine also stands in the right margin as a vertical link. The journal index is a 'Liner notes' tracklist by date. /transparency/ is 'Credits': one block per app (role and value in Apple's terms, plus source status), headed by the app's spine laid flat as a horizontal bar, never a coloured side border. The alternatives index is 'Versus', grouped under our app's flat spine bar. About is 'Pressed by one person'; support is 'The counter'; 404 is 'Not in the catalogue', followed by the shelf.

Materials

cloudberry-painted shop wall (the drenched ground) · record spines in each app's own colour · black plastic genre divider cards · square sleeve faces carrying the app's world · the white label cartouche (the one constant) · round white price stickers · printed back-cover tracklist · inner-sleeve white sheet for liner notes · shrink-wrap sticker (the Quick Answer)

Colour strategy

Drenched: the cloudberry wall is the ground of every Persuade surface; black divider cards and type set the structure; the only other colours are the apps' own, on their spines and sleeves. Read pages keep the yellow as masthead band and put the column on inner-sleeve white. · light

Type rationale

Krona One is a semi-extended, low-contrast sans with the stance of mid-century Nordic label and advert lettering, wide enough to own a spine at 16px set vertically and a 72px H1. Familjen Grotesk, from a Stockholm studio, is compact with a high x-height, built for tracklists and calm enough for liner-note reading. Total about 45 KB.

New assets needed

A clean vector studio mark, also cut as a centre-label roundel; the PNG has a baked checkerboard. Data: per-app studio_swatch {ground, ink} for spines and sleeves (ink must reach 4.5:1 on its ground), sampled from icons now and replaced with each chosen microsite's ground. Optional later: per-app SVG wordmarks for sleeve faces. QR SVGs, icons and screenshots exist; spines, dividers and stickers are CSS.

Private software for iPhone, iPad, Watch and Mac

SECOND ROLL

Page 100

European broadcast teletext: Yle Teksti-TV (still on air in Finland) and BBC Ceefax (1974-2012), and its Level 1 grammar: a 40x24 character grid, seven colours on black, double-height rows, 2x3 block-mosaic graphics, three-digit page numbers with 100 as the index, four Fastext colour keys, and MIX mode, where text sits over the live TV picture.

The studio is a teletext service. Every app, post and manifest has a three-digit page you can type, Fastext keys route the sections, and each app's own picture shows through in MIX. It refuses the hero-plus-card grid by making the homepage a P100 index.

  • #000000
  • #D9D9D9
  • #FFFF00
  • #00FFFF
  • #00FF00
  • #0000FF
  • #FF0000
Type
Tiny5 400 (Fontsource, 9 KB) with Radio Canada Big 400, 600 and 400 italic (Fontsource, 11 KB each), none: Tiny5 covers the real data (page numbers, clock, plist keys)
Light
A viewer on the sofa in a dark Finnish living room on an October evening, the TV's teletext page the only light in the room. Scheme: dark.
Signature
Page search plus MIX. Typing three digits (anywhere on desktop, or in the keypad field on touch) makes the header counter roll 'P2--', 'P20-', 'P207', and the page goes, as on a TV. Hovering or focusing an index line switches MIX on: the black ground drops away and that app's own icon art fills the screen behind boxed text. Technique: a vanilla JS keydown listener (ignored inside inputs and with modifier keys) reads a Liquid-rendered JSON map of page number to URL. MIX is pure CSS: :has(.line:is(:hover,:focus-visible)) swaps a background layer whose image is each line's inline --pic custom property. No JS: lines are plain links, the keypad field is not rendered (it is an enhancement, not content), and MIX still works through CSS. Reduced motion: the counter shows the final number at once, and MIX is already instant.
Remembered as
The Lagerland site was a teletext page: 'P100 LAGERLAND' in the corner, yellow double-height titles, an index of apps with page numbers. I typed 207 and it jumped to Observa, and when I hovered a line, that app's icon came on air behind the text.
Risk
Retro-broadcast nostalgia is strong in Finland, the UK and Europe but unknown to many US visitors. A pixel face and seven full-saturation colours tip into 8-bit costume if Tiny5 ever reaches running text or headings in Read mode. The dark-only column carries 15-minute posts, and MIX over busy icon art (WanderWiki) needs every line boxed. The 'receive-only' idea must apply to the apps' declared network calls only, never to the website, which runs GoatCounter.
Full style card

First viewport, desktop

1440x900 as one 40x24 teletext page on black. Row 1: the header row in Tiny5 24px, 'P100' in magenta, 'LAGERLAND 100' in white, 'Mon 05 Oct' and a live '12:10:45' in yellow (no JS: build date, no clock). Rows 2-4: a blue band with the block-mosaic LAGERLAND in yellow across 1100px and the mosaic star mark in white at the right. Rows 5-8: the H1 in double-height Tiny5 yellow, two lines: 'Private apps for iPhone, / iPad, Watch and Mac.' Row 9: the lede in Radio Canada Big 20px white: '19 apps by one developer in Finland. No trackers, no ads, no accounts.' (count computed). Row 10 is split. On the left, the keypad 'PAGE _ _ _' in Tiny5 cyan with a blinking cursor. On the right, a boxed green newsflash: 'LEDGER 400 · TRACKING DOMAINS 0 · AD SDKs 0 · 18 MANIFESTS + 1 PENDING · AUDITED 11 JUN 2026' (computed). Rows 11-20: the P100 need index in two 20-column columns, 19 lines plus '200 All apps by need'. Each line is boxed black: cyan page number in Tiny5 18px, name in Radio Canada Big 600 19px white, a short need in 400 16px #D9D9D9. The newest release (Xiangqiful, 219) is selected on load, so MIX is on: its 1024px icon art fills the right 60% at viewport height behind the boxed lines, with no upscaling. Rows 21-23: the boxed subtitle panel for the selected app: tagline, price.value in green, cyan 'Go to 219 Xiangqiful', the official App Store badge (40px, on black) and the QR (100px, white quiet zone) at the right end. Row 24: Fastext keys in red Apps 200, green Journal 300, yellow Ledger 400 and cyan Index 100.

First viewport, phone

390x844, black. Header row 28px: 'P100 LAGERLAND 100 05 Oct 12:10' in Tiny5 13px (magenta number, yellow date). A 72px blue mosaic band with LAGERLAND in yellow blocks. H1 in double-height Tiny5 yellow, 30px, two lines; lede in Radio Canada Big 16/1.45 #D9D9D9, three lines. Keypad row 52px: 'PAGE', a three-digit numeric field (inputmode=numeric, 48px tall) and a cyan 'GO'. From y≈330, the index: blue genre band rows (32px, white Radio Canada Big 600) and need-lines 48px tall (cyan page number in Tiny5 16px, 28px squircle icon chip, name in Radio Canada Big 600 17px, need at 15px). The HEALTH band and six lines are visible. MIX is off on phones. The Fastext row is fixed at the bottom: 52px, four equal keys with black labels on red, green, yellow and cyan fields.

App Store route

The index is the routing: each need-line links to /apps/<slug>/, and its page number works as a typed shortcut (201-219 go to microsites; 501-604 go to alternatives pages, which wear their app's world). Selecting a line (hover or focus) puts that app on air behind the page (MIX) and fills the subtitle panel: tagline, price.value verbatim in green, a cyan 'Go to 207 Observa', the official App Store badge (unaltered, on its own black box) and, on desktop, the app's QR in a white quiet-zone box. Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly show the badge only. The sticky bar is the Fastext row (fixed at the bottom on mobile; the last grid row stays fixed on desktop). Smart App Banner: only on journal posts and guides with exactly one mentioned app. Icons are never redrawn into mosaic. The teletext frame stays uniform on purpose, and each app's art appears only as itself, in full colour: as the MIX picture and as the 28px squircle chip on mobile lines.

Page sequence

  1. Header row (page number, service, date, clock), the persistent frame
  2. P100 masthead: mosaic band, double-height H1, lede (the about-strip text, AI-canonical)
  3. Keypad row and the boxed transparency newsflash (computed counts → 400)
  4. Need index: 19 need-lines → microsites, with the MIX picture and subtitle panel (tagline, price, badge, QR) for the selected app
  5. P101 'New on air': the newest release (computed) and the latest two journal posts with page numbers
  6. P400 ledger excerpt: the 6-app transparency sample as a teletext table (blue header band, green values) → 'all 19, page 400'
  7. P500 Versus: four comparisons as results lines with dot leaders, plus the computed count → 500
  8. P800 About: founder line (Antti Aittamaa, one developer, Finland, since 2025), then six FAQ entries with yellow questions and white answers, all visible
  9. Close: contact line (email) and 'Back to 100'
  10. Footer P899: the full page directory (every page number → URL), studio links, privacy, support, 'Made on a MacBook at 63°N'

Navigation

Three systems, all plain links underneath. The header row shows where you stand (the current page number in magenta). The Fastext row of four coloured keys is on every page: red Apps 200, green Journal 300, yellow Transparency 400, cyan Index 100; on posts, red and green become previous and next. The keypad takes any three-digit page on any page; on desktop you can type digits anywhere outside a field, and the header counter rolls. Page map, computed by Liquid in ascending date order so numbers never change: 100 home; 200 /apps/ (201-219 microsites); 301-342 journal; 400 transparency; 500-699 alternatives; 700 guides (701-705); 710 /for/ (711-714); 800 about; 810 support.

Motion

Teletext has no easing: everything changes on a frame. On first load, once per session and only under html.js, rows arrive top to bottom in about 12 frames over 400ms, like a page being received; content is server-rendered visible, and the effect only replays it. The header counter rolls while digits are typed, the clock ticks seconds, and the cursor blinks in 1s steps. No fades, slides, glow or parallax. Reduced motion: no row arrival, the clock shows minutes without ticking, and the cursor is steady.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Every Read page is a numbered teletext page. The header row reads 'P312 LAGERLAND 312 date clock'. A blue band carries the section name in double-height Tiny5 yellow; the title is Radio Canada Big 700 at 40px, yellow on black; the meta line is Tiny5 cyan. The column is Radio Canada Big 18/1.65 #D9D9D9 on #000 at 66ch, with cyan underlined links. Each H2 sits on a full-width blue band row (white Radio Canada Big 700, 24px), teletext's new-background row. The Quick Answer is a boxed newsflash: a black panel opened by one full-width yellow band row titled 'Quick answer', with white 18px text. Tables have a blue header band and green values; label-to-value rows use dot leaders; plist keys are green Tiny5 16px. The Fastext row sits at the foot, sticky on mobile: red previous, green next, yellow section index, cyan 100. The journal index is P300, one line per post (date yellow, title white, page cyan). /transparency/ is P400, with in-page sections 401-419. The alternatives index is P500, results-style lines grouped under our app's name. Guides are P701-705, /for/ is P711-714, about P800, support P810. 404 reads 'PAGE NOT IN SERVICE' with the header counter still searching, followed by the P100 index.

Materials

40x24 character grid (36 x 37.5px cells at 1440x900) · header row: page number, service name, date, clock · full-width colour band rows · double-height title rows · 2x3 block-mosaic graphics (LAGERLAND wordmark, star mark) · boxed text over the MIX picture · Fastext row of four coloured keys · dot-leader index lines with cyan page numbers

Colour strategy

Full palette, each teletext colour with one job: yellow for titles and date, cyan for links and page numbers, green for declared data and prices, white for frame text, and blue for band rows (only behind text). Red, green, yellow and cyan are the Fastext keys; magenta is reserved for the current page number. No glow, scanlines or CRT curvature. · dark

Type rationale

Among Fontsource faces, Tiny5's blocky caps and stepped diagonals sit closest to the SAA5050 teletext character generator. It sets the header row, page numbers and double-height titles (transform: scaleY(2), a real teletext gesture) and never sets running text. Radio Canada Big is the open typeface made for a public broadcaster (CBC/Radio-Canada), with open apertures for screens: the broadcaster's voice for the reading column and app lines. Total about 42 KB.

New assets needed

A clean vector studio mark, plus a hand-authored 2x3 block-mosaic version of the star mark and of the LAGERLAND wordmark (SVG or CSS grid; a small vector task). Data: a per-app index_line front-matter field (28 characters or fewer, the need phrase on P100) and the Liquid page-number map. MIX uses the existing 1024px icons; screenshots and QR SVGs exist.

Observa

/apps/observa/ + its privacy and support pages + 8 comparison pages

What the page must prove: Within one viewport, the page has to prove four things. Observa turns your own data into a sentence about you: a real-form insight with its n and confidence, labelled as a sample. That sentence is measured against your own 60-day normal, not a population average. It is computed on the device. And it is free to start ('Free — Pro from $2.99/mo'), with the official App Store badge and, on desktop, the QR.

The default page this refuses: A dark navy or black dashboard: a floating iPhone mockup, neon activity and recovery rings, a 0–100 score dial, a glowing HRV line chart, a 'Your health, decoded' headline, a four-up feature-card grid and three pricing cards.

Today's page, for comparison
Picked
ObservaBodoni Moda

Apple Health Insights for Sleep, HRV & Recovery.

Sleep, energy & recovery insights.

THE ROLL

Atlas of Nights

Printed star atlases: the engraved Didone lettering of Bode's Uranographia (1801) and Wil Tirion's Sky Atlas 2000.0 field plates (white stars on deep blue, a coordinate grid, a magnitude legend, Bayer Greek designations). Also the observer's red-light rule and the observing log.

Your nights are stars plotted against your own 60-day baseline, and an Observa pattern is a constellation: a named shape of nights that belong together. As every star atlas admits, that is an association, not a cause. The page refuses the glowing score-ring dashboard.

  • #0E1C3A
  • #16274B
  • #2C406B
  • #E8ECF4
  • #9DAACB
  • #F2A766
  • #E0694B
Type
Bodoni Moda, variable opsz + wght, used at 500–700 (latin file ~45 KB): headlines at 36px and up, and constellation names in spaced capitals with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/700 (~12 KB each): all reading text, buttons, price statement, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono 400 (~10 KB), only for real measurements: n=14, 87%, p ≤ 0.10, σ axis labels, observing-log dates
Light
In bed around 22:30 with the room dark, phone dimmed and Night Shift on, the visitor is deciding whether last night's sleep means anything. So the page is dark and dark-adapted: warm accents, no large bright fields.
Signature
Draw the constellation. Three habit buttons under the sentence (Late leg day · Coffee after 14:00 · Screens in the last 30 min) redraw the apricot lines through that habit's nights on the same 60-star sky, using SVG stroke-dashoffset (700ms). They also swap the plate's metric label (deep-sleep share / resting heart rate) and reveal that habit's sample sentence from example_insights, with n and confidence where the data gives them (n=14 · 87%; n=23 · 91%). Without JS, the first constellation is drawn statically and all three sentences render as a list under the plate. With reduced motion, lines appear complete and the swap is instant.
Remembered as
The sleep app whose page was a star chart: my late-leg-day nights were joined into a constellation, and it said constellations are patterns, not causes.
Risk
This is the literal reading of the name and the most guessable direction. Dark navy with stars slides into a generic 'space' theme, or into the near-black-neon cluster, the moment anyone adds glow or twinkle. Didone on a dark plate can read as luxury fashion. The metaphor only lands if 'association, not cause' is printed next to every constellation. A night world may sit close to the sibling AfterShift.
Full style card

First viewport, desktop

At 1440×900, a 64px cartouche bar sits on top: icon 28px and 'Observa' in Bodoni Moda 600 24px at left, chart-index links (Sky · Catalogue · Method · Plans · Dark sky · Questions) in Atkinson 15px #9DAACB at right. The rest of the viewport is one atlas plate. 60 day-meridians run every 20px across x=120–1320, labelled along the bottom edge in Mono 12px (−60d … today). σ parallels run left to right, the 0σ line heavier and labelled 'your 60-day baseline' in Atkinson 13px, with the ±1σ zone tinted #16274B. The upper-left empty sky (x 120–780, y 110–420) holds the H1 'Apple Health Insights for Sleep, HRV & Recovery.' in Bodoni Moda 600 72/76px #E8ECF4. Below it: 'Your data already knows why.' in Atkinson 700, then the subheadline in Atkinson 19px #9DAACB at 46ch. The lower right (x 760–1320, y 450–770) holds 60 star nights. Fourteen of them sit below −1σ, ringed in ember and joined by apricot lines lettered 'LATE LEG DAY' (Bodoni 500 spaced caps 18px). Next to them: 'You sleep 18% less deeply on days you train legs after 18:00.' in Atkinson 700 22px, then Mono 13px 'n=14 over 60 days · 87% confidence · association, not cause', then the caption 'Sample insight on an illustrative sky' and three habit buttons in a row. The lower-left legend panel (x 120–680, y 690–860) holds 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' in Atkinson 700 22px, the official black App Store badge at 52px tall, and the QR at 104px on its own white tile with 'Point your iPhone camera here' at 13px.

First viewport, phone

At 390×844, a 56px cartouche: icon 24px and 'Observa' in Bodoni 600 20px at left, an 'Index' button at right. The H1 follows in Bodoni Moda 600 40/44px (4 lines, 16px gutters) on the plate ground, then 'Your data already knows why.' and the subheadline cut to two lines in Atkinson 17px (full text stays in the DOM). Next comes a full-width legend block: 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' in Atkinson 700 19px and the App Store badge at 48px tall, with no QR. Then the plate at 358×280 (60 meridians at 5.8px, labels every 20 days, constellation drawn), its sentence below in Atkinson 700 19px with Mono 12px numbers. The top of the plate is visible at the fold.

App Store route

The badge sits inside the atlas legend panel, where the panel's hairline is its frame and Apple's black artwork is untouched. The QR shows at 1024px and up only, on a white 'finder card' tile inside the same legend, dark-on-white as generated. The price statement is always 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' from price.value, in Atkinson 700. When the legend panel leaves the viewport, a 64px bottom margin strip (#16274B, 1px #2C406B top rule) slides up as the sticky bar: icon, 'Observa' in Bodoni 18px, price, and the badge at 40px. It hides again over the closing plate. The Smart App Banner meta goes in the head, and the cartouche leaves room for Safari's banner. The closing plate repeats the legend panel with badge, QR and price.

Page sequence

  1. The plate: H1, pre_headline, subheadline, an illustrative 60-night sky with the 'Late leg day' constellation and its sample sentence, three habit buttons, and the legend panel with price, badge and QR.
  2. Chart legend: the Quick Answer (quick_answer, speakable) as a 70ch Atkinson 20px paragraph on #16274B, with the Quick reference <details> directly beneath, visible and crawlable.
  3. Tonight's sky: example_insights.intro, then the six sample insights as six index rows of the plate. Each row has a 160×100 mini-plate with its own constellation, the headline in Atkinson 700 24px, the body, the tag, and the Mono n/confidence where given.
  4. Star catalogue: the ten metrics from the FAQ as a real table with columns for designation (α HRV (SDNN) … κ ECG sinus rhythm), metric, what Observa says about it, and source (Apple Watch, Oura, Whoop, Garmin, Fitbit via Apple Health; ECG needs Apple Watch).
  5. Limiting magnitude: the how_it_works intro and steps 1–6 numbered (HowTo) as an observing procedure. A magnitude legend shows that patterns below n ≥ 10 and p ≤ 0.10 stay unreported. The four value_points sit as plate notes.
  6. Through the eyepiece: six screenshots in a scroll-snap strip in plain black device frames with their front-matter captions, and the six features as a two-column list.
  7. Observing conditions: who_for ×5 and who_not_for ×4 as two columns, 'Observa is for you if' and 'Look elsewhere if'.
  8. Editions: the plans as one 4-column table (Free · Pro · Monthly · Pro · Annual · Lifetime). The Annual column is topped by a 2px apricot rule (highlight), Lifetime is marked 'Best long-term value', the plans_footnote sits below and the badge repeats.
  9. Other observers: five testimonials quoted verbatim with initials and source (the French one with its translation), no stars.
  10. Dark-sky site, the privacy section: a ledger of transparency.yml facts (network calls none · third-party SDKs 0 · tracking domains 0 · account not required · data leaves device no · analytics none), the Apple label sentence and privacy.notes, with links to /transparency/ and the privacy policy.
  11. The observer: the founder block with heading, story, signals, support email and response time.
  12. Questions: the 12 FAQs as <details> rows on catalogue hairlines.
  13. Other charts: alternatives_to as eight links to /alternatives/<slug>/ ('Apple Health (for interpretation)' as plain text), plus the related_journal link.
  14. Observing log: release_notes as dated Mono rows, then the freshness line 'Built by Lagerland Apps · updated 2026-07-11 · first released 2026-01-01'.
  15. Closing plate: 'Your sky is already in Apple Health.' with the legend panel (price, badge, QR), then the shared Lagerland strip.

Navigation

The cartouche is the microsite nav: the 'Observa' wordmark plus chart-index anchors (Sky · Catalogue · Method · Plans · Dark sky · Questions), which is the jump_nav set. An IntersectionObserver underlines the current section with a 1px apricot rule; without JS these are plain anchors. On mobile, an 'Index' <details> panel lists the same anchors plus Privacy and Support. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.

Motion

Slow and astronomical. On first view the stars come out brightest-first over 1.2s (opacity only), then the constellation draws at constant speed. No twinkle, parallax or glow. Section reveals are 300ms opacity fades, gated by html.js with the 2.5s safety net, so content is never hidden without JS. With prefers-reduced-motion everything is static and visible at once.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the eight alternatives pages keep the cartouche and open with a 200px plate strip (grid and a scatter of stars, no constellation) carrying the H1 in Bodoni Moda 600 48px. The reading column is 66ch of Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 18/1.65 #E8ECF4 on #0E1C3A, with Mono for 'last updated'. On the privacy page, policy sections are catalogue entries. On the alternatives pages, the 4-point compare grid becomes a two-column catalogue table (Observa vs the competitor: scope, where compute happens, what you get back, account & pricing), 'pick Observa if' / 'keep X if' become two lists, and the FAQ is <details>. Each page closes with a slim legend panel holding price and badge.

Materials

Atlas plate: deep-blue ground with a fine grid of 60 day-meridians and σ parallels (+2, +1, 0, −1, −2) · White star dots sized like magnitudes; constellation lines 1.5px apricot, member nights ringed in ember · Engraved lettering: Didone spaced capitals laid along constellation lines · Legend panel: #16274B fill with a 1px #2C406B hairline, like an atlas key · Star-catalogue table with Greek designations and hairline rules · Observing-log rows with Mono dates

Colour strategy

Committed · dark

Type rationale

Engraved celestial atlases of the Bode/Burritt era were lettered in Didone romans, and Bodoni Moda's optical sizes keep those hairlines crisp on a dark plate. The Braille Institute drew Atkinson Hyperlegible for low-vision legibility, which suits a dimmed phone at bedtime, and its Mono sibling sets the numbers in the same voice. About 79 KB in total.

New assets needed

None. The plate, grid and constellations are inline SVG built from an illustrative 60-value array kept in the page and labelled illustrative. The icon, screenshots and QR already exist.

ObservaSchibsted Grotesk

Apple Health Insights for Sleep, HRV & Recovery.

Sleep, energy & recovery insights.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

The Morning Bulletin

Public-service weather bulletins: the Finnish Meteorological Institute's readings against the 1991–2020 climate normal ('3° below normal'), the BBC Shipping Forecast's fixed spoken order of areas, the newspaper weather box, and the forecast's stated probability.

This is a body bulletin, not a dashboard. Every reading is a calm sentence set against your own normal with its confidence beside it, and the numbers open only when asked. The opening has no charts at all, which refuses the score-ring dashboard and the floating phone.

  • #F2F4F5
  • #FFFFFF
  • #16212B
  • #56636E
  • #1F5FA8
  • #B4471B
Type
Schibsted Grotesk 700/800 (variable wght, latin ~46 KB): H1, area names, prices with Public Sans 400/600 (variable wght, latin ~26 KB): bulletin sentences and all body text, tabular figures (tnum) for n and confidence, none; figures are set in Public Sans with tnum
Light
A weekday at 06:45, standing at the kitchen window in grey northern daylight, phone in one hand and coffee in the other, checking the weather and last night's sleep in the same minute. That makes the page light.
Signature
Sentence ⇄ numbers. Each bulletin row is a <details> whose summary is the sentence. Opening it shows the numbers the app reveals on tap (how_it_works step 5): a normal-range bar with a white ±1σ corridor on grey and one tick for the reading, labelled 'your 60-day normal (illustrative band)', plus the n, the window and the confidence. JS only animates the height (180ms) and slides the tick into place (240ms). Without JS, native <details> works fully. With reduced motion, rows open instantly and the tick is static.
Remembered as
The one that read like a morning weather bulletin ('Sleep: below normal'), where every line opened to show its numbers against my own normal.
Risk
This is Impeccable's pick and the most familiar of the seven: 'readiness' and forecast language are already common in recovery apps. The craft has to live in the bulletin's typographic discipline, so no weather symbols are used. A chart-free opening may undersell the app's rich dark UI, which only appears from the fifth section. 'Forecast' implies prediction, so copy must say 'normal' and 'reading' and never promise future days. Watch the sibling Soon., which carries weather in its UI.
Full style card

First viewport, desktop

At 1440×900, a 56px header bar on #F2F4F5: icon 28px and 'Observa' in Schibsted 800 22px at left; Today · Normal · Readings · Plans · Privacy · Questions in Public Sans 600 15px at right. The H1 'Apple Health Insights for Sleep, HRV & Recovery.' is set in Schibsted Grotesk 800 68/72px #16212B, left-aligned at x=120 and running two lines across 1200px. Under it: 'Your data already knows why.' in Public Sans 600, then the subheadline at 20px #56636E, 64ch. Then a white bulletin sheet spans x=120–1320 under a 3px ink top rule. It holds four 64px reading rows drawn from example_insights, for example: Sleep, 'Deep sleep 18% lower on nights after a leg day past 18:00.', 'below normal' in blue, '87% · n=14'. And: Heart, 'Resting heart rate +4 bpm the morning after coffee past 14:00.', 'above normal' in rust, '91% · n=23'. Area names are in Schibsted 800 30px, sentences in Public Sans 20px, and every row has a chevron that opens its numbers. The sheet's last row is the issue row: 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' in Schibsted 800 24px, the official App Store badge at 52px, the QR at 104px with 'Scan with your iPhone camera' at 13px, and 'Sample bulletin from the app's example insight cards' at 13px #56636E.

First viewport, phone

At 390×844, a 52px bar: icon and 'Observa' in Schibsted 800 20px at left, a 'Sections' button at right. The H1 in Schibsted 800 38/41px (4 lines), then 'Your data already knows why.' and the subheadline in Public Sans 17px. The issue block comes next in DOM order: 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' in Schibsted 800 20px and the App Store badge at 48px, with no QR. Then the bulletin sheet runs edge to edge with 16px padding. Each row stacks: area name (Schibsted 800 22px) at left with the against-normal word (15px) at right on one line, the sentence below in Public Sans 17px, and '87% · n=14' at 14px. The first reading row sits at the fold.

App Store route

The App Store badge is the bulletin's issue row (the way to receive the bulletin), with Apple's artwork untouched on white. The QR sits in the issue row at 1024px and up. The price statement 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' leads the row in Schibsted 800, taken from price.value. Once the issue row scrolls away, a 60px white sticky bar with a 3px ink top rule slides up: icon · 'Observa' · price · badge at 40px. The Smart App Banner meta goes in the head. The closing section repeats the issue row with price, badge and QR.

Page sequence

  1. Bulletin: H1, pre_headline, subheadline, four sample reading rows from example_insights (each expandable to its numbers), and the issue row with price, badge and QR.
  2. The short forecast: the Quick Answer (speakable) as one 70ch Public Sans 20px paragraph on white, with the Quick reference <details> beneath it, visible.
  3. What 'normal' means here: one paragraph contrasting a weather service's 30-year normal with Observa's 60-day personal normal. Then the four value_points as plain sentences in a two-column list, and the how_it_works intro with steps 1–6 numbered (HowTo).
  4. The readings: the ten metrics read in a fixed order, like the shipping forecast ('HRV (SDNN). Resting heart rate. Sleep efficiency. …'), each with one line of meaning. A source line follows: Apple Watch, Oura, Whoop, Garmin, Fitbit via Apple Health; ECG needs Apple Watch.
  5. Every morning on your iPhone: six screenshots in a scroll-snap strip on #16212B panels (to match the app's dark UI) with their front-matter captions, and the six features as a definition list.
  6. Conditions: who_for and who_not_for as a two-column table, 'For you if' and 'Not for you if'.
  7. Subscriptions: one bulletin-style table with columns Free · Pro · Monthly · Pro · Annual · Lifetime and the price row in Schibsted 800 32px. The Annual column sits on the white 'normal' fill (highlight), Lifetime is marked 'Best long-term value', and the plans_footnote follows.
  8. Letters: five testimonials quoted verbatim with initials and source (French with translation), no stars.
  9. Where the bulletin is computed: 'On your iPhone. Nowhere else.' Then the transparency.yml facts as reading rows (network calls · third-party SDKs · tracking domains · account · data leaves device · analytics), the Apple label sentence and privacy.notes, with links to /transparency/ and the privacy policy.
  10. Who issues it: the founder block (heading, story, signals, support email, response time).
  11. Questions: the 12 FAQs as <details> rows on the bulletin grid.
  12. Other services: alternatives_to as eight linked rows ('Observa vs AutoSleep'; 'Apple Health (for interpretation)' as plain text), plus the related_journal link.
  13. Past issues: release_notes as dated issue lines, then the freshness line (Built by Lagerland Apps · updated 2026-07-11 · first released 2026-01-01).
  14. Closing issue row: 'Your first patterns need about 14 days of data.' (from the FAQ) with price, badge and QR, then the shared Lagerland strip.

Navigation

The header bar carries the six anchors (the jump_nav set). On scroll it condenses to 44px, and the current anchor gets a 2px ink underline. On mobile, 'Sections' is a <details> list that also includes the Privacy policy and Support. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.

Motion

Broadcast cuts, not fades. Sections appear without entrance animation. The only motion is row expansion, the tick settling into the normal band, and the sticky bar sliding in over 160ms. With reduced motion there are no transitions at all.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the eight alternatives pages read as bulletin notices. They keep the same header bar, set the H1 in Schibsted 800 48px, and add a one-line issue stamp (page type · last updated) in Public Sans 14px. The reading column is 68ch of Public Sans 18/1.6 on a white sheet over #F2F4F5. On the alternatives pages the compare grid becomes fixed-order rows (Scope · Where compute happens · What you get back · Account & pricing) with Observa and the competitor in two columns, 'pick Observa if' / 'keep X if' become two lists, and the FAQ is <details>. Each page closes with the issue row (price and badge).

Materials

Bulletin sheet: white panels with a 3px ink top rule and 1px row hairlines · Fixed-order reading rows on a 4-column grid: area · sentence · against normal · confidence · Anomaly words with 8px square ticks in the below-normal and above-normal colours · Normal-range bar (inside expanded rows only): white ±1σ corridor on grey with one value tick · Issue row and issue stamps: the bulletin's own date-and-subscription line

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

Schibsted Grotesk was drawn for the Nordic newspaper group whose papers carry the daily weather page. It is sturdy and slightly blunt, with big figures that hold up at 70px. Public Sans is the plain sans of government public information: the bulletin's neutral reading voice, with tabular numerals for readings. About 72 KB in total.

New assets needed

None.

SECOND ROLL

Sixty-Row Blanket

The temperature blanket (knitters' one-row-per-day colour record keyed to a temperature chart) and Ed Hawkins' warming stripes, knitted into scarves. Also the knitter's 'lifeline' thread, the woven garment and care label, and the app icon's folded ribbon.

Sixty nights, one knitted row each, every row dyed by how far that night sat from your own normal, so the pattern Observa finds is visible in the cloth. Making the data a textile you read by colour refuses charts and score rings.

  • #D9D0DA
  • #1F2248
  • #4B3C7A
  • #EE9A5A
  • #A8421E
  • #1A1C24
  • #FFFFFF
Type
Handjet (@fontsource-variable/handjet full file: wght + ELGR element-grid + ELSH element-shape axes, latin ~19 KB): H1 and section heads at 800, with the element shape tuned in build so letters read as rows of stitches with Familjen Grotesk 400/600 (variable wght, latin ~18 KB): all reading text, key labels, tables, price, none; tabular figures from Familjen Grotesk for n, σ and prices
Light
A late Saturday morning, still in bed under the duvet with low winter sun across the covers, reading Observa's weekly reflection on the phone. That makes the page light.
Signature
Re-dye against your normal. A two-state switch sits under the blanket. 'Against an average adult' colours all 60 rows against one population reference, and most rows collapse into one or two yarns: the flat, uninformative picture. 'Against your own 60 days' re-dyes the rows against your baseline. The late-leg-day nights then stand out in indigo, and the sentence 'You sleep 18% less deeply on days you train legs after 18:00 · n=14 · 87% confidence' appears beside them. Technically, a class on the blanket swaps a CSS custom property per row, and background-color transitions stagger top to bottom (6ms per row, 280ms each) like dye wicking. Without JS, both blankets render (side by side on desktop, stacked on mobile), each with its caption. With reduced motion the swap is instant.
Remembered as
The striped-blanket page: one row per night, and when I switched from 'average adult' to 'my own 60 days' the colours rearranged and my leg-day nights stood out in indigo.
Risk
It ranks sixth for resonance: knitting is not native to the quantified-self audience and can read craft-cute against a statistics app. The drenched multi-colour bands need strict AA pairing per band (rust and violet take white text only). Handjet is idiosyncratic and must stay at 40px or above. Both reference states are illustrative and must say so. Warm textiles can drift toward the spent cozy-cream palette, so heather and indigo must hold the ground, never cream.
Full style card

First viewport, desktop

At 1440×900 everything sits on heather knit. At the top is an 8px indigo cast-off scallop. The nav row (y 8–64) holds a woven-label wordmark at x=120: a 160×40 indigo label with a dashed white stitch border, the icon at 24px and 'Observa' in Handjet 700 26px white. Blanket · Pattern · Lifeline · Plans · Care label · Questions sit at right in Familjen 600 15px ink. The H1 'Apple Health Insights for Sleep, HRV & Recovery.' runs two lines in Handjet 800 104/98px ink across x=120–1200, followed by 'Your data already knows why.' in Familjen 600 and the subheadline at 20px, 60ch. Then comes the dominant move, full bleed at 1440 wide: the blanket, 60 rows of 5px (300px tall), each row the yarn of one illustrative night with last night at the top. The left gutter is labelled 'last night', '30 nights', '60 nights ago' in Familjen 12px, and the right gutter holds the 5-yarn key with σ ranges in tabular figures. Sewn onto the blanket at x=860–1320 is an indigo woven-label patch (460×210) holding 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' in Familjen 600 22px white, the official App Store badge at 52px, and the QR at 104px on its white tile with 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. Directly under the blanket: the reference switch ('Against an average adult' / 'Against your own 60 days') in Familjen 600 16px, and the caption 'Illustrative nights; sample insight from the app's example cards'.

First viewport, phone

At 390×844: the cast-off scallop, then the woven-label wordmark (Handjet 700 20px) at left with a 'Contents' button at right. The H1 in Handjet 800 52/50px (4 lines) ink on heather, then the pre_headline and the subheadline cut to two lines in Familjen 17px (full text stays in the DOM). App Store route

Price and badge are sewn onto the blanket as a woven label: Apple's black badge sits untouched inside the indigo patch, and the badge's own outline keeps it distinct. The QR shows at 1024px and up inside the same label, on a white tile. The price 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' comes from price.value. Once the hero label leaves view, a 60px indigo ribbon with a dashed stitched top edge rises as the sticky bar: wordmark, price, badge at 40px. The Smart App Banner meta goes in the head. Page sequence

  1. Blanket (hero): H1, pre_headline, subheadline, the 60-row blanket with its key, the woven-label action patch, and the reference switch.
  2. Quick answer: on a heather band, the Quick Answer (speakable) as a 70ch Familjen 20px paragraph, with the Quick reference <details> beneath, visible.
  3. The pattern in the cloth: example_insights.intro (stating these are sample cards), then the six insights as six full-width bands, each in the yarn of its direction (below normal indigo/violet, above normal apricot/rust, holding steady heather). Each band has the headline in Handjet 800 44px, the body in Familjen 18px, and the tag and n/confidence in tabular figures.
  4. Lifeline: one sentence of analogy ('Knitters run a lifeline through a row they trust; your 60-day baseline is that row'), then how_it_works steps 1–6 numbered (HowTo) with the apricot thread running through step 2, then the four value_points as short sentences.
  5. Yarn label, i.e. what it reads: the ten metrics as fibre content, a 'Spun from' line (Apple Watch, Oura, Whoop, Garmin, Fitbit via Apple Health; ECG needs Apple Watch), and a 'Gauge' line (n ≥ 10 nights, p ≤ 0.10).
  6. Off the needles: six screenshots in a scroll-snap strip on an indigo band, where the app's navy UI sits naturally, with captions in white Familjen. The six features follow as a two-column list.
  7. Who it fits: who_for and who_not_for as two columns on apricot, 'Fits you if' and 'Look elsewhere if'.
  8. Sizes: the plans as a pattern-sizing table with Free · Pro · Monthly · Pro · Annual · Lifetime across and features down. The Annual column is on apricot (highlight), Lifetime is marked 'Best long-term value', and the plans_footnote follows.
  9. What people said: five testimonials quoted verbatim on the violet band in white Familjen 20px, with initials and source (French with translation), no stars.
  10. Care label, the privacy section: an indigo woven care label listing the transparency.yml facts plainly (stays on device · network calls none · third-party SDKs 0 · tracking domains 0 · no account · analytics none), the Apple label sentence and privacy.notes, with links to /transparency/ and the privacy policy.
  11. Made by: the founder block on heather (heading, story, signals, support email, response time).
  12. Questions: the 12 FAQs as <details> rows, separated by single knitted rows.
  13. Compared with: alternatives_to as eight links to /alternatives/<slug>/ ('Apple Health (for interpretation)' as plain text), plus the related_journal link.
  14. Rows added: release_notes as dated lines, then the freshness line (Built by Lagerland Apps · updated 2026-07-11 · first released 2026-01-01).
  15. Cast-on edge: a closing indigo band with 'The first rows are already in Apple Health.', price, badge and QR, then the scalloped cast-on edge and the shared Lagerland strip.

Navigation

The woven-label wordmark plus six anchors (Blanket · Pattern · Lifeline · Plans · Care label · Questions), which form the jump_nav set. The current anchor gets a 2px apricot thread underline. On mobile, 'Contents' is a <details> list that also includes Privacy and Support. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.

Motion

Slow and vertical, like textile. The only choreography is the dye stagger running down the rows and the sticky ribbon rising over 200ms. Bands do not slide or parallax. Hovering a row outlines it with a 1px ink line, no shadow. With reduced motion there is no motion.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the eight alternatives pages keep the cast-off edge and the woven-label header. Under an H1 in Handjet 800 56px runs a 24px 'selvedge': the 60 rows compressed into one thin stripe. The reading column is 68ch of Familjen Grotesk 18/1.65 in ink on heather. Policy sections are set as care-label lines. On the alternatives pages the compare grid becomes a pattern-sizing table (Observa | competitor across; Scope, Where compute happens, What you get back, Account & pricing down), 'pick / keep' become two columns, and the FAQ is <details>. Each page closes with a woven-label CTA patch holding price and badge.

Materials

Stockinette knit: an inline SVG V-stitch texture at ~6% contrast over flat yarn colours (text sits on the flat layer) · 60 knitted rows, one per night, from a 5-yarn key · Scalloped cast-off (top) and cast-on (bottom) edges · Woven labels: indigo patches with a dashed white 'stitched' border for the wordmark, the action and the care label · The lifeline: a single 2px apricot thread drawn through one row · Pattern-sizing tables (sizes across, amounts down) for the plans

Colour strategy

Drenched · light

Type rationale

Handjet is an element-based typeface built so letters can be assembled from units such as stitches or cross-stitch, so the headlines here are knitted in rather than printed on. Familjen Grotesk, from a Stockholm studio, is a calm Nordic grotesk whose squared joins sit beside the stitch grid without competing. About 37 KB in total.

New assets needed

None. The stitch texture is an inline SVG pattern, and the rows are divs built from an illustrative 60-night array in two reference states, kept in the page and labelled illustrative.

Today's page, for comparison
Picked
ChessfulSaira

Stop guessing. Start understanding.

Understand your mistakes. Improve every game.

THE ROLL

The Sensory Board

The dedicated chess computers of 1977–1990: Fidelity Electronics' Chess Challenger (1977, the first commercial unit) and its Sensory boards, Hegener + Glaser's Mephisto, Novag and SciSys/Saitek. They had a printed playing surface with an LED at each square that lit the from- and to-square of the machine's move. They also had a strip of membrane keys (NEW GAME, LEVEL, TAKE BACK, HINT, VERIFY, INFO), a small LCD readout, a level picked on many models by pressing a square, and a printed level table in the manual. The offline engine you bought once, and it never told you why.

The page is the offline chess machine rebuilt to do what it never could. The board lights the move you played and the better one, the readout says why in a sentence, and LEVEL picks one of 40 different players by square instead of one engine at 64 settings. It refuses the phone-in-a-bezel split hero and the dark eval-graph dashboard.

  • #26292B

Type
Saira (variable, wdth 50–125, wght 100–900; @fontsource-variable/saira full-axis latin 99 KB). H1 and section legends use wdth 112 wght 700, membrane-key legends wdth 100 wght 600 caps 14px, and the 'CHESSFUL' brand plate wdth 125 wght 800. with Red Hat Text 400/600 (@fontsource/red-hat-text, 14.5 KB each) sets the manual's reading text: the LCD sentence, quick start, Q&A, privacy and about prose at 16–22px., Doto 700 (@fontsource/doto, 4 KB) is a dot-matrix face used only inside the LCD for real data: move lines (Nxd5? BEST Bf4), ELO numbers and square coordinates.
Light
A player at the kitchen table on a weeknight with the unit flat under the overhead lamp. The matte light-grey plastic is lit by the room, and the red and green LED points are the only emitted light → light (color-scheme: light).
Signature
Level by Square. The LEVEL board is a CSS grid of 64 <a> squares, with the 40 opponents on a1–h5 and ranks 6–8 printed blank. Tapping or arrow-keying to a square (roving tabindex, Enter to select) lights its LED and writes 'PEBBLE · 400 · BALANCED' to the LCD through an aria-live polite region, and the matching level-table row is marked. Without JS, each square is a plain link to its row in the fully visible level table, and the LCD server-renders the first opponent. Under reduced motion the LED switches instantly with no fade or blink.
Remembered as
A grey chess-computer page. The board lit red on my mistake and green on the better move, a little display told me why in one sentence, and pressing LEVEL let me pick one of forty named opponents by square.
Risk
Retro hardware can tip into nostalgia cosplay or a toy look. It has to stay matte, quiet and functional, with the board doing real work. The board-plus-control-panel arrangement must read as one instrument (one housing, keys, wells), not as copy-left/product-right. The chess computer is exactly the 'one engine at levels' that Chessful argues against, so the copy must make that the point and never imply a slider. Younger players may not know the machine, though lit squares and labelled keys read without the reference. Red and green are never the only cue: 'you played' and 'best was' are always printed. A wrong position or roster detail is a visible factual error.

Navigation

The six membrane keys are the microsite nav: NEW GAME (#pricing, red cap), LEVEL (#opponents), TAKE BACK (#templates), HINT (#how-it-works), VERIFY (#privacy), INFO (#quick-reference and #faq). Each key carries a plain sub-legend ('LEVEL · 40 opponents'). The active section's key shows a lit red LED dot. Past the hero the key strip pins to the top with the badge. On mobile, KEYS opens a <details> 2×3 key grid.

Motion

Only LEDs move. A lit LED fades in over 120ms as the previous one goes out. HINT blinks the green pair twice (2×300ms), the way a real unit shows its move, then holds steady. Membrane keys press in 1px on :active. No scroll reveals, parallax or sliding panels. prefers-reduced-motion gives instant states with no blink.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives are the unit's printed manual. The graphite key strip is the masthead (brand plate, six keys linking back to the microsite, badge right), housing grey is the frame, and the reading column is a #EEEFEA plate 68ch wide in Red Hat Text 17/28 graphite with Saira 700 headings. Privacy opens with the VERIFY LED panel (transparency facts), then the policy text. Support is the 'Service' page: the email in Saira 700 24px, response time, what to include, and the maker's plate. Alternatives print 'Chessful or Chess.com' on the housing. The comparison runs as a spec table on the plate, 'Pick Chessful if… / Stay with Chess.com if…' become the Suitable / Not suitable boxes, then Q & A, with a module well and badge at the foot.

The main legend is Saira caps with a Red Hat 11px sub-legend saying what the key opens · Recessed LCD window (#A7B29A, 2px inset shadow) carrying a Doto move line and a Red Hat sentence · Program-module well: a recessed slot in the housing where the official App Store badge sits with the price printed beside it · Model-label sticker: a #EEEFEA rectangle with fine print holding the QR and the maker line · Diagram pieces from an open-licence SVG set

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

Saira's squared shoulders read as pad-printed legends on 1980s consumer electronics (the period's Eurostile register) without sci-fi costume. One file gives the wide brand plate and normal-width keycaps. Red Hat Text keeps long instructions comfortable at 16px with open apertures in the same engineered-grotesk tone. Doto is the readout's own matrix and stays on data. Total ≈133 KB.

New assets needed

(1) The full 40-opponent roster exported from the app (name, ELO, style, tier). Screenshots show only nine names and tiers of five; the a1–h5 layout assumes 8 tiers × 5, and if that is wrong the opponents go in rating order. (2) Six illustrative positions (FEN) authored for the six example_insights, engine-checked and labelled 'illustrative position'. (3) An open-licence SVG piece set (e.g. cburnett, CC BY-SA 3.0, credited in the footer). Everything else (icon, screenshots, QR, badge) exists.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

Move by Move

The annotated-games book: Irving Chernev's Logical Chess: Move by Move (1957), which explains every move of 33 master games in plain words, and the tradition it started (Everyman's 'Move by Move' series, the club-library game collection). Its furniture is a contents page, 'who this book is for', a preface, games headed by players and opening, bold figurine moves each followed by a sentence, printed diagrams with diagonally hatched dark squares and a side-to-move mark, a frontispiece facing the title page, chapter exercises with solutions at the back, and a colophon.

The page is the chess book every stuck club player is told to read, written about your own games. Your move is in bold with its '?', one sentence explains it, a hatched diagram shows the turning point, and the exercises are built from your losses with the solutions at the back. It refuses the dark-navy app-landing hero and the centipawn-graph analysis page.

  • #151515
  • #5F5F5A

Type
Literata (variable, opsz 7–72, wght 200–900; @fontsource-variable/literata opsz+wght roman latin 110 KB) at opsz 72 wght 650 for the title, chapter heads and contents. No italic display anywhere. with Literata at opsz 12–18, wght 400 for annotations and prose (18/30px), wght 700 for figurine moves, and opsz 8 for diagram coordinates and running heads., No third face. Figurines (♔♕♖♗♘♙) are inline SVG from the diagram piece set, sized 0.9em on the baseline.
Light
A club player on the morning commute, reading on the phone in daylight the way they would read a chess book on the train: white paper, black ink, one green marking pen → light.
Signature
Play through. Every bold move in an annotation is a button bound to its diagram. Tap '♘xd5?' to see the position after your move with the played squares outlined, and tap 'Better was ♗f4' to switch to the improvement with the green ring (aria-pressed on the move buttons). Each diagram server-renders both positions as static <table> boards. JS shows one at a time and swaps on tap. Without JS, both print side by side at half size, captioned 'After your move' and 'After the better move'. Under reduced motion the swap is instant with no crossfade.
Remembered as
It read like a chess book about my own games. There was a hatched diagram, my move in bold with a question mark, and one plain sentence telling me what I'd missed. The App Store button sat where a publisher's name goes on a title page.
Risk
This is the most familiar of the three. A bookish serif page sits next to the editorial-serif cluster that AI pages fall into. It is the pick because the annotated book is literally the lineage of Chessful's promise, and it escapes the cluster only by being a chess book rather than a magazine: hatched diagrams, bold figurine moves, a contents page and running heads, white not cream, no italic display, no tracked labels. The spread must collapse to one honest page on phones, never a narrow column with fake page edges. The frontispiece facing the title page must read as a book spread, not copy-and-product. A wrong diagram will be spotted by players. Literata's 110 KB leaves no room for a second face.

Navigation

A real contents page is the nav. The verso running head carries 'Contents', which opens a <details> list of chapters (works without JS). The recto running head always names the current chapter, server-rendered as the first chapter and then updated by IntersectionObserver. On mobile the running head is the top strip with 'Contents'. No hamburger icon, no pills.

Motion

Paper barely moves. Diagram swaps crossfade over 160ms, and the sticky running-head strip slides 52px in over 180ms. No scroll reveals, parallax or animated numbers. prefers-reduced-motion makes everything instant.

SECOND ROLL

Key to Symbols

Chess Informant (Šahovski Informator, Belgrade, from 1966) published master games annotated without words, in figurine algebraic notation and a language-independent sign system. The signs include ! good move, ? mistake, ?? blunder, !? interesting, ?! dubious, □ only move, △ with the idea, ± clear advantage, +− winning, ∞ unclear, ⌓ weak point, → attack, ⇆ counterplay and N novelty. Each volume explains them once, at the front, in a multilingual 'Key to symbols' table.

Chess's most famous annotation system was built to need no words, and Chessful's whole point is the words. The page is set as one long key to symbols: every sign a reader half-knows, followed by the sentence it never said, so the signs are the navigation and the sentences are the product. It refuses the board-in-a-phone hero and the eval-graph dashboard, and there is no board in the first viewport at all.

Type
Anybody (variable, wdth 50–150, wght 100–900; @fontsource-variable/anybody full-axis latin 57 KB). Sign glyphs (? ! ?! !? N 0) use wdth 150 wght 900 at 96–220px, H1 and row headlines wdth 80 wght 800, nav and labels wdth 90 wght 600, and moves wght 700. with Source Serif 4 (variable wght 200–900; @fontsource-variable/source-serif-4 wght roman latin 51 KB) sets Chessful's sentences, FAQ, about prose and privacy text at 18–26px in weights 400/600., Inline SVG for the non-ASCII signs (□ △ ± ∓ ⌓ ∞ → ⇆), drawn to Anybody Black's stroke weight, and for figurines. Noto Sans Math (270 KB) and Noto Sans Symbols 2's symbols subset (382 KB) bust the budget and are rejected.
Light
Late evening on the sofa, the lost game still open on the phone in a dark room. The page arrives as a saturated cobalt field with paper-white signs → dark (color-scheme: dark).
Signature
Symbols / Sentences. A masthead toggle (aria-pressed, inserted by JS) sets data-mode='notation' on <html>. The whole page then collapses into pure annotation: moves, signs and the engine line only (e.g. '♗d3? (♕d2!)', '+3.8 → −8.1'), with every sentence hidden. Pressing again brings the words back, so the visitor feels exactly what Chessful adds. Words is the default, and crawlers always get both. Without JS there is no toggle: each row prints the sentence large with its notation line small beneath it. Under reduced motion the swap is instant with no crossfade or height animation.
Remembered as
A bright blue page with a giant question mark next to 'Stop guessing' and an exclamation mark next to 'Start understanding'. Every section was marked with a chess annotation sign, and a switch turned the whole page into symbols and back into plain sentences.
Risk
It relies on chess-literate wit. Visitors who have never seen annotation signs must still get it instantly, so every sign always carries its word. A cobalt drench is loud for a calm brand, and it may read 'fintech blue' to anyone without the signs, so long reading happens only on paper panels. Signs used as section markers can slide into decoration, so each must keep its real chess meaning (? mistakes, △ with the idea, ⌓ weak point, N novelty, ∞ unclear, !? worth a try, ?! dubious). Having no board above the fold is a bold bet in a category where visitors expect one, so the screenshots must carry the visual proof. The toggle could be mistaken for a language switch, so it is labelled plainly.
