App Store route

The official black badge sits on cobalt in the install row and is never recoloured. The price is set as that row's headline. The QR is the install row's sign: a scannable sign in the sign column on a paper tile at ≥1024px with hover:hover. On touch and mobile the app icon replaces it. Sticky bar: after the install row leaves, the masthead gains the price (Anybody 700 16px) and a 40px badge at its right end. On mobile a 60px cobalt strip with a 2px paper rule is fixed to the bottom with the icon, price and badge. The Price row (#pricing) is a sub-key of four entries on a paper key page: plan name | price | what's in it. Annual is marked with a gold '!' ('recommended, ~50% cheaper than monthly') and Lifetime with 'Best long-term value', followed by plans_footnote. The install row (QR/icon, price, badge) repeats after the comparison and at the foot. The Smart App Banner meta stays in head.

Page sequence

  1. Masthead: icon, wordmark, sign nav, Symbols / Sentences toggle
  2. Hero key rows: '?' Stop guessing. / '!' Start understanding. with the example-1 sentence and the engine line / install row (QR or icon, price, badge)
  3. 'In short' row: quick_answer on cobalt at 22/32px, speakable
  4. 'Key' row: the ai-canonical quick reference as an open <details> paper key page (spec table: engine, platforms, price, account, network, opponents, dimensions, languages)
  5. '?' rows (#templates): six key rows, one per example_insight. Each has the tag as row label, the headline in Anybody 800 32px, the body in Source Serif 19px, a gold '!' line with the better move, the pattern name and a notation line drawn from the body's own moves (no invented evaluations)
  6. '⌓' weak point → Training: value point 2 plus the five skill dimensions as a sub-key (tactics, defense, positional play, openings, endgames). Spaced repetition, Free 3 sessions/week vs Premium unlimited, 90/180/365-day trends, link to the 30-motif post
  7. '△' with the idea → Method (#how-it-works): how_it_works steps numbered 1–6 (real sequence; HowTo)
  8. 'Screens' row: six screenshots on paper tiles in a horizontal snap strip with captions
  9. '40' row: the forty opponents (feature 3, roster names once exported, link to the forty-opponents post). The other features and value points follow as a plain sub-key
  10. '!?' Worth a try if… (who_for 6) and '?!' Probably not for you if… (who_not_for 4, linking Chess.com, Lichess and Magnus Trainer pages)
  11. '±' Compared (#compare-heading-chessful): 'In notation, ± means one side stands better. Here is where, row by row, including where the others do.' comparison_table on a paper key page with the Chessful column in bold, intro, footnote, then the install row
  12. 'Price' row (#pricing)
  13. '0' row (#privacy): '0 tracking domains · 0 third-party SDKs · 0 accounts' as a transparency facts table on paper, privacy.notes, links to /transparency/#chessful and the privacy policy
  14. 'About' row: show_body under about_heading on a paper key page, 66ch, in-body links kept
  15. 'Maker' row: founder heading, story, 4 signals, studio link, support email + response time; then 'Readers write': the two real Reddit quotes (S., V.V.)
  16. 'N' novelty → Roadmap: shipped / targeted items with their dates + disclaimer
  17. '∞' unclear → Questions: all 14 FAQ open on a paper key page (FAQPage)
  18. 'See also' row: related_journal, the training and 30-motif posts, the best-chess-apps guide, the six alternatives pages, Shogiful and Xiangqiful
  19. Closing install row; maker/freshness line (Built by Lagerland Apps · first released 2026-04-01 · last updated 2026-05-13); shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

The key is the nav. The masthead lists signs with their words ('? Mistakes', '△ Method', '⌓ Training', '± Compared', 'Price', '∞ Questions') as plain links, and the active row's sign is underlined 2px paper. On mobile the 'Key' button opens a <details> list of every row (sign + word + anchor), the literal key to the page. Signs always carry their word, never a sign alone.

Motion

Typographic only. Signs never animate. On toggle, sentences and notation crossfade over 140ms and rows change height without animation. Signs hold their place as long rows scroll past (CSS sticky, no JS). No reveals, parallax or counters. prefers-reduced-motion makes everything instant.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Cobalt stays the frame: the masthead with sign nav, and the page title in Anybody wdth 80 wght 800 on cobalt. The reading column is a paper key page (#F6F5F0, ink #101536) at 66ch in Source Serif 4 18/30. On desktop the sign column persists as the margin. Privacy has '0' beside the transparency table, then the policy text. Support has 'Write' beside the email (Anybody 700 26px), the response time and what to include. Alternatives use '±' beside the comparison table, '!?' and '?!' beside 'Choose Chessful if… / Stay with Chess.com if…', '∞' beside the FAQ, and the install row at the foot. On mobile the sign column shrinks to 56px with signs at row starts.

Materials

Cobalt drench: flat #2338B0 with no gradient or texture, like a cloth-bound reference volume · The key table: one two-column grid runs the whole page, a sign column (desktop 280px, mobile 72px) and a gloss column. Rows are divided by 2px paper rules, the key's printed rules. It is real table structure, not cards · Sign glyphs: Anybody 900 expanded for ASCII signs, plus SVG strokes for □ △ ± ⌓ ∞ ⇆. Signs are position: sticky inside their rows, so the sign stays beside a long gloss · Paper key pages: #F6F5F0 panels inset in the gloss column carry all long reading (FAQ, comparison table, about, privacy) in ink. White-on-blue paragraphs are never longer than three lines · Figurine notation in bold Anybody with SVG figurines. The screenshots are the only boards on the page

Colour strategy

Drenched · dark

Type rationale

The page argues that notation is the machine and sentences are the teacher, and the type says the same. One variable grotesk spans the key's two jobs: expanded black for signs that read at a glance, condensed for dense key columns, the way a reference periodical's one sans runs both cover and key. Anybody's sturdy, slightly ink-trapped forms keep their character at 220px. A calm transitional book serif carries every sentence Chessful speaks. Total ≈108 KB.

New assets needed

(1) A small SVG set for the non-ASCII signs (□ △ ± ∓ ⌓ ∞ → ⇆), drawn to Anybody Black's stroke weight (~1 KB each). (2) Inline SVG figurines from an open-licence piece set (e.g. cburnett, credited). (3) Optional: the 40-opponent roster for the '40' row. No diagrams are needed. Screenshots, icon, QR and badge exist.

Shogiful

/apps/shogiful/ + its privacy and support pages + 6 comparison pages

What the page must prove: Within the first viewport, show a real kind of shogi mistake explained in one plain sentence ('You dropped the silver to 4d. A knight drop on 3c forked king and rook.') on a board labelled in Western notation. Beside it sit the working App Store badge, the desktop QR and the price statement 'Free — Premium from $1.99/mo'.

The default page this refuses: A dark navy/black page with a gold glow (the register of the app's own 王-koma icon), a 3D wooden board inside an iPhone bezel, kanji everywhere, ink-wash, samurai or sakura cues, a split hero with a badge row, then a grid of feature cards.

THE ROLL

The Club Tag Wall

The 名札掛け (nafuda-kake) of a Japanese shogi club (将棋道場/将棋センター): hinoki name tags hung on a lacquered rail under kyu/dan header plaques and re-hung on promotion. Around it on the same wall: the seat-fee plaques (席料), the printed house rules, the cork board with review and 次の一手 quiz sheets, the ○△× marks of Japanese evaluation charts, the framed operating licence by the door, and the owner's hanko stamp.

The page is one club wall read top to bottom. The AI opponents and the visitor's own blank tag hang on a real rank rack, and that rack is also the navigation. The offer hangs as fee plaques and the coaching proof is pinned up as a review notice. It refuses both the category's dark-navy-and-gold 3D-board hero and the split-hero template.

Type
Shippori Mincho B1 800 (32 KB): headline plank, rank plaques, upright-stacked names on 64px tags with BIZ UDPGothic 400/700 (54 KB): every printed notice, the FAQ, tables and prices, Yusei Magic 400 (17 KB): the club owner's marker notes on notices, e.g. 'scan with your iPhone camera', 'beat each one twice'
Light
A chess player who has just lost to a drop reads on their phone in the evening, as if standing in front of a neighbourhood shogi club's wall under flat fluorescent tubes: shadowless cool-white light on painted plaster and pale hinoki. The scheme is light only.
Signature
Re-hang your tag. A hinoki YOU tag with a vermilion edge hangs from the nav rail under the plaque of the section in view. When the section changes, the tag lifts off its nail, slides along the rail and settles with a damped 3° pendulum swing (CSS transform transition; IntersectionObserver sets data-at on the rail). Without JS the tag sits fixed under 'Review' and every plaque is a plain anchor link. Under reduced motion the tag jumps to its new nail with no lift and no swing.
Remembered as
The shogi app whose page was a club wall: a row of wooden name tags for the AI opponents, and my own blank tag that slid along the rail as I scrolled.
Risk
The world carries the ladder and the offer better than the core proof. If the build lets the review notice fall below the first viewport, the page reads as a club with an opponent ladder, which is PiyoShogi's strength rather than Shogiful's. The roster conflict blocks the rack until the owner confirms it. Celadon, hinoki and vermilion slide into Japan-heritage kitsch the moment brush textures, washi or sakura creep in, so the room must stay a fluorescent-lit municipal club. Upright-stacked Latin on tags tops out at about 8 letters.

App Store route

Badge: the official Apple artwork, never altered, mounted on a lacquer tag-board that hangs from the rail like a tag, with the price lettered on the mount above it. QR: printed on a pinned paper card with a marker caption, shown at ≥1024px and on non-touch devices only. Price pills: the Fees section hangs four hinoki fee plaques (Free $0 / Monthly $1.99 / Annual $9.99 with a vermilion hanko for '~58% cheaper than monthly' / Lifetime $19.99 'Best long-term value'), each with its features on a paper slip below and plans_footnote in small print on the board base. Page sequence

  1. Rail and hengaku plank: headline, subheadline, badge mount with price, QR card, and the pinned review notice as the first example_insight (hero + proof)
  2. Quick Answer: the posted 'About this club' notice, a paper sheet at 68ch with quick_answer in BIZ 19px, stamped with the club hanko and marked speakable
  3. Quick reference: the club information card pinned beside it, the ai-canonical <details> rendered open, listing platforms, price, engine, offline, account
  4. The rack: 10 opponent tags under 4 tier plaques plus the YOU tag. Feature facts as marker notes: untimed with no clock or byoyomi, beat each one twice to unlock the next
  5. The review board (#templates): the six example_insights as pinned review sheets of mixed sizes. Each has a vermilion category hanko, the headline in BIZ 700, the body, and 'Pattern: …' in marker
  6. Piece guide notice: value point 'Play shogi without reading kanji' plus the 8-piece English table from the journal (name, kanji, move, promotes to) as a printed chart, linking to the journal post
  7. Promotion rules board (#how-it-works): how_it_works intro plus 6 numbered paper strips pinned as a ladder from 'game ends' to 'tomorrow's training', emitting HowTo
  8. Photos on the board: the 7 screenshots as pinned prints in a horizontal scroll-snap strip with marker captions
  9. House rules and inspection record: privacy notes as rules (no account, no ads, no tracking, works offline), next to the framed licence showing transparency.yml facts (0 SDKs, 0 tracking domains, analytics none, network calls, UserDefaults CA92.1), linking to /transparency/ and the privacy policy
  10. Membership notices: 'This club is for you if…' (who_for 6) and 'Try another club if…' (who_not_for 4, linking the Shogi Wars, Lishogi and 81Dojo pages)
  11. Fees board (#pricing): four fee plaques plus slips plus footnote
  12. Club cross-table (#compare-heading-shogiful): comparison_table as a posted chart with competitor columns under lacquer plaques. Each cell has a ○△× mark plus its text, with intro and footnote, and a badge mount at its foot
  13. Owner's note: founder story as a signed letter in a sleeve ('Why we built this'), with signals, the studio link, support email and response time
  14. About this club (show_body): the markdown body on one long notice under about_heading
  15. Club calendar: roadmap items. Shipped items get a vermilion 'DONE' hanko and targeted ones show their date, with the disclaimer
  16. Questions at the desk (#faq): 15 Q&As as <details> on paper, all open server-side
  17. Other clubs in town: alternatives_to as six small tags linking /alternatives/…; related journal as a pinned clipping; Xiangqiful and Chessful as two 'sister club' tags
  18. Door plaque: closing badge mount with price and QR. Hanko-stamped freshness line: Built by Lagerland Apps · first released 2026-06-11 · last updated 2026-06-11
  19. Shared thin 'A Lagerland app' footer strip

Navigation

The top lacquer rail is the rank rail. Its header plaques are the section links (Review · Rack · Method · Rules · Fees · Questions), and the visitor's YOU tag hangs under the plaque of the section in view. On mobile the rail scrolls horizontally with snap, and the active plaque stays scrolled into view. The microsite has no hamburger and no other menu.

Motion

Only hanging things move: tags and plaques enter by dropping 8px and swinging to rest (420ms, cubic-bezier(.3,1.4,.5,1)). Pinned paper never moves, and body text never fades. There is no parallax and no counters. prefers-reduced-motion removes every entrance and swing.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are posted documents on the same wall: celadon frame, the same lacquer rail (its first plaque returns to /apps/shogiful/), and the title lettered on a lacquer plank. The reading column is one long paper notice (#F7F6F1), 68ch, BIZ UDPGothic 17/28px ink, pinned with two pins. Privacy: the policy as the notice, with the framed transparency inspection record beside it on desktop and above it on mobile. Support: 'Ask at the desk' with the email lettered on a hinoki plaque, plus response time and what to include. Alternatives: the plank reads e.g. 'Shogiful or Shogi Wars', the comparison is a ○△× posted chart, the verdict is two notices ('Pick Shogiful if…' / 'Pick Shogi Wars if…'), the FAQ is desk cards, and a badge mount sits at the foot.

Materials

Flat celadon plaster (solid colour, no photo texture) · Hinoki tags: #ECDDBF with 4%-contrast grain hairlines (repeating-linear-gradient), a drilled hole at the top, hung on a 6px nail dot · Lacquered rails and plaques: solid #2A2622 bands and blocks lettered in paper white · Pinned notice paper: #F7F6F1 sheets with a 1px edge and CSS pin dots, rotated at most ±1.5° · Hanko stamps: vermilion CSS ring with Shippori lettering, used for categories, 'shipped', the highlighted plan · ○△× evaluation marks drawn in CSS (circle, triangle, cross) with visually hidden Yes/Partial/No text · Board diagrams: CSS 9×9 or 5×5 sumi grids with clip-path wedge pieces lettered in Hodges letters (K R B G S N L P), ownership shown by which way the wedge points

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

Shippori Mincho B1's ink-pooled heavy mincho reads as sumi lettering on wood, and its Latin holds up stacked upright on narrow tags. The specimen check showed Yuji Syuku's and Yuji Boku's Latin fails at that. BIZ UDPGothic is Morisawa's universal-design gothic used on Japanese municipal and school notices, a public-legibility face that matches the promise of a board anyone can read. Yusei Magic is the magic-marker hand of handwritten club annotations. Total ≈103 KB.

New assets needed

None are required to ship: every fixture is CSS (flat colour, hairlines, clip-path wedges) and runs on the existing icon, screenshots, QR and badge. Owner inputs: (1) the confirmed opponent roster, meaning names, strengths and the four tier labels, because the front matter and screenshot 7 disagree; (2) optionally, the app's Western piece set exported as SVG to replace the Hodges letters on the diagram wedges.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

The Big Board Hall

The ōban (大盤) of the public commentary session (大盤解説会) and televised shogi: a giant vertical magnetic board on which a professional slides flat piece plates and places arrow magnets while explaining each move aloud. It comes with the side trays that show each player's pieces in hand and the lower-third caption of the broadcast.

The page is one giant demonstration board with a commentator. A real 9×9 HTML board stays on stage while the commentary scrolls under it, so every claim is shown as a move: a red 'you played' magnet, a green 'best was' magnet and one spoken sentence. It refuses the screenshot-in-a-bezel hero and the eval-graph analytics page.

  • #1C2230
  • #F2F0E8
  • #15171C
  • #FBF7EC
  • #B8352A
  • #18743F

Type
Dela Gothic One 400 (13 KB): title band headline, plate letters (K R B G S N L P), section titles with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/700 (24 KB): the commentator's sentences and all reading, Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono 400 (10 KB): real notation only, i.e. moves (P*3d, S*4d, N*3c, P-7f), square labels 9…1 / a…i, move lists
Light
An audience member in a hotel-ballroom commentary session with the house lights down, watching one lit white board on stage. The scheme is dark for the hall, with one large lit plane.
Signature
Magnet replay. While Commentary is in view, the board is position: sticky. As each worked-example caption reaches the caption slot, the plates slide square to square into that example's illustrative position, which is stored as an SFEN string on the caption in server-rendered HTML. The red 'you played' and green 'best was' arrows then draw in from tail to head. Without JS, every caption renders with its own static board diagram above it, built from the same position data, so nothing is missing. Under reduced motion, positions swap instantly with arrows already drawn.
Remembered as
A huge white shogi board I could read without kanji. As I scrolled, the magnets moved, red for what I did and green for what I should have done, with one plain sentence underneath.
Risk
It is familiar: a big board is what every chess and shogi page leads with, and many runs land here. It earns its place only if the board is real HTML with moving magnets and captions, never a picture. Sticky scrollytelling is fragile on mobile (address-bar resize, iOS sticky jank) and has to fall back cleanly to stacked diagram-plus-caption pairs. A wrong illustrative position is a factual error any shogi player will spot. The dark hall sits near the dark-plus-accent cluster, so the lit board must stay the dominant light.

Page sequence

  1. Stage: title band headline and sub, the big board with an illustrative drop position, the hand trays, the lower-third caption (first worked example), and the price, badge and QR on the right flank
  2. Quick Answer: the commentator's opening statement on a lit plate directly under the stage, marked speakable
  3. Programme facts: the ai-canonical quick reference as an open <details> plate
  4. Commentary (#templates): the six example_insights pass through the caption slot one by one while the board stays pinned and replays each illustrative position
  5. Pieces in English: value point 1 plus the journal's 8-piece table as a strip of magnet plates (letter, kanji, English name, move, promotes to), linking to the journal post
  6. Method (#how-it-works): six numbered lit plates on a line from 'game ends' to 'tomorrow's training', emitting HowTo
  7. Replay monitors: 7 screenshots in a horizontal snap strip with captions
  8. Programme: features 6, including the 10 opponents and untimed play, as two-column programme text on a lit plate (not cards)
  9. Seats in this hall / Better in the arena: who_for 6 and who_not_for 4, linking the Shogi Wars, Lishogi and 81Dojo pages
  10. Fees (#pricing): four lit plates plus the footnote
  11. Scoreboard (#compare-heading-shogiful): comparison_table on a lit plate with the Shogiful column tinted, plus intro and footnote, then the badge strip
  12. Nothing leaves the hall: privacy notes plus the transparency.yml facts as a plain table, linking to /transparency/ and the privacy policy
  13. Why we built this: founder story, signals, studio link, support email, response time
  14. About (show_body) on a long lit plate under about_heading
  15. Next sessions: roadmap as a schedule list (shipped, targeted, under consideration) with the disclaimer
  16. Questions from the floor (#faq): 15 Q&As, open server-side
  17. Other halls: alternatives_to links; related journal; Xiangqiful and Chessful
  18. Closing stage call: badge, price, QR, then the line 'Built by Lagerland Apps · first released 2026-06-11 · last updated 2026-06-11'
  19. Shared thin 'A Lagerland app' footer strip

Navigation

A slim hall strip with six plain text links, and the active section underlined in board-white. On mobile the 'Programme' button opens a <details> list. Inside Commentary, the board's file labels 9…1 double as a jump list to the six worked examples.

Motion

Motion is the commentator's hand and nothing else: plates slide in straight lines (180ms ease-out) and land with a 1.04→1 snap, and arrows draw over 240ms. The hall, text and plates never fade or parallax. prefers-reduced-motion turns this into instant state changes.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The hall is the frame: slate ground, the same strip nav, and the page title in Dela Gothic on the title band. The reading column is one lit plate (#F2F0E8), 68ch, Atkinson 17/28px ink. Privacy: the policy plate with a plain transparency table at its head. Support: one caption plate with the email in Atkinson 700 24px and the response time. Alternatives: the title band reads e.g. 'Shogiful or PiyoShogi', with an optional small board diagram. The comparison table and the honest verdict are plain text on the plate, the FAQ is 'Questions from the floor', and the badge strip sits at the foot.

Materials

Lit steel demonstration board: flat #F2F0E8, a 2px #15171C 9×9 grid, file numbers above and rank letters at the side in mono · Flat magnet plates: clip-path pentagon wedges in #FBF7EC with a 2px bottom edge for thickness, pointing up or down to show the owner (real shogi ownership grammar) · Arrow magnets: solid red for 'you played' and dashed green for 'best was', square to square, so colour is never the only cue · Side trays for pieces in hand: narrow lit strips holding plates with ×2 counts · Lower-third caption plate: a lit band carrying the spoken sentence · The hall: slate ground for all sections below the stage, with content on lit plates

Colour strategy

Full palette · dark

Type rationale

Dela Gothic One is the heavy Japanese telop/event-poster gothic, and its chunky Latin capitals read from the back row like printed magnet plates. Atkinson Hyperlegible, the Braille Institute face with letterforms built to be told apart at distance and for low vision, is the commentator's voice and Shogiful's legibility promise. Its mono sibling keeps notation in the same family. Total ≈47 KB.

New assets needed

Six illustrative positions (SFEN), one per worked example. They must be authored, checked with an engine and labelled 'illustrative position'. Optional: the app's Western piece set as SVG to replace the Hodges letters on plates. Otherwise it runs on the existing icon, screenshots, QR and badge.

SECOND ROLL

Weekly Manga Chapter

A shogi manga chapter as printed in Japanese weekly magazines and their English editions: the colour opening page (巻頭カラー), panel grids with slanted gutters, speech balloons and narration boxes, screentone, 集中線 focus lines, and Japanese sound effects (パチッ, the snap of a piece on the board) kept in the art with small English translations beside them. It also borrows the yonkoma strip, the obi band and the 奥付 colophon. The explainer pages of shogi manga such as March Comes in Like a Lion are a cultural reference only; no art, characters or logos are borrowed.

The page is one manga chapter read top to bottom. The coaching loop is told in panels: a board panel, the drop, focus lines slamming into the square you missed, and the explanation in a balloon. The English edition's translated SFX carry 'the teacher that speaks your language'. It refuses both the luxury wood-and-gold board page and the flat infographic.

Type
Potta One 400 (25 KB): chapter and section titles and the English SFX glosses with Zen Old Mincho 400/700 (31 KB): narration boxes, FAQ, notes pages, tables, Shantell Sans 600 (46 KB), set in caps: speech-balloon lettering only, with lines kept short
Light
A reader on an evening commuter train flipping through a weekly manga magazine printed on tinted newsprint under the carriage's daylight-white lights. The scheme is light (the colour opener uses the app's navy as a printed colour page).
Signature
Focus-line drop. When a board panel enters the viewport, the 集中線 contract toward the missed square (a CSS custom property animating the mask radius), the dropped piece plate cuts in, and the パチッ SFX outline draws on (SVG stroke-dashoffset) with its English gloss appearing beside it. The balloon cuts in last. Without JS, the server-rendered final state shows lines, plate, SFX, gloss and balloon all present. Under reduced motion the final state is static.
Remembered as
The shogi app page that was a manga: focus lines slamming into the square where I should have dropped my knight, a huge パチッ with '(snap)' beside it, and pink and yellow newsprint pages.
Risk
To a serious chess convert, manga can read as 'for kids and anime fans'. Caps comic lettering hurts long reading, so balloons must stay headline-short and all long copy must live in mincho narration. With no drawn characters, panels can look like diagrams in boxes, so the focus lines, SFX and balloons have to carry the drama. Drenched stocks tip into noise if colour changes per panel rather than per signature. The SFX must be correct Japanese and glossed. IP care: generic manga grammar only.

Navigation

A table of contents (目次). The navy top bar's 'Contents' link opens a full-height contents page as a <details> panel, so it works without JS, listing the sections by their in-world names. On desktop the six main entries also sit inline in the bar. The change of newsprint stock signals which signature you are in, and every section heading is a Potta One title in a narration box.

Motion

Cuts, not tweens: panel contents appear in reading order with hard cuts 120ms apart, like turning to the next panel. Only the focus lines (300ms) and SFX strokes (250ms) animate continuously, and nothing fades or uses parallax. prefers-reduced-motion shows everything at once.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the alternatives pages are the volume's back matter. Each uses one newsprint frame (sky for privacy, pink for support, lemon for alternatives) with the title in Potta One on a narration box. The reading column is a white notes page at 68ch in Zen Old Mincho 18/30 ink. An alternatives page opens with one 'versus' panel in which two balloons quote each product's real positioning from the page ('the arena' / 'the practice room'). The comparison table and verdict follow as plain text, the FAQ as reader Q&A, and the okuzuke colophon closes the page.

Materials

Tinted newsprint stocks, one per signature, with a 3% ink-dot grain via radial-gradient · Panel borders in 3px ink with slanted gutters (clip-path polygons) and lettering that breaks the borders · Screentone dot fields at 10/20/30% (radial-gradient patterns) · 集中線 focus lines (repeating-conic-gradient masked radially) centred on a board square · Speech balloons (white, 2px ink, clip-path tails) and rectangular narration boxes · Katakana SFX as outlined SVG paths with Potta One English glosses · Board panels: CSS 9×9 or 5×5 ink-line grids with wedge plates in Hodges letters · The app's real screenshots cropped into panels as the colour insert · Obi bands for prices and the okuzuke colophon box for the freshness line

Colour strategy

Drenched · light

Type rationale

Potta One's brush-pop strokes read as hand-lettered manga titling, and its Latin carries the same hand as the katakana SFX. Zen Old Mincho is the old-style mincho of tankōbon body text with a sound Latin, so long reading stays calm. Shantell Sans in caps stands in for the comic lettering of English manga editions. The katakana SFX ship as outlined SVG paths rather than a Japanese font subset. Total ≈102 KB.

New assets needed

Katakana SFX outlined as SVG paths (パチッ at minimum; derived from an OFL face), plus six illustrative board crops (positions) labelled 'illustrative position'. Optional: the app's Western piece set as SVG. Focus lines, screentone and stocks are all CSS, and it otherwise runs on the existing icon, screenshots, QR and badge. No character art is needed or allowed.

Xiangqiful

/apps/xiangqiful/ + its privacy and support pages + 5 comparison pages

What the page must prove: The first viewport has to show three things. First, one mistake named in xiangqi's own words, using the app's own string (e.g. 'Your horse stepped into the line and handed the enemy cannon the screen it needed.'), proof that the review explains rather than scores. THE ROLL

Bilingual Concourse

Bilingual metro wayfinding of Hong Kong, Taipei and Guangzhou: the Chinese name set large in Hei over its English twin on white vitreous-enamel panels, glazed square-mosaic station walls in one station colour, strip line maps with station dots and interchange rings, and dashed lines for planned extensions on network maps. It borrows the grammar only; no operator's name, logo, roundel, typeface or colour code.

The page is a station. Every heading is a bilingual sign (character over English, the hybrid piece set as a principle), the opponent ladder and your reviewed game are line maps, and the App Store is the Exit. It refuses both the screenshot-in-a-phone product page and the red-and-gold 'Chinese' costume.

Type
Noto Sans TC 900 for the character line of every sign: 象棋 at 168px in the hero, section characters at 72–96px. It comes from a one-time ~60-glyph subset (the 14 piece characters including 傌 俥 炮 砲, 楚河漢界, 象棋, the section terms). Source Sans 3 700 sets the English line beneath: 64px in the hero, 40px on section signs. with Source Sans 3 400/600: panel copy at 19px/1.55, sign small print at 15px, the FAQ and fare table., Source Code Pro 500 for real data only: WXF/ICCS notation (C2=5, H2+3), move numbers on the game line, opponent strengths 400–1900.
Light
A commuter on an underground concourse under flat white ceiling light, reading enamel signs on a glazed teal tile wall while waiting for the train → light.
Signature
'The line of your game'. An inline SVG route strip runs the full width: an illustrative 40-move game where each move is a station marker whose shape encodes the seven grades (best / great / good as filled dots of decreasing size, book a grey ring, inaccuracy a half-filled dot, mistake a ring with a bar, blunder a closed-station square, with a line key). Red's and Black's moves alternate above and below the line. The six key moments are interchange rings. Tapping or hovering one (a real <a href='#moment-n'>) slides its named-mistake sign under the strip with a small position diagram. On desktop a train marker travels the strip in step with scroll (CSS animation-timeline: view(), IntersectionObserver fallback). No-JS: the strip renders static and all six interchange signs are printed in order beneath it. Reduced motion: no train travel; signs swap without the slide.
Remembered as
The xiangqi app whose page was a metro station: every heading was a Chinese character over its English name, my game was drawn as a line with the mistakes as interchanges, and a black Exit sign took me to the App Store.
Risk
The world is borrowed from public transport, not from xiangqi. If line metaphors leak into the copy it becomes a costume. Siblings are already using transit and wayfinding (allpaid's departures poster, earnlock's junction post), so this one must hold to its own devices: bilingual character-over-English signs, glazed tile, the game as a graded line. No yellow, no timetable grid. The drenched teal must stay ground, with all reading on enamel. Bilingual section terms must be checked against the app's zh-Hant localization.

Navigation

The white enamel line strip at the top is the microsite nav: the page's sections as stations on one black line, with scrollspy enlarging the current station dot. On mobile the 'Line' button opens a full-height vertical line map (links as stations, 48px targets) on enamel over the tile. Sub-pages show the same strip with their own station highlighted and a 'Xiangqiful' terminus linking home. Focus rings are a 3px sign-black ring with a 2px enamel offset.

Motion

Signage doesn't animate. Only things that move in a station move: the train marker along a line (linear, tied to scroll), the 'you are here' ring hopping between stations (120ms linear), and signs sliding 8px from their mounting edge with opacity (180ms ease-out). No parallax, no scale, no bounce, no hover lift. Under prefers-reduced-motion everything is static except focus rings.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the five alternatives pages keep the tile ground and the line strip (with their own station lit). The reading column is one long enamel panel, 68ch, SS3 19px/1.6 in sign-black. H2s are bilingual signs where a true term exists (e.g. 私隱 / Privacy) and English-only otherwise; no invented Chinese. Privacy sections become notice panels with small data-flow pictograms (device → nothing leaves). Support is a 'Help point' panel with the email as the call button. Alternatives pages are an interchange board: 'Xiangqiful ↔ Xiangqi.com' as two connecting lines, the comparison as a connections table, the FAQ as enquiries, and an Exit panel to /apps/xiangqiful/.

Materials

glazed square mosaic tile: 24px tiles, 2px grout, a two-tone glaze variance from a 4-tile inline SVG pattern; flat, no sheen · vitreous-enamel sign panels: 6px radius, a 1px #0A4E53 edge, printed-flat colour, no drop shadow · strip line map: a 6px sign-black line, 12px station dots, 20px interchange rings, a terminus bar · the inverse Exit panel: a sign-black panel with white type and a stroked exit pictogram (the only black panels on the page, and they always lead to the App Store) · dashed planned-extension line in #8A9095 · wayfinding pictograms drawn as 2.5px stroked SVG (exit, info i, arrow, no-entry, interchange): no emoji, no icon font

Colour strategy

Drenched · light

Type rationale

Source Sans is the Latin half of Source Han Sans (= Noto Sans TC), so each bilingual sign is one superfamily, as a real sign system is. It sits in the humanist lineage of Chinese-metro English signage, and it carries the pinyin tone marks the opponents need (Xiǎobǎo, Nǎinai Chén), which Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Sofia Sans lack. Budget: SS3 latin 400/600/700 47 KB, plus a cut ~4 KB/weight pinyin-vowel file instead of full latin-ext, SCP 500 12 KB and the CJK subset ~30 KB, ≈ 100 KB in total.

New assets needed

(1) A one-time Noto Sans TC 900 woff2 subset of ~60 glyphs (~30 KB, pyftsubset), named without any Reserved Font Name. (2) A cut pinyin-vowel file from SS3 latin-ext (ā á ǎ à ē é ě è ī í ǐ ì ō ó ǒ ò ū ú ǔ ù ü). (3) SVG exports of the app's seven western piece symbols from its asset catalog; do not redraw them. (4) A stroked pictogram set (exit, info, arrow, no-entry, interchange). (5) From the developer: an illustrative WXF game with Pikafish grades and the six FENs behind the example_insights; until then the strip is labelled 'illustrative'. (6) The full opponent list (10th name, strengths 6–9). Everything else runs on the existing icon, QR and screenshots.

XiangqifulFira Sans Extra Condensed

Chinese chess, taught properly.

Master xiangqi. Move by move.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

After-Round Big Board

The tournament commentary board (大盤 / 掛盤講棋): a giant vertical white magnetic board on a stand, flat discs set on its intersections, slotted name plates above it, a flip move-counter, a ledge tray holding captured discs. A master replays the round for the hall with a pointer and blue dry-erase marker. Chinese TV xiangqi lectures used the same rig for decades.

The page is the after-round lecture. One big lit board stays pinned in the hall and re-sets for each chapter while the commentary scrolls beside it, so the review mechanism is performed rather than described. It refuses the static hero screenshot and the wood-and-gold chess page.

Type
Fira Sans Extra Condensed 800/700: the banner-plate H1 at 80–96px/0.95, chapter verdicts at 32–44px, name plates (RED · You / BLACK · Shīfu · 1,900), the flip counter numerals at 56px with Fira Sans 400/500: commentary and all reading copy at 19px/1.6, WXF move record in tabular figures, Noto Serif TC 900 subset only: the disc characters and the 楚河 漢界 river lettering, the bold Ming face screen-printed on demonstration boards and discs
Light
A club player in the darkened commentary hall after the last round, on a folding chair, watching the master work the big magnetic board under a bank of stage lights; the board is the brightest thing in the room → dark ground, light board.
Signature
'The Lecture'. On desktop the board is position: sticky in the centre column while chapters scroll on the right and the record updates on the left. When a chapter crosses the reading line, its FEN (in a data attribute) re-sets the board. Discs lift (shadow 0→4px), slide straight along the grid with transforms (240ms, at most 3 discs per change) and seat; marker arrows draw via stroke-dashoffset (400ms); the flip counter turns. One IntersectionObserver, about 4 KB of JS. No-JS and mobile: every chapter carries its own server-rendered static SVG diagram above its text, and the sticky board is just chapter 1's diagram. Reduced motion: discs jump, marks appear whole, the counter changes without a flip.
Remembered as
The page was a big demonstration board in a dark hall. The discs actually slid to new squares as I scrolled, and a blue marker circled the exact mistake the app was naming.
Risk
Honest familiarity: this is my top-ranked direction because it is the most literal carrier. The board is the category's own object, so it sits closest to 'chess app shows a board'. Demonstration-board commentary is also shogi's 大盤解説 and a chess-tournament fixture, so it could converge with Shogiful or Chessful unless the white enamel, blue marker and Ming-bold discs stay specific. It is the most JS-dependent of the three, so the no-JS chapter diagrams must be first-class. Positions must come from the app, not be composed for the page.

Navigation

A slim programme strip on #34322E: the app's name plate plus six plate-tabs (Lecture · Opponents · Pieces · Homework · Admission · Questions). Scrollspy turns the active tab to enamel with a blue marker underline. During the lecture the flip counter on the board doubles as the chapter indicator ('3 / 6'). On mobile a 'Programme' button opens a sheet of plates. Focus is a 3px marker-blue ring on enamel and a 3px #E8E4DA ring on graphite.

Motion

Only what a commentator does moves: a disc lifts, slides and seats; a marker stroke draws at hand speed; a plate flips (160ms). Nothing else in the hall moves: no scroll reveals, no parallax, no hover lift on cards. With prefers-reduced-motion, state changes are instant.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages keep the graphite hall and the programme strip. The board retires to a small static diagram in the masthead (the opening position) under a banner plate carrying the page title. The reading column is an enamel card, 68ch, Fira Sans 19px/1.6 in #18181A, with H2s in ExtraCond 700 and tables set like the results sheet. Alternatives pages face two name plates across the board ('Xiangqiful — the practice room' / 'Xiangqi.com — the arena', in the copy's own words), then the comparison as the results sheet, the verdict lists on enamel cards, and the FAQ from the floor.

Materials

matte white enamel board: screen-printed 9×10 intersections, the river band with 楚河 漢界 in Ming bold, palace diagonals, file/rank figures in the margin · flat magnetic discs: matte, with a 3px rim ring, red or black characters on enamel-white faces (the hybrid set adds the western symbol) · brushed-aluminium frame and ledge tray, drawn flat (#A7ABAE fill, 1px highlight line, no gradient sheen) · slotted name plates and a two-digit flip counter above the board · blue dry-erase marker strokes as inline SVG (round caps, slight width variance): arrows, circles, ticks and question marks drawn as paths, never glyphs · graphite hall ground with the stage riser as section bands

Colour strategy

Restrained · dark

Type rationale

The board's slotted name plates and flip counter need narrow, heavy capitals that fit long pinyin names (Nǎinai Chén, Shuāngpào) in a slot, and Fira Sans Extra Condensed is one of the few condensed faces on Fontsource with full tone marks. Fira Sans text keeps one superfamily so the commentary reads like the hall programme. Budget: ExtraCond 800 + 700 latin 50 KB, Fira Sans 400/500 latin 48 KB, cut pinyin-vowel files ~4 KB/weight, Serif TC subset ~35 KB ≈ 145 KB.

New assets needed

(1) A one-time Noto Serif TC 900 subset for the disc characters and the river (~35 KB). (2) Cut pinyin-vowel files for Fira Sans and Fira Sans Extra Condensed. (3) From the developer: FEN positions for the six example_insights moments and the five opponent-style sketches; until then each is labelled 'illustrative position'. Piercing the Heart is transcribed from screenshot 5. (4) SVG exports of the app's western piece symbols for the piece-set switch. (5) The marker-stroke set (arrow, circle, tick, question, cross) drawn once as SVG. (6) The full opponent list (10th name, strengths 6–9). Otherwise it runs on the existing icon, QR and screenshots.

SECOND ROLL

The Mistake Notebook

The Chinese school exercise book: a stapled 練習本 on pale green 護眼 eye-care paper, a printed 方格 grid with 田字格 practice boxes for learning characters one at a time, and the 錯題本 (mistake notebook) every student keeps, copying each wrong answer to redo it. The teacher marks it in red ballpoint: tick, circle, cross, a wavy underline under the key line, a short comment and a 訂正 correction to rewrite.

The page is your mistake notebook. Each entry is one mistake copied from a game, marked in red, explained, given one thing to do next game and dated for review, so Xiangqiful's loop (play → named mistake → tomorrow's training) is the page's structure. It refuses the feature-card grid and the dark 'engine analysis' dashboard.

  • #EAF2E4
  • #A9CDB2
  • #2F6B4A
  • #2F3336
  • #141414
  • #C81E1E

Type
LXGW WenKai TC 700/400: the H1 at 84px (mobile 38px), section headings at 40–48px in ink, the teacher's red comments at 22–26px (400), the Kai model characters in the 田字格 boxes, all from one hand with Lexend 400/500: body at 18px/1.65, printed fields and nav at 14px, tabular figures for WXF moves, dates and prices, none: no mono. Notation and numbers use Lexend tabular figures
Light
A player at a desk by a daylit window with the exercise book open, a pencil, and the teacher's red pen beside it → light.
Signature
'Marking'. When each mistake entry reaches the reading line, the teacher's red pen marks it: the wrong move is struck through, the better square circled, the wavy underline runs under the key sentence and 'Review — due today' writes in. These are SVG stroke-dashoffset draws at hand speed (500–700ms, staggered 120ms). Each entry also has a 'Try the correction' <details> that reveals the better-move arrow on the pencil board (no JS needed). No-JS: every mark is present statically. Reduced motion: marks appear complete, with no drawing.
Remembered as
It was an exercise book: my own mistake copied onto green squared paper, marked up in red pen, with the next thing to practise written underneath and a note that it was due for review today.
Risk
Paper plus red pen sits nearest the cream + serif + red cluster. The pale green 護眼 paper, the Kai hand display and the Lexend body keep it out; it fails if the paper drifts warm or the display goes serif. A school notebook can read as child-facing or condescending to experienced diaspora players, so the teacher's voice must stay the app's adult copy, with no stickers, stars or grades. A sibling (Chessful's scoresheet, Shogiful's problem book) could also land on paper, so the 錯題本 and 田字格 specifics must lead. Keep red marks to a few per screen.

App Store route

Page sequence

  1. Today's mistake (hero): header fields, H1, secondary, the copied position marked in red with the app's explanation and 'Review — due today', the foot row with price, badge and QR
  2. Inside cover: quick_answer written as the first pencil paragraph at 20px (speakable), beside the printed reference table that is the 'Quick reference' <details>, summary visible
  3. Learn the pieces one at a time: a 田字格 row of seven boxes (Kai model character, western symbol, hybrid, English name, one-line movement rule from the FAQ: cannon jumps exactly one to capture, horse blocked at the leg, stalemate is a loss). Value point 'Play xiangqi without reading Chinese'; screenshot 3 tipped in with its caption
  4. Six mistakes, marked (example_insights): six notebook entries, each with the tag as a printed field, headline in pencil, body, and the 'next game' sentence in red with a red mark
  5. How the notebook fills itself (how_it_works heading 'From your last move to tomorrow's training.'): six steps in printed number boxes (a real sequence), the 60/25/15 plan drawn as a red tally bar with its numbers in text; HowTo schema
  6. Class register: the ten opponents as a register table (pinyin name, strength, style line, two empty 'beaten' tick boxes showing the beat-twice rule). Feature 'Ten teahouse opponents'; screenshots 7 and 1
  7. Homework: 80 lessons in 8 named tracks, nine drill modules, 902 mate problems with Piercing the Heart (mate in 3) copied in from screenshot 5 under 'Find the mate. Every move must give check.' Link to the journal essay; screenshots 2, 5, 6
  8. Report card: the five skills named (tactics, defense, positioning, endgame, openings), feature 'Progress and a skill profile' with the own-estimate caveat, screenshot 8. No invented scores
  9. Fees slip (plans): a printed four-row table (Free $0 / Monthly $1.99/mo / Yearly $9.99/yr 'Best value' / Lifetime $19.99 once), feature lists as <details>, plans_footnote, badge
  10. Is this notebook yours? who_for with red ticks (6), who_not_for with red crosses (5), drawn as SVG
  11. Other schools (comparison_table): a ruled table on the grid, 5 apps × 6 rows, the honest footnote, links to the five alternatives pages
  12. A note from the publisher (founder): story, five signals, studio link, maker/freshness line
  13. What's not collected (privacy): the six notes as a ruled list, Apple's 'Data Not Collected', links to /transparency/ and the privacy policy
  14. Next term (roadmap): 1.0 items ticked in red, 'Under consideration' items in pencil, the disclaimer
  15. Questions in the margin (faq): 17 <details>
  16. Back cover: Shogiful and Chessful, the journal post, closing badge + QR, then the Lagerland strip

Navigation

A printed header row along the top of the leaf: 'Xiangqiful' plus contents links (Today's mistake · Pieces · Mistakes · Method · Opponents · Homework · Fees · Questions) in Lexend 500 14px #2F6B4A. Scrollspy draws a red pencil underline under the current entry. On mobile a 'Contents' button opens the inside-cover contents table as a sheet. Focus is a 2px #141414 ring with a 2px paper offset, with red never used for focus.

Motion

Only the pen moves: strokes draw once, in writing order, and never redraw on scroll-back. Paper, grid and type never move: no reveals, no parallax, no hover lift. <details> open without animated height. Under prefers-reduced-motion nothing draws.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages are single leaves of the same notebook in its lined (橫線) variant for prose. The printed header row is kept; the reading column is 66ch of Lexend 19px/1.65 pencil-graphite with headings in WenKai 700 ink. Red appears only where a teacher would mark: on privacy, 'Data Not Collected' circled; on alternatives, ticks against the honest verdict lists. Support is a 'note to the teacher' leaf with the email as the action. Alternatives pages open with a two-column 'compare' exercise ruled on the grid (Xiangqiful | Xiangqi.com).

Materials

pale green 護眼 paper as the full ground, with a printed 28px 方格 grid (CSS background-image, 1px #A9CDB2) · 田字格 boxes with a dotted cross for the piece-character row · the xiangqi board drawn in pencil over the grid: its 9×10 lines land on grid lines, discs are pencil circles with Kai characters · red ballpoint marks as SVG strokes: tick, circle, cross, a wavy underline, an arrow for the correction · the gutter: a 24px soft fold shade with two steel staples · the inside-cover printed reference table (exercise books print a table there) for the Quick reference

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

LXGW WenKai's Latin is drawn from Klee One's textbook hand, so one Kai face writes both the model characters a pupil copies and a teacher's neat red comments, and it covers the pinyin tone marks. Lexend was built from reading-proficiency research for learners, a fit for 'taught properly', and also covers pinyin. Neither is a serif display, which keeps paper + red out of the cream/serif cluster. Budget: WenKai latin 400/700 36 KB + Lexend latin 400/500 29 KB + cut pinyin-vowel files ~12 KB + Kai CJK subset ~45 KB ≈ 122 KB.

New assets needed

(1) A one-time LXGW WenKai TC 700 + 400 subset of the ~60 needed characters (~45 KB). (2) Cut pinyin-vowel files for WenKai and Lexend. (3) The red-pen mark set as SVG strokes (tick, cross, circle, wavy underline, arrow), drawn once. (4) From the developer: FEN positions for the six example mistakes, labelled illustrative until supplied; Piercing the Heart transcribed from screenshot 5. (5) SVG exports of the app's western piece symbols. (6) The full opponent list. Otherwise it runs on the existing icon, QR and screenshots.

GymLogger X

/apps/gymlogger-x/ + its privacy and support pages + 3 comparison pages

THE ROLL

Phone in the Locker

Changing-room locker banks of municipal gyms and Nordic swimming halls. Powder-coated sheet steel (RAL 6033 mint turquoise is almost exactly the icon's check-mark teal), rows of pressed louvre vents at the top and foot of each door, and 8px dark seams between doors. Two-ply engraved laminate plates (navy face cut through to a white core) are screwed on with slotted screws. A pressed-steel card holder takes a slid-in label, and the cam lock's key hangs on a coiled plastic wrist band with a numbered tag. Inside: a hat shelf, a hook, laminated house-rules sheets, and the manufacturer's riveted data plate at the foot.

The page is one locker door, and the phone is shut inside it. The App Store action hangs on the key's wrist band, the thing you actually carry onto the floor. This refuses the category's floating-phone neon hero by making the product's absence from the first viewport the argument.

Type
Big Shoulders Display 800 (@fontsource/big-shoulders-display; latin woff2 14.6 KB): H1 112px/0.9 on desktop and 52px on mobile, door-scale vinyl lines at 56px with Public Sans 400/600 (@fontsource/public-sans; 2 × 14.6 KB): body 17–18px/1.6 on the laminated sheets; 600 caps at +0.08em for the engraved plates and the stamped key tag; tabular figures for kg and prices, none. Prices and measurements use Public Sans with tabular figures, and there is no mono costume.
Light
A lifter in a gym changing room before a session, under flat cool fluorescent tubes: the phone goes onto the locker shelf, the key band goes onto the wrist. Deep painted steel with light lettering, so the scheme is dark (color-scheme: dark).
Signature
Open the locker. A door panel (the same #235c58 steel with louvres and a lock) covers the interior section. When the section is 35% in view, an IntersectionObserver swings it open: rotateY 0 → −105deg around its left hinge, perspective 1800px, 800ms cubic-bezier(.3,.7,.2,1) with a 3° settle, revealing the phone screenshots on the shelf. A scroll-snap row lets you take shots off the shelf one by one. No-JS: the door panel only exists under html.js, so the interior and all screenshots render open. A 2.5s safety net forces it open. Reduced motion: the door is drawn at its open end state with no swing, and the key tags do not sway.
Remembered as
The page was a teal gym locker door. The App Store button hung on the orange locker-key wristband, and when I scrolled the door swung open with the phone sitting on the shelf inside.
Risk
A locker is a mundane, even unlovely object, so it could read as facility signage rather than desire unless the plates, louvres and key band are crafted precisely. The hero deliberately shows no app UI; proof arrives one scroll later when the door opens, so the Quick Answer card must carry the rule summary. A ~9,000px page stretches a real door's proportions, so the interior after the swing has to carry most of the length. The teal drench leans on the icon colour and must read as painted steel, not brand fill.

App Store route

The badge is mounted on the key tag hanging from the lock (Apple artwork, unaltered, on the orange plastic). The price is stamped on the same tag from price.value. The QR hangs as a second tag on the same ring (≥1024px only). The sticky bar is a 64px steel strip that slides up from the bottom edge once tag 1 leaves the viewport: the orange band runs coiled along it, ending in a tag with the badge and '$39.99 once · Free to start'. Pricing is the coin-lock tariff plate: an engraved instruction plate listing Free / Pro Monthly / Pro Annual / Lifetime with the highlight label, plans_footnote as its small print, and the badge set beside the coin slot. The closing repeats tag 1 under the manufacturer's plate. The Smart App Banner is the native iOS meta, untouched.

Page sequence

  1. Top louvre band: engraved brand plate + nav plates
  2. Door face (hero): cut-vinyl H1 + subheadline; card holder with the Quick Answer (speakable); four trust plates; cam lock → key band → tag with badge + price; QR tag on desktop

  7. Coin-lock tariff plate: plans (4) + highlight label + plans_footnote + badge

  9. Notes taped inside the door: 5 real testimonials (initials, source, French with translation, no stars); who_for / who_not_for on two engraved plates, 'This locker is yours if' / 'Use another locker if'

Navigation

Engraved laminate plates screwed into the top louvre band: the brand plate links to the top; Wrist · Rule · Price · Questions are anchor links, with Privacy and Support as smaller plates to the sub-pages. Focus ring: a 3px orange #f0811a outline offset 3px, like the band. On mobile, one 'Menu' plate opens (details/summary, no JS) the attendant's key board: a dark #112b2c panel of hooks, each with an orange tag link (sections, Privacy, Support, vs Strong, vs Fitbod, vs Jefit).

Motion

Heavy and mechanical, moving only like steel and plastic. The door swings with a damped settle (800ms). The key tag sways 3° on hover or focus and settles in 600ms. The sticky band strip slides up in 200ms. Nothing fades or floats in, and every other region holds still on the steel.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the Strong, Fitbod and Jefit pages keep the door frame: the same top louvre band with the brand plate plus a page plate ('Privacy policy', 'Support', 'Strong alternative'), and steel in the margins only. The reading column is one laminated A4 sheet riveted to the door (#fbfbf8, 68ch, Public Sans 18px/1.65 #14202b), with headings as small engraved plates in the flow and tables as the laminated register. Alternatives pages: page.title in cut vinyl above the sheet; quick_answer in the card holder; 'Pick GymLogger X if / Stay with Strong if' as two engraved plates; the existing FAQ as key tags; the key tag with badge at the foot. Correct the Strong page's false 'Mac-and-iPhone' line. Support: an 'Ask at the desk' sheet with email, response time and what to include. No door swing on Read pages.

Materials

flat powder-coated sheet steel with 1px edge highlights (no texture images) · pressed louvre vents: rows of 64×10px rounded slots (inline SVG pattern) · 8px door seams; at desktop width the neighbouring doors show at the viewport edges (aria-hidden) · two-ply engraved laminate plates with slotted screw heads (CSS) · pressed-steel card holder with a slid-in white card · cut-vinyl lettering, flat with no effects · laminated A4/A5 sheets with rivets and a clear lamination margin · orange coiled key band and tags (inline SVG coil) · dark locker interior with hat shelf and hook · riveted manufacturer's data plate

Colour strategy

Drenched · dark

Type rationale

Big Shoulders was drawn from Chicago's civic signage. It is the condensed municipal grotesk of public facilities, it reads as die-cut vinyl on a changing-room door, and its narrow set fits a tall door. Public Sans was built for public-service notices, which is the voice of a laminated facility sheet and of an engraving machine's plain caps. Total about 44 KB.

New assets needed

No raster art: louvres, plates, lock and key band are CSS or inline SVG, and the badge, QR and screenshots exist. A production task for every style: 2–3 real Apple Watch screenshots (set entry with RPE prompt, rest timer, session summary), plus corrected alt text for all six existing screenshots.

GymLogger XChivo

Strength training log for iPhone & Apple Watch.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

Three White Lights

Powerlifting meet officiating under IPF and national-federation rules. The referee light board shows three round lenses, white = good lift, red = no lift, appearing together once all three referees have pressed. Coloured fault cards are raised beside a red light to name the reason. The lifter or coach hands in an attempt card within a minute to declare the next weight. The Technical Rules book is written in numbered clauses, and the scoring table's results sheet carries Wilks, DOTS and GL points.

The plateau rule is judged in public like a lift. Three lenses read your sessions, red lights come with a card naming the possible cause, and the next attempt stays yours. This refuses the category's 'AI coach' black box and floating-phone hero with a working judging console.

  • #d5e3ec
  • #fbfbf9
  • #121619
  • #17191c
  • #ffffff
  • #d32b1f
Type
Chivo 900 (@fontsource/chivo; 14 KB): H1 84px/0.95 on desktop and 42px on mobile, the verdict line 28px, attempt weights with Chivo 400/600 (2 × 15 KB): body 18px/1.6 on rulebook paper, clause titles and nav in 600, Chivo Mono 500 (@fontsource/chivo-mono; 12 KB): weights, reps, e1RM, points and prices in the console, attempt card and results sheet. These are real measurements, aligned to the decimal (182.5).
Light
A lifter at the scorer's table of a local meet, attempt card in hand, under the hall's flat white LED high-bays, with the light board on its stand at the platform edge. Forms and card stock are daylight objects, so the scheme is light; the black housings carry the lenses.
Signature
Call the lift. The console runs the published rule's strength-and-volume test on six editable illustrative sessions: Epley e1RM per session, a least-squares trend over the last four against a threshold you set inside the 0.05–1% clamp, volume change against −3%, and a 'fatigue signal' toggle or a six-session run for confirmation. After a 400ms deliberation pause the three lenses switch together, as on a real board: red for each stalled signal, white otherwise. Three reds raise the red cause card ('Plateau flagged … your call'); two reds read 'Monitoring'; three whites read 'Good lift: keep progressing'. It is labelled simplified: the app also needs ≥8 sessions, 12 weeks of history and confidence > 0.4. No-JS: server-rendered example values with the lenses in their computed state and the verdict printed. Reduced motion: no pause; lenses switch instantly.
Remembered as
Three big lights on a black board. I typed my bench numbers, they went red together with a card saying 'possible causes… your call', and the prices were set like attempts: opener, second, third.
Risk
Familiarity: the three lights are powerlifting's most recognisable image and sports-judging is a known fitness-brand move, so this is the most expected of the seven. Meet vocabulary may feel competitive to the hypertrophy lifter or the K.D. visitor 'who doesn't live in the gym'. Verdict copy must stay calm, matching the app's 'informs without lecturing' stance. The live demo simplifies the real rule and must say so on its face. LiftLog's microsite could also reach for barbell sport, so this world needs coordinating with it.

SECOND ROLL

Show Your Working

The program spreadsheets passed around r/weightroom and r/powerlifting in the 2010s: Wendler 5/3/1 calculators, nSuns 5/3/1 LP, GZCL's Jacked & Tan and The Rippler, Candito 6-Week, Sheiko in Excel. They share a dark merged title band, yellow 'enter your Training Max' input cells, percentages rounded to 2.5 kg by formula, AMRAP '+' cells, a deload tab, week tabs along the bottom, conditional-format fills, a README tab, and the formula bar where lifters checked the maths.

The page is one workbook where every number shows its formula: the plateau test, e1RM, the annual saving, the lifetime break-even. This refuses the category's 'trust our AI' copy and turns the lifter's own habit of checking the sheet into the proof.

Grids are cramped at 390px, so only columns A–C are shown and the comparison scrolls inside its range. Carlito is plain at display size, so the navy band and scale must carry the headline. THE ROLL

The Loaded Sleeve

The IWF and IPF calibrated-disc colour code that every platform loader reads at a glance. Discs run 25 kg red, 20 blue, 15 yellow, 10 green and 5 white, and the change plates use the same colours (2.5 red, 2 blue, 1.5 yellow, 1 green, 0.5 white). The bar is 20 kg, the collars 2.5 kg, and the heaviest plates load innermost. Kilos are printed on matte rubber faces in a heavy wide grotesk, and the knurled steel shaft runs between the sleeves.

The page is one bar standing upright, loaded in true order with one of every calibrated plate, and each section is a plate you read by colour. The hero is a working loader that turns any weight into plates per side, as LiftLog's session does, and the price reads 'the empty bar is free for 7 days, then load what you can'. It refuses the gym-photo-plus-phone-mockup hero and the incumbent cream template.

Disc faces and loader numerals are wdth 125/900 with tabular figures ('25', '40 kg per side'). with Mona Sans, variable wght at wdth 100 (latin ≈40 KB), in 400 and 600 at 18px/1.6. It sets paragraphs, the quick answer, method notes, FAQ and tables, with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums wherever there are figures.
Light
A weightlifter loading a bar between attempts in a club training hall at midday: pale concrete walls, chalk on the floor, daylight from high windows, reading the sleeve by colour from three metres → light (color-scheme: light, single scheme).
Signature
Load the bar. The hero input 'Bar 20 kg + [ ] kg' (type=number, inputmode=decimal) drives the side-view sleeve. About 50 lines of vanilla JS solve plates per side greedily from IWF discs (25/20/15/10/5/2.5/2/1.5/1/0.5, optional 2.5 kg collars, or 45/35/25/10/5/2.5 lb on a 45 lb bar) and re-stack the sleeve: plates slide on from the sleeve end, heaviest first, 60ms apart, translateX 24px→0. The readout updates in tnum, and totals that can't be loaded show the nearest loadable weight. The price section reuses the same sleeve, so choosing a tier disc slides it on. No-JS: the sleeve is server-rendered at 100 kg with its readout text, and the input appears only under html.js. Reduced motion: plates appear in place. The drawing is aria-hidden, and the readout is live text in an aria-live region.
Remembered as
The page was a barbell standing up, loaded with red, blue, yellow and green plates for sections. I typed 140 and it showed the plates per side, and the price was 'the empty bar is free for seven days, then load what you can'.
Risk
Five saturated plate colours turn toy-like if slabs get rounded, glossy or gradient. They must stay matte, square-cut rubber with ink type and white reading surfaces. The colour code is native to barbell and weightlifting gyms, but machine-and-dumbbell lifters may not read it, so every slab and nav chip also carries its title in words. Mapping tiers onto plate colours must never suggest that more money buys more app, so 'same app' is printed on every disc.

Navigation

The header shows text links, each preceded by an 8×24px edge-on chip in its section's plate colour: 'The set · Price · Programs · Method · FAQ' (Mona 600 15px, ink). Past the hero it becomes a sticky 48px concrete strip, and the current section's chip widens to 16px. Labels are always visible, so colour is never the only cue. On mobile, a 'Plates' button opens a panel listing every section as a labelled full-width edge-on slab in loading order. No-JS: plain anchors, and the mobile panel is a <details>. Focus: a 3px ink outline with a 2px concrete offset; on coloured slabs, a 3px white outline (a yellow one on the yellow slabs).

Motion

Only things that are loaded move. Plates slide onto a sleeve (160ms each, 60ms stagger, ease-out) in the loader and when a tier is chosen, and the sticky slab-strip slides up in 180ms. Section slabs, text and screenshots stay put, with no scroll reveals and no parallax. Reduced motion: everything is placed instantly.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The same upright bar, shorter: concrete ground, the knurled shaft at the left edge, and one slab at the top in the page's plate colour (privacy: yellow 1.5; support: green 1; alternatives: blue 2) carrying the H1 in Hubot wdth 112/800 44px. Below it, a white reading column of 66ch in Mona 400 18px/1.65, ink, with tables in Mona tnum and 1px ink rules. Privacy: the transparency rows come first as a table, then Overview, Data collection, Storage, Third parties, Health data, Children and Changes. Support: a numbered 'What to include' list and the mailto address at 22px. Alternatives (Hevy, Caliber, Ladder, Heavyset): the quick answer, a two-column LiftLog-vs-competitor table, pick-if lists and the FAQ, closed by a collar CTA with badge, QR and price. No loader on Read pages.

Materials

Pale concrete hall wall (#E4E4E0) as the page ground, flat and without texture. · The bar: a knurled steel shaft (28px on desktop, 10px on mobile) runs the full page height at the left edge. The knurl is a repeating CSS diamond pattern in ink at 22%, with the centre and ring marks shown as plain gaps. · Plate slabs: each section opens with a full-width slab in its plate colour, seen edge-on where it threads onto the shaft. Slab height steps down with disc thickness (25 kg = 168px through 0.5 kg = 32px). The rubber is matte flat colour with a 1px darker rim line, and the section title sits on the slab. There are no kg stamps on section slabs: colour carries the weight. · The loader's sleeve diagram: a side view at 1:4, with a knurl stub, inner collar, bumpers drawn as 180px-tall rubber rectangles whose thickness is proportional to kg, smaller change plates, an outer collar, and kilos printed vertically on each plate. · Tier discs: true circles with the tier name and price printed on the face, used once in the price section. · The collar: a 2.5 kg steel band that closes the page above the footer. · Chalk: two or three flat white smudges on the concrete beside the loader (inline SVG, 30% white, aria-hidden).

Colour strategy

Full palette · light

Type rationale

GitHub drew Hubot Sans as the mechanical counterpart to Mona Sans: squared bowls and flat cuts that read like the wide, heavy grotesk printed on bumper-plate faces and stamped into collars, with an expanded width for plate lettering. Mona is its drawn reading partner, so the plate labels and the prose share one skeleton. Two files, ≈133 KB.

New assets needed

None. Slabs, the knurled shaft, the sleeve diagram and the tier discs are CSS and inline SVG. It uses the existing icon, screenshots 1–6, QR and badge.

Session in Progress

LiftLog's own shipped iPhone session view (screenshots 1–2), carried to page scale the way an iPad or desktop LiftLog would lay it out. It has a navy ground with rounded card surfaces and 1px hairlines, and a pill top bar (tool cluster · 'Push day' · Finish). There is a workout timer card, then exercise cards with '# KG REPS' set rows in big white tabular numerals ('100 × 5') and a green completed state per row. The custom keypad has ±2.5, Next → and the wide 'Log set · start rest' key. PR amber marks personal bests.

The page is a live workout session. Sections are exercise cards whose rows complete as you reach them, and the visitor logs a real set on a working copy of LiftLog's custom keypad, which prints e1RM, plates per side and a PR moment. The product proves itself in its own grammar instead of posing inside a phone mockup. It refuses the incumbent split hero and the category's photo-plus-neon page.

Type
Host Grotesk, variable (wght 300–800; one latin file ≈20 KB). The H1 is 800 at 60px. Card titles are 700 at 28–34px. Set numerals are 700 at 112–200px on desktop and 56–72px on mobile. with Host Grotesk 400 and 500 at 17–18px/1.55 for card notes, the FAQ and method text. 600 at 13px with +0.06em tracking is used only for real column heads (#, KG, REPS), as the app does.
Light
A lifter between working sets on a bench under the gym's overhead LEDs, phone face-up at arm's length, a chalky thumb on the glass and 90 seconds left on the rest timer → dark (color-scheme: dark, single scheme: the app's own navy, the one LiftLog ships).
Signature
Log a set. The empty set row is a button that opens the custom keypad as a bottom sheet built like the app's: a 4×4 grid with ±2.5, '.', backspace, 'Next →' and the wide 'Log set · start rest' key, under the header line 'Bench press · Set 2 · WEIGHT'. The visitor types a weight, presses Next, types reps, then logs. The row springs (scale 0.98→1, 220ms), a green fill sweeps across it (300ms) and the check disc fills. A result line then prints e1RM by Epley (weight × (1 + reps/30), flagging sets over 10 reps as less reliable, as plateau_disclosure says) and plates per side on a 20 kg bar. If the set beats the illustrative previous 100 × 5, the values turn PR amber with a 'PR' label. navigator.vibrate(10) fires per key where supported. iOS Safari has no web haptics, so the sheet says 'The haptics are in the app.' Everything is labelled 'Demo — nothing is saved or sent.' No-JS: the card ships with row 1 logged (100 × 5, e1RM 116.7 kg, 25 + 15 per side) and the keypad shown as a static figure (aria-hidden, keys disabled), and the empty row reads 'Log your own sets in the app'. Reduced motion: no spring or sweep, only the state change.
Remembered as
The website was the app. I typed 120 × 3 on its keypad, the row swept green, and it told me my estimated max and which plates to load.
Risk
This is the closest of the three to the product, and so the closest to a generic dark app page. Navy with white numerals and a green state can slide into the 'near-black plus one accent dashboard' rut unless the giant numerals and the working keypad stay dominant. Because it borrows the app's own palette, it looks most like the screenshots and least like a world of its own, and sits nearest the incumbent's dark phone shot. The keypad demo must stay clearly labelled and never imply haptics on the iPhone web.

Navigation

The app's pill top bar, sticky at 64px on navy with a 1px hairline beneath. Motion

The app's own physics: a spring on set completion (220ms with a slight overshoot), a 300ms green sweep, and the keypad sheet sliding up in 240ms over a 40% navy scrim. Exercise cards complete at most three of their rows once as they enter view (IntersectionObserver, 120ms steps). Nothing else moves. Reduced motion: no springs or sweeps, and rows render complete.

Privacy: the transparency rows lead as a label/value set table in tnum, then the policy sections as card sections. Support: a numbered 'What to include' list and the email in a 20px pill. Materials

Session navy ground (#0C1220) with no texture, exactly as the shipped app. · Card surfaces: #151D2F, 20px radius, 1px #2A3550 hairline, and the app's single elevation level (a 1px top highlight, no drop shadows). · Pill controls: 999px capsules on #151D2F with a hairline, used for the top bar, section tabs and two fact chips per card. · Set rows: real column heads (#, KG, REPS) above big tabular numerals. The completed state is a green fill sweeping across the row with a drawn SVG check disc, never a coloured left border. · The custom keypad: a 4×4 grid of #2A3550 keys (12px radius, 64px tall), with ±2.5, '.', backspace, 'Next →' and the wide light key 'Log set · start rest' (#E8ECF3 with navy text). · PR amber values for personal bests and the PR moment.

Colour strategy

Restrained · dark

Type rationale

Host Grotesk's figures are tabular by default, so every weight, rep, price and time lines up in columns with no feature switch. That is the app's own 'tabular numerics from end to end' rule. Its compact, neutral grotesk forms fill SF Pro's role from the shipped app without imitating Apple's system face. LiftLog promises 'one display typeface', so its microsite loads one 20 KB file, the lightest in the catalogue.

New assets needed

None. The keypad, cards, pills, checks and sweep are CSS and inline SVG. It uses the existing icon, screenshots 1–6, QR and badge.

SECOND ROLL

Summer Games Programme

Otl Aicher's identity programme for the 1972 Munich Olympics. It used one grotesk family (Univers) in a few widths and a strict modular grid. Its sport pictograms were built on a 45°/90° construction grid, and its cool daylight palette of light blue, green, silver and orange left out black and red on purpose. It also produced colour-coded venue guides and event schedules, and surcharge stamps sold for the Games (postage plus a voluntary supplement for the athletes' fund). This is a reference only: the page never names Munich and uses none of the licensed artwork.

LiftLog's own rule ('one accent color, one display typeface, one spacing scale') scales up into a sports identity programme. The page is the official programme for your training: a white modular guide with original lift pictograms, the programs as an event schedule, and pay-what-you-can as four perforated surcharge stamps (the same $9.99 base, plus a supplement toward the work). It refuses the category's dark gym aesthetic, and even the app's own navy.

Type
Pathway Extreme, variable (opsz 8–144, wdth 75–100, wght 100–900, tnum; one latin 'standard' file ≈97 KB). The H1 is set at opsz 144, wdth 100, 700, 72px. Module titles are opsz 144 700 at 36px. Venue-band labels and schedule heads are wdth 75/600. with Pathway Extreme at opsz 18, wdth 100, 400 and 600, 18px/1.6, for guide text, the FAQ and stamp captions. wdth 75/600 with tabular figures sets the schedule tables, the comparison grid and all prices.
Light
A lifter planning next week's block on a phone at a sunlit window seat or park bench in mid-afternoon, in the open daylight of a sports park → light (color-scheme: light, single scheme).
Signature
Pick your stamp. The four tiers are radio inputs drawn as perforated stamps on one sheet. Choosing one 'tears' it: translateY −8px, rotate −2°, with a perforation shadow line beneath. A receipt line then prints under the sheet, for example 'Generous — $29.99 once = 9.99 + 20.00 toward new programs and analytics. Same app as every stamp.' Selection and the receipt run on CSS :has(:checked), so they work without JS; JS adds only the tear motion. No-JS: all four stamps and their full captions are visible, with Generous pre-checked from its highlight flag. Reduced motion: no tear, just a 3px orange outline on the chosen stamp. The sheet is captioned 'You choose in the app after day 7.'
Remembered as
A bright page like an Olympic programme, with little lifting pictograms. The price was four postage stamps for the same app, and you pick how much extra to stick on.
Risk
This is the furthest from iron and from the app's own navy, so a lifter may read it as a design-history homage rather than a tool. The pictograms carry the page: weak drawing sinks it, and imitating Aicher's figures too closely is a licensing problem. The full palette needs discipline: white text only on #23733D and #123B63, never on light blue or orange. Both C and A use several colours on light grounds, so C must keep colour inside grid modules on white paper, and A must own the full-bleed slabs.

Page sequence

  1. Programme cover (hero): the venue band, the H1, the light-blue pictogram module, the quick_answer, the white admission module (price, badge, QR) and the orange stamp sheet, with hero.pre_headline as its footnote.

A green module carries the programs pictogram, with screenshot 5 beside it.

  6. 'Admission' page: the full stamp sheet in an orange 8-column module. It holds the trial ticket (7 days, $0, no card, no auto-renew) and four stamps at 200×256, each captioned with its plan summary and features. Then plans_footnote, the features 'Restraint is the design' and 'Pay-what-you-can pricing — once', and a link to the journal post.
  7. 'Who it's for' page: who_for and who_not_for in two columns with drawn yes/no marks.
  8. 'Compared' page: the comparison_table with LiftLog's column on a light-blue band, the intro and footnote. Then the alternatives_to links (Hevy, Caliber, Ladder, Heavyset, and Strong pointing to GymLogger X's page).
  9. 'Data' page: a dark-blue module with 'Privacy by default', the transparency rows as a table, privacy.notes, and links to /transparency/#liftlog, the privacy policy and support.
