Navigation

The dark-blue venue band: 'LiftLog' plus six pictogram + label signs (Session, Programs, Progress, Admission, Data, Questions), each a link with its label always visible. On scroll it pins as a 48px band, and the current page's sign sits on a chip of its module colour. On mobile, 'Index' opens a full-width panel with the six signs as a 2×3 grid of labelled colour tiles; this grid is the menu only, never the page structure. No-JS: anchors, and the band is static. Focus: a 3px orange ring with a 2px paper offset (on the band, a 3px white ring).

Motion

Systematic and brief. Module pictograms slide 12px in from the left once on entry (180ms), the stamp tear runs 200ms, and the sticky band slides in 180ms, all with one standard ease-out. No parallax, no looping, no text reveals. Reduced motion: none of it.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The same programme as guide pages: the venue band, then a title row with a 2×2 colour module and its sign beside the H1 at opsz 144 700 44px. Privacy uses dark blue with a 'data' sign, support green with an 'info point' sign, and alternatives light blue with a 'two figures facing' sign. Below that, a white 66ch column in 400 18px/1.65 dark blue, with tables at wdth 75/600 tnum and 1px silver rules. Privacy: the transparency rows come first. Support: a numbered 'What to include' list and the email at 22px. Alternatives: a two-column LiftLog-vs-competitor table with LiftLog on the light-blue band, pick-if lists, the FAQ, and the stamp strip with badge and QR as the closing CTA.

Materials

Programme paper (#FBFCFC), flat. Colour lives only inside grid modules, never in full-bleed bands, which keeps this style clear of A's slabs. · The visible programme grid: 12 columns, 24px gutters, 96px square modules, with 1px silver rules printed where the guide marks module edges. · Colour modules: flat light-blue, green, light-green, silver and orange squares and oblongs (1×1, 2×1, 2×2, 4×2) carrying pictograms, key facts and the stamp sheet. · Original pictograms on a 45°/90° construction grid: filled dark-blue figures with round-ended limbs, and the barbell as one bar with two discs. · Perforated stamps: white stamp paper with CSS radial-gradient perforation masks, set on the orange module. · The venue band: a dark-blue sign strip with white pictogram + label pairs.

Colour strategy

Full palette · light

Type rationale

Aicher ran the whole programme on one grotesk across its widths. Eduardo Tunni's open neo-grotesk does the same in a single file, with a width axis for condensed timetables and an optical-size axis that keeps the 72px titles tight and the 15px schedules open. One family, ≈97 KB. The App Store badge's black is the only black on the page, and it is Apple's.

New assets needed

An original pictogram set, drawn as inline SVG on a 45°/90° grid. That means six lifts (bench press, squat, deadlift, overhead press, pull-up, row) and six page signs (session, programs, progress, admission stamp, data, info point). This is a production drawing task, and the figures must not be traced from or closely resemble the licensed 1972 set. Everything else runs on existing assets (icon, screenshots 1–6, QR, badge).

Fixes queued before this style is built (5)

World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for.   • majorDefine the interim state: until the set is drawn, modules carry the app icon, a 400w screenshot crop or a large tabular figure (for example '100 × 5'). List the twelve SVGs as a gated production task with an originality review, so the owner never selects a style on the strength of art that hasn't been drawn.

Or the category standard, played straight: The category standard played straight: a dark gym photo under moody light, a condensed italic caps headline, a neon-green accent with glows, a phone mockup on the right with the badge row under the copy, then three feature cards, a subscription-style pricing table with a 'Most popular' ribbon, and a FAQ accordion. This is the owner's standing exit, not a recommendation.

AfterShift

/apps/aftershift/ + its privacy and support pages + 2 comparison pages

What the page must prove: At a glance: this app reads your roster, not a 9-to-5. A daytime sleep and a nap show up as real recovery, and a score sits before your next shift. Next to that, the free download (official badge, plus a QR on desktop) and the honest price: 'Free — Premium from $3.99/mo, $24.99/yr, or $39.99 lifetime'.

The default page this refuses: A dark navy or indigo sleep-app page with moon-and-stars imagery and a glowing ring or big sleep score. It has a split hero (headline left, iPhone right, badge row), four icon feature cards and a pricing table. This is what Calm, Rise and Sleep Cycle ship, and what the incumbent Paper & Ink template does in cream.

Today's page, for comparison
Picked
AfterShiftBarlow Condensed

Sleep & recovery built around your shifts.

The shift-worker sleep app where naps count as real recovery.

THE ROLL

Tape & Twill

Night-crew uniform cloth: navy polycotton twill with retroreflective silver tape edged in fluorescent yellow (the triple-band trim of EN ISO 20471 / ANSI 107 paramedic, fire and plant hi-vis), plus embroidered name tapes and sewn patches. The display face, Barlow, takes its letterforms from California highway signs and licence plates.

The page is cut from night-crew uniform cloth. Its one move is a strip of retroreflective tape that is the rotation itself: shifts in hi-vis, sleep and naps in silver, and both flare alike when light crosses them. It refuses the category's moon-and-glow dashboard and its split phone hero.

  • #18222F
  • #101822
  • #EEF1F3
  • #8F969E
  • #D3D9DF
  • #D6F03A
  • #FF6B35
Type
Barlow Condensed 700 and 800, caps, tracking +0.02em. H1 and section heads are set as uniform back-lettering, the way 'PARAMEDIC' is set across a jacket. Barlow's letterforms come from California highway signs and licence plates, the retroreflective lettering of the night road. with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400, 600 and 400 italic. The Braille Institute designed it to keep letters distinct at low acuity, which is how people read 13 hours into a night shift., Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono 500, only for clock times, durations and prices in tables (19:00–07:00, 25 min, $24.99).
Light
A paramedic or firefighter at 06:50 crossing the station apron to the car after a 12-hour night, phone in hand, lit by bay floodlights and passing headlights → dark, single scheme (color-scheme: dark).
Signature
Headlight Pass. Each tape band is a row of real <span> segments (shift, sleep, nap, cutoff) with text labels beneath. When a band first enters the viewport (IntersectionObserver), its silver segments switch from unlit #8F969E to lit #EEF1F3 one after another, left to right, over about 900 ms, like a passing car's lights. Naps switch exactly like core sleep. On pointer devices, hovering or focusing a segment lights it again and shows its time in a sewn tooltip. There is no glow, blur or sheen: retroreflection is a flat value change plus the bead texture brightening. No-JS: every segment renders lit and every label is printed text. Reduced motion: everything is lit on load with no sequence, and hover changes the value only.
Remembered as
The sleep-app page made of uniform cloth: a strip of reflective tape ran across it, and when the light passed, the naps lit up exactly like the main sleep.
Risk
Navy with fluorescent yellow sits close to the 'dark + one neon accent' rut and to emergency-service livery. It holds only if the yellow stays flat fabric (panels and tape) and never becomes glowing lines, and if no Battenburg checks, insignia or service words (PARAMEDIC, FIRE) appear. Nurses and pilots don't wear reflective tape, so the world speaks most directly to medics, fire and plant crews. Large hi-vis areas are bright for someone heading to day sleep, so yellow must stay under about 12% of any viewport.

App Store route

The Smart App Banner meta stays in the head. The official Apple badge (black artwork, never altered) always sits on a flat hi-vis yoke panel with clear space at least the badge's height. The price statement from price.value is set on the same panel. On desktop (≥900px) the QR (assets/qr/aftershift.svg) is printed on a lit-silver ID-tag plate stitched to the panel. Sticky bar: once the hero panel leaves view, a 60px triple-band tape slides up from the bottom edge. Its deep-twill centre carries the icon, 'AfterShift · Free' and the badge at 120px, with yellow edges top and bottom. The Plans rows repeat the badge, and the closing yoke panel repeats badge, QR and price. The nav's 'Get it free' tab goes to app_store_url.

Navigation

A deep-twill name-tape bar that does not stick. It holds the stitched AFTERSHIFT wordmark (microsite home), six in-page links in Atkinson 15px (Score, Naps, Caffeine, Rotations, Plans, FAQ) and a hi-vis 'Get it free' tab to the App Store. Under 900px the links fold into a 'Menu' button. It drops a deep-twill sheet of links in Barlow Cond 700 caps 30px, divided by 1px unlit-silver stitch lines. A 4px hi-vis bar under a label marks the current section. Focus everywhere is a 3px hi-vis outline with a 2px navy offset.

Motion

One verb: light passes. Band segments step from dull to lit in sequence (900 ms per band, linear, once). The sticky tape slides up in 200 ms ease-out, and the menu sheet drops in 160 ms. Nothing fades in, nothing parallaxes, and headings never move. The screenshot row scrolls natively with scroll-snap.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The privacy, support and methodology pages and the OffShift and Shift Worker alternatives keep the name-tape nav and the twill ground. The masthead is a short band: the page title in Barlow Cond 800 caps 56px lit silver over one full-bleed tape seam with no timeline segments. Reading column: Atkinson Next 400, 18px/1.65, #D3D9DF on #18222F, 66ch. Comparisons become two-column ruled tables, with the AfterShift column headed by a hi-vis tab and the competitor's by deep twill. Honest trade-offs ('If you live on your Watch, this is OffShift's territory') sit in stitched deep-twill patches. Support puts the email on a lit-silver ID-tag plate with the response-time line. Methodology sets its four inputs as four tape strips. Each page ends with a slim hi-vis panel holding badge, price and a link back to /apps/aftershift/.

Materials

Navy polycotton twill ground: a 45° twill drawn as a 2px repeating-linear-gradient at 4% contrast, never a photo · Triple-band tape, 64px: yellow 22% / silver 56% / yellow 22%. The silver carries a 1px micro-bead dot texture. It stays flat: no blur, no glow, no sheen sweep. · Embroidered name tape: a deep-twill strip with a 1px dashed silver stitch border · Sewn patches: deep-twill panels with dashed stitched edges, used for the quick answer, the founder and the score · Hi-vis yoke panels: flat fluorescent-yellow surfaces that carry the action, never more than about 12% of any viewport · A lit-silver satin care label for the Quick reference

Colour strategy

Committed · dark

Type rationale

About 93 KB of latin font: Barlow Condensed 2×22 KB, Atkinson Next 3×13 KB, Mono 10 KB. Condensed caps for lettering sewn onto cloth and a legibility face for tired reading. No serif and no italic display.

New assets needed

None. Tape, twill, stitches and patches are CSS or inline SVG. It uses the icon, the six screenshots, the QR and the OG card, all of which exist.

AfterShiftArchivo

Sleep & recovery built around your shifts.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

The Breakroom Rota

The ward or station duty rota. An A3 sheet typed in a utilitarian grotesk, run off the office photocopier and pinned to the breakroom corkboard. It has an admin header (period, issued, approved), a grid of staff by days filled with D/E/N/LD/OFF codes, a key of codes and notes at the foot, plus a highlighter stripe along your own row and biro amendments. Related: the named crew-rotation charts (DuPont, Pitman 2-2-3).

The page is the rota sheet plus the rows AfterShift adds under your shifts: sleep, naps, last coffee, and a highlighted Shift Recovery Score before every block. The worker's own schedule is visibly the baseline. It refuses the category's moon-and-score dashboard and its phone-on-the-right hero.

  • #151715
  • #4D524C
  • #7A7F78
  • #F6EE5A

Type
Archivo variable (wdth 62–125, wght 400–900). The title block is set at wdth 112 / 800, cell codes (N, OFF, SRS) at wdth 62 / 700, and headings at wdth 100 / 700. Omnibus-Type drew Archivo for tables and data-dense print, so one family covers a rota's typed header and its cramped day cells, as the office template does. with Archivo variable at wdth 100, weights 400 and 600, 18px, with tabular figures for every time (19:00–07:00)., Reenie Beanie 400, a quick biro scrawl, for at most four margin notes. Each repeats real copy (for example 'naps count here'); no content exists only in handwriting.
Light
A nurse or medic at 18:40 before night handover, reading the new rota pinned to the breakroom corkboard under a cool fluorescent tube → light, single scheme (color-scheme: light).
Signature
Your Rota, Completed. The hero is a real <table>. The pattern tabs (4-on-4-off, Pitman 2-2-3, DuPont, 12-hour, on-call) re-letter the SHIFT row from inline JSON holding the real pattern definitions. They also move the NAP and SCORE marks so a score always sits before the first shift of each block (illustrative placement, labelled). When the table enters view, a yellow highlighter stroke draws once along the SCORE row (600 ms, SVG mask). Tapping a day column highlights it and opens the matching screenshot slip beside the table. No-JS: the 4-on-4-off table prints complete with the SCORE row highlighted, and the other patterns print statically under 'Patterns on file'. Reduced motion: the highlight is static and tabs swap instantly.
Remembered as
It looked like the rota on the breakroom wall, and under my shifts it had filled in when I'd sleep, a nap, and a highlighted recovery score before every block.
Risk
Familiar. A day grid is the category's own calendar interface (AfterShift's Roster tab is one) and the most obvious 'shift' image, so the page can read as a spreadsheet or a scheduling app instead of a sleep app. The illustrative grid values must be labelled every time or they read as claims. The handwriting turns cute past four notes. Turning the sheet to days-down on a phone has to stay the same sheet, not become a second layout.

Left cell (x96–1000): H1 'Sleep & recovery built around your shifts.' in Archivo wdth 112/800, 64px/1.0, 3 lines, with hero.subheadline below at 19px/1.5 (60ch). Right admin cell (x1000–1344), ruled into rows. 'Price': 'Free — Premium from $3.99/mo, $24.99/yr, or $39.99 lifetime'. 'Install': official App Store badge at 156px + a 104px QR captioned 'Scan with your iPhone'. 'Issued': 3 Apr 2026. 360–860: the completed rota. Pattern tabs (4-on-4-off · Pitman 2-2-3 · DuPont · 12-hour · On-call) in Archivo wdth 75/600. Below them a <table> with a 200px row-label column and 8 day columns (Day 1–8: N N N N OFF OFF OFF OFF). Rows: SHIFT (shaded 19–07 cells), SLEEP (09:30–15:30), NAP (pink cells, a 25-min nap before each night), LAST COFFEE, and SHIFT RECOVERY SCORE (a yellow-highlighted row with a value before each shift). The caption reads 'Illustrative block: values modelled on the app's own screens'. At the score row's right end, a biro note 'scored against your NEXT shift' with a hand-drawn arrow.

0–44: sheet strip with icon + 'AfterShift' on the left and a 'Sheets' button on the right. 60–232: title block in a 2px toner frame inset 16px: H1 in Archivo wdth 100/800, 40px/1.0, 3 lines, then the subheadline at 16px over 4 lines. 244–376: ruled admin box with the price line (15px), the official badge at 156px and 'Issued 3 Apr 2026'; no QR. 392–844: the pattern tabs as a horizontally scrolling row, then the rota printed as a personal sheet. The first four days are visible, with the 'Illustrative block' caption below.

App Store route

The Smart App Banner meta stays in the head. The badge (official black artwork) sits in the 'Install' row of the rota's admin box, the same kind of ruled form cell a real rota uses for period and approval. On desktop the QR sits beside it ('Scan with your iPhone'), and the 'Price' row holds the price statement from price.value. Sticky bar: once the admin box leaves view, a 56px paper strip pins to the bottom under a 2px toner rule. A yellow highlighter band sits behind 'AfterShift · Free — Premium from $3.99/mo', next to the badge at 120px. The Rates sheet ends with the badge under the plan table. The Notes sheet ends with a second admin box (badge, QR, price, issued dates).

Page sequence

  1. Sheet strip nav: wordmark, sheet index (Rota · Key · Rates · Notes), Download link
  2. Sheet 1, Rota: ruled title block (H1, subheadline, admin box with price, badge, QR and issued date)
  3. The completed rota (signature): pattern tabs and a table of SHIFT / SLEEP / NAP / LAST COFFEE / SHIFT RECOVERY SCORE, with the illustrative label and the biro note
  4. 'Note to all staff': a ruled box directly under the grid holding quick_answer (speakable) at 19px. Beside it on desktop (below on mobile) is the 'Sheet summary' box: the Quick reference ai-canonical <details>, crawlable.
  5. Sheet foot: trust row (iPhone · No account · No ads · 0 third-party SDKs, linking to /transparency/#aftershift) + 'Sheet 1 of 4 · Issued 3 Apr 2026'
  6. Sheet 2, Key: value_points as four 'Standing rules', each a bold statement and one line, no cards
  7. The Key: features as code entries. SRS, Shift Recovery Score, with its four inputs and a methodology link; SLP, sleep stages in context; FRG, fatigue & fragmentation; CAF, smart caffeine timing; IMP, calendar shift import; TRD, trends. Each code sits in a toner-framed cell, the term in Archivo 700, the definition at 18px.
  8. Patterns on file: a ruled table defining DuPont, Pitman 2-2-3, 4-on-4-off, 12-hour, swing and on-call from the FAQ, each drawn as a one-line code strip
  9. Attachments: six screenshots pinned in a row (6-up at 200px on desktop, scroll-snap on mobile) in thin toner frames with typed caption slips
  10. Sheet 3, Rates & terms: a plan table with columns Free / Premium Monthly / Premium Annual (yellow highlighter) / Lifetime and features as rows, then plans_footnote and the badge
  11. Applies to / Does not apply to: who_for and who_not_for as two ruled lists
  12. Data handling: the transparency record as a ruled two-column form (network calls, SDKs, analytics, permissions, what leaves the device), linking to transparency, the privacy policy and support
  13. Sheet 4, Notes: the memo 'Why AfterShift exists.' (show_body prose, 68ch), signed with the founder block (Lagerland Apps, Independent Apple studio · Finland, bio, signals, response time, email, methodology link)
  14. Queries: 18 FAQ <details> in ruled rows, questions in Archivo 600
  15. Cross-references: the OffShift and Shift Worker alternatives, methodology, the journal post, /for/shift-workers/, and Observa for steady 9-to-5 sleepers
  16. Closing admin box: price, badge, QR and the maker line (Issued by Lagerland Apps · updated 3 Apr 2026 · first issued 1 Jan 2026), then the shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

The sheet index in the top strip (Rota · Key · Rates · Notes) links to the four sheets. On scroll, a 40px sticky strip keeps the index visible with the current sheet under a yellow highlighter stroke (IntersectionObserver; without JS the strip stays static at the top). On mobile, a 'Sheets' button opens a ruled list of the four sheets and their sub-entries (Score, Naps, Caffeine, Patterns, Plans, Privacy, FAQ). Links are biro blue with a 1px underline. The focus ring is 3px biro blue with a 2px paper offset.

Motion

Pen and highlighter only. Each highlighted element gets one highlighter stroke when it first enters view (600 ms, ease-out, left to right), and each biro note draws its stroke once (500 ms). Tab swaps re-letter cells instantly, and sticky strips slide in 180 ms. No fades on body text, no parallax.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The privacy, support and methodology pages and the alternatives pages are single typed memos on the same paper. Each has the sheet strip nav (with 'Back to the rota') and a ruled title block: the title in Archivo wdth 112/800 52px, and an admin box with the issued date, the contact email and, on alternatives, the badge and price. Reading column: Archivo 400, 18px/1.6, 68ch, toner on paper. Comparisons become ruled rota-style tables with the AfterShift column under yellow highlighter. Honest trade-offs sit in boxes ruled all round in 1px biro blue. Support has a 'Queries to' row with the email and response time. Methodology sets its four inputs as a Key.

Materials

Photocopy paper, full-bleed: the page is the sheet · Toner grid: 2px toner outer rules, 1px rule-grey inner rules, shift cells shaded with a 12% toner tint · Highlighter strokes: yellow and pink bands behind ink with slightly ragged ends (SVG mask, multiply blend) · Biro: 1.5px blue hand-drawn SVG circles, arrows and underlines, with Reenie Beanie notes · Ruled admin boxes (Price, Install, Issued), drawn like the period/approved box of a real rota · Sheet headers: each group of sections opens with a ruled header row (Sheet n of 4 · title · issued date)

Colour strategy

Restrained · light

Type rationale

About 119 KB of latin font: Archivo full variable 90 KB + Reenie Beanie 28 KB. A rota is typed, photocopied and corrected by hand, so the page uses one data grotesk with a width axis and one biro, nothing else.

New assets needed

None. The grid, highlighter and biro marks are CSS or inline SVG. It uses the icon, the six screenshots and the QR, all of which exist.

SECOND ROLL

Follow the Line

Hospital and plant wayfinding: coloured vinyl floor lines that peel off at junctions ('follow the blue line'), dark hanging sign blades with reversed text and arrow pictograms, and white enamel directory plaques. Set in Signika, a face drawn for wayfinding and signage, with its Negative cut for light-on-dark panels.

Four floor lines, one for each of the Shift Recovery Score's four inputs, run the length of the page. Each peels off to its own station, and all four meet again at the score, so the method is something you walk rather than read. It refuses the category's stacked feature cards and phone-on-the-right hero.

  • #E3E7E1
  • #17201E
  • #10423B
  • #1D5BC9
  • #178048
  • #F2C230
  • #C2412A
Type
Signika Negative 600 and 700, for every reversed word on the dark sign blades (nav, H1 sign, section signs). The Negative cut is thinned so white letters on a dark panel don't bloom, which is exactly what a back-lit corridor sign needs. with Signika 400, 600 and 700. Anna Giedryś drew it for wayfinding, where information has to read at a glance. It sets body text, plaques, tabular times, and 13px caps labels printed on the tapes., Signika 700 caps for the tape labels. There is no third family; a wayfinding programme runs on one.
Light
A nurse or plant operator walking a long corridor between wards or bays at 03:10 under cool ceiling panels, speckled grey-green lino underfoot, coloured lines running ahead → light, single scheme (color-scheme: light).
Signature
Follow the Line. Each section has real tape elements: a vertical bundle in a left gutter (desktop x200–420, mobile x16–52). At each station, one tape turns 90° with a mitred corner and runs under that station's sign blade. Tape segments draw downward at walking pace as you scroll, using a CSS scroll-driven animation (animation-timeline: view(), scaleY 0→1) with an IntersectionObserver class as fallback. Hovering or focusing a station label dims the other three tapes to 30%, so one input's route reads on its own. No-JS: every tape is fully drawn. Reduced motion: tapes are drawn with no scroll link, and hover only dims.
Remembered as
Four coloured floor lines ran down the page like a hospital corridor; each turned off to explain one part of the score, and they all met at the Shift Recovery Score.
Risk
Wayfinding signage can read as a real hospital. It must avoid NHS-like blue and Frutiger, any real hospital pictogram set, and the green running-man exit sign. Nurses will recognise it at once; pilots and fire crews see it less. The tape bundle's geometry across breakpoints is the hardest build of the three. At 390px the 36px gutter narrows the reading column to about 318px. Four saturated colours can tip into a children's map if the lino and blades don't hold them down.

On the right (x880–1344), the white enamel directory plaque: 'Get AfterShift' (Signika 700, 22px), the price line from price.value, the official App Store badge at 168px, and a 120px QR with 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. 600–900: the floor begins. App Store route

The Smart App Banner meta stays in the head. The official badge sits on a white enamel directory plaque (dark badge on white, clear space at least the badge's height), with the price statement from price.value. On screens 900px and wider, the QR sits on the same plaque with 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. Page sequence

  1. Ceiling-blade nav: wordmark, directory links with arrows, 'Get it'
  2. Hero sign (H1), subheadline, enamel action plaque (price, badge, QR), and the four tapes setting off
  3. Information plaque: quick_answer (speakable) and a trust row (iPhone · no account · no ads · 0 third-party SDKs, linking to transparency)
  4. Directory plaque: the Quick reference ai-canonical <details>, 'AfterShift in one screen', crawlable
  5. Blue station, sleep quality: the tape peels right under the sign blade 'Sleep, read against your rotation', with the 'Sleep stages in context' feature and its 'deep sleep at 11 a.m.' copy, plus a screenshot
  6. Green station, continuity: the fatigue & fragmentation feature, the methodology's continuity text and the trends screenshot
  7. Yellow station, nap contribution: value point 'Naps count here', the 20 / 90 / 45-min nap lengths from the methodology, and the nap and plan screenshot
  8. Red station, next-shift proximity: recovery decay, the caffeine-timing value point and feature, calendar shift import, and a plaque table of rotation patterns (DuPont, Pitman 2-2-3, 4-on-4-off, 12-hour, swing, on-call), with the caffeine and roster screenshots
  9. Junction, Shift Recovery Score: all four tapes turn in and end at one floor decal. A plaque gives the score's definition (0–100, forward-looking, informational, not a diagnosis), the recovery screenshot and a methodology link, beside a badge plaque
  10. Reception, just past the junction: plans as four enamel price plaques in a row, with Annual marked by a yellow tape strip (highlight: true), then plans_footnote
  11. Who this corridor is for / not for: who_for and who_not_for as two directory lists
  12. Nothing leaves this building (privacy): the transparency record on a plaque (network calls none, 0 SDKs, analytics none, Calendar read-only, HealthKit read sleep, your iCloud only if enabled), linking to transparency, the privacy policy and support
  13. Why AfterShift exists: show_body prose, then the founder plaque (Lagerland Apps, Finland, bio, signals, response time, email, methodology link)
  14. Help desk: 18 FAQ <details> as directory rows whose arrow pictograms turn on open
  15. Other routes: the OffShift and Shift Worker alternatives, methodology, the journal post, /for/shift-workers/, and Observa for 9-to-5 sleepers
  16. Exit plaque: tagline, badge, QR and price, plus the maker line (Built by Lagerland Apps · updated 3 Apr 2026 · first released 1 Jan 2026), then the shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

A ceiling sign blade across the top, not sticky. Its directory entries carry inline-SVG arrows: a down arrow for anchors on this page, a diagonal arrow for links that leave it (the App Store). On mobile, the 'Directory' button drops a green blade listing every station, each with a 12px swatch of its tape colour beside the name; colour is never the only cue. The only sticky element is the download blade. Focus is a 3px #F2C230 outline with a 2px green offset on blades, and a 3px ink outline on lino.

Motion

Lines advance with the walker: tapes draw with scroll position, never on a timer. Sign blades and text never move. The Directory blade drops in 160 ms, the sticky blade slides in 200 ms, and FAQ arrows turn 90° in 120 ms.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The privacy, support, methodology and alternatives pages keep the ceiling blade and the lino, and each title hangs on a sign blade (Signika Negative 700, 48px). One tape runs down the left of the reading column as a route cue: blue for privacy, green for support, red for alternatives, all four for methodology (whose sections are the four inputs). Reading column: Signika 400, 18px/1.62, ink on lino, 66ch. Comparison tables become directory plaques with ruled rows, the AfterShift column headed by a yellow tape strip. Honest trade-offs sit on white plaques with a 1px ink frame. Each page ends at an exit plaque with badge, price and a 'Back to AfterShift' arrow.

Materials

Speckled vinyl lino ground: sparse 2–3px flecks drawn with CSS radial-gradients, never a photo · Floor tapes, 50px wide, in four colours: mitred 45° corners where they turn, a 1px darker wear edge, caps labels printed on the tape · Hanging sign blades: deep-green panels with a 4px radius, hung on 2px ink rods, white Signika Negative text and inline-SVG arrow pictograms · White enamel directory plaques (#F4F7F5, 1px ink frame) for the action, the quick answer, the privacy record and the plans · Floor decals: circular station markers where a tape ends

Full palette · light

About 119 KB of latin font: Signika 400/600/700 + Signika Negative 600/700. One wayfinding family split by polarity, nothing decorative.

New assets needed

None. Tapes, blades, plaques, arrows and lino flecks are CSS or inline SVG. It uses the icon, the six screenshots and the QR, all of which exist.

EarnLock

/apps/earnlock/ + its privacy and support pages + 12 comparison pages

What the page must prove: The first viewport must show that unlocking costs a number of real steps rather than a tap or a timer. It should show that number live and attached to the locked apps (the shield copy), that one goal unlocks everything until midnight, and that it is free with a $19.99 lifetime option. THE ROLL

Exact Steps Only

Japanese street vending machines (jidō hanbaiki). Sources: the backlit display window with product dummies on shelves, the price button under every item that lights once enough credit is in, the dot-matrix/LED credit display and contactless reader pad on the control column, the operator's price-setting panel inside the door, the riveted maker's nameplate, and the sales-audit printout the operator pulls.

The doomscroll is merchandise behind glass with a single price tag, your daily step goal, and the page is the machine that sells it. Every selection button lights at once when enough steps are in. This refuses the category's dark-gradient phone hero and its 'wall' framing in favour of the developer's 'price tag, not punishment'.

  • #C8CCC4
Type
Dela Gothic One 400. A heavy Japanese gothic whose Latin is drawn to sit with kana, the voice of machine marquees and sticker lettering. Only H1/H2 on the marquee and plates. with M PLUS Rounded 1c 400/700/800. The rounded gothic of Japanese machine button labels and product cards: 800 for dummy names and prices, 700 for buttons and the price card, 400 for body at 17–18px., Doto 700. Dot-matrix LED face used only for real numbers: the credit display ('INSERT 2,026 STEPS'), live counts, dates on the nameplate.
Light
Someone in a station underpass or office corridor at night stands at a machine whose own fluorescent-backlit window is the brightest thing there. The machine face is light and the surround is dark, so the scheme is light with a dark frame (color-scheme: light).
Signature
Insert steps. Three keys beside the credit display ('+500 steps', '+1,000 steps', 'Walk the rest'), or a range input skinned as the coin slot, subtract from the Doto display (INSERT 2,026 → 0). At zero, a class change lights every price lamp in one 120ms sweep, each shelf label flips 'LOCKED' to 'OPEN UNTIL 23:59', and the coil under 'Instagram' turns once. The operator presets (4,000 / 8,000 / 12,000) reprice every button at once. The whole demo is labelled 'Demo — illustrative, not your data'. No-JS: the window renders locked with the real price on every button and a printed line under the shelves: 'All lamps light together when today's goal is met — then every app stays open until midnight.' Reduced motion: lamps switch instantly, digits jump to the final value, the coil does not turn.
Remembered as
A sage-green vending machine where Instagram and TikTok sat behind glass priced at 4,000 steps. When I 'inserted' steps, every button lit up at once.
Risk
The machine can tip into a novelty prop, so the product window stays a hero-only device and every later section must read as plain set text on enamel or lit panels. A vending machine implies per-item prices; every button must carry the same single daily goal or the page misstates the mechanism. App names behind glass flirt with third-party trademarks, so names are text only, with no logos.
Full style card

First viewport, desktop

Dark corridor #1C201D. One machine, 1120px wide, centred, top edge at y=24, runs past the fold. Marquee (1120×184, 16px sage enamel frame around a lit #F4F6EF panel): app icon 72px at left, then H1 'Block the doomscroll until you move.' in Dela Gothic One 60px/1.02 ink over 2 lines, with 'Earn your screen time.' in M PLUS Rounded 800 22px under it. Below, the body in its real form: display window 752px (left) | 32px enamel mullion | control column 336px (right). The window shows two shelves (about 290px each) of typographic dummies: 'Instagram' 'TikTok' 'X' / 'YouTube' 'Reddit' 'Anything you pick' (M PLUS 800 22px on grey packs, chrome coils beneath). Each has a price button '4,000 steps' (M PLUS 700 15px) with an unlit lamp and a tiny sage ring glyph at 49%, echoing the icon. Control column, top to bottom from y=232: amber Doto 30px credit display 'INSERT 2,026 STEPS' (336×96); price card 'Free — Premium from $1.99/mo or $19.99 lifetime' (M PLUS 700 17px) at y≈350; the official App Store badge at 56px tall in a brushed-steel bill-acceptor bezel at y≈430; QR 128px in the contactless-reader pad captioned 'Scan with your iPhone camera' at y≈510; keypad nav (2×3 keys) at y≈670. Badge, price and QR all sit above the fold.

First viewport, phone

16px corridor gutters; the machine is 358px wide. Marquee: icon 44px, then H1 in Dela Gothic One 34px/1.05 (3 lines) on the lit panel, then 'Earn your screen time.' M PLUS 800 17px. Below it the amber credit strip (358×56) 'INSERT 2,026 STEPS' Doto 22px. Then the bill-acceptor row: official badge 48px tall with the price statement beside it in two lines (M PLUS 700 14px). Then the window begins with one shelf of three dummies (Instagram, TikTok, X; 18px names, '4,000 steps' buttons), cut by the fold at y≈780 to pull the scroll. No QR below 1024px. The keypad collapses into the sticky top strip's 'Keypad' key.

App Store route

Smart App Banner stays in head; Safari draws it above the marquee. Apple's badge is never redrawn: it sits recessed in the brushed-steel bill-acceptor bezel with a small printed 'Get it here' plate above it. The QR occupies the contactless-reader pad, desktop ≥1024px only. The price statement comes from price.value, printed on the price card; plans appear later as the operator's price list. The sticky bar is the pickup bin: when the control column scrolls off, a 64px dark #1C201D push-flap bar slides up from the bottom with amber Doto 'FREE · $19.99 LIFETIME', the price.value line in M PLUS 700, and the badge at 40px. On mobile it is full-width and the QR is omitted. The closing CTA ends at the machine's foot, the pickup bin, with badge, QR and price.

Page sequence

  1. Marquee: hero.headline H1, hero.secondary, icon + name
  2. Display window + control column: locked app names (from hero.subheadline and screenshot 1) with identical '4,000 steps' price buttons; amber credit display; price.value price card; badge; QR; trust stickers on the column side ('iOS 17 + watchOS 10', '0 third-party SDKs', 'No account', 'No ads')
  3. 'How this machine works' screwed enamel plate under the window: the visible Quick Answer (quick_answer + speakable). The ai-canonical Quick reference <details> hangs below it as the hinged service-door panel; its summary is always visible and its content is in the HTML
  4. 'Inside the door: you set the price': the operator's price panel. Goal presets Light 4,000 ≈ 35-min / Standard 8,000 ≈ 75-min / Challenge 12,000 ≈ 110-min (screenshot 7) and the units steps / active minutes / active kcal (Free vs Premium marked). The demo controls live here, with the Sunday-self vs Thursday-self line paraphrased from the journal
  5. 'Test-vend week': the spotlight (Shadow Week) heading + lead. Stats are printed as a thermal sales-audit slip ('7 days', 'Your data', 'One tap'), plus the app's own graduation numbers '23 would-be blocks · ~30m/day', labelled 'from the app's screen'
  6. 'How it vends': how_it_works 3 steps as the machine's real 1-2-3 instruction decal (HowTo), each with its full detail
  7. 'Display samples': the 7 screenshots stand as lit dummies on a horizontal scroll-snap shelf behind glass, each with its alt text as a printed shelf label
  8. Side-panel plate 'Why this machine is different': value_points (4), set as a ruled list on enamel
  9. 'Selection directory': features (9) as a two-column directory on the lit window, name in M PLUS 800 with description in 400
  10. Operator's price list placard: plans Free / Monthly / Yearly (lit lamp = highlight) / Lifetime as printed rows with tabular prices and feature lines, plus plans_footnote and a die-cut 'Family Sharing · up to 5' sticker
  11. 'Accepted payment': comparison_table (EarnLock vs Opal, one sec, ScreenZen, Apple Screen Time; EarnLock column lit green) with the footnote and an inline badge, then the alternatives_to list as 'Other machines on this platform' linking to the 12 /alternatives/ pages (Apple Screen Time unlinked)
  12. 'This machine is for / not for': who_for and who_not_for as two printed stickers; 'never parental control' is set in bold
  13. Operator's permit card inside the door: founder (Lagerland Apps, Finland) heading, bio, signals, support email and response time
  14. 'Customer questions': faq (14) as <details> rows on the lit window
  15. 'What this machine records: nothing': a privacy audit slip from transparency.yml (third_party_sdks 0, network calls none, data leaves device: No, 3 permissions), privacy.notes, the Apple label line, links to /transparency/, the privacy policy and support
  16. Notice pinned on the side: related_journal essay link + 'The unlock cost has to live outside the app'
  17. Pickup bin, the closing CTA: badge + QR + price.value
  18. Riveted maker's nameplate: 'Built by Lagerland Apps · Finland · v1.0 · first released 2026-05-22 · last updated 2026-05-22' (dates in Doto)
  19. Corridor floor: 'Other Lagerland apps' as a row of small machine nameplates, then the shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

The machine's selection keypad. Six black rubber keys with white legends ('Prices', 'How it vends', 'Shadow week', 'Compare', 'Questions', 'Privacy'; M PLUS 700 14px) on a brushed-steel plate in the control column, as plain anchor links. The 'EarnLock' wordmark on the marquee links to top. On scroll and on mobile, a 52px sage enamel strip pins to the top with icon + name and a 'Keypad' key that drops the 2×3 key grid. Keys show a themed focus ring (3px #2F6B2A plus a 2px window-colour gap).

Motion

Mechanical on/off. Lamps snap on in 80ms, LED digits step in fixed increments, one coil revolution (600ms ease-in-out) happens only on a demo 'vend', and the pickup bar slides up in 200ms. Sections are static enamel: no scroll fades, no floating, no glow beyond a lit lamp.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the 12 alternatives pages show the machine with its service door open. The corridor surround and a sage enamel marquee strip carry the page title (Dela Gothic One 40px). Inside, the backlit #F4F6EF window is the reading column: M PLUS Rounded 400 18px/1.6, 68ch, ink 16.6:1. Alternatives pages open with an 'Accepted payment' plate (EarnLock: steps | Opal: tap or timer) above the real two-column table. 'When should I pick X instead' is a printed notice, and the FAQ is <details> rows. Support is the 'Out of order? Call the operator' sticker with the email and response time. Privacy opens with the audit slip summarising the transparency row before the policy text.

Materials

baked enamel steel in flat sage with a faint orange-peel (inline SVG feTurbulence at 3% opacity) · backlit polycarbonate window with fluorescent falloff, brighter at the top edge (one linear-gradient, no glow halo) · chrome spiral coils under each product dummy (CSS repeating-linear-gradient diagonals) · typographic product dummies: app names on tall pale-grey packs, with no third-party logos · price buttons with a lamp dot, unlit or lit · brushed-steel keypad plate with black rubber keys · amber dot-matrix credit display window · screwed white enamel instruction plates (four CSS screw heads) · thermal-paper sales-audit printout with a torn edge (CSS mask) · riveted maker's nameplate · push-flap pickup bin (dark) at the machine's foot

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

Three faces, about 85 KB latin total. Dela carries the machine's shouting marquee voice, M PLUS Rounded is what a buyer actually reads on the buttons, and Doto appears only where a real machine shows a number.

New assets needed

None. Enamel, coils, keypad, LED, plates and the pickup bin are CSS and inline SVG; product dummies are typographic (app names only). Uses the existing icon, 7 screenshots and assets/qr/earnlock.svg.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

The Junction Post

Swiss hiking-trail signalisation (Schweizer Wanderwege): arrow-tipped yellow blades stacked on a galvanised post, each naming destinations with the walking time. Also the white location plate on top, yellow diamond waymarks along the route, the white-red-white tip for mountain paths, and the trailhead information board.

The shield is a signpost, not a wall. Instagram is a destination 2,026 steps away, and the page is a waymarked route from the junction post (offer + action) to the summit (open until midnight). This refuses the category's lock-and-wall imagery and its phone-in-the-centre hero.

  • #F6C700
  • #141412
  • #E8EBE6
  • #FFFFFF
  • #8E9594
  • #C8202A
  • #2E6B34
Type
Signika 600/700. A humanist sans drawn specifically for wayfinding and signage (low contrast, open apertures, legible at distance), standing in for the Frutiger-family lettering on Swiss trail blades. Used for blades, the location plate and headings. with Fira Sans 400/500/600. From the Meta lineage of Spiekermann's transit-signage work and built for long reading on screens; tabular figures (tnum) carry every step count and walking time.
Light
A walker at a trail junction on an overcast afternoon reads the post in flat, shadowless daylight, so the scheme is light (color-scheme: light).
Signature
Re-sign the post. A three-position switch under the blades (Light 4,000 ≈ 35 min / Standard 8,000 ≈ 75 min / Challenge 12,000 ≈ 110 min, the app's own presets) and a 'steps walked' slider re-letter every destination blade at once. Digits roll in 180ms and the goal blade's time updates. At 0 remaining, every destination reads 'open until midnight' and the tips switch to arrival green. Labelled 'Illustrative — your numbers come from Apple Health.' No-JS: the post renders the Light example (2,026 steps on every blade), with the three presets listed as a printed line under it. Reduced motion: text changes instantly with no roll.
Remembered as
A yellow hiking signpost told me Instagram was 2,026 steps away, and even the prices were written on the signs.
Risk
Familiarity: 'walking → hiking trail' is the most obvious bridge from this product, it is the developer's own metaphor, and it topped the ranking for that reason. Yellow blades can read as Swiss-tourism pastiche. The Wanderwiki sibling's name invites the same trail world, so if both pages go trail, one must yield. Large areas of yellow tire the eye on a long page, so blades stay headings only and the reading happens on white boards.

Page sequence

  1. Junction post: location plate (icon, name, platforms), H1 blade, destination blade (locked apps with remaining steps, from screenshot 1), goal blade (Light 4,000 ≈ 35-min walk, from screenshot 7), register box (badge, price.value, QR)

  14. Blade 'Leave no trace': privacy (data_collection none, notes, Apple label) with the transparency row (0 SDKs, no server, data leaves device: No), linking to /transparency/, the privacy policy and support
  15. Route pamphlet: related_journal ('What an iPhone app can actually block') + 'The unlock cost has to live outside the app'
  16. Summit, the closing CTA: 'Open until midnight.' with badge, QR and price.value. The summit plate carries maker/freshness: Built by Lagerland Apps · v1.0 · first released 2026-05-22 · last updated 2026-05-22
  17. 'Other trails from Lagerland' (other apps), then the shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

A junction cluster. The sticky white location-plate header (56px) has icon + 'EarnLock' at left and, at right, five small yellow arrow tabs: 'Prices', 'Shadow Week', 'How it works', 'Questions', 'Privacy' (Signika 600 15px, CSS arrow tips; no unicode arrows). On mobile one yellow 'Routes' blade opens a vertical stack of the same blades. Section waymarks on the rail double as anchor targets. Focus ring: 3px #2E6B34 with a 2px white gap.

Motion

Grounded and still: signs don't swing and the page doesn't animate on scroll. The only motion is digits re-lettering on the blades (180ms vertical roll) and the sticky blade sliding in (200ms). Waymarks are static.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The location-plate header, then one yellow blade carrying the page title (Signika 700 40px) pointing right, then the white trailhead board as the reading column: Fira Sans 400 18px/1.65, 66ch, on the overcast ground with the route rail at left. On alternatives pages the title blade becomes a two-way blade ('EarnLock' ← | → 'Opal'), the compare table sits on a white board, and 'When should I pick Opal instead' sits under a white-red-white tip. Support is the trail-keeper contact plate; privacy opens with the 'Leave no trace' transparency summary.

Materials

powder-coated yellow aluminium blades with arrow tips (CSS clip-path polygon), single- and multi-destination · galvanised round post as the page spine (22px bar, one-pixel linear sheen) · stainless clamp bands where blades meet the post · white enamel location plate on top of the post · yellow diamond waymarks (rotated squares) marking each section's start on the route rail · white-red-white blade tip for the hard parts · white trailhead info boards with a thin map-frame border for long reading · grey steel register box bolted to the post (holds badge, price, QR)

SECOND ROLL

Belt-Clip Counter

The clip-on pedometer: Yamasa's 1965 manpo-kei ('10,000-steps meter') and its 1990s LCD descendants. Elements: a moulded plastic shell, a reflective grey-green LCD with fixed icon segments (STEPS, KCAL, MIN), MODE and RESET buttons, silkscreened legends, a 7-day memory, and a belt clip and battery-cover label on the back.

Your phone becomes the pedometer. The viewport is framed by its cobalt shell, the reflective LCD is the page ground, the remaining count is the headline object, and MODE cycles steps → minutes → kcal. This refuses the category's glowing dark dashboard and neon rings: a passive LCD lit by the sun.

  • #C5CDB3
  • #1C2117
  • #B0B89D
  • #2443B8
  • #F4F3EE
  • #8DB879
Type
DSEG7 Classic 400/700. Real 7-segment LCD digit forms, used only for live counts, prices, dates and times; 400 sets the ghost '88,888' underlay and 700 the lit digits. with Hanken Grotesk 400/500/800. The plain neo-grotesk of silkscreen legends on moulded plastic. 800 sets the H1 and section heads on the LCD, 500 the shell legends, 400 the body at 18px.
Light
A walker on a pavement at midday glances down at the counter clipped to their waistband in direct sun. The LCD is reflective with no backlight, so the scheme is light (color-scheme: light).
Signature
MODE. A real <button> on the shell cycles the big reading through the app's own shield copy: '3,412 STEPS UNTIL UNLOCK' (Free) → '18 MIN EXERCISE UNTIL UNLOCK' (Premium flag lit) → '187 KCAL UNTIL UNLOCK' (Premium). Segments switch the way an LCD does. A small RESET key shows '00:00 — resets at local midnight'. The memory rows keep all three readings visible at all times, so JS only changes which one is large. No-JS: the steps reading is large and the other two print in the memory rows, so nothing is missing. Reduced motion: an instant swap with no 80ms segment fade.
Remembered as
The whole page was a blue pedometer. A huge grey-green LCD said 3,412 steps until unlock, and pressing MODE switched it to minutes and calories.
Risk
A fixed device bezel can read as a gimmick and costs width on phones, so it shrinks to 6px rims at 390. The low-chroma grey-green LCD ground can read as dull unless the cobalt shell and the giant count carry the energy. DSEG7 has no letters or '$', so faces must mix carefully in prices. Long reading on an LCD ground has to hold its 10:1 contrast with no texture behind text.

App Store route

The QR is on a white adhesive label, ≥1024px only. price.value is silkscreened on the shell, and plans become LCD price readouts. Page sequence

  1. Shell strip + LCD hero: H1, the giant remaining count, fixed unit segments, memory rows for the three goal units with Free/Premium flags, and hero.subheadline as the LCD caption
  2. Cobalt button panel: MODE key, price.value, badge, QR, silkscreen trust legends ('NO ACCOUNT · NO SERVER · 0 THIRD-PARTY SDKs · iOS 17 + watchOS 10')
  3. 'READ ME' display page: the visible Quick Answer (quick_answer + speakable). The ai-canonical Quick reference <details> is the 'INFO' submenu below it (summary visible, content in HTML)
  4. '7-day memory': the spotlight (Shadow Week) heading + lead, with seven LCD day cells D1–D7. Only the real example values are shown: Day 2 = 4 would-be blocks, week total 23, ~30m/day (screenshots 2, 5, labelled); the other cells show ghost '--'. spotlight.stats sit beneath
  5. 'How it counts': how_it_works as three LCD screens in sequence, 1 SET · 2 COUNT · 3 UNLOCK (HowTo), each with its full detail
  6. 'The shield': screenshot 1 large on the LCD with the shield copy, plus value_points (4) as a plain list
  7. 'Display frames': the 7 screenshots in a horizontal scroll-snap row, alt text as captions
  8. 'Modes & functions': features (9) as the device's function table (name | what it does)
  9. 'Prices': plans as readouts ($ in Hanken, digits in DSEG7: 0 / 1.99 per mo / 9.99 per yr / 19.99 once). Yearly is an inverse band; plans_footnote and Family Sharing follow
  10. 'Compared with': comparison_table on the LCD with the EarnLock column in inverse, the footnote and an inline badge; then alternatives_to linking to the 12 /alternatives/ pages
  11. 'Fits / doesn't fit': who_for and who_not_for as two columns
  12. Back label (cobalt panel, silkscreen white): founder (Lagerland Apps · Finland) heading, bio, signals, support email + response time
  13. 'Questions': faq (14) as <details>
  14. 'No transmitter inside': privacy on the battery-cover label. data_collection none, notes, Apple label; transparency figures in DSEG7 ('0' SDKs, '0' tracking domains, network calls 'None'), linking to /transparency/, the privacy policy and support
  15. 'Further reading': related_journal + the unlock-cost essay
  16. Closing CTA: the LCD shows '0' / 'OPEN UNTIL 23:59' with badge, QR and price.value
  17. Silkscreen maker line on the shell: Built by Lagerland Apps · v1.0 · first released 2026-05-22 · last updated 2026-05-22 (dates in DSEG7); other Lagerland apps; shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

Silkscreened legends on the top shell strip ('PRICES', 'SHADOW WEEK', 'HOW IT COUNTS', 'QUESTIONS', 'PRIVACY'; Hanken 500 14px, +0.04em) as anchor links, underlined in silkscreen white on hover and focus. On mobile a 'Menu' shell key opens the list on an LCD panel. The fixed bezel keeps the strip visible. Focus ring: 3px #1C2117 on the LCD and 3px #F4F3EE on the shell.

Motion

LCD physics. Segments turn on and off with an 80ms opacity change and no easing or travel; the count changes digit by digit. Nothing slides or reveals on scroll except the sticky shell strip (200ms). The bezel never moves.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The same fixed cobalt bezel and top strip. The LCD ground carries a calm column: Hanken 400 18px/1.6, 68ch, ink 10:1; page title Hanken 800 44px; dates and figures in DSEG7. Alternatives pages open with a two-reading LCD ('EarnLock: steps' | 'Opal: tap or timer') before the real table, with 'When should I pick X instead' as a plain list. Support is the back label with the email and response time. Privacy opens with the 'No transmitter inside' summary from the transparency row.

Materials

reflective LCD panel: flat grey-green with a faint 2% polarizer gradient, no glow · 7-segment digits over unlit ghost segments · fixed LCD icon segments: 'STEPS', 'MIN', 'KCAL', a lock glyph, a 'PREMIUM' flag (inline SVG) · moulded cobalt ABS shell as a fixed viewport bezel with a 36px outer radius · silkscreen-white legends printed on the shell · sage rubber MODE key and a small recessed RESET key · white adhesive label for the QR · battery-cover back label (maker plate, no-transmitter privacy statement)

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

DSEG7 is the only face that makes the count read as an instrument reading. It has no lowercase letters or '$', so every word, unit and currency sign is in Hanken, as on a real LCD's printed legend. About 60 KB latin.

New assets needed

None. Shell, LCD, segments and keys are CSS and inline SVG; DSEG7 provides digits and ghost segments. Uses the existing icon, screenshots and QR.

Pawza

/apps/pawza/ + its privacy and support pages + 6 comparison pages

What the page must prove: Four things in one viewport. Paper becomes a record: a vet document read into typed fields you confirm, which is the app's own line 'Snap it. Pawza files it.' It happens on the device with no account. It costs 'Free — Pawza Pro from $2.99/mo' and is free for one pet. And the working App Store badge is there, plus the QR on desktop. Warmth for the pet comes from the real records and the dog and cat in the screenshots, not from cartoon paws.

The default page this refuses: A pastel teal-and-orange pet-app landing page: a smiling retriever photo or cartoon dog, a floating phone mockup at right, paw-print confetti, rounded bubbly sans (Nunito/Quicksand), a 'Your pet's health in one place' headline over a badge row, three paw-icon feature cards, star testimonials and three pricing cards.

THE ROLL

Thirteen-Pocket File

The household 13-pocket expanding file in translucent blue polypropylene, sold in every supermarket stationery aisle: a fan of staggered index tabs with white insert labels, a front label panel and an elastic closure. It joins two sources: the developer's journal image of 'the drawer of paper in your kitchen', and the app's own value point 'Snap it. Pawza files it.' The journal's twelve record categories supply the index.

The page is the pet's expanding file. Loose vet paper goes into the front pocket, Pawza reads it and files it behind the right tab, the index tabs are the navigation, and every section is a pocket whose heading tab steps across the page like real cut tabs. It refuses the split-hero phone mockup and the pastel paw-print landing page.

Type
Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 800 (H1 108/96px desktop, 56/52px mobile; prices) and 600 (index-tab labels and section-tab H2s, 17–19px) with Sofia Sans 400/600 (body on paper 18/1.55, typed slips, tables), none; dates and prices are set in Sofia Sans, right-aligned in table columns
Light
A Sunday afternoon at the kitchen table the day after a vet visit: an owner with a creased certificate, a receipt and a prescription label beside a blue plastic expanding file, in flat window daylight. That makes the scheme light: white paper is the reading surface, and the saturated plastic is an object colour, not darkness.
Signature
'File it'. In the Scanning pocket, a sample certificate is set in HTML with the field values from screenshot 2 (Vaccination certificate · 15 May 2026 · Dr. Sarah Chen, DVM · Riverside Animal Hospital · 41.2 kg · next visit due 15 May 2027) and labelled 'Sample document — values from Pawza's App Store screenshots'. A real <button> 'Snap it' starts the sequence. A 2px #FFD23F read-line sweeps the sheet top to bottom (900ms, transform only), and each field it passes gains a yellow underline. A typed white slip then slides out from behind the sheet, listing Title, Date, Veterinarian, Clinic, Weight and Next visit due, each with a real 'Confirm' checkbox (step 4: nothing is saved until you confirm). Once all are ticked, the slip slides down behind the Records tab and 'Reminder set before 15 May 2027' appears under the Reminders tab. Without JS, the certificate and the filled slip render side by side, the checkboxes are plain inputs, and the steps text explains the flow. With reduced motion there is no sweep and nothing slides: 'Snap it' swaps to the filled slip instantly, and a static 'Filed under Records' line replaces the drop.
Remembered as
The pet app whose site was a blue plastic accordion file. The tabs were the menu, and I watched a vet certificate get read, confirmed and dropped behind the Records tab.
Risk
The world reads as admin: it sells order more than love, so the dog and cat photos in the screenshots and the hero copy have to carry the warmth. A saturated blue ground across 14 sections can tire the eye, so every long text must sit on white paper. The tab cascade must keep headings scannable (3 slots on mobile). The sample certificate must never look like a real clinic's document.

App Store route

Page sequence

  1. Front pocket (hero): the tab-row nav; three papers standing in the pocket mouth (the sample certificate with its 'To file' flag); the front label with H1, secondary, price, badge and QR; the typed card with subheadline and pre_headline.
  2. Summary card: quick_answer (speakable) typed on a white ruled index card, 22px at 64ch. The Quick reference <details> is a second card stapled behind it, its summary line always visible.
  3. Scanning pocket: the how_it_works intro and steps 1–6, numbered as a filing procedure (HowTo); the 'File it' demo with the sample certificate; screenshot 2 (Review) in a CSS iPhone lying in the pocket.
  4. Records pocket: the value point 'Snap it. Pawza files it.'; features 1, 2 and 5 as typed sheets of different heights, each title on its visible top edge; screenshots 4 and 1; the journal's twelve record categories as an index list linked to /journal/pet-medical-records-what-to-keep/.
  5. Reminders pocket: value point 2 ('Never miss a shot, dose, or checkup'), feature 3, and screenshot 3 (Overdue / This week / Later).
  6. Weight pocket: feature 4 and screenshot 5.
  7. Photos pocket: feature 6 and screenshot 6.
  8. Vet PDF pocket: screenshot 7 as the one sheet that leaves the file (it rises above its own tab line), feature 7, and the FAQ answer 'Can I share my pet's history with a vet?'.
  9. Household pocket: value point 4, screenshot 8 (Bruno and Luna), and who_for / who_not_for as two typed lists, 'Keep a Pawza file if…' and 'Not the right file if…'.
  10. Privacy pocket: value point 3 and feature 8. transparency.yml as a filing table: network calls none · data leaves the device only to your iCloud, if on · tracking domains 0 · analytics none · third-party SDKs 1 (ZIPFoundation, local archive handling, no network) · account none · permissions Camera, Photo Library, Local notifications · Required Reason APIs 2. Then privacy.notes, the Apple label sentence, and links to /transparency/ and /apps/pawza/privacy/.
  11. Compared pocket: the comparison_table intro; the 4-column table (Pawza · 11pets · PetDesk · Pawprint × 8 rows) on a white sheet; the footnote; six index cards linking /alternatives/11pets/, /petdesk/, /pawprint/, /medika/, /petnoter/ and /vetkeep/.
  12. Plans pocket: one typed price-list sheet with four rows: Free $0; Pro · Monthly $2.99/mo; Pro · Yearly $19.99/yr, carrying the yellow flag '7-day free trial · about 44% cheaper than monthly'; Lifetime $39.99 once ('Best long-term value', Family Sharing). Each row's features open as <details>. Then plans_footnote, price, badge and QR.
  13. Questions pocket: the 13 FAQs as <details>, each summary a white label strip (FAQPage).
  14. Back cover: the About body printed on the inside back cover (19px, 66ch); journal links (pet-medical-records-what-to-keep, vet-paperwork-stays-on-your-phone); the maker line 'Built by Lagerland Apps · first released 6 June 2026 · updated 6 June 2026 · iOS 17.6 or later · 43 languages' (count computed); other Lagerland apps as small tab labels; the closing label (price, badge, QR); the shared Lagerland strip.

Navigation

The index tabs are the nav. The top row holds seven anchor tabs. After the hero it condenses into a sticky 44px row, and the current pocket's tab rises 6px and gets a 3px #FFD23F top edge (IntersectionObserver; static without JS). On mobile, 'Tabs' is a <details> that lists all 13 pockets as stacked white insert labels, plus Privacy policy and Support. Inside the page, each pocket's H2 sits in its own tab on the pocket's top edge. Scrolling goes front-to-back through the file, every pocket at the same scale, and each pocket's tab moves one slot right (6 slots on desktop, 3 on mobile), so the headings descend the page as a real cut-tab cascade. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.

Motion

Pocket physics. Paper only moves vertically, in and out of pockets (translateY, 220–280ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)). Tabs lift 4–6px on hover and when current. There are no fades, no parallax and no entrance cascades: sections are simply there. The strap slides up in 180ms. With reduced motion, every movement becomes an instant state change.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are each a single sheet pulled from the file. Above the sheet is a 120px cobalt band holding the tab row, with a front tab 'Pawza' linking back to /apps/pawza/ and the page's own tab lifted ('Privacy policy', 'Support', 'Pawza vs PetDesk'). The reading column is one white sheet: 68ch, Sofia Sans 400 18/1.6 #14161C, H1 in SSEC 800 56px, H2s in SSEC 700 30px. Tables are filing tables with 1px rules. The alternatives verdict becomes two typed lists, 'Choose Pawza if' and 'Choose PetDesk if'. FAQs are <details>. Support is a contact sheet: the email as one large typed line, and what to include as a checklist. Every page ends with the elastic strap and the badge.

Materials

Cobalt polypropylene pocket faces (flat #2347A6). Stacked back pockets darken to #1A3684 (more layers of plastic), with a 2px #3A5FC0 lip at every pocket mouth. · Index tabs: 148px wide with 10px rounded top corners, stepping one slot right per pocket, each holding a white insert label ruled in 1px ink · White paper (the sample certificate, typed slips, the printed vet PDF): square corners, a 1px #14161C rule, and a 0–2° tilt only where paper stands up out of a pocket · The front label: white with a double 1px rule frame, glued flat on the pocket face · A yellow 'To file' adhesive flag (#FFD23F) on the newest paper · A black woven elastic strap (the sticky bar): #14161C with a faint repeating-linear-gradient weave and a white stitch line

Colour strategy

Drenched · light

Type rationale

Index-tab inserts are narrow strips printed in condensed grotesk. Extra Condensed fits 'Vaccinations' or 'Vet PDF' on a 148px tab at 17px, and at 108px it fills the front label the way a printed label strip fills its tape. Sofia Sans is the same design at normal width, so tabs, labels and papers read as one print job. Four static latin files come to about 64 KB. Verified: @fontsource/sofia-sans-extra-condensed and @fontsource/sofia-sans, weights 100–900.

New assets needed

None. The plastic, tabs, labels, strap and sample certificate are CSS/HTML. It uses the existing icon, screenshots 1–8, assets/qr/pawza.svg and the Apple badge.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

The Vaccination Booklet

The pet vaccination booklet and the vaccination pages of pet-passport-style booklets: a pocket-sized stapled booklet with a ruled grid per page (vaccine and manufacturer · batch no. · date given · valid from · valid until · veterinarian). The vet sticks in the peel-off label from the vaccine vial, presses the clinic's rubber stamp in violet ink and writes the dates in ballpoint. Field labels are printed in several languages because the booklet travels. Generic booklet only: no government emblem, no blue EU cover, no official wording.

The page is the booklet Pawza reads. Each spread is a ruled record page where the vet's stickers, stamp and ballpoint are the 'as written' layer and Pawza's typed fields are the 'as read' layer in the same grid, so the scan is shown in the paper the visitor already owns. It refuses the pet-app phone mockup and the clinical white EHR.

  • #E8EFE6

Type
Encode Sans Expanded 800 (H1 58/60px desktop, 38/40px mobile) and 700 (spread titles 22–28px, prices) with Encode Sans 400/600 (body 18/1.6, typed 'as read' values) with Encode Sans Condensed 600 (multilingual field labels, 11–13px, in narrow grid column heads), Reenie Beanie 400, the vet's ballpoint, only for illustrative handwritten dates in the 'as written' layer. It is always paired with the typed value and aria-hidden.
Light
The front desk of a boarding kennel under flat ceiling fluorescents: the owner flips through the dog's dog-eared booklet because the kennel wants proof of Bordetella. That makes the scheme light: cool, even light on pale green security-tint pages.
Signature
'As written ⇄ As read'. A two-state switch (two real radio inputs styled as paper tabs) sits above the vaccination grid. 'As written' shows the vet's layer: stickers, ballpoint dates and the violet stamp. 'As read' shows Pawza's layer: in every cell a typed value in Encode Sans 600 replaces the ballpoint (Rabies · 7 May 2026 · 7 May 2027 · Dr. Sarah Chen, DVM · Riverside Animal Hospital), each followed by a small violet 'confirmed' tick, and the highlighter becomes the line 'Reminder before 4 Nov 2026'. It is pure CSS (:has() on the radio state): cells cross-dissolve over 160ms, staggered 40ms per row in reading order. Both layers are always in the DOM, and the typed values are the accessible text. Without JS it works unchanged; where :has() is unsupported, the two layers stack in each cell, ballpoint above and typed below. With reduced motion the swap is instant, with no stagger, and the highlighter is static.
Remembered as
The site was the dog's vaccination booklet: stickers, a violet vet stamp, ballpoint dates. One switch turned the scrawl into typed Pawza records.
Risk
This is the familiar route. The booklet is the category's own document, which is why it ranks #1 and also why it is the safe pick: document-as-page is a known editorial move. Overdone, it reads as a government form, so the multilingual labels and stamps must stay sparse. Handwriting fonts look fake at scale, so it stays on dates. It must not resemble the EU pet passport (no emblem, no blue cover, no 'European Union'), and screenshot 7's real vaccine brand must not reach the stickers.

Navigation

The running head is the nav: a 48px cover-green bar, sticky after the hero, with 'Pawza' at left and anchors at right (Vaccinations · How it reads · Treatments · For the vet · Privacy · Fees · Questions). The current spread's link gets a 2px #F3E26B underline. 'Contents' opens a <details> set like the booklet's contents page, listing each section with its folio range. Every spread carries running heads (left 'Pawza · Pet health record', right the section title) and folios at its outer corners. Mobile shows 'Contents' only. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.

Motion

Ink, not paper. Nothing slides, flips or turns pages. The only motion is ink changing state: 160ms cross-dissolves in reading order, the highlighter drawing left to right once (320ms) when the grid first enters view, and the sticky strip sliding up in 180ms. Stamps never 'slam'. With reduced motion, everything is static.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are single booklet pages. A cover-green frame (24px on desktop, 8px on mobile) and a running head ('Pawza · Privacy policy · Datenschutz · Confidentialité') carry the world. The reading column sits on plain #E8EFE6 with no guilloche behind the text: 66ch, Encode Sans 400 18/1.6 #17201B (14:1). H1 is Expanded 800 40px and H2s Expanded 700 24px. Comparison tables are ruled booklet grids with Condensed 600 heads. The 'Honest verdict' pair becomes two ruled columns, 'Choose Pawza if' and 'Choose 11pets if'. FAQs are <details>. Support is a 'Notes' page: the email as a typed line in Expanded 700 24px, and what to include as a ruled checklist. Each page closes with the Get Pawza box.

Materials

Cover board #234536, visible as the frame around every spread (40px on desktop, 8px on mobile) · Security-tint pages #E8EFE6 with fine guilloche line work in #CFDDCF in the outer margins only, never behind text · Ruled grids: 1px ink column rules, 0.5px #CFDDCF row rules, trilingual Condensed heads (Vaccine · Impfstoff · Vaccin; Valid until · Gültig bis · Valable jusqu'au) · Peel-off vial labels: white stickers with a 3px die-cut radius, carrying a generic vaccine name and a 'sample' lot line. No manufacturer names. · A violet rubber clinic stamp (#5B3C94), tilted −4°, its ink slightly uneven via an SVG mask · Ballpoint dates (#2340A0), one yellow highlighter swipe, and two staples in the gutter

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

Encode Sans comes in true expanded, normal and condensed widths of one design, which gives the booklet's three printed voices one family: wide titles as on certificates, condensed trilingual labels squeezed into grid heads, and normal-width text and typed values. Reenie Beanie is a hurried ballpoint scrawl, the exact thing the scan reads. That is its only job. Five static latin files come to about 108 KB. Verified: @fontsource/encode-sans-expanded, encode-sans-condensed and encode-sans (100–900) and reenie-beanie (400).

New assets needed

One small guilloche tile, a hand-drawn SVG line pattern of about 2 KB, as a production task. Until it exists, a plain #E8EFE6 page with #CFDDCF ruling works. Stickers, stamps and ballpoint are HTML/CSS plus Reenie Beanie. Everything else exists: icon, screenshots, QR, badge.

SECOND ROLL

Fresh Snow Trail

Animal-track field guides: Olaus J. Murie's A Field Guide to Animal Tracks (Peterson series, 1954) and Mark Elbroch's Mammal Tracks & Sign (2003). They supply life-size print plates, gait diagrams, and the dog-versus-cat rule (dogs register claw marks; cats walk with claws retracted). These meet the owner's own winter ritual: the dog's first trail across fresh snow. It is the literal reading of the name (paw), taken as reading evidence rather than as a sticker.

The page is one dog's trail across fresh snow. Every print is a dated record, the dashed prints ahead are reminders, and the open snow where nothing walked is the privacy story: every track your pet makes is kept, and nothing tracks you. It refuses the category's cartoon paw-print confetti by turning the paw into field-guide evidence.

  • #F7F9FB
  • #E3EAF1
  • #A9BACD
  • #7A8FA8
  • #12232E
  • #4E6076
  • #D6E83C
Type
Albert Sans 800 (H1 112/104px desktop, tracking −0.025em; 50/48px mobile; section heads 44px; prices) with Albert Sans 400 (body 18/1.6) and 500 (trail labels, dates, nav 14–15px), none
Light
The first walk of a January morning after overnight snow in the park: an owner in gloves, lead in one hand and phone in the other, a low white sun throwing blue shadows into the dog's fresh prints. That makes the scheme light: cold, high-key white.
Signature
'Read the trail'. Every labelled print is a <details> whose summary is the print, the date and the title. Opening one presses the print deeper (its floor shadow darkens over 200ms) and unfolds the record as a note in the snow. The note shows the fields Pawza holds for it, taken from the screenshots (for example 'Annual vaccinations · 7 May 2026 · Rabies, DHPP, Bordetella · Dr. Sarah Chen, DVM · Riverside Animal Hospital'), and how it got there: photographed certificate, read on this iPhone, confirmed by you. Dashed future prints open to the reminder (step 5: one gentle nudge before it's due, never a daily nag). As the visitor scrolls, the lane's prints press in one at a time (scale .94→1 with the shadow deepening, 240ms, once each, via IntersectionObserver). Without JS, native <details> works, every print is drawn already pressed, and the 7 May note is open by default. With reduced motion, prints are static and pressed, notes open without animation, and the ball jumps instead of rolling.
Remembered as
A dog's trail walked across white snow on the page. Every print was a vet record with a date, the dashed prints ahead were reminders, and the privacy part was untouched snow.
Risk
Paw prints are the category's most clichéd motif. Only the field-guide rigour keeps this out of sticker territory: anatomically right pads, claws on the dog and none on the cat, a real trot pattern and dated leader labels. A cold white-and-blue scheme can drift toward the clinical opposite, and a winter scene in July is a seasonal mismatch. The hero proves the scan only through a note, with the screenshot one section down, so it is the weakest of the three at showing 'paper becomes record' above the fold. All trail data is sample data from the screenshots and must stay labelled.

Navigation

The top bar's anchors (Scan · Records · Reminders · Vet PDF · Privacy · Plans · Questions) become a sticky 48px snow bar after the hero. The current stop is marked by the tennis ball under its link, which rolls between links (transform, 240ms). The lane of prints down the page is the visible route, with each section's H2 set beside its print. On mobile, 'Trail' is a <details> list of the stops, each bulleted with a small inline SVG print, plus Privacy policy and Support. Lagerland is linked only from the shared footer strip.

Motion

Pressing, not moving. The only motion is depth: prints deepen as they enter view or open, notes unfold (height 200ms), the ball rolls between nav links (240ms), and the sticky bar rises in 180ms. Nothing slides in from the sides and nothing parallaxes. Falling-snow particles are refused outright. With reduced motion, everything is static.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the six alternatives pages are calm snowfields. A short trail of six small prints walks down the left margin from the top bar's 'Back to Pawza' link to the H1; that is the only world element in the body. The reading column is 68ch, Albert Sans 400 18/1.65 #12232E on #F7F9FB (15:1). H1 is Albert Sans 800 52px and H2s 800 28px. Tables get #E3EAF1 header rows and 1px #A9BACD rules. Alternatives pages set the two 'Choose … if' lists side by side, the FAQ as <details>, and the action row at the end. The privacy page's third-parties section sits on an untrodden band with the transparency.yml facts. Support shows the email in Albert Sans 800 28px and what to include as a list.

Materials

Fresh snow #F7F9FB crossed by broad #E3EAF1 drift bands (low-contrast radial gradients, no blur) · Pressed prints as inline SVG pad clusters: a #7A8FA8 floor, #A9BACD walls and a 1px white sun-side rim. Dog prints have claw nicks; cat prints have none and are rounder. · Hairline leaders (1px #4E6076) from prints to dated labels · Dashed print outlines for prints not yet made (the reminders) · The tennis ball: a 10px #D6E83C disc ringed in ink · Untrodden bands: sections where the trail is absent (privacy)

Colour strategy

Restrained · light

Type rationale

Albert Sans (Usted, 2021) is a geometric grotesk in the Scandinavian-modernist vein. Its open apertures stay crisp in cold, high-key light, and at 800 it is dense enough to hold a white field the way the dark prints do. One family keeps the snowfield quiet, so the prints are the only drama. Three static latin files come to about 36 KB. Verified: @fontsource/albert-sans, weights 100–900.

New assets needed

Two accurate inline SVG print symbols, as a production task: a dog print (four toe pads, heel pad, claw marks) and a cat print (no claws, rounder, three-lobed heel pad), drawn from field-guide references at about 1–2 KB each. Until they exist, a CSS radial-gradient pad cluster stands in. No raster art.
