Page sequence

  1. Console strip + headline + the countdown board ('T-30 Book flights', status lamps, a monitor bay with the real countdown card)
  2. Console shelf: the Quick Answer (speakable), badge, price, QR, and the trust line 'iOS · 0 third-party SDKs · no ads · no account · events stay on your iPhone'
  3. Countdown sequence (#templates): six engraved template keys (TRIP 30D · WEDDING 90D · PREGNANCY 40WK · BIRTHDAY 14D · GRADUATION 21D · MOVE 45D); the selected template prints as a press-kit milestone table (T-time | task) on paper, and the board above follows the row in focus
  4. Countdown procedure (#how-it-works): the how_it_works intro and 6 numbered steps (a real sequence) on paper, each step's T-anchor in B612
  5. What the instrument does: show_body under about_heading, with the four value_points as run-in heads in one paper column
  6. Monitors (#features): 7 portrait monitor bays in a snap-scroll bank, each with an engraved legend (HOME, MOMENTS, EVENT, PLAN, TIMELINE, WIDGETS, SEARCH) and the matching feature text; the widgets bay lists Home / Lock / StandBy and the six styles
  7. Range weather: one paper panel stating that the forecast appears from T-10 via Apple WeatherKit (Premium), using a place name or approximate coordinates only
  8. Go / no-go poll: who_for as 5 GO lines and who_not_for as 3 NO-GO lines, each with its lamp and the word
  9. Range reports: the five Reddit testimonials with initials as a quiet paper list
  10. Manifest (pricing): Free / Premium Monthly / Premium Annual (lamp lit = highlight) / Lifetime as a table with price, billing and contents; the plans_footnote; badge
  11. Launch manifest (roadmap): Flown (2 shipped), NET 2026 Q4 (Apple Watch), NET 2027 H1 (iPad, macOS), Proposed (shared events), where NET means 'no earlier than', matching the 'targets, not commitments' wording; disclaimer
  12. Crew of one (founder): 'Rebuilt from TheWait — by the person who shipped it.' on an engraved nameplate ANTTI AITTAMAA · FINLAND, with bio, signals, response time and mailto
  13. Comparison (#compare-heading-soon): a paper table with an amber key-light rule on Soon.'s column; footnote; badge
  14. Press questions (FAQ, 14 details as Q / A); the Fact sheet = the Quick reference ai-canonical <details>; Flight rules = the transparency facts (0 SDKs, coarse destination only, no account) linking /transparency/, plus privacy policy and support links
  15. Closing: a small board reading 'T-0' with badge + QR; related journal, alternatives_to links, other Lagerland apps (computed), the maker/freshness line as the press kit's issue line; shared footer strip

Navigation

Engraved keys in the console strip: PLAN MODE, MONITORS, MANIFEST, FACT SHEET, DOWNLOAD. They are rectangular keys with B612 caps legends, and the current section's key is lit amber with ink. Mobile: a 'Keys' button opens a details panel of the same keys, each 48px tall. Focus: a 3px #FFB21E ring with a 2px #0F1110 inner rule, matching a lit key.

Motion

Procedural and discrete: values swap and nothing glides. Lamp digits cross-fade over 120ms, keys depress 1px for 80ms, and lamps switch on instantly. The only other motion is a 150ms fade-in on the sticky remote clock.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages keep the console strip, then a short black board as masthead showing the page's name in B612 caps (e.g. 'DAYS MATTER ALTERNATIVE') with a lamp line. The body is press-kit paper (#F6F7F8) in Public Sans 18px/1.65 at 66ch. Tables have B612 heads over paper rows. The privacy policy appears as numbered 'flight rules' sections under its real headings (overview, data collection, storage, third parties, children, changes). The support page is one console panel with the email and the response-time line. Alternatives pages end on the shelf with badge, price and QR.

pale blue-grey painted console steel (#D3DAE2) as the ground, with 1px darker panel seams and four corner screws per panel drawn in CSS · one matte-black countdown board carrying lamp-digit numerals (Doto) and a white B612 task line · engraved rectangular keys (1px inset light/dark edges, B612 caps legends) for navigation and template selection, with the selected key lit amber · GO / NO-GO status lamps: round 12px lamps always paired with the words · press-kit paper sheets (#F6F7F8) for tables, FAQ and the fact sheet · portrait monitor bays (black, 18px radius) holding the real screenshots

A lamp grid for numbers, an instrument face for legends and a civic text face for reading: three jobs, each face doing one. About 64 KB: Doto 700 ≈ 4 KB, B612 400/700 ≈ 32 KB, Public Sans 400/600 ≈ 28 KB.

New assets needed

None new. A crop of screenshot 3's photo card for the hero monitor bay comes from the existing PNG; the board, keys, lamps and screws are all CSS.

Or the category standard, played straight: a pastel-gradient hero with a tilted iPhone and stacked widgets beside 'Never miss a moment', a live DD:HH:MM:SS demo timer, a row of four icon feature cards (Widgets · Weather · Checklists · Privacy), three pricing cards with 'Most popular', a star strip and an FAQ accordion.

AppMeta

/apps/appmeta/ + its privacy and support pages + 1 comparison page

What the page must prove: In one viewport: this is a native Mac app (macOS 14+) for App Store Connect. It holds every locale side by side inside Apple's character limits and shows each change before it reaches Apple, demonstrated with real metadata rather than claimed. Keys stay in Keychain, and it talks only to Apple (plus an AI provider you choose). The real price: a free download with demo mode, then $17.99/year or $29.99 lifetime. A working install path: the official badge, and on a phone a way to send the page to the Mac.

The default page this refuses: The dark Mac dev-tool landing page in the Raycast/Linear school: an indigo-violet gradient mesh lifted from the icon, a floating macOS window screenshot with a glow, a 'Download on the Mac App Store' button, an SF-Symbol feature grid, a green-check comparison table and two pricing cards. Its cousin is the terminal-green CLI look used for anything near Fastlane.

Today's page, for comparison
Picked
AppMetaFinlandica

App Store Connect. Finally native.

App Store Connect, native on your Mac.

THE ROLL

One Box Per Letter

Comb-field forms in drop-out ink. On OCR forms the boxes and labels are printed in red drop-out ink so the scanner reads only the black entries (the IRS 'Copy A' convention). Tax returns and landing cards use one box per character. Finland's bilingual Finnish/Swedish official forms carry the printed correction rule: strike through, write the correct entry above, initial.

The page is a form whose boxes are Apple's real field limits (30 for name, 30 for subtitle, 100 for keywords), printed in drop-out red, with AppMeta's own metadata typed in black. The character budget, the correction (the diff) and the signed declaration (the push) are its working parts. It refuses the dark dev-tool landing page with a floating Mac window.

  • #FDFDFB
  • #E0352B
  • #B8211A
  • #FCE9E6
  • #16161A
  • #5E5E63
Type
Finlandica 700 (@fontsource/finlandica, 11.7 KB): H1 at 92px/0.98 desktop and 44px mobile; H2 part bands at 30px, white on form red with Finlandica 400 (11.4 KB): body 18px/1.55 at 64ch; labels at 14px in 700, Courier Prime 400/700 (18.6 + 19.3 KB), used only for typed entries inside comb fields and their counts ('29/30'). This is real character-counted data at one glyph per box, and AppMeta's own field editors are monospaced too.
Light
An indie developer at the Mac in office daylight during ship week, filling the same fields for the twelfth locale. White bond paper, one scheme (color-scheme: light).
Signature
'Try the Subtitle field'. A real <input> styled as a 30-box comb: Courier Prime, letter-spacing matched to a repeating-linear-gradient box grid, placeholder 'App Store Connect, done right', and aria-describedby pointing at the count. The HTML ships maxlength=30; about 30 lines of JS raise it to 40, update the typed count ('29/30') and set a CSS variable that tints the overflow boxes. Past 30 it prints 'Over by 8: App Store Connect will not accept this. AppMeta flags it before you push.' Nothing is submitted or sent. No-JS: the comb still takes typing up to 30 characters, and the static 7/30 and 29/30 rows carry the point. Reduced motion: there is no motion to remove; colour changes are instant.
Remembered as
The AppMeta page was a red tax-style form. Its subtitle filled 29 of 30 boxes, and when I typed my own subtitle in, the boxes went red at 31.
Risk
Forms carry friction: the page could read as more paperwork rather than relief, and full-commitment red on white can tip into alarm. Red must stay apparatus and never mean 'error'; the black typed data carries the warmth. Combs must be pin-sharp at every size, because a sloppy box grid kills the idea. The mobile comb wrap (15 boxes per row) needs careful tuning so words do not break unreadably.

App Store route

The badge sits in the 'For office use only: Apple' panel, the one part of a form the applicant never fills in. It is Apple's artwork, untouched, on a white mount, 56px on desktop and 48px on mobile. The price statement is printed tick lines from price.value and plans, never interactive checkboxes. The QR (96px) sits at the panel foot on ≥1024px only, since a Mac app needs it less. On phones it is replaced by 'Send this page to your Mac'. The sticky bar is the perforated return slip: a 64px bond strip with a dashed scarlet perforation along its top edge, reading 'AppMeta: App Store Connect for Mac · Free download · $17.99/yr or $29.99 once', with the badge at 40px. It rises from the bottom when the panel badge leaves view (IntersectionObserver); without JS it never appears and the static badges remain. The closing 'Declaration' part repeats the badge beside a signature line. Smart App Banner meta stays in head.

  19. Part 'Issued by': founder (Organization) heading, story, signals, response time and external link (count computed), plus the freshness line 'Built by Lagerland Apps · first released 1 Feb 2026 · updated 13 May 2026'
  20. Part 'Notes on completing this form': FAQ ×16 as details/summary
  21. 'Summary of entries' box: the Quick reference ai-canonical <details>, open and visible
  22. 'See also': the three related journal posts and related apps (AppMeta Pulse, Mockly)
  23. Declaration: a typed declaration line, signature rule, badge, price and QR
  24. Shared 'A Lagerland app' footer strip

Navigation

The form head carries the parts index as red underlined Finlandica 600 links (Fields · Corrections · Locales · Procedure · Fees · Notes), each pointing to a part-band id. On mobile a text button labelled 'Parts' (no hamburger glyph) opens the same list as a full-width ruled column under the head. Every part band ends at right with 'Back to top of form'. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.

Motion

Paper holds still. Entries are present on load with no typing animation, so content is never hidden. Comb boxes darken their stroke on hover and focus (no movement). The return slip slides up 64px in 160ms ease-out when it first appears. Anchor jumps scroll smoothly. Reduced motion removes the slide and the smooth scroll. No scroll reveals.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy becomes a 'Data protection notice' form: the same head and red part bands, with a calm reading column of Finlandica 400 18px black on bond white at 66ch for overview, collection, storage, third parties, children and changes. Above it, typed fact boxes ('Data collected: none', 'Tracking: no', 'Account: your own ASC API key') link to the transparency row. Support becomes a 'Request for assistance' form: a mailto link whose prefilled body lists what to include (app version, macOS version, what happened), the response time, and no web form that collects anything. /alternatives/app-store-connect-web/ becomes a 'Comparison of forms': a two-column ruled table (AppMeta vs ASC web on speed, localisation, safety, credentials), the 'Pick AppMeta if' and 'Stick with ASC web if' lists as tick lists, FAQ notes, and a closing declaration with the badge.

Materials

Comb fields: one typed glyph per box, with boxes drawn by a repeating-linear-gradient sized to the mono advance (pure CSS) · A 1px scarlet hairline grid on a 12-column sheet inside a 2px scarlet outer frame · Part bands: reversed white Finlandica 700 caps on form red, named and never numbered · Shaded 'For office use only: Apple' panels in drop-out tint · Typed corrections: the entry struck with a 2px black line, the correction typed above, an initials box beside it · Drawn tick boxes (CSS squares) with typed 'X' marks, which are print and never interactive checkboxes · Signature and date rules for the declaration · Screenshots mounted as 'Attachment 1–4' sheets, each with a red label strip

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

Finlandica is Helsinki Type Studio's 2021 grotesk for Finland's country brand. Its crossed 7 comes from Nordic handwriting, and its narrow proportions fit labels into tight boxes, so it reads as the Finnish public form this Finnish studio actually fills in. No sibling world uses it. Courier Prime is the typewriter that filled forms before the web, and mono appears only where each character occupies one counted box. About 61 KB in total.

New assets needed

None new: it runs on the icon, the four landscape screenshots, the QR and 11.png's real entry text. Recommended production task: Apple's official 'Download on the Mac App Store' badge artwork to replace the iOS badge on Mac-only pages.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

Passed for Press

The prepress proof. Linotype and Monotype galley proofs were marked with standard proofreaders' marks (BS 5261-2 / Chicago Manual of Style: caret, delete, stet, transpose, the 'Qy' query). The Dylux blueline was the final contact proof, printed entirely in one blue, which the client signed 'OK to print' before plates were made.

The page is one long galley proof of AppMeta's own App Store copy, printed in blueline blue, with its changes marked in the margins and a sign-off box that is the download. 'See every change before it goes to Apple' becomes the way the page is read rather than a feature bullet. It refuses the dark landing page with a glowing window screenshot.

  • #E8EDF7
  • #17337A
  • #2E4A94
  • #9FB0D8
  • #1B1B1B
  • #FFFFFF
Type
Charis SIL 700 (@fontsource/charis-sil, 22.3 KB): H1 at 104px/0.98 desktop and 46px mobile; H2 at 40px; margin side-heads at 17px with Charis SIL 400 (22.6 KB): galley text 19px/1.6 at 66ch; 400 italic (23.8 KB) only for the short marginal instructions in black ('11 inserted', 'dup. stem'), None. Counts and limits use Charis lining figures; there is no mono.
Light
A developer at the Mac the afternoon before a release, checking the last proof before anything goes to Apple: a blueline sheet under even daylight. One light scheme (color-scheme: light), with the ground tinted blue so the page reads drenched rather than white.
Signature
'Show marks / As printed'. One toggle switches every marked galley between the marked proof and the clean printed line, mirroring AppMeta's diff preview against the pushed state: <del> collapses, <ins> drops into the line in blue type, and the marks and marginal notes fade. A small class toggle in JS keeps state in the URL hash. No-JS: the marked proof shows, and each marked passage is followed by its server-rendered 'As printed' line, so both states are in the HTML. Reduced motion: the swap is instant, with no fade and no mark drawing.
Remembered as
The AppMeta page was one long blue proof sheet with pencil marks. The 11 new locales were marked in like corrections, and the download was a box that said 'OK to print'.
Risk
Honest familiarity: a paper proof sits close to the print/editorial register AI pages drift toward. It avoids italic display and mono labels, but a weak build becomes a blue blog post. An all-blue page can feel cold and monotonous, and the screenshots are its only colour. Many developers do not know proof marks, so every mark needs a plain-language note beside it.

Navigation

The job docket carries the contents (Locales · Fields · Price · Queries) as underlined blue Charis links, with the 'Show marks / As printed' toggle beside them. Margin side-heads label every section, and each section ends with 'Back to the head of the galley'. On mobile a 'Contents' text button opens the list under the docket, and side-heads move inline above their paragraphs at 17px 700.

Motion

Only the pencil moves. When a marked passage first enters view, its SVG marks draw on (stroke-dashoffset, 400ms, staggered 60ms) under html.js; the text never moves and is visible throughout. The toggle cross-fades marks in 200ms. The slug strip slides up in 160ms. Reduced motion shows the marks already drawn and makes every swap instant. No scroll reveals of text.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy and support pages are 'Imprint' galleys: the same blue sheet and docket, and a calm reading column of 66ch Charis 400 19px blue on the tinted sheet (10:1) with side-heads in the margin. They carry no proof marks except one stamp, 'Data collected: none', linking to /transparency/#appmeta. Support is 'Queries to the printer': a mailto link with prefilled subject and body, plus the response time. /alternatives/app-store-connect-web/ is a two-proof comparison: AppMeta and the ASC web UI as facing columns on the galley (stacked on mobile) with the differences marked, the FAQ set as queries, and the sign-off box with the badge.

Materials

One galley strip: a 680px text column running the full page length, with pale-blue galley edges and crop marks at the sheet corners · Proofreaders' marks as hand-drawn inline SVG in grease-pencil black (caret, delete loop, stet dots, transpose curve), with the matching marginal instruction aligned to the marked line · <del>/<ins> semantics on every marked change: black strike over blue type, inserted words written above a caret · The sign-off box: a 2px black stamp rectangle with three options ('OK to print' ticked, 'OK with corrections', 'Revised proof'), holding the badge · Tipped-in colour proofs: the four screenshots in true colour on white mounts with two pale tape strips (CSS), the only full-colour objects on the sheet · Margin side-heads instead of headings stacked over text, and a 2px halftone dot tint for shaded boxes

Colour strategy

Drenched · light

Type rationale

Charis SIL is SIL's open extension of Bitstream Charter, which Matthew Carter drew in 1987 to stay crisp on the 300-dpi laser printers that ran off proofs. macOS bundles Charter, so @font-face lists local('Charter') before the self-hosted file and Mac visitors download nothing, a fitting answer to 'Finally native'. Its sturdy, low-contrast serifs and the rule of no italic at display size keep it out of the high-contrast editorial cluster. About 69 KB in total, near zero on a Mac.

New assets needed

None. The marks are hand-coded inline SVG paths, and the page runs on the existing icon, screenshots and QR. Recommended: Apple's 'Download on the Mac App Store' badge artwork.

SECOND ROLL

The Fifty-Language Leaflet

The multilingual instruction leaflet folded into every boxed device. Its cover carries a language index of reversed code tabs ('EN · DA · DE · ES · FI · FR …'), and the same text repeats per language under each tab. It is set in a wide-coverage sans on thin 40–60 gsm paper where the reverse shows through, with a specifications table, a 'not included' line and the manufacturer block on the back panel.

An App Store listing is a fifty-language leaflet, and AppMeta edits every panel side by side. So the page opens on the full index of the 50 ASC locale codes as both its navigation and its proof, with three real panels of one release note next to each other. It refuses the single-window screenshot hero.

Type
Noto Sans variable (@fontsource-variable/noto-sans, one latin wdth+wght file of 60 KB). H1 at wdth 75 / wght 800, 72px/1.0 desktop and 42px mobile; code tabs at wdth 62.5 / wght 800, 20px white on black with Noto Sans at wdth 100, wght 400/600: body 18px/1.55 at 66ch; tabular figures (tnum) for character counts, None. A single variable file covers condensed tabs and text. Endonyms in non-Latin scripts (বাংলা, ગુજરાતી, தமிழ், اردو, 日本語) use the visitor's system script fonts.
Light
The developer at the Mac in daylight, unfolding a release in every language at once: thin printed paper on a desk. One light scheme (color-scheme: light).
Signature
'The language index'. Tapping, hovering or focusing any of the 50 code tabs fills a single card under the grid with that locale's English name, its endonym in its own script, and whether Apple added it in 2026. All of this is real data, server-rendered in the Languages panel, which JS clones into the card. No-JS: each tab is an anchor to its Languages row, and :target highlights the row in violet. Reduced motion: the card swaps instantly.
Remembered as
The AppMeta page opened on a grid of fifty little black language tabs with eleven in purple, and three real release notes side by side, like the leaflet in a new phone box.
Risk
Fifty reversed tabs can read as a heavy wall of codes, though this audience lives in these codes. The instruction-leaflet register risks feeling like a manual rather than a pitch, so the cover panel has to sell. Endonyms depend on system script fonts. The real multi-locale text is GymLogger X's, not AppMeta's own, and must be labelled plainly. All three rolled worlds are paper, so this one leans on its index topology and the app's own violet to stand apart.

Navigation

The leaflet's own index is the navigation. The header carries Contents links named after the panels. Motion

Folds never animate. Only the tabs respond: on hover or focus a tab lifts 2px and inverts in 120ms. The index card cross-fades in 150ms, and the folded-edge strip slides up in 160ms. Reduced motion removes the lift and makes swaps instant. No scroll reveals.

Noto exists to set every script without tofu, the very problem 50 locales pose. It is also the real voice of multilingual inserts, and its width axis gives the leaflet's cramped condensed codes and its readable body from one 60 KB file. No sibling world uses it.

Or the category standard, played straight: the dark Mac dev-tool landing page played straight. AppMeta Pulse

/apps/appmeta-pulse/ + its privacy and support pages + 3 comparison pages

What the page must prove: In one viewport: what it shows (portfolio proceeds, subscriptions, refunds and downloads in Apple's terms, at a glance); that it cannot change anything in App Store Connect except review replies you send; that nothing is collected and queries go straight to Apple; the real price (free trial, from $0.99/mo, $8.99/yr, $17.99 lifetime); and a working install path (the official badge, plus the QR on desktop).

The default page this refuses: A dark indigo-to-black SaaS analytics landing page: glowing cyan-violet line chart, floating iPhone showing the dashboard, KPI tiles (big number over a small label), feature card grid, three equal pricing cards, testimonial carousel. In effect the app icon's palette blown up to page scale, the AppStats / Appfigures / RevenueCat marketing pattern.

Today's page, for comparison
Picked
AppMeta PulseB612

The fast, calm App Store Connect dashboard.

The monitoring-first App Store Connect dashboard for indie iOS developers.

THE ROLL

Seven-Day Chart

Short & Mason and Negretti & Zambra seven-day barograph charts, and Esterline Angus / Leeds & Northrup strip-chart recorders: printed blue rulings, day divisions, violet aniline pen ink, a red event pen, and the printed label block in the chart's corner.

The page is one roll of recorder chart paper fed past a fixed pen. A week of portfolio proceeds is traced in violet against last week in graphite, recorded by an instrument whose label block reads 'Controls: none'. It refuses the dark gradient dashboard of floating KPI tiles.

  • #F2F6F4
  • #B9CFE3
  • #2D5B8C
  • #5A2D9C
  • #5F6670
  • #C23A2B
  • #18212E
Type
B612 700, plus 400 for printed legends (@fontsource/b612; latin 400+700 about 34 KB) with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400/500/700 (@fontsource-variable/atkinson-hyperlegible-next, wght file about 34 KB), B612 Mono 400 (@fontsource/b612-mono, about 19 KB), used only for real readings: daily figures, value-scale numerals, endpoint paths
Light
An indie developer at a kitchen table or café counter in 7 to 9 am daylight, phone in hand, reading what Apple published overnight. That means light chart paper, one scheme (color-scheme: light).
Signature
Read the pen, a reading cursor. Each day band is a focusable row; arrow keys move between rows. Hover, tap or focus draws a 1px violet hairline across both traces and prints that day's reading and the same day last week in the left margin (about 40 lines of vanilla JS reading data attributes that mirror the server-rendered table). Without JS, the readings column is a real <table> printed beside the bands, so every value is visible. With reduced motion, the cursor jumps without easing and the trace is already inked.
Remembered as
A page made of chart paper: a violet pen line tracing a week of App Store proceeds against last week's grey line, a label block that said 'Controls: none', and the download badge riding on the pen carriage.
Risk
If the label block and the two traces are weak, chart paper reads as generic graph paper or an engineering costume. Time running down the page is unfamiliar, and the illustrative week could be mistaken for live data, so the labels must be explicit. The grid behind type has to be suppressed under every text column to hold contrast.
Full style card

First viewport, desktop

1440x900. Top 48px is the chart's printed edge: 'AppMeta Pulse' in B612 700 18px chart-blue at x 120; anchor links Record · Wiring · Price · Questions · Privacy in B612 400 14px at right. Chart-paper grid full-bleed behind everything, with the rulings suppressed to paper under every text block. y 88–250: H1 'The fast, calm App Store Connect dashboard.' in B612 700 80px/0.98 body ink, two lines across x 120–1180. y 262–320: hero.subheadline in Atkinson 21px, 62ch. y 340–480: the label block, a 2px chart-blue ruled box from x 120 to 1320 split into cells: FOR (pre_headline) · RECORDS (proceeds, units, subscriptions, trials, refunds, downloads) · CONTROLS (none for builds, pricing or metadata; writes only the review replies you send) · PRICE ('Free trial — from $0.99/mo · $17.99 lifetime', figures in B612 Mono) · the official black App Store badge at 48px · QR at 104px captioned 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. y 505–900: the record. A pen line labelled 'Data up to 6 Feb · illustrative week traced from the app's screenshots' sits above seven 54px day bands running downward, newest under the pen. The left 240px of each band prints the day and its rounded reading in B612 Mono. x 400–1180 is the Proceeds channel on a printed €0–200 scale, with the violet trace (this week) and graphite trace (previous week). x 1220–1320 is the event channel, with violet new-subscription ticks and red refund ticks. Beside the pen: '992,55 € vs 909,21 € · +9.2%'. No phone mockup in the first viewport.

First viewport, phone

390x844, 16px gutters. A 44px printed edge holds the wordmark and an 'Index' button. H1 in B612 700 40px/1.02 runs 3–4 lines. The first sentence of hero.subheadline follows at 17px. The label block is stacked as ruled rows: FOR, CONTROLS (none for builds, pricing or metadata), PRICE ('Free trial — from $0.99/mo · $17.99 lifetime'), then a full-width cell with the official badge at 44px tall, around y 560–620. RECORDS sits under the badge. No QR. At y 700–844 the pen line and the first two day bands of the record appear: readings at left, a 200px trace channel, a 20px event channel.

App Store route

The official black App Store badge has its own cell in the chart's label block, next to the price cell, and is never redrawn. Desktop adds assets/qr/appmeta-pulse.svg in the next cell, captioned 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. The sticky bar is the pen carriage: once the label-block badge leaves the viewport, a 56px ruled band slides in (top on desktop, bottom on mobile; chart-blue rules on paper) holding a drawn violet nib, 'From $0.99/mo · $17.99 lifetime' in B612 Mono, and the badge at 36px. The price statement comes only from price.value and plans. The Price section and the end of the chart repeat badge and QR. Smart App Banner meta stays in head and sits above the chart's top edge on iOS.

Page sequence

  1. Printed top edge: wordmark and anchor links
  2. Header band: H1 (hero.headline) and hero.subheadline
  3. Label block: FOR (hero.pre_headline, set as a form field, not an eyebrow) · RECORDS · CONTROLS · PRICE (price.value, plus Lifetime from plans) · official badge · desktop QR
  4. The week's record: seven day bands, violet this week against graphite previous week, a readings <table>, '992,55 € vs 909,21 € · +9.2%', refund and new-sub ticks, captioned as illustrative from 1.png and 5.png
  5. Operator's note: quick_answer in a ruled note panel (speakable), with hero.secondary as its closing line
  6. Wiring: value_points 'Monitoring by design' and body paragraph 3 as the instrument's wiring list. Reads (GET salesReports, subscription reports, analytics, catalog, reviews); the two writes (customerReviewResponses when you send, analyticsReportRequests); not wired (builds, pricing, metadata, TestFlight). Endpoints in B612 Mono, linked to /apps/appmeta-pulse/api-access/
  7. Event marks: the other three value_points as red-ticked annotations along the strip
  8. What each pen records: Apple's vocabulary legend (proceeds, sales, units, refunds, active subscriptions, trial conversions, cancellations) from body paragraph 4 and the sales-vs-proceeds FAQ
  9. Screens: six screenshots in thin iPhone bezels on a horizontal scroll-snap strip, captions in B612
  10. Channels: features x6 as a ruled legend table (channel | what it records)
  11. Range: who_for and who_not_for as two ruled columns, Suits / Doesn't suit, keeping the link to AppMeta
  12. Price: plans as three ruled rows (Free trial $0; Pro $0.99 mo · $8.99 yr; Lifetime $17.99 one-time, bracketed in violet 'Best long-term value'), plans_footnote in small print, badge and QR
  13. Why AppMeta Pulse exists: the show_body essay in a 66ch unruled reading column
  14. Maker's imprint: founder block (Organization, Lagerland Apps, Finland) with heading, bio, signals, response_time, external_link
  15. Other instruments: alternatives_to. AppStats, App Sales — Store Reports and Appfigures link to their /alternatives/ pages with one honest trade-off each; the App Store Connect app and RevenueCat appear as plain mentions
  16. Operator's log: FAQ x13 as ruled details/summary lines
  17. Privacy record: data_collection none, tracking false, no account, notes x6, and the transparency row's network-call list, linked to /transparency/, the privacy policy and support
  18. Further reading (the two journal posts) and Also from Lagerland (AppMeta, Mockly)
  19. End of chart: closing badge, QR and price; the Quick reference <details> (ai-canonical) as a spec sheet; the freshness line 'Built by Lagerland Apps · updated 25 Mar 2026 · first released 1 Feb 2026'
  20. Shared 'A Lagerland app' footer strip

Navigation

Nav lives on the chart's printed top edge: wordmark plus five anchor links in B612. On mobile an 'Index' button opens the chart legend as a ruled list. From 1100px wide, the right-edge event channel doubles as the jump nav (jump_nav: true): every section has a red event tick with its printed name, and the tick for the section in view turns violet. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.

Motion

Ink, not glide. On first view the violet trace inks downward from the pen once (SVG stroke-dashoffset, 900ms, linear). Event ticks appear in place with an opacity step and no movement. The pen carriage travels 8px into place in 160ms. Nothing fades in on scroll, and no counters run. With prefers-reduced-motion, everything is pre-inked and the carriage appears without travel.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support, the /api-access/ methodology page and the three alternatives pages keep the printed top edge, with a label block as the page header (Title · App · Last updated · back to /apps/appmeta-pulse/). Rulings recede to the margins; a 68ch unruled paper column carries Atkinson 18px/1.6 body-ink text, with H2s in B612 700 chart-blue. Privacy data lists are set as a printed legend table. Alternatives pages show the head-to-head as a two-pen record: one row per fact (monthly, yearly, lifetime, what the privacy label declares, notifications/widgets, platforms), with AppMeta Pulse in violet ink and the competitor in graphite, followed by 'Pick … if' columns and the FAQ as the operator's log. The support page is a label block with email, response time and a ruled 'what to include' checklist.

Materials

Recorder chart paper: CSS repeating-linear-gradient rulings (fine every 8px, heavy every 40px), with day bands as heavy horizontal rules and printed day labels in the left margin · Violet pen trace (this week) and graphite trace (previous week) as inline SVG polylines that step once per day, because Apple reports daily · Red event-pen ticks in a 24px right-edge channel marking each section start · The chart's printed label block: a ruled box of cells headed For / Records / Controls / Price · Pen carriage: a fixed ruled band carrying a drawn violet nib, used as the sticky download bar · Thin iPhone bezels for the six screenshots laid on the strip

Colour strategy

Full palette · light

Type rationale

B612 is Airbus and Intactile's cockpit display face, drawn so instrument values can be read at a glance. It is the chart's printed-legend voice and sets every headline. Atkinson Next shares its open, unambiguous counters, which keeps the FAQ and essay calm. The mono appears only where the content is real measurement or code. Total is about 87 KB, with no italic serif and no mono costume.

New assets needed

None. The grid is CSS. Traces are inline SVG from illustrative values traced off 1.png and 5.png and labelled as such. The nib is a three-path inline SVG. Existing screenshots, icon and QR cover the rest.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

The Morning Listings

The newspaper markets section read at breakfast: WSJ 'Money & Investing' and FT share-price service listings, agate stock tables with their 'How to read the tables' key, boxed Reader Services and subscription-rates panels, and the reader's yellow highlighter.

The page is the morning markets page, and your apps are the listed holdings. Yesterday's figures sit in agate tables, Apple's vocabulary is the key to the tables, and the download lives in the Reader Services box. It refuses the dark KPI-tile dashboard and its floating phone.

  • #E6E5E0
  • #F3F2EE
  • #151515
  • #5B5B57
  • #F2E94E
  • #9C9A92
Type
League Gothic 400, variable wdth 75–100 (@fontsource-variable/league-gothic, about 19 KB) with Libre Franklin 400/600/800 (@fontsource-variable/libre-franklin, about 29 KB) with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums for agate tables, None. Agate tables and endpoint paths use Libre Franklin tabular figures.
Light
Breakfast at the kitchen table in daylight: the developer reads what closed yesterday the way a holder reads share prices. That means light newsprint, one scheme (color-scheme: light).
Signature
Read the key: cross-highlighting between the 'How to read these tables' key and the listings. Each key term links to its column or row id. Tapping, hovering or focusing a term swipes the highlighter across the term and the matching table column (vanilla JS toggles a class; a CSS background-size swipe runs 220ms). Without JS, the links jump by fragment and CSS :target highlights the column header and the definition. With reduced motion, the highlight fills instantly.
Remembered as
It was a morning newspaper's market page: my apps were the listings, the key at the bottom explained proceeds vs sales, and the download sat in a yellow-highlighted subscription box.
Risk
This is the most familiar of the three: newspaper and editorial layouts are a frequent 'creative' answer and sit next to the broadsheet-editorial cluster. It has to stay sans and roman, with the highlighter used only for real marks. The studio's own Read world may also go editorial, which would blur this microsite's identity. Dense agate tables are tiring on a phone. The stock-market framing must never imply investment returns, so every column is labelled in Apple's terms.
Full style card

First viewport, desktop

1440x900. Section flag band at y 0–76: 'AppMeta Pulse' in League Gothic 56px ink at left; dateline 'Data up to yesterday · from Apple's App Store Connect API' in Libre Franklin 13px grey at centre; the Inside index links at right; then the 4px plus 1px double rule. Banner at y 100–330: H1 'The fast, calm App Store Connect dashboard.' in League Gothic 120px/0.92 across all 12 columns, two lines. Three zones at y 360–900. Columns 1–3: the standfirst (hero.subheadline, Libre Franklin 19px), then 'In brief' (quick_answer, speakable) at 16px. Columns 4–9: the listings table 'Your portfolio, yesterday', with five illustrative rows from 2.png (DriftLines, GymLogger X, Taskful Day, TheWait, WanderWiki) in proceeds · downloads · 7-day € columns as the app shows them; the total row '992,55 € · +9.2% vs previous 7 days' is highlighted, captioned 'Illustrative listing — figures as shown in the app's App Store screenshots'. Columns 10–12: the Reader Services box on halftone, with H2 'Get AppMeta Pulse', the official badge at 48px, the QR at 120px captioned 'Scan with your iPhone camera', rates in agate (Free trial · $0.99 a month · $8.99 a year · $17.99 lifetime) with the 'from $0.99/mo' line highlighted, and 'iPhone · iPad · Mac'.

First viewport, phone

390x844, 16px gutters. A 56px flag: 'AppMeta Pulse' in League Gothic 32px and an 'Inside' button, then the double rule. H1 in League Gothic 56px/0.95, three lines. The first sentence of hero.subheadline in Libre Franklin 17px. A full-width Reader Services box on halftone: the official badge at 48px, the highlighted line 'Free trial — from $0.99/mo · $17.99 lifetime', and 'iPhone · iPad · Mac'. App Store route

The Reader Services box (halftone tint, 1px ink border) is the action: the official badge untouched, the desktop QR, rates taken from price.value and plans, with the subscription line highlighted. The sticky bar is a folded flag strip: a 56px newsprint band with the double rule, 'AppMeta Pulse — from $0.99/mo · $17.99 lifetime' and the badge at 36px. It appears when the Reader Services badge leaves view (bottom on mobile, top on desktop). The Subscription rates box later carries all three plans, and a closing Reader Services box repeats badge and QR. Smart App Banner meta stays in head.

Page sequence

  1. Section flag: 'AppMeta Pulse', dateline, Inside index, double rule
  2. Banner: H1 hero.headline across all 12 columns
  3. Standfirst (hero.subheadline) and 'In brief' (quick_answer, speakable)
  4. Listings: 'Your portfolio, yesterday', an illustrative agate table from 2.png with the highlighted total 992,55 € · +9.2% (from 1.png and 5.png)
  5. Reader Services box: badge, desktop QR, rates, platforms
  6. Lead story 'No buttons that can break anything': value_points 'Monitoring by design' and body paragraph 3, with a sidebar table 'What it calls' (reads / the two writes / never called) linking to /apps/appmeta-pulse/api-access/
  7. Briefs: the other three value_points as run-in briefs in one column, with hero.secondary as the lead brief
  8. Photos: six screenshots as captioned photos across three columns (a swipe row on mobile)
  9. How to read these tables: Apple's vocabulary key (proceeds, sales, units, refunds, active subscriptions, trial conversions, cancellations), each term linked to its listing column
  10. What's covered: features x6 as a two-column agate list with bold run-in heads
  11. Who it suits / Who it doesn't: who_for and who_not_for in two columns
  12. Subscription rates: plans as an agate rates table, with the Lifetime row highlighted 'Best long-term value' and plans_footnote as fine print
  13. Comparable listings: alternatives_to as a table. AppStats, App Sales — Store Reports and Appfigures link to /alternatives/ with each page's real prices and privacy-label facts; the App Store Connect app and RevenueCat appear as unlinked rows
  14. Column: 'Why AppMeta Pulse exists.' (show_body essay) with the byline Lagerland Apps, plus a founder bio box (Organization) with signals and response time
  15. Letters: FAQ x13 as question-and-answer disclosures
  16. Disclosures: privacy block and transparency row, with links to the privacy policy, support and /transparency/
  17. Fact box: the Quick reference <details> (ai-canonical) styled as a company-profile box; folio freshness line (Built by Lagerland Apps · updated 25 Mar 2026 · first released 1 Feb 2026)
  18. Further reading (the journal posts) and related listings (AppMeta, Mockly)
  19. Closing Reader Services box: badge, QR, rates
  20. Shared 'A Lagerland app' footer strip

Navigation

An 'Inside' index sits in the flag like a front-page index box: Listings · Key · Rates · Disclosures · Letters · Column. On mobile, the 'Inside' button opens it as an agate list under the flag. A folio line at the foot of each section ('AppMeta Pulse · Listings') doubles as a back-to-top link. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.

Motion

Print holds still; only the highlighter moves. It swipes left to right (background-size 0 to 100%, 220ms ease-out) on hover, focus or :target, and the sticky flag strip drops 6px in 140ms. No scroll reveals and no counters, because the numbers are printed. With prefers-reduced-motion, swipes become instant fills.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

The privacy page becomes 'Disclosures': section flag, banner title, a single 66ch column of Libre Franklin 18px with League Gothic subheads, data lists as agate tables, and the transparency row as a boxed fact panel linking /transparency/. The support page becomes 'Reader Services': a halftone box with email and response time, and 'what to include' as an agate checklist. The /api-access/ page is set as a markets explainer with endpoint tables in agate. Alternatives pages become 'Comparable listings': a head-to-head agate table (for AppStats: $0.99 vs $2.99/mo, $8.99 vs $19.99/yr, $17.99 vs $49.99 lifetime, privacy label declares none vs usage data and diagnostics, notifications and widgets). The winning cell is highlighted for whichever side wins it, AppStats' wins included. Then the article runs in one column, followed by the 'Letters' FAQ.

Materials

Newsprint ground on a 12-column grid with 24px gutters and ink column rules · Agate tables: 13px Libre Franklin tabular figures, ruled every row, totals in 800 weight · A double rule under the section flag (4px plus 1px) · Boxed panels with a halftone dot screen (CSS radial-gradient, 3px dots) for Reader Services and the fact box · The yellow highlighter swipe as a slightly skewed background band behind ink · The six screenshots run as captioned 'photos' in thin iPhone bezels

Colour strategy

Restrained · light

Type rationale

League Gothic revives Alternate Gothic No. 1, the tall condensed headline gothic of American newspapers; it sets the section flag, the banner and the section heads. Libre Franklin revives Franklin Gothic, the newspaper's workhorse sans, used here for body text, datelines and agate stock tables. All sans and all roman: no italic display serif and no tracked mono labels, which keeps the page out of the broadsheet-editorial cliché. About 48 KB.

New assets needed

None. Halftone, rules and highlighter are CSS; screenshots, QR and icon already exist.

SECOND ROLL

Hand-Hung Scoreboard

Hand-operated ballpark scoreboards: Wrigley Field's 1937 centre-field board and Fenway Park's Green Monster board (green-painted steel, numeral plates hung by hand, line scores, out-of-town scores, ball/strike/out lamps), with the tall name-board tiers of heritage cricket scoreboards.

The page is the scoreboard you read from the stands. The portfolio's numbers are hung as plates, the price is hung as plates, and a lamp panel shows Build, Pricing and Metadata lamps that are not wired. It refuses the floating-phone hero and the KPI-tile grid.

  • #1D4733
  • #133524
  • #EEF2EC
  • #A9C2B3
  • #F4B63F
  • #2F5D47
  • #F7F8F4
Type
Archivo 800 at wdth 125 (Expanded) for plate numerals, board lettering and headings (@fontsource-variable/archivo, wdth file about 90 KB, which also covers the text width) with Archivo 400/500 at wdth 100 from the same variable file, None. Every figure uses Archivo tabular numerals on plates.
Light
The board is read from the bleachers in daylight: the developer glances at it between other things, with morning sun on painted green steel. The board's green is the ground, in one dark scheme (color-scheme: dark); this is a daylight object, not night mode.
Signature
Test the lamps. A 'Test the lamps' plate on the lamp panel runs the board's lamp test: REVIEW REPLIES and ANALYTICS REQUESTS light in sequence, while BUILDS, PRICING and METADATA stay dark and their labels print 'No code for this', linking to /apps/appmeta-pulse/api-access/. The fact comes from the FAQ and the methodology page. About 25 lines of vanilla JS toggle classes, and the button announces its result through aria-live. Without JS, the lamps are server-rendered in their true states (two lit, three dark) with the full labels visible. With reduced motion, the test lights both lamps at once, with no sequence.
Remembered as
A green ballpark scoreboard with my apps' numbers hung on plates, and a lamp panel where Builds, Pricing and Metadata never lit up because they aren't wired.
Risk
A ballpark board can read as gamified, or as American-sports-specific to a global indie audience and a calm brand. A drenched dark green is heavy for long reading, hence the scorecard panel. A 'score' framing can imply your apps compete with each other. The plate grid needs strict tabular alignment at 390px or it collapses into a tile grid.
Full style card

App Store route

The official badge sits on an enamel sponsor panel bolted into the board. The badge is never altered; the panel takes a 2px amber frame when it has focus. Desktop adds the QR on the same panel, captioned 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. The price statement is hung as plates from price.value and plans (Free trial · $0.99/mo · $8.99/yr · $17.99 lifetime) and is never invented. The sticky bar is the board's bottom rail: a 60px green rail with the badge on a small enamel panel and two price plates ($0.99 /MO · $17.99 LIFETIME). It appears once the sponsor panel scrolls away (bottom on mobile, top on desktop). The Ticket window section and the final board repeat badge and QR. Smart App Banner meta stays in head.

Page sequence

  1. Nameplate band: board name plate and painted nav
  2. Board header: H1 (hero.headline) painted, hero.subheadline, and a name-board row 'FOR: indie iOS developers shipping multiple apps' (hero.pre_headline as a board row, not an eyebrow)
  3. Lamp panel: BUILDS, PRICING, METADATA dark ('not wired'); REVIEW REPLIES ('only when you send') and ANALYTICS REQUESTS lit; the 'Test the lamps' plate; value_points 'Monitoring by design'; link to /apps/appmeta-pulse/api-access/
  4. Price plates and sponsor panel: four price plates, the official badge, the desktop QR
  5. Message board: quick_answer (speakable) with hero.secondary
  6. Line score: per-app rows from 2.png and the PORTFOLIO total 992,55 € · +9.2% (from 1.png and 5.png), labelled illustrative
  7. Out-of-town board: six screenshots as inset screens in thin iPhone bezels on a horizontal scroll-snap row, with painted captions
  8. Name boards: features x6 as long name plates, each with a one-line description (the cricket batting-order tier)
  9. Ground rules: Apple's vocabulary (proceeds vs sales, units, refunds, active subscriptions, trial conversions, cancellations) and the other three value_points
  10. Who it's for / not for: who_for and who_not_for in two painted columns
  11. Ticket window: the full plans as three plate rows with their features, Lifetime marked 'Best long-term value' by a lit amber lamp, plans_footnote, badge and QR
  12. Visiting teams: alternatives_to as a mini line score per competitor, linking /alternatives/appstats/, /alternatives/app-sales-store-reports/ and /alternatives/appfigures/; the App Store Connect app and RevenueCat as plain rows
  13. Scorecard: the 'Why AppMeta Pulse exists.' essay (show_body) on the enamel scorecard panel, with the founder Organization block (bio, signals, response time) beneath
  14. Questions: FAQ x13 as name-plate disclosures on the scorecard panel
  15. Privacy board: privacy block and transparency row, with links to the privacy policy, support and /transparency/
  16. Programme notes: the journal posts; also from Lagerland: AppMeta, Mockly
  17. Final board: closing badge, QR and price plates; the Quick reference <details> (ai-canonical); a maker plate line (Built by Lagerland Apps · updated 25 Mar 2026 · first released 1 Feb 2026)
  18. Shared 'A Lagerland app' footer strip

Navigation

Painted links run across the board's nameplate band: Score · Lamps · Price · Questions · Privacy, in Archivo 600 15px white with an amber underline on hover or focus. On mobile, a 'Menu' plate opens a full-width list of painted name plates. On desktop, the jump nav (jump_nav: true) is a row of unnumbered section name plates that sticks under the nameplate band like the board's inning header. Lagerland appears only in the shared footer strip.

Motion

Manual, never electronic. When the line score first enters view, the plates arrive with a short hinge flip (rotateX -90° to 0°, 180ms, 50ms stagger, once); the real numerals are already in the DOM. Lamps switch on with a 120ms fill change inside the lamp only, with no outer glow. The bottom rail travels 8px. No counters and no scroll scrubbing. With prefers-reduced-motion, plates and lamps are simply in place.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support, /api-access/ and the three alternatives pages keep the green board as the frame. Each has the nameplate band, the page title painted in Archivo Expanded 800, and one row of word plates (DATA COLLECTED: NONE · TRACKING: NO · ACCOUNT: NONE). These are words on plates, not big-number tiles. The reading column is an enamel scorecard panel (#F7F8F4, board-green text, Archivo 18px/1.6, 68ch) set into the board. Alternatives pages become a two-team line score: rows for AppMeta Pulse and the competitor, columns $/MO · $/YR · LIFETIME · PRIVACY LABEL · WIDGETS, with real values from each alternatives page hung as plates. The competitor's wins are shown as lit too. 'Pick … if' columns and the FAQ follow on the scorecard. The support page is a scorecard panel with email, response time and what to include.

Materials

Painted green steel as the page ground, with faint panel seams (1px #2F5D47) every 960px · Hung plates: square tiles in plate green with a 1px top highlight and a 1px bottom seam (no offset shadow) and white Archivo Expanded numerals · Lamp panel: round lamps as flat radial fills, amber when lit and dark when not, with painted labels and no outer glow · Enamel sponsor panels: white rectangles that frame the official App Store badge and the QR · Painted board lettering for headings directly on the green · Enamel-white scorecard panel for long reading (essay, FAQ) and for Read mode

Colour strategy

Drenched · dark

Type rationale

Archivo revives late-19th-century American grotesques, the era of ballpark sign painting. Its expanded heavy numerals fill square plates the way painted plate numerals do, and the same alphabet at normal width carries the reading text: one sign-painter's alphabet in two widths. It is neither condensed nor mono, so it does not echo the other two styles. About 90 KB.

New assets needed

None. Plates, lamps, seams and panels are CSS. Line-score figures are the numbers printed in 2.png and 1.png/5.png, labelled as such. Badge, QR, icon and screenshots already exist.

Fixes queued before this style is built (4)
  • blockerRe-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block.   • majorAdd one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).
  • majorMake it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.
  • majorCorrect the front matter before build: 'Truly zero tracking. About a third of AppStats' monthly price ($0.99 vs $2.99).' Drop the Appfigures clause until its price is sourced on the alternatives page.

Or the category standard, played straight: the category's SaaS analytics landing page played straight. An indigo-to-black gradient taken from the icon, a floating iPhone showing the 7-day dashboard, three KPI tiles, a feature card grid, three equal pricing cards with Lifetime highlighted, and an FAQ accordion, in an SF-like grotesk at the craft level of Apple's own product pages.

Mockly

/apps/mockly/ + its privacy and support pages + 8 comparison pages

What the page must prove: The first viewport has to prove six things. It is a Mac app that makes App Store screenshots (H1 from front matter). One layout becomes every required size and locale, shown as trims at true ratios or as the 39 locales, not just stated. The frames are real 3D, and the preview is the export. Nothing leaves the Mac until you push to Apple. The real price is '$12.99 — one-time purchase' with Family Sharing, against subscription tools. There is a working install path: the official badge opening the listing, a small QR on desktop, and a send-to-Mac path on phones.

The default page this refuses: The screenshot-SaaS landing page: a violet-to-indigo gradient hero reading 'Create stunning App Store screenshots in minutes', three glossy 3D iPhones floating at angles, a template gallery grid, feature icon cards, three-tier monthly pricing, a logo wall and an FAQ accordion, as on AppLaunchpad, Screenshots.pro, Previewed and Rotato. Mockly's own icon (a violet tile with a tilted phone) and its UI (lavender on a dark indigo editor) sit inside this default.

THE ROLL

The Graded Nest

The multi-size dressmaking pattern sheet as printed in Burda Style and Finland's Ottobre Design: overlapping pieces in several print colours, each size traced in its own line style (solid, dashed, dotted, dash-dot), a size key, piece numbers in large outlined numerals, notches, grainline arrows, and multilingual instructions in the margin. Also the industrial grading nest, where one base piece is graded to every size by proportional rules at cardinal points.

Mockly's percentage-based layout is grading: one base layout graded to every App Store Connect size. The page is that pattern sheet. Six pieces (iPhone, iPad, Mac, Watch, Apple TV, visionOS) carry the FAQ's 17 export sizes, nested in their own line styles at one true scale. The caption and device notches sit at the same percentages in every size. It refuses the floating-phones-on-violet hero and the feature-card grid.

  • #F1F2EE
  • #1A1C20
  • #C2182B
  • #1C55C0
  • #17723A
  • #7A2EA8

Type
Saira Condensed 800 for the H1, outlined piece numerals (1.5px text-stroke, no fill) and section heads; 600 with tabular figures for size labels set along the lines and the size key (@fontsource/saira-condensed, latin about 18 KB per weight). with Albert Sans variable, weights 400–700 (@fontsource-variable/albert-sans, latin about 32 KB). Instruction columns at 17–18px/1.6 and tables., Saira Condensed 600 with tabular figures for grade tables (cardinal points in % and px), nothing in mono.
Light
A maker at a big cutting table in daylight, the pattern sheet unfolded flat, highlighter in hand, tracing their size through the nest. So the scheme is light.
Signature
Name: 'Trace your size'. Technique: the size key is a real fieldset of 17 radio inputs. CSS :has() on the sheet lays a 10px highlighter stroke under the chosen outline in every piece, fades the other sizes to 35% opacity, and reveals that size's column in the grade chart. JS enhancement lets the visitor drag the caption grade point on the traced piece, or nudge it with the arrow keys. Every graded size moves its point to the same percentage, and a line prints, e.g., 'x 50.0% · y 12.0% → 621 × 323 px on 6.5″ (1242 × 2688)' for each size. No-JS fallback: the whole nest with all 17 sizes drawn, the key working through :has() (CSS only), and a server-rendered grade table listing the pixel position of each cardinal point for every size. Reduced motion: the highlight switches instantly, with no stroke wipe.
Remembered as
'A dressmaking pattern sheet where every App Store size was nested like dress sizes in red, blue and green dashed lines. I picked 6.9-inch in the key, it lit up in highlighter yellow, and the caption notch sat in the same spot in every size.'
Risk
Sewing patterns are not this audience's home ground. The key and one line ('Mockly grades one layout to every size') must land in seconds, or the nest reads as decoration. The sheet is dense by nature, and on phones only one piece shows at a time. Drawing 17 sizes at one true scale needs care, and that precision makes any wrong dimension visible: the 6.9″ 1290×2868 drift has to be fixed first. The highlighter and dashed lines must stay crisp at 2x.

App Store route

The official badge sits inside the title block (the pattern's price box) on paper, black with Apple's own outline, never recoloured. On a Mac it opens the Mac App Store listing. The price statement comes from price.value, with 'Family Sharing included · no subscription' (FAQ). The QR (assets/qr/mockly.svg) shows at 84px beside the badge on screens ≥1024px only, captioned 'Opens the listing on your phone — save it for your Mac'. It is secondary because Mockly is Mac-only. On phones, 'Send this page to my Mac' uses navigator.share (AirDrop or Handoff), falls back to copy-link, and without JS shows the plain URL to type on the Mac. The sticky bar is a paper strip at the bottom with a 1.5px ink top rule, like the size key's edge: 'Mockly · $12.99 once · macOS' in Saira 600 plus the badge at 120px. It appears once the title block's badge leaves the viewport, and only under html.js. The closing title block repeats the badge, price and QR. The Smart App Banner meta (app-id=6756589122) stays in head.

Page sequence

  1. Pattern sheet (hero): the sheet-edge strip, the full nest of 6 pieces and 17 sizes at true scale, the title block with H1, subheadline, price, badge and QR, and the 'Trace your size' key
  2. Pattern description: quick_answer (speakable) as the envelope's description box. Beside it, the ai-canonical Quick reference, always visible, as the 'Pattern information' chart: suits macOS · sizes 17 · locales 39 · price $12.99 once, Family Sharing · data collected none · third-party SDKs 0 · network only to App Store Connect when you upload, and to your AI provider with your key when you translate · account none for the app, ASC credentials in Keychain · first released 1 Feb 2026 · revised 27 May 2026 · formerly ScreenFlow Studio
  3. Notions (what you need): your raw screenshots in a folder, optionally an App Store Connect API key and an AI provider key. Set as the pattern's notions list, from how_it_works and privacy.notes
  4. Grading: the 'Percentage-based precision layout' feature, expanded as the grade-rule chart. Cardinal points in % against px for every size (illustrative layout, labelled), with the draggable grade point (signature)
  5. Made-up views: real exports as view A (1.png, a Mac 2880×1800-class export of iPhone, iPad and Watch in 3D) and view B (TheWait portrait set cropped from 3.png). Captioned with value point 'Real 3D, not flat mockups' and the example_insights determinism and size notes
  6. Sewing order: how_it_works intro and 6 numbered steps (real sequence, HowTo schema), each with outlined Saira step numerals and its screenshot: folder and inspector 3.png, layout 2.png, localise 6.png, render 4.png, upload 5.png
  7. Instructions in 39 languages: value point 'Ship in every App Store locale'. The real ten-language caption from the GymLogger X project (6.png) is set as a pattern's multilingual instruction column: EN 'Train smarter. Log faster.', DE 'Smarter trainieren. Schneller protokollieren.' and so on, each lang-tagged. Then the 39 FAQ locales as a two-column register, with the RTL note
  8. Delivery: direct App Store Connect upload (5.png), Keychain, and the developer-stated '234 screenshots in under two minutes' from example_insights, attributed
  9. Cut at home: privacy. Nothing reaches a Lagerland server; privacy.notes and app_privacy_label; transparency facts linked to /transparency/#mockly; privacy policy link
  10. Pattern price: value_math ($12.99 once against $19–$49/month, or $228–$588 a year) as a yardage-chart style table, plans_footnote, and the badge
  11. Fit notes: who_for as 'Fits', who_not_for as 'Does not fit', each with its honest redirect (fastlane in CI, Figma for campaigns, no preview video)
  12. Other patterns for the same garment: alternatives_to as 8 linked comparison pages, one factual line each
  13. Designed by: founder (Organization, Finland, one-person studio since 2025), story, 4 signals, 'Email us directly', response time. release_notes as 'Pattern revisions' with dates
  14. Questions: all 12 FAQ, open, 66ch
  15. Further reading: related_journal plus the four other Mockly journal posts, and related apps AppMeta and AppMeta Pulse
  16. Closing title block: badge, price, QR. The maker line 'Built by Lagerland Apps · first released 1 Feb 2026 · last updated 27 May 2026', privacy policy and support links, and the shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

The sheet-edge strip is the navigation: Grading · Views · Sewing order · Languages · Price · Questions, plus 'Get Mockly' (jump_nav anchors). The current section's link sits on a highlighter underlay. On mobile, 'Contents' opens a details panel of the same links in 48px rows. The six piece chips in the hero are in-page controls, not navigation. Sub-pages carry a breadcrumb drawn as a dashed cutting line with labelled stops (Lagerland — Mockly — Privacy).

Motion

Drawn-line motion only, under html.js. The highlighter stroke wipes once along the traced outline (stroke-dashoffset, 420ms ease-out-quart). Other sizes fade over 160ms. The grade point follows the pointer 1:1 with no easing. The sticky bar slides up in 160ms. There are no scroll reveals, and the nest is fully drawn without JS. prefers-reduced-motion turns all of it off.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages become the pattern's instruction sheet. They keep the paper ground and the sheet-edge strip, and the title block sets the page title in Saira Condensed 800 at 44px. The reading column is Albert Sans 18px/1.6 ink at 66ch. Tables are ruled like the pattern's measurement chart. Outlined numerals appear only where order is real. Privacy opens with the 'Pattern information' chart of transparency data (data collected none, SDKs 0, network only on upload or requested translation, ASC account only to upload) linked to /transparency/#mockly, then the policy sections. Support is a ruled 'Pattern help' box: email, response time, and what to include. Alternatives pages open with a two-piece nest: Mockly's graded piece (17 sizes) beside the competitor drawn as one grey outline, labelled only with facts from that page (e.g. 'Rotato: animated video, subscription'). Then the comparison as a measurement chart, 'Choose Mockly if' / 'Keep Rotato if' as fit notes, the FAQ, and the price box with badge.

Materials

Flat pattern-paper ground with two faint sheet-fold creases (1px ink at 6%) where the sheet was folded into the magazine · Piece outlines as 2px strokes in piece ink. The largest size is solid, then dashed 8/4, dotted 2/3 and dash-dot 10/3/2/3, as in the key · Size labels set along each line with SVG textPath in Saira Condensed 600, 12–13px, in the piece ink · Notches: 8px ticks across every outline at the layout's cardinal points (caption top 6%, caption foot 18%, device top 30%; illustrative layout), plus a 10px ring grade point at the caption centre · A double-headed grainline arrow per piece, marking which edge is up (portrait or landscape) · A 96px outlined piece numeral and the piece name ('iPhone · cut 4 sizes from one layout') inside each piece · Title block and size key as opaque paper boxes with a 1.5px ink border, sitting over the nest the way a real sheet's legend box does · Made-up views: real screenshots printed flat in 1px ink frames with outlined view letters A, B, C · Highlighter: 10px #E4F53A stroke under the traced line, round caps, multiply blend

Colour strategy

Full palette: four piece inks (iPhone red, iPad blue, Mac green, Watch violet) on cool pattern paper. Apple TV and visionOS print in ink black, as Burda prints some pieces. Highlighter yellow marks only the size being traced. Colour always means 'which piece'. · light

Type rationale

Pattern sheets label pieces and sizes in a condensed technical sans, so '6.9″ · 1290 × 2868' fits along a 2px cutting line or inside a narrow Watch piece. Saira's squared curves echo plotter-drawn grading lines. Albert Sans is a geometric grotesk drawn from Scandinavian modernism: the plain, friendly instruction voice of a Nordic pattern magazine. Total is about 68 KB.

New assets needed

None new as raster. The nest is inline SVG drawn from the FAQ's 17 sizes, and the screenshots exist. Derived crops of 3.png (the four TheWait portrait exports) come from the existing file. Recommended: a _data/mockly_sizes.yml (family, label, w, h) so the SVG, grade table and quick reference render from one source. The owner should first verify the 6.9″ dimension.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

OK to Upload

Offset-litho prepress. The imposed contract proof on a press sheet: ganged cells with crop marks, registration targets, the CMYK colour control strip along the gripper edge, and slug lines naming each version. Multilingual versioning, where only the black text plate is changed per language. The ISO 3664 viewing booth, with its neutral N8 grey surround and 5000 K light, where the client signs 'OK to print'.

The page is one imposed proof sheet of Mockly's output. The same composition is ganged up at every App Store Connect trim, each cell slugged with device · locale · slot · px. The text plate swaps per language while the artwork stays registered. The headline is itself one trimmed cell, and an 'OK to upload' box holds the price and the badge. It refuses the floating-phones-on-gradient hero and the template's feature-card grid.

  • #C7C8C5
  • #FBFBF9
  • #141414
  • #0093D3
  • #D6007E

Type
Chivo variable, weights 400–900 (@fontsource-variable/chivo, latin about 33 KB). 900 for the H1 and cell captions, 700 for section heads and the approval box. with Chivo 400/600 from the same file, at 18px/1.6 in a 66ch column., Chivo Mono 400 (@fontsource/chivo-mono, latin about 12 KB), only for slug lines: device, locale code, slot, pixel dimensions, reduction %, dates. All of these are real data.
Light
A client and a press operator at the viewing booth: the proof pinned flat on the N8 grey wall under 5000 K daylight-balanced light, checking trims and registration before signing. So the scheme is light.
Signature
Name: 'Plate change'. Technique: each illustrative cell's caption is live HTML on its own K layer, positioned in % over the CMY artwork. Ten plate tabs (real buttons with aria-pressed) swap the K layer text in every cell on the sheet at once. The strings are the ten from 6.png, with lang attributes. Slugs update their locale code (en-US → de-DE), and longer German and French lines re-wrap inside the same % box, showing type and positions preserved. A 'Separations' toggle pulls the C, M, Y and K layers 12px apart (CSS transforms, mix-blend-mode multiply), and labels K 'text layer: the only plate that changes per language'. No-JS fallback: the EN plate shows in the cells, and the ten translations are printed in full as the plate register (locale · line 1 · line 2). The Plates section shows the four separations statically. Reduced motion: the swap and the separation are instant.
Remembered as
'A printer's proof sheet in a grey booth. The headline was itself one of the trimmed screenshots, with crop marks and a slug saying 2880 × 1800. I clicked DE and every cell's caption changed while the colours stayed put, and an OK-to-upload box held the App Store badge.'
Risk
This is the familiar strong idea for a design tool, and the one most likely to slide into costume. Crop marks and colour bars become decoration unless every cell is a real trim at a true ratio and the plate change really works. Booth grey can feel drab, so the sheet must stay bright and dominant. Seventeen trims make a long vertical strip on phones. The CMYK plate is a comparison, not a claim: Mockly exports RGB PNGs, so copy must say 'like the black plate in print'. Slugs print pixel dimensions prominently, so the 6.9″ drift must be fixed first. The hero uses 6.5″ 1242×2688 meanwhile.

App Store route

The badge sits in the 'OK to upload' approval box, unaltered on sheet white; on a Mac it opens the Mac App Store listing. The price statement is the box's first field, from price.value, with 'Family Sharing included' from the FAQ. On screens ≥1024px the QR (96px) is the box's third field, 'Scan: listing on your phone', smaller than the badge because Mockly is Mac-only. On phones the box carries 'Send this page to my Mac' (navigator.share, then copy-link, then the printed URL without JS). The nav's 'OK to upload' button jumps to the box. The sticky bar is the gripper edge: a white strip pinned to the bottom, the colour control strip as its top border, 'Mockly · $12.99 once · macOS' in Chivo 700 and the badge at 120px. It appears under html.js after the approval box leaves the viewport. The closing approval box repeats the badge, price and QR. The Smart App Banner meta stays in head.

Page sequence

  1. Hero imposition: colour strip, slug and nav line, the H1 hero cell at Mac trim (re-imposed at the phone's trim on mobile), the ganged illustrative iPhone and Watch cells, the plate register, and the approval box with price, badge and QR
  2. Job ticket: quick_answer (speakable) as the ruled job description. Beside it, the ai-canonical Quick reference, always visible, as the job specification: platform macOS · price $12.99 once, Family Sharing · export sizes 17 · locales 39 · data collected none · third-party SDKs 0 · network only to App Store Connect when you upload, and to your AI provider with your own key when you translate · account none for the app, ASC credentials in Keychain · first released 1 Feb 2026 · last updated 27 May 2026 · formerly ScreenFlow Studio
  3. Trims: all 17 FAQ sizes ganged in one imposition at 10%, grouped by family, each with crop marks and a px slug. The 'Percentage-based precision layout' feature is the caption: 'One layout, set in percentages, imposed on every trim'
  4. Plates: localisation. A separations diagram shows the C, M and Y plates fixed and the K plate changing. The ten real translations from the GymLogger X project (6.png) form the plate register, labelled as real Mockly output. The 39 FAQ locales follow as a locale register with the RTL note, plus value point 'Ship in every App Store locale' and 3.png's 39-locale list
  5. Contract proof: real Mockly exports mounted as signed proofs with slugs: 1.png (3D iPhone, iPad and Watch) and the TheWait portrait set cropped from 3.png. The example_insights notes become proof notes, 7.png's numeric rotation is shown, and value point 'Real 3D, not flat mockups' plus 'preview matches export, re-render tomorrow and the bytes are identical'
  6. Press run: how_it_works intro and 6 steps as the job's routing column (real sequence 1–6, HowTo schema), each with its station screenshot: 3.png, 2.png, 6.png, 4.png, 5.png
  7. Dispatch and the in-house press: direct App Store Connect upload (5.png, with the developer-stated 234 screenshots in under two minutes). Then privacy as 'No service bureau': the journal's argument that web tools render on a vendor's server, privacy.notes, app_privacy_label, and transparency facts linked to /transparency/#mockly and the privacy policy
  8. Quotation: value_math as a printer's quote ($12.99 once against $19–$49/month, or $228–$588 a year), Family Sharing, plans_footnote, and the badge. release_notes as the proof history, revisions dated 1 Feb → 5 Apr 2026
  9. Specification fit: who_for as 'Approved for'. who_not_for as magenta proof queries, each with its honest redirect (fastlane in CI, Figma for campaigns, single-locale apps, no preview video)
  10. Other presses: alternatives_to as 8 slugged links to the comparison pages
  11. Printer's imprint: founder (Organization, Finland, one-person studio since 2025), story, 4 signals, 'Email us directly', response time
  12. Queries: all 12 FAQ, open, 66ch
  13. Further reading: related_journal and the other Mockly posts. 'Same press': AppMeta and AppMeta Pulse
  14. Closing approval box: badge, price, QR, the signed line. Maker line 'Built by Lagerland Apps · first released 1 Feb 2026 · last updated 27 May 2026', privacy policy and support, and the shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

The slug line is the navigation: Trims · Plates · Proof · Press run · Dispatch · Quote · Queries (jump_nav anchors), plus the solid 'OK to upload' button. The current section gets a 12px registration target before its link and a 2px K underline. On mobile, 'Contents' opens a details panel of the same links in 48px rows, ruled like a job ticket. Sub-pages carry a slug-style breadcrumb (Lagerland / Mockly / Privacy) in Chivo Mono 12px.

Motion

Registered, mechanical motion only, under html.js. The K layer crossfades in 120ms. Separations slide 12px out and back over 240ms ease-out-quart. Registration targets never spin. The sticky gripper bar slides in 160ms. There are no scroll reveals. prefers-reduced-motion turns everything off.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages become further proof sheets. The booth surround and white sheet stay, with the colour strip on top and a slug breadcrumb. The title is in Chivo 900 at 48px, and the reading column is Chivo 400 18px/1.6 at 66ch. Tables are ruled in K like a job spec. Privacy opens with the job-spec table of transparency data, then the policy sections (overview, data collection, storage, third parties, sensitive data, children, changes, contact). Support is 'Job enquiries': email, response time, and what to include as a ruled list. Alternatives pages open with a two-cell gang: Mockly's cell (17 trims, $12.99 once) beside the competitor's cell in a grey hairline, carrying only facts from that page. Then the comparison as a spec table, 'Approve Mockly if' and 'Keep Rotato if' as two ruled lists, the FAQ as queries, and the approval box with badge.

Materials

Booth: flat N8 grey, 32px visible around the sheet on desktop and 8px on mobile · Sheet: bright white, square corners, a 1px #A9AAA7 edge, no shadow, no texture · Colour control strip along the gripper edge: 12px patches of C, M, Y and K solids, 25/50/75% tints, CM/MY/CY overprints and a grey-balance patch, repeated across the full width · Registration targets: 24px circle-and-cross in K at the sheet's mid-edges and at each section's corner · Crop marks: 1px K, 16px long, set 6px outside every cell's trim corners · Slug lines in Chivo Mono 12px under each cell, flush to the trim's left edge · Cells trimmed at exact App Store Connect aspect ratios, each stating its reduction ('reduced to 25 %'). Illustrative cells hold a flat process-tint field, a device outline as a K hairline with a magenta-tint screen, and the caption in Chivo 900 on its own K layer · 'OK to upload' approval box: a 1.5px K ruled box with fields (Price · Platform · Family Sharing · Approved) and a signature line · Proof queries: magenta 24px circles with numbers and hairline leaders in the margin, used only for honest caveats (who_not_for, no preview video) · Focus: 3px K outline with a 2px white offset

Colour strategy

Restrained: neutral booth grey and bright sheet white, with process black for everything that reads. Process cyan, magenta and yellow appear only where print puts them: the colour control strip, registration targets, the illustrative cell artwork and the plate-separation demo. Magenta also marks proof queries. Colour never decorates text. · light

Type rationale

Chivo is Omnibus-Type's grotesque in the Akzidenz line, drawn for headlines: the job-printer's sans that sets real pack and ad copy. Its 900 holds as a caption inside a 103px Watch cell and as a 56px H1 alike. Chivo Mono shares its skeleton, so slugs like 'iPhone 6.5″ · de-DE · 03 · 1242 × 2688 px' read as the RIP's printed marks from the same hand. Total is about 45 KB.

New assets needed

None as new raster. The colour strip, crop marks and registration targets are CSS or inline SVG, and the illustrative cells are CSS. Derived crops come from existing files: the four TheWait portrait exports from 3.png, and the GymLogger X canvas from 2.png. Recommended: _data/mockly_sizes.yml as the single source for trims and slugs.
