Thumb-Index Leaflet

The multilingual instruction leaflet packed with electronics and appliances: an accordion-folded strip of thin paper, a cover listing every language code, a model plate box, thumb-index tabs bleeding off the edge, a wordless exploded diagram with numbered leader-line callouts, the same layout repeated per language, Arabic and Hebrew set from the back, and closing 'Technical data' and 'Service' panels. Printed in two inks.

Mockly's localisation pass, shown as the leaflet every multilingual product ships. One layout repeats with positions and type preserved. A wall of the 39 App Store locale codes is the cover. A thumb index re-sets a real caption in place, and an exploded parts diagram keys the real Mockly window. It refuses the floating-phones hero, the split hero and the card rows.

Type
Noto Sans Display variable, wght 100–900 and wdth 62.5–100 (@fontsource-variable/noto-sans-display, latin wdth file about 70 KB). wdth 62.5 / 900 for the H1 and the 39-code wall; wdth 75 / 800 for panel heads, callout numerals and the demo captions. with Noto Sans variable wght (@fontsource-variable/noto-sans, latin about 36 KB), 400/600, at 18px/1.6 in a 66ch column., Noto Sans 600 with tabular figures for Technical data, callout keys and prices. Endonyms in non-Latin scripts (日本語, العربية, עברית, ไทย, हिन्दी, 한국어, 简体中文) fall back to the visitor's system fonts, so no CJK or Arabic files are downloaded.
Light
Someone unboxing at a desk in daylight, pulling out the leaflet, unfolding it panel by panel down the strip, thumb finding their language tab. So the scheme is light, printed in two inks.
Signature

'Schneller protokollieren.' re-wraps inside the same % box, showing positions and type preserved. Pressing a code in the wall that has no sample (e.g. JA) scrolls to its register row: endonym plus 'Translated in Mockly with your own AI key — no sample on this page'. No-JS fallback: tabs are anchor links to the Languages panel, where all ten captions are printed side by side as visible lang-tagged rows; the cover demo shows EN. Reduced motion: the caption swap and tab slide are instant.
Remembered as
'It looked like the instruction leaflet from a gadget box: a violet cover with a wall of 39 language codes and a model box holding the App Store badge. I pressed DE on the edge tab and the little screenshot's caption switched to Smarter trainieren in the same spot.'
Risk
The violet cover sits next to the category's purple and the icon. It only works as flat two-ink print: any gradient, glow or floating phone turns it into every screenshot SaaS page. Leaflets are humble, so the page can read as documentation rather than persuasion unless the cover's code wall, model box and live caption land at once. Only ten real translations exist, so 29 codes link to the register instead of demoing, and that must be labelled. Non-Latin endonyms depend on system fonts. Moving Technical data to the front departs from real leaflet order, for the sake of AEO.

Motion

Paper motion only, under html.js. The pressed tab slides 8px outward in 120ms, and captions crossfade in 140ms. Panels never fold or reveal on scroll. The sticky strip slides down in 160ms. prefers-reduced-motion turns all of it off.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages become other sections of the same leaflet. A short violet cover band is the masthead: icon, 'Mockly', and the page title in Noto Display wdth 62.5/900 at 48px white. Below are white panels with fold creases and the 'EN' corner marker. The reading column is Noto Sans 18px/1.6 black at 66ch. Privacy opens with the boxed 'Before you start' facts (transparency data, link to /transparency/#mockly), then the policy sections. Support is the 'Service' panel: email, response time, and a 'what to include' list. Alternatives pages open with a 'Comparable products' Technical data table (Mockly against the competitor, facts from that page only). Then 'Choose Mockly if' and 'Keep frameit if' as tick and cross lists, the FAQ as a troubleshooting table, and the model box with badge.

Materials

Two-ink print on thin white paper. Each panel is a full-width band, separated by a horizontal fold crease: a 1px #6B6880 line at 40% with a 16px shade at 4% black on one side (valley or mountain) · The violet cover drenched edge to edge. White type on it, flat ink · Thumb tabs: 56×44px violet blocks bleeding off the right edge, stepped down the edge, with codes in white Noto Display 800. The active tab is black with white text and sits 8px further out · Model box (the product's rating-plate box): white, 2px black border, black text, holding the price, badge and QR · Exploded diagram: 3.png with 1.5px violet leader lines ending in 28px violet discs with white numerals, and a key table beneath · Line pictograms: 1.5px black strokes for the six steps (folder, device frame, percentage grid, text block with two scripts, stacked files, upload tray) · Every panel's outer corner carries 'EN' in a small violet box: the leaflet's own language marker, accurate for this page · Ticks and crosses for fit notes drawn as 1.5px SVG strokes, not Unicode · Focus: 3px black outline with a 2px white offset (on the cover: a 3px white outline with a 2px black offset)

Colour strategy

Committed, two-ink print. Mockly violet (the icon's colour) drenches the cover panel and prints the thumb tabs, callout discs and links. Black prints all reading text. Inside panels are white thin paper with violet 15% tint bands. There are no gradients and no glow, so the violet reads as flat ink, not the category's gradient. · light

Type rationale

Noto exists so one design covers every script without 'tofu' boxes. It is the family multilingual leaflets and operating systems fall back on, which is Mockly's promise of 'fonts preserved' across 39 locales. Its condensed display widths fit 39 codes, long German and French headings and the caption plates into fixed panel widths without shrinking: the exact problem Mockly solves for captions. Total is about 106 KB.

New assets needed

Six small 1.5px line pictograms for the steps (new inline SVG, a small drawing task). The trim line drawings are CSS or SVG. Callout coordinates need mapping onto 3.png. Crops of 3.png come from the existing file. No new raster.

Or the category standard, played straight: the screenshot-SaaS page. A violet-to-indigo gradient hero reads 'App Store Screenshot Maker for Mac' over three glossy 3D phones floating at angles, with the badge and QR beside it. MediaKit

/apps/mediakit/ + its privacy and support pages + 14 comparison pages

What the page must prove: One native app handles every format and picks the right tool itself. The file never leaves the device, shown through the transparency record rather than claimed. It is free to start: a 3-day full trial, five tools free forever, Pro from $3.99/mo. The official App Store badge (opening the Mac App Store on a Mac) and, on desktop, the QR for the iPhone must sit within reach.

The default page this refuses: The converter page: a giant dashed 'Drop file here / Upload' box over a grid of MP4-to-MOV format pills on a purple gradient (CloudConvert, Convertio). The other default is the Mac-utility page: a centred icon over a big dark window screenshot, then a feature-card grid and a three-tier pricing table (Permute, HandBrake sites).

THE ROLL

Processed In-House

The 1980s–2000s one-hour photo minilab counter: the printed drop-off envelope (FILM TYPE / SIZE / FINISH / SETS / SERVICE: 1-hour, next day, send out), its perforated claim-check stub, the backlit price board above the counter, the index print and the print wallet that came back.

The page is the drop-off envelope of a lab that never sends anything out. 'Send out' is printed and then struck through, and ticking a file type routes it to its tools. It refuses the converter category's dashed upload box and its format-pill grid.

  • #19A7E0
  • #101418
  • #FFFFFF
  • #0A6C93
  • #D1006F
Type
Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 900 with Sofia Sans 400, 600, Sofia Sans Condensed 600 (field labels, tick-box labels, price-board rows)
Light
A Mac or iPhone owner at a bright desk in daytime with a file too big to send, reading the page the way you read an order form handed across a lit retail counter. So the scheme is light.
Signature
Name: 'Tick the file type'. Technique: the FILE TYPE row is a real radio group. Ticking one, via CSS :has(:checked) with no JS, draws the magenta tick, re-inks the PROCESS and PRESETS rows for that type, and moves the in-house stamp onto it. JS enhancement: drop a real file onto the envelope (or 'Choose a file' on phones). The browser reads only file.name, ticks the matching type ('.HEIC → Image') and prints 'Nothing left this page — only the file name was read'. No-JS fallback: the Video row is pre-ticked and every type's full tool list is printed statically in the Index print below, so no content depends on the control. Reduced motion: the stamp and tick appear instantly, with no press.
Remembered as
'It was a cyan photo-lab envelope where Send out was printed and crossed out. I ticked Video and it listed the tools, and the download button was the claim-check stub.'
Risk
It leans on a ritual many visitors under 30 never did, and the cyan drench with condensed caps could tip into retro pastiche or risograph-zine trend. The photo-lab frame may read as 'a photo app' unless all six file types are visible in the first viewport. The order form's density has to stay legible at 390px.

App Store route

The official badge lives untouched on the white claim-check stub, framed only by the perforation; on a Mac it opens the Mac App Store. The desktop QR (assets/qr/mediakit.svg, ≥1024px) sits on the stub as 'Scan with your iPhone camera'. The sticky bar is the stub torn off: a white strip with a dashed perforation on its top edge, 'MediaKit · Free to start · Pro from $3.99/mo' plus the badge at 120px. It appears once the hero stub scrolls away and never shows without JS. The price statement is price.value printed on the stub, and the full price board comes later. The Smart App Banner meta (app-id=6761451361) sits in head, and iOS Safari draws it above the flap.

Page sequence

  1. Envelope face (hero): headline and subheadline printed on cyan; the order form (FILE TYPE → PROCESS → PRESETS → SERVICE with 'Send out' struck through → PROOF print of the real result screen); the claim-check stub with badge, QR and price.value
  2. Printed instructions: quick_answer as the envelope's opening paragraph (speakable), directly under the form. Beside it, the ai-canonical Quick reference as an always-open ruled 'Lab use only' box: platforms, iOS 17+/macOS 14+, Universal Purchase, price, data collected none, network none, account none, open-source libraries 1 (Unrar.swift)
  3. Send-out route vs in-house: the journal's six steps an uploaded file takes, printed as a carbon slip with every line struck through, against 'Drop. Done.' (value_points[0]); privacy.notes and transparency facts, linked to /transparency/#mediakit
  4. Index print: value_points as the sheet caption, then six strips (Video, Audio, Image, PDF, Archive, Ebook) of tool names drawn from features and the screenshots. Ebook lists its formats (EPUB, CBZ, HTML, RTF). The five free-forever tools are ringed in magenta, and '152 tools in all' comes from front matter
  5. Standing orders: the six Shortcuts actions and menu-bar access (features[5]) set as a repeat-order slip
  6. Print wallet: the 8 Mac screenshots as borderless prints in a horizontal scroll-snap strip, each with a back-print caption naming the screen (tool picker, result, Trim, audio Convert, PDF tools, ZIP compress, GIF Maker x2)
  7. Is this lab for you: who_for as ticked boxes, who_not_for as empty boxes with the honest redirect (Final Cut or Resolve; a free web tool for one file a year)
  8. Price board: the four plans as backlit board rows (name, price, summary, features). Pro Annual sits on the highlighted row, Lifetime keeps its 'Best long-term value' label, and plans_footnote follows as small print
  9. Counter questions: all 7 FAQ answers printed open in a 64ch column (FAQPage)
  10. Other labs in town: alternatives_to as a printed list. 14 names link to their /alternatives/ pages; Keka and ImageOptim appear as plain text
  11. From the lab notebook: the two journal posts
  12. Closing claim check: a full-width perforated stub with badge, QR and price; the maker/freshness line as a photo-paper back-print (Lagerland Apps · first released 1 Apr 2026 · last updated 13 Apr 2026); privacy policy and support links; other Lagerland apps as one printed line; then the shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

The envelope's top flap is the nav: 'File types · Tool index · Price list · Questions · Privacy' set as printed tab labels, with 'Download free' at the right. The current section is underlined in magenta. On mobile, 'Menu' is a details/summary that folds down like the flap, with the same five links at 44px rows.

Motion

Paper does not animate; ink lands. On a tick, the stamp presses (scale 1.04 to 1 with an opacity fade, 120ms ease-out) and the tick draws in 90ms. The sticky stub rises 8px over 160ms. Perforations, prints and sections never move or scroll-reveal. Under prefers-reduced-motion every state change is instant.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages wear the envelope's back. A 72px cyan flap band carries the page title in Extra Condensed 900 ink, and a 24px cyan strip runs down each margin. The reading column is a white knock-out at 66ch in Sofia Sans 18px/1.6 ink. The privacy policy's sections are printed terms headed in Condensed 600, followed by a ruled 'Lab use only' box of transparency facts. Support is a counter slip that lists, as empty tick boxes, what to include (device, OS version, file type, what happened), with the email address. Alternatives pages set the head-to-head as a two-column ruled order form ('MediaKit | HandBrake'), 'Pick MediaKit if…' as ticked boxes and 'Stick with HandBrake if…' as empty boxes, then FAQ open, ending with the perforated claim stub.

Materials

Flat flood-printed cyan stock with no texture, as printed paper reads on screen · White knock-out form panels with 1px ink rules and 24px drawn tick boxes (CSS, never unicode) · Perforation: 2px dashed ink rule with 12px semicircle punches at both ends (the claim-stub tear line, reused as the section divider) · Magenta rubber-stamp ring (SVG textPath circle, 132px): 'PROCESSED IN-HOUSE · ON THIS DEVICE' · Borderless 'prints': Mac screenshots cropped 3:2 with a one-line back-print caption · Index-print strips: dense rows of tool-name cells read like a table · Themed focus: 3px magenta outline offset 2px on white, 3px ink outline on cyan

Colour strategy

Drenched: the ground IS the envelope's flood-printed process-cyan stock edge to edge. Form panels are knocked out to white. All type on cyan is black ink, and one magenta 'second ink' is reserved for ticks, rings and the in-house stamp. · light

Type rationale

Photo envelopes and lab price boards were set in heavy condensed grotesk to fit long option rows on a narrow form. Extra Condensed 900 gives that printed-stationery shout at 116px without running off the envelope. Sofia Sans 400/600 is the plain typed fill-in voice for reading copy, and the Condensed cut sets form labels. One superfamily works like a lab's matched stationery set. Four files total about 63 KB.

New assets needed

None required: stock, rules, perforations and the stamp are CSS/SVG, and prints are cropped from existing screenshots. Optional: portrait iPhone screenshots of MediaKit (none exist) for one iPhone print in the wallet, and a _data/mediakit_tools.yml with all 152 tool names by type so the index print can be complete and frame-numbered.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

Zone One Network

The schematic metro diagram: Harry Beck's 1933 Underground diagram and Vignelli's 1972 New York map (octilinear lines, ticks for stations, rings for interchanges), fare-zone maps with shaded zone boundaries, and the in-car strip map that unrolls one line vertically.

MediaKit's routing drawn as a working network. Five lines in the app's own per-family colours leave one interchange called Drop, and every station is a real tool. The whole network sits inside a dashed Zone 1 boundary marked 'your iPhone or Mac', and the cloud converters' route runs outside it, never connected. It refuses the converter's upload box and the utility page's feature-card grid.

  • #0F1214

  • #7B2FBF
  • #D2336A

Type
Overpass 800 (headline, line names), 600 (station names on the map) with Atkinson Hyperlegible Next 400, 700, Overpass 800 tabular figures in the line roundels and fare table
Light
Someone mid-errand reading a station's network map on a white enamel panel under bright platform light: glanceable, coloured lines, black type. So the scheme is light.
Signature
Name: 'Drop at Drop'. Technique: the Drop interchange is a real drop target, with a 'Choose a file' input on touch. JS reads only file.name (never the contents) and maps the extension using the FAQ's format lists. The matching line stays in full colour while the other four fade to 20% ink, and a departure-board line prints 'IMG_0937.HEIC → Image line: Convert · Compress · Resize · Strip EXIF · OCR', then 'Only the file name was read. Nothing left this page.' Without JS, hovering or focusing a legend roundel isolates its line with CSS :has(). Format chips (MP4 MOV MKV · MP3 FLAC WAV · HEIC RAW PNG · PDF EPUB · ZIP RAR) are plain links to each line section. No-JS fallback: the full static map with every line and station visible. Reduced motion: the line isolation switches instantly, with no line-draw.
Remembered as
'A white metro map where every station was a tool. Five coloured lines met at Drop, all inside a dashed Zone 1 that said your iPhone or Mac, and the cloud converters' line sat outside it, never connected.'
Risk
This is the most familiar strong idea: 'a subway map of X' is a well-worn explainer trope, and it is where many runs would land. It only earns its place if stations are working links and the legend really is the navigation, not a poster. The octilinear SVG has to be laid out by hand once and maintained when tools change. On phones the network collapses to strip maps, so the whole-network view is a desktop-first moment. Station lists stay partial until the full tool catalogue exists.

  10. Connections: alternatives_to as an interchange list (14 linked pages; Keka and ImageOptim as plain names), the two journal posts, and other Lagerland apps as 'other networks'
  11. Board here: closing badge, QR and price; the map imprint line (Lagerland Apps · first released 1 Apr 2026 · revised 13 Apr 2026); privacy policy and support; shared 'A Lagerland app' strip

Navigation

The line legend is the navigation. Five roundels (V Video, A Audio, I Image, D Documents, Z Archive) jump to their line sections, followed by 'Fares', 'Questions' and 'Download free'. The current line's roundel gains an ink ring. On mobile, 'Lines' opens a details panel listing the roundels and named links at 44px rows. Sub-pages use a breadcrumb drawn as a short ink line with stops (Lagerland → MediaKit → Privacy).

Motion

Lines draw once on first load (stroke-dashoffset, 700ms ease-out-quart, staggered 80ms per line), but only under html.js, so the map is fully drawn without JS. Isolation crossfades over 180ms, the departure line types in over 240ms, and the sticky next-station bar slides up 160ms. Sections never reveal on scroll. prefers-reduced-motion turns everything off.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and alternatives pages become station information pages. A route-bar breadcrumb runs across the top (an ink line with stops Lagerland → MediaKit → this page), and the title is set in Overpass 800 on white enamel. The reading column is Atkinson 18px/1.6 ink at 66ch, with tables set as timetables. The privacy policy's sections become stops on a vertical ink contents line (Overview → Data collection → Storage → Third parties → Children → Changes → Contact), with a 'Network facts' table of transparency data. Support is a 'Help point' panel with the email address and a stop-list of what to include. Alternatives pages draw a two-line comparison strip ('MediaKit network: five lines' vs the competitor's single grey line, labelled only with facts from the page), then the comparison as a timetable, 'Pick MediaKit if…' and 'Stick with HandBrake if…' as two strip lists, FAQ, and the Fares box.

Materials

White vitreous-enamel ground, flat, with the map frame's rounded 12px corners · 10px line strokes with 45° and 90° bends only (inline SVG drawn from front-matter tool names) · Station ticks: 4px ink. Interchanges: white disc with a 6px ink ring. Free-forever stations: filled ink disc keyed 'Free forever' · Line roundels: 28px coloured discs with one letter (V A I D Z), used as legend and navigation · Zone 1 boundary: 2px dashed ink rounded rectangle, ink-at-6% fill, label set into its top edge · Cloud-converter route: 3px grey dashed line with hollow stops, outside the zone · Timetable tables: black header rule, 1px ink row rules, tabular figures · Themed focus: 3px ink outline with a 2px white inner ring

Colour strategy

Full palette: five named line colours (Video, Audio, Image, Documents, Archive), taken from the app's own per-family tints, run on white enamel with black type. Zone 1 is filled with ink at 6% over the ground, and the cloud route is ink-grey dashed. Colour only ever means 'which line'. · light

Type rationale

Overpass is the open revival of Highway Gothic, the FHWA sign alphabet. These are the most-read wayfinding letterforms in North America, so headings and line names read as enamel signage. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next was drawn for the Braille Institute to keep letters and figures apart, which matters on a map full of 'OCR', 'EXIF', 'RAR v5', 'AES-256' and 'R128'. Four files total about 60 KB.

New assets needed

None required: the diagram is hand-placed inline SVG built from front-matter tool names, and the screenshots exist. Strongly recommended: a _data/mediakit_tools.yml with all 152 tool names by family, so every line can show its full station list and not only the tools named in features and screenshots. Optional: portrait iPhone screenshots for the strip-map sections.

SECOND ROLL

The Whole Rack

The broadcast master-control machine room: the 19-inch EIA-310 equipment rack (1U = 1.75in) with rack ears and oval screw slots, silkscreened front panels of standards converters and loudness processors, jewel pilot lamps, rotary input selectors and rack-mount confidence monitors. Every format conversion used to be its own box here.

Every conversion used to be a separate box bolted into a rack. The page is one rack seen from the front, where every box is a module of the same app, stacked unit by unit as you scroll. It refuses both the converter's upload box and the Mac-utility page's icon-over-screenshot.

  • #0B0E14

Type
Michroma 400 with Barlow 400, 500, B612 Mono 400 (real readouts only: 55.3 MB → 42.7 MB, 0:42, 1920×1080, 152, 21, 6, prices in the plan rows)
Light
A video editor or podcaster in a dim edit suite at night, the room lit only by the Mac screen and the rack's pilot lamps. So the scheme is dark.
Signature
Name: 'Input selector'. Technique: a five-detent rotary knob that is a real radio group (arrow keys move detents). With CSS only (:has(:checked)), selecting a detent turns the knob, lights that lamp amber, and switches the Output monitor to that processor's real screenshot. JS enhancement: drop a real file into the engraved well (or 'Choose a file' on phones). The browser reads only file.name and file.size, sets the knob from the extension, and prints 'IN: IMG_0937.MOV · 55.3 MB → Video processor · read in your browser only' in B612 Mono. No-JS fallback: the Video detent is pre-selected, every processor module below shows its own screenshot and tools, and nothing depends on the knob. Reduced motion: the knob jumps to the detent and the lamp switches without the 80ms fade.
Remembered as
'The page was one blue equipment rack. Every tool was a module bolted in as I scrolled, I turned a knob to Audio and the monitor changed, and the download sat in its own Output panel next to a green Network: none lamp.'
Risk
A skeuomorphic hardware rack can tip into costume or dated pastiche. Dark navy with amber lamps sits one step from the 'near-black plus one accent' cluster, so the anodise must stay visibly blue and the lamps flat. Michroma is very wide: headlines drop to 26px on phones and long words need care. Consumer visitors may not know a broadcast rack, so the idea leans on the visible 'every box in one' reading rather than recognition.

  2. Master module (7U): headline, subheadline, INPUT selector and drop well

Navigation

The 1U nav module carries push-button legends: Input, Processors, Price, Manual (FAQ), Privacy, and 'Download free'. An amber pilot lamp lights beside the section in view, using IntersectionObserver, and the static first item is lit without JS. On mobile, 'Menu' opens a details panel styled as the rack's unit index, listing every module with its U position.

Motion

Hardware-literal and terse. The knob rotates 30° per detent over 140ms (ease-out-quart), lamps switch on in 80ms with no glow or bloom, the monitor crossfades in 100ms, and the sticky 1U strip slides up over 160ms. Modules are bolted in: no scroll reveals and no parallax. Under prefers-reduced-motion all states are instant.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

On privacy, support and alternatives pages the rack frame stays: rails with screw slots in the margins, a 1U legend strip at the top with the page title in Michroma, and a serial plate at the foot. The reading column is one manual-page module: Barlow 17px/1.65 #EEF2F7 on #12203F at 66ch, headings in Michroma 22px, and tables set as spec plates with B612 Mono used only for figures. The privacy policy's sections are manual chapters, with a spec-plate table of transparency facts. Support is a 'service request' module with the email address and a lamp-bulleted list of what to include. Alternatives pages set the comparison as a spec sheet (rows: scope, encoder depth, platform, privacy; columns: MediaKit | HandBrake), 'Pick MediaKit if…' with green lamps and 'Stick with HandBrake if…' with amber lamps, then the FAQ and the Output module with the badge.

Materials

Blue-anodised brushed faceplates: base #1B2F5E with a horizontal repeating-linear-gradient grain at 3% contrast (CSS) · Black rack rails both sides with clear-anodise ear plates and an oval screw slot every 1U (CSS radial gradients). 1U = 48px desktop / 40px mobile sets the page's vertical rhythm · 2px recessed seams between modules; engraved 1px hairline frames around control groups · Pilot-lamp jewels: 12px flat circles with a 2px white specular dot, lit or unlit, never haloed · Rotary selector knob: 120px, five engraved detents (radio group) · Rack-mount confidence monitors: 16px black bezel around real Mac screenshots · Serial plate: an engraved rectangle for the maker/freshness line

Colour strategy

Committed: deep blue-anodised aluminium (the icon's navy-steel) covers about 60% of the surface as module faceplates, framed by black rack rails. White silkscreen sets all type, and amber and green pilot-lamp jewels are the only saturated marks, each with a job: amber means selected or active, green means on-device or free. There is no glow anywhere. · dark

Type rationale

Michroma revives Microgramma Extended, the wide capitals silkscreened onto 1970s–80s broadcast and studio rack panels. Its single weight is right for silkscreen, where legends have one ink weight. Barlow is a low-contrast industrial grotesk drawn from California plates and highway signs, and it reads as the operator's manual on dark at 17px. B612 Mono was drawn for Airbus cockpit displays, and it appears only where a real figure is read out. Four files total about 81 KB.

New assets needed

None required: rails, anodise grain, lamps and the knob are CSS/SVG, and the monitors show existing Mac screenshots. Optional: portrait iPhone screenshots of MediaKit, so one monitor can show the iPhone app, and the _data/mediakit_tools.yml catalogue for complete front-panel tool legends.

Or the category standard, played straight: the dark Mac-utility product page, with a centred app icon and headline over a large Mac window screenshot on a deep gradient, a 'Download on the App Store' badge with a QR beside it, a row of format/feature cards, a three-column pricing table, an FAQ accordion and a footer, in the Permute / CleanShot register.

Millrace

/apps/millrace/ + its privacy and support pages + 5 comparison pages

What the page must prove: That a level is a closed problem with a proven answer. The first viewport must show the arrival queue in full, the exact target and the budget. The real example is Level 58 in screenshot 1: build exactly 64 on the marked cell, 8 moves left, queue 2 4 2 4 4 4. It must also say that every level's shortest solution is proven before it ships. Alongside that: free in full (price.value 'Free — optional theme packs & undo tokens'), no ads, no account, the working App Store badge, and the QR on desktop.

The default page this refuses: The mobile-puzzle landing page: a candy gradient or a dark glossy backdrop, bouncy rounded type, floating 3D tiles and confetti, a centred phone mockup, a laurel-and-stars 'Addictive!' strip, a stat row and a feature-card grid. 2048-likes add a beige-and-orange tile grid in a rounded sans. The incumbent already ships a version of this: cream page, serif H1 on the left, amber gameplay phone on the right, a badge row.

THE ROLL

The Amber Race

The mill race as built, seen from directly above, which is exactly what the app icon draws: the plank-lined headrace from weir to wheel, its sluice gate set in stop-log grooves, the staff gauge bolted to the race wall, the miller's painted toll board. Water colour comes from the app's own amber-liquid level screens (screenshots 1, 3, 5) and from peat-stained races that run tea-amber. The FAQ supplies the mapping: 'a steady flow arriving at one point… keep the channel clear while you build the delivery.' This is the list's one literal reading, committed fully.

The page is one millrace followed downstream. You enter at the red-orange inlet gate, where the queue of arriving tiles waits and the download sits, and the page flows reach by reach to the green vault gate where the delivery is made: the icon scaled into a site. It refuses the category's glossy phone-in-a-gradient hero and the incumbent's copy-left/phone-right split.

  • #F0C77A
  • #3B2616
  • #1F1209

Type
Rokkitt 600/700/800 (@fontsource/rokkitt, variable 100–900, ~13 KB per latin weight). A Memphis-model slab whose square serifs read as letters routed into a plank or cast on gate gear. Sets the H1 on water (104px desktop / 46px mobile, 800, -0.01em), every beam title (40px / 28px, 700, #F7E4BF on walnut), the staff-gauge depths and tile numerals (600, tabular lining). with Alegreya Sans 400/500/700 (@fontsource/alegreya-sans, ~24 KB per weight). A humanist sans with calligraphic warmth that holds long paragraphs on a mid-tone ground. Body 19px/1.6 on water at 68ch; captions 15px 500; the price statement 20px 700 on the inlet beam., None. Budgets, odds and counts use Rokkitt tabular figures; no mono anywhere.
Light
Looking straight down into a plank-lined race at midday. The water is tea-amber and lit through to the plank floor, with walnut walls on either side and painted gate beams casting soft shadows on the surface. Light scheme only (color-scheme: light).
Signature
'The gate.' In the how_it_works reach, one inline SVG holds 1,000 tiny amber squares, one per candidate level, floating upstream of four stop-log grooves. Each step is a stop-log. As a step scrolls into view, IntersectionObserver adds .seated and its log drops 24px into the groove in 220ms. When the fourth is seated, the field sinks to 6% opacity except a handful of squares that pass under the gate and stay lit, captioned 'Roughly one to eight candidates in a thousand survive, depending on the chapter.' Which squares pass is illustrative and labelled so. No-JS: the logs render seated, the field already sunk, the survivors lit, and every step's text present. Reduced motion: final state at once, no drops.
Remembered as
A website that was a wooden water channel full of amber water. Numbered tiles were queued against a red-orange gate where the download button was, and a green gate at the bottom 'delivered' it to my phone. A thousand little squares went into the sluice and about eight came out.
Risk
This is the literal reading. It can tip into theme-park water and turn the page into a picture of the icon, so every reach must work as set text on water, with beams carrying real headings and actions. A long amber drench tires the eye on dense sections, which is why tables and FAQ answers move to oak and shallows. The world sits close to the app's own amber screens; that helps recognition but risks reading as one giant screenshot. The narrow single channel leaves wide desktop margins quiet by design. A linen bank must never creep in, or the page falls into the cream cluster.

Navigation

The headrace beam: wordmark and icon (linking to top) and five anchor links set into the walnut in #F7E4BF type. On mobile a 'Menu' peg opens a <details> drop, a walnut board hanging under the beam with the same links at 20px, and needs no JS. The beam scrolls away with the page; the sticky inlet bar is the only pinned element. Focus is a 3px #1F1209 ring with a 2px #F7E4BF gap on water, inverted on walnut.

Motion

Everything moves downstream or not at all. In the hero reach only, the caustic layer drifts down 1,400px in 40s (linear, looping) and the queue tiles bob 2px on a 6s ease-in-out loop. Stop-logs drop once, vertically, and the sticky inlet bar rises from the bottom edge in 220ms. Beams, gauge and text never animate, and nothing fades in on scroll. prefers-reduced-motion: still water, static tiles, logs already seated.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the five alternatives pages (Threes, KAMI 2, Flow Free, Two Dots, Suika Game) are a quieter side race: the same walnut walls and headrace beam nav. The page title sits on a walnut beam (Rokkitt 800, 44px / 30px). The reading column is the shallows (#F0C77A) in Alegreya Sans 400 19px/1.65 at 66ch, ink 11.5:1, with no caustics and no tiles. Alternatives pages open with two short beams naming each game and what it asks ('Millrace: deliver one exact value' / 'Threes: survive an endless board'). The table is set on oak with walnut heads, the FAQ is <details> rows split by plank seams, and the page closes on a small inlet beam with the badge. Privacy opens with the staff gauge reading the transparency row, linked to /transparency/. Support is the millwright's plate: email, response time and restore-purchase steps.

Walnut for sections, red-orange for the inlet, green for the vault · Floating tiles: glossy amber blocks (top face #F9D27A to #F0B548, 6px side #C98A28, radius 10px) with Rokkitt numerals, used only where a tile is real information · Stop-logs: four horizontal oak boards (#9A6A3A grain) seated in iron grooves at the gate · Staff gauge: a white-enamel depth board (#F4F1EA, ink 16:1) with black E-graduations, bolted to the left wall · The miller's toll board: a painted walnut sign with #F7E4BF lettering and ruled price lines · A recessed walnut plate inside the inlet beam that seats Apple's black badge with its clear space; a white enamel plate for the QR

Type rationale

Two families, about 110 KB across six files. The slab belongs to timber and cast iron, and the humanist sans to the person reading on the bank. Neither is a training default, and no sibling microsite uses either.

New assets needed

None. Walls, water, beams, logs, gauge and tiles are CSS and inline SVG. It uses assets/icons/millrace.png, the nine screenshots and assets/qr/millrace.svg. The board replica copies only what screenshot 1 shows (Level 58 mid-game) and is captioned as such.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

Turn the Card

Boxed single-player logic games and their challenge decks, such as Binary Arts/ThinkFun's Rush Hour (1996) and its stablemates. One board and a deck of numbered challenge cards graded in colour tiers from Beginner to Expert, setup on the front and solution on the back, in a vacuum-formed tray inside the box with a folded rule sheet. Lineage only: no ThinkFun names, trade dress or card art.

Every Millrace level is a challenge card whose front is the closed problem and whose back is its proof. The page lays one card on the box tray, lets you turn it over, and unfolds the rule sheet beneath. It refuses the phone-mockup hero: the product's real claim, a proven shortest solution, is printed on the back of a card.

Type
Gabarito 800/900 (@fontsource/gabarito, ~20 KB per weight). A sturdy geometric with open counters and toy-box weight whose numerals hold both at card-corner size (24px) and at 120px. Its name is Portuguese for 'answer key'. Sets the tray-printed H1 (88px desktop / 40px mobile, 900), card indices, tier bands and rule-sheet panel titles (36px, 800). with Figtree 400/600 (@fontsource/figtree, ~11 KB per weight). A plain, friendly geometric grotesque for rule-sheet instructions at 18px/1.6 and card copy at 15–16px, with 600 for card facts and the price statement., None. Moves, budgets and odds use Gabarito tabular figures.
Light
A kitchen table by a window in daylight, the game box open on its cobalt plastic tray and the first card already dealt on white card stock. Light scheme (color-scheme: light): the tray is a saturated mid-dark ground, but every reading surface is white card.
Signature
'Turn it over.' The hero card is a <button aria-pressed> holding two faces. Click, tap or Enter turns it on the Y axis (CSS 3D, rotateY 180°, 520ms, perspective 1200px) to reveal the back. The back reads: 'Shortest solution: 5 moves, proven by breadth-first search over every position. Budget: 7. Random play wins this card 1.31% of the time, computed exactly. All 280 thoughtless strategies fail it.' It carries the green 'proven' seal, and a second press turns it back. The fanned tier cards turn the same way to show each chapter's depth and budget. No-JS: without html.js, front and back render as two cards side by side (stacked on mobile) labelled 'Front' and 'Back' on the tray, so every word is visible. Reduced motion: the faces swap with no rotation.
Remembered as
A blue game-box page with one white challenge card in the middle. I turned it over, and the back said the shortest solution was 5 moves, proven, and that random play wins 1.31% of the time.
Risk
Familiar: a challenge-card deck is the first physical analogue anyone reaches for with a level-based puzzle. That is why it tops the list and also why it is the least surprising, and ThinkFun's trade dress must be kept at arm's length. Six tier colours on a cobalt tray can read juvenile, louder than the studio's calm voice. The card diagram is only as honest as the level data behind it, and the turn is the page's single proof device, so it must stay fast and keyboard-operable. The triptych hero must not collapse into a copy/product split at mid widths.

App Store route

The Smart App Banner sits in head. The official badge is printed on a white sticker block on the tray, never redrawn: black on white with clear space. The QR shares that sticker on desktop (≥1024px) only. The price statement is price.value, set in Gabarito on the sticker. Sticky bar: when the sticker leaves the viewport, a 60px cobalt rim strip rises from the bottom with the icon, 'Millrace · Free, no ads' (Figtree 600 16px white) and the badge 40px, and hides over the closing block. The plans reappear as the rule sheet's price panel. Closing CTA: 'The other 63 cards are on the App Store', with the deck back lying face-down on the tray beside the badge, QR and price. The comparison's inline CTA is a badge strip printed under the table.

Page sequence

  1. Tray rim strip: icon, wordmark, pre_headline as descriptor, six index-tab anchor links
  2. Hero: H1 printed on the tray; Card 1 (Warm-up) in its well with the deck's 64 stepped edges; hero.secondary at left; the price/badge/QR sticker at right
  3. The same card turned over (signature): Level 1's proof. Shortest solution 5 moves, proven by breadth-first search; budget 7; random play wins 1.31%, computed exactly; all 280 no-lookahead strategies fail it. Carries the green 'proven' seal
  4. Rule-sheet panel 'Millrace in one paragraph': quick_answer as the visible Quick Answer (speakable), then the ai-canonical Quick reference <details> as a folded flap whose summary is always visible
  5. Panel titled with about_heading (anchor: rules): the body's opening paragraphs and hero.subheadline, with two cards lying on the sheet edge, 'Blocked inlet' and 'Overshoot', each a card-front diagram with its sentence from features[1]. Diagrams are labelled illustrative
  6. Panel 'The deck' (anchor: deck): the six chapters as six tier cards fanned on the tray, overlapping at ±6° (a fan, not a grid). Each face shows tier, level count, proven shortest (5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10–16) and budget range from the journal table. value_points[2] sits under the fan
  7. Panel carrying how_it_works.heading (anchor: proof): the intro and the four steps as a numbered 1–4 diagram strip (real order, HowTo): candidate card, solver, 280 strategies, tier. Journal figures sit in the margin: one to eight in a thousand survive; random-play ceiling 2%
  8. Panel 'What's in the box': features (9) as the box-side contents list with tick boxes, plus value_points 0, 1 and 3 as three lines printed on the box side
  9. Screenshot strip: the nine screens in iPhone bezels on the tray in a horizontal scroll-snap row, with captions as printed labels
  10. Panel carrying example_insights.heading (overline dropped): the intro, then the five Coach and Hint lines as small tip cards along the sheet edge, each tag on a tier band
  11. Panel 'Prices' (anchor: prices): plans as a printed price list. Free first, marked 'The whole game', with its seven inclusions; then Theme packs, Complete Collection and Undo bundles, followed by plans_footnote and pricing_note
  12. Panel 'Compare' (anchor: compare): comparison_table intro, the ruled table with the Millrace column on a sky band, the footnote, a badge strip, and alternatives_to linking the five /alternatives/ pages
  13. Panel 'Who it's for': who_for and who_not_for as two columns of tick and cross boxes
  14. Panel carrying the founder heading as H2 (overline dropped): bio, signals with the count computed, support email and response time, and the studio backstory link
  15. Panel 'Questions' (anchor: faq): ten <details> rows
  16. Panel 'Nothing in this box is collected' (privacy): app_privacy_label, the notes, transparency-row values, and links to /transparency/, the privacy policy and support
  17. Related journal panel: link to the essay on how the levels are made
  18. 'You might also like': other Lagerland apps as small icon chips on the tray
  19. Closing tray: the deck back face-down with badge, QR and price; the maker/freshness line printed on the rim
  20. Shared Lagerland footer strip

Navigation

The tray's rim strip carries six index tabs (white card, 4px tier-colour top edge in chapter order), as plain anchor links. Past the hero the strip pins to the top at 48px on cobalt, and the tab for the panel in view lifts 4px. On mobile the tabs become a horizontal scroll row under the wordmark. Focus is a 3px white ring with a 2px cobalt offset on the tray, and a 3px ink ring on cards.

Motion

Cards move like cards. A turn is on the Y axis (520ms, cubic-bezier(.3,.7,.2,1)). On first view the six tier cards deal from the deck's position along a short arc, 60ms apart and 260ms each (html.js only; the static fan is the default), and the sticky rim strip rises in 200ms. Nothing loops, floats or parallaxes. prefers-reduced-motion: no deal, and the turn becomes an instant face swap.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the five alternatives pages show only the rule sheet on the tray, with no hero card; the tab rim strip stays. The title is printed on a tier band at the sheet's head (Gabarito 800, 44px / 30px), and the reading column is the white sheet in Figtree 400 18px/1.65 at 66ch, ink 17:1. Alternatives pages open with two cards face-up: Millrace's Card 1 and a plain typographic card for the competitor ('Threes · endless board · next-tile hint'), with no competitor art or logos. Then come the real table, the honest verdict as two tick-box columns, FAQ <details> and a badge strip. Support is a 'Missing a piece?' panel with email, response time and restore-purchase steps. Privacy opens with a 'Contents of this box' list that reads the transparency row (data collected: none · tracking domains: 0 · third-party SDKs: 0 · account: none), linked to /transparency/.

Cobalt vacuum-formed tray: flat #23408E with a moulded well around the hero card (inset shadow 0 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.25), 1px top highlight, 24px radii) · White card stock with die-cut 14px corners, a 1px #E6E2D8 edge and a soft 0 10px 24px shadow on the tray · The deck stack under the hero card: 64 stepped 1px edges whose colours follow the real chapter sizes (4 sky, 12 green, 12 yellow, 12 orange, 12 teal, 12 black) · Tier bands: a 44px coloured band across each card's top with the tier name and card number · Flat-printed board diagrams: cells #EDE7DA, amber tiles with ink numerals, the inlet as a red-orange bar on its edge cell, the vault as a green bar with the target ghosted in its cell · The rule sheet: one long white sheet with accordion creases (1px line + 24px soft gradient) between panels, each panel headed by a tier-coloured band · A round green 'proven' seal printed on card backs

SECOND ROLL

Par Is Proven

Golf's paper: the club scorecard and the tour yardage book. The scorecard has HOLE, YARDS, PAR and STROKE INDEX rows, OUT and IN subtotal columns, the marker's and player's signature boxes, and local rules printed on the back. The yardage book is a pocket book with a measured plan of every hole and distances pencilled to the yard. It is grounded in the app's own copy, 'the par you are chasing is a computed fact rather than an estimate'. Tee red and the green are the app's inlet and vault colours.

The page is the scorecard for a 64-hole course whose par was computed, not assigned. The hero prints the PAR row across all 64 holes (five, five, five, five, then twelve sixes, through to 10–16), and the rest of the page is the back of the card and the yardage book. It refuses the gradient-and-phone puzzle page for a document a player fills in with a pencil.

  • #FBFBF8
  • #1C5B3A
  • #121412
  • #4F5357
  • #CFE3B8
  • #C7372B
  • #F3C318
Type
Antonio 700 (@fontsource/antonio, ~11 KB). A bold condensed gothic in the line of the Trade Gothic Bold Condensed headers printed on scorecards, narrow enough to fit 64 hole numbers across one row. Sets the uppercase H1 (128px/0.9 desktop, 58px mobile), the row labels HOLE, PAR, MAX and YOU, and section heads (44px). with News Cycle 400/700 (@fontsource/news-cycle, ~13 KB per weight). A News Gothic revival, the face of printed tickets, forms and scorecard small print. Body 18px/1.6, local rules 17px, table cells 15px with 700 for figures., Kalam 400 (@fontsource/kalam, ~22 KB). A pencil hand used only where a person writes on the card: the Coach and Hint lines pencilled into the yardage-book margin (real app strings) and the marker's initials. Never for any number the page asserts.
Light
A player at the first tee on a bright overcast morning, card and pencil in hand: cool white card stock printed in two inks, course green and black, with grey pencil marks. Light scheme only (color-scheme: light).
Signature
'Hole by hole.' Every hole number on THE CARD is a focusable button. Hovering, focusing or tapping one fills its column fairway-green, drops a flag-yellow marker above it, and writes a readout under the card such as 'Hole 23 · Pressure · par 7, proven · max 8–9'. The readout uses chapter values now, and per-hole target, arrivals, exact budget and random-play odds once the level table is supplied. Arrow keys move along the row. Chapter brackets jump to the yardage pages, and holes 1, 44 and 58 have full pages. No-JS: the card is a complete, readable <table> with th scope, the readout line shows the key statically, and the links still jump. Reduced motion: the column fills with no transition.
Remembered as
A golf scorecard for a 64-hole course. The par row went five, five, five, five, then sixes and sevens, and it said par was proven by a computer. Tactics plays to par 72, and the download button was in the signature box.
Risk
Golf is a borrowed world with country-club connotations a puzzle audience may not share, and the metaphor has seams. The move budget is not golf's maximum-score rule, so the card must define Par and Max right under the grid. A 64-hole row is dense at 1440 (~16px cells), and the page depends on folding cleanly into chapter strips on mobile. An uppercase condensed H1 can shout against the studio's calm voice. If the rules, folds and pencil are weak, white card and green ink collapse into a generic form.

Page sequence

  1. Card header strip: icon, wordmark, pre_headline folded into the descriptor line, five uppercase anchor links
  2. Hero: H1 (hero.headline) in condensed green caps; hero.secondary as one line
  3. THE CARD (anchor: card): the 64-hole scorecard with HOLE, CHAPTER, PAR, MAX and a blank YOU row, chapter subtotals (20 · 72 · 84 · 96 · 108 · —) and the key line. This is the signature interaction
  4. Signature box row: PRICE (price.value), DOWNLOAD (badge), SCAN (QR, desktop)
  5. Course description box: quick_answer as the visible Quick Answer (speakable), then the ai-canonical Quick reference <details> as the card's folded flap, summary visible
  6. LOCAL RULES on the back of the card (anchor: rules; about_heading as the panel title): the body's opening paragraphs and hero.subheadline set as rules. 'The inlet': block it and the next arrival has nowhere to land. 'Exact delivery': overshoot and the value is gone. 'Max': the budget, never more than two over par and equal to it on two levels. 'Nothing is random': the whole queue is in view. 'Freeplay': the endless board, no par
  7. HOW PAR IS SET (how_it_works.heading; anchor: par): the intro and the four steps numbered 1–4 (real order, HowTo) down a ruled column, each with its detail. The margin carries the journal's figures: 280 strategies, 2% random-play ceiling, one to eight in a thousand survive
  8. THE YARDAGE BOOK: three featured holes as pocket-book pages in ink line with measured callouts, each beside its real screenshot in an iPhone bezel. Hole 1 (Warm-up): exactly 16, 3 arriving, par 5, max 7, random play 1.31%. Hole 44 (Deep Water): exactly 64, 9 arriving, par 9. Hole 58 (Mastery): screenshot 1's mid-round position, exactly 64, 8 moves left
  9. Course notes: value_points (4) as four ruled notes with headings
  10. The caddie (example_insights.heading, overline dropped): the intro, then the five Coach and Hint lines pencilled in Kalam in the yardage-book margin, each with its tag and its body in News Cycle
  11. On the course: screenshots 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 in a horizontal scroll-snap strip with printed captions
  12. Course facilities: features (9) as a ruled two-column list
  13. FEES (anchor: fees): 'Green fee: none' is the Free plan, with its seven inclusions and highlight_label. Then the pro-shop list: Theme packs $1.99 each (four packs), Complete Collection $5.99, Undo bundles 10/50/200 with streak payouts. plans_footnote and pricing_note follow as small print
  14. OTHER COURSES (anchor: compare): comparison_table as a ruled scorecard grid with the Millrace column on fairway, the dated footnote, a DOWNLOAD box, and alternatives_to linking the five /alternatives/ pages
  15. Members / Not for you: who_for and who_not_for as two ruled columns
  16. The course designer (founder, overline dropped): heading, bio, signals with the count computed, support email and response time, studio backstory link
  17. QUESTIONS (anchor: faq): ten <details> rows ruled like card rows
  18. Local rule, nothing leaves your pocket (privacy): app_privacy_label, the notes, the transparency-row figures, and links to /transparency/, the privacy policy and support
  19. Related journal: 'How the par is proven', linking the essay (related_journal.anchor as the link text)

Navigation

The card's header strip: wordmark and five uppercase anchor links in Antonio 700, green on white, with a 2px green underline on hover and focus. It is not sticky; the box-row bar is the only pinned element. On mobile, 'Menu' opens a <details> panel ruled like a card row, with the links at 20px. Focus is a 3px #1C5B3A outline with a 2px white offset everywhere, and focusable table cells also take the fairway fill.

Motion

Paper does not move. The only motion: the hole-column fill (120ms), the flag marker settling 6px (160ms) and the sticky box row sliding up (200ms). The readout swaps text with no animation. There are no scroll reveals and no counters. prefers-reduced-motion: fills and the sticky row appear instantly.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the five alternatives pages are the back of the card: the same header strip, then the title in Antonio 700 uppercase green (48px / 32px) under a crease. The reading column is the card itself in News Cycle 400 18px/1.65 at 66ch, black ink 17.9:1, with section heads in Antonio 700 28px green and tables ruled like the scorecard. Alternatives pages open with a two-player card: 'MILLRACE | THREES' columns with the rows What a game asks · Measure of success · Ads · Price · Privacy label, and a fairway fill on Millrace's column. After it come the existing comparison, the verdict as 'Play Millrace if / Play Threes if' columns, FAQ <details> and a DOWNLOAD box. Privacy opens with a 'Local rule' box that reads the transparency row and links to /transparency/. Support is 'Ask the starter': email, response time and restore-purchase steps.

Materials

Cool white card stock with a fine paper tooth (inline SVG noise at 3%) and fold creases where a scorecard folds (1px line + 16px soft shadow) · A heavily ruled scorecard grid: 1.5px green outer rules, 0.75px inner rules, condensed caps row labels, and a subtotal column after each chapter · Pencil: graphite strokes in Kalam #4F5357 and pencil underlines drawn as SVG paths with a jittered stroke · Yardage-book drawings: a featured level's board in 1.5px ink line, fairway-green empty cells, amber tile squares with ink numerals, a red tee marker at the inlet edge, a yellow flag pinned in the vault, and measured callouts in the margin (par, max, arrivals) · The signature box row: three ruled boxes (MARKER · PLAYER · DATE on a real card) used as PRICE · DOWNLOAD · SCAN · A punched hole with a pencil loop at the card's top-left corner (CSS), the only ornament

Colour strategy

Restrained · light

Type rationale

About 60 KB across four files. A condensed gothic plus News Gothic is how scorecards are actually printed, and the pencil marks the one thing on a card that is not printed. No sibling uses any of the three.

New assets needed

Data, not art: the 64-row level table (target, arrivals, proven shortest, budget, random-play odds) and the start positions of Levels 1 and 44, exported from the app's level library. Until then the card prints only what is already sourced: par by chapter (exactly 5 to 9; 10–16 for Mastery), max by chapter range, and the subtotals. The yardage pages draw only the tiles visible in screenshots 1, 2 and 4, with inlet and vault placement marked 'illustrative layout' where not visible. Otherwise it uses the existing icon, nine screenshots and QR.

Fixes queued before this style is built (3)
  • blockerRe-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.
  • majorAdd one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).
  • majorMake it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

Or the category standard, played straight: a molten-amber gradient page with glossy 3D tiles floating around a centred iPhone playing Level 58. Above it, 'Sixty-four levels. One inlet. Nothing is random.' with the App Store badge and QR. Below, a four-stat row (64 levels · 6 chapters · 17 themes · 0 ads), a feature-card grid, the comparison table, then the FAQ.

WanderWiki

/apps/wanderwiki/ + its privacy and support pages + 2 comparison pages

What the page must prove: Three things in one screen. (1) The offer: Wikipedia as a swipe deck on iPhone, in 33 language editions, with three modes, no ads and no account. (2) One thing no rival can show: the native category mapping (German + Science gives Wissenschaft, Physik, Chemie, not 'Science' translated), or the 33 editions present in their own scripts. (3) The action and the price: the official badge (plus the QR on desktop), 'Free 3-day trial, then $1.99/mo, $8.99/yr or $24.99 lifetime', and 'iPhone, iOS 18.2+'.

The default page this refuses: The 'knowledge app' page: a deep navy starfield with a glowing globe, gold sparkles and an open book ('Unlock a universe of knowledge'), two iPhone mockups of fanned swipe cards on the right, 'the TikTok of Wikipedia', a badge row, then three equal feature cards (Random / For You / Today) and an FAQ. The app's own icon (puzzle globe, orbit swoosh, gold stars, open book) already sits in this rut, and the app UI's black full-bleed cards pull towards it.

Today's page, for comparison

WanderWikiBricolage Grotesque

Swipe Wikipedia in 33 languages. Ad-free.

THE ROLL

Par Avion

International airmail stationery under the Universal Postal Union, whose working language is French. The air letter or aerogramme: one prepaid pale-blue sheet that folds into its own envelope, with printed dashed fold lines, 'Fold here · Plier ici' and 'No enclosures' warnings. Also the blue PAR AVION label with its English or national-language line, red-and-blue chevron borders, perforated stamp sheets with marginal inscriptions, the round date cancel, and the convention that an address is written the way the destination reads it, with only the country line in a lingua franca. Grammar only: no postal operator's name, post horn, crown or real stamp design.

The page is one air letter unfolded. Wikipedia arrives from 33 editions, each addressed the way its own edition reads (German + Science goes to Wissenschaft, Physik, Chemie, not to 'Science' translated). The editions are a sheet of stamps, 'no enclosures' is the no-ads rule, and the App Store badge delivers the app to your iPhone. It refuses the starry-globe 'universe of knowledge' page with fanned phone mockups, and the white Wikipedia look-alike.

Type
Bricolage Grotesque, variable (@fontsource-variable/bricolage-grotesque, the opsz + wght file, latin 77 KB). The H1 is set at opsz 96 / 800: 112px on desktop, 48px on mobile. Panel titles use opsz 72 / 700 at 44–56px. PAR AVION labels and the stamp codes (de, fi, ja) are caps at opsz 24 / 800, tracked +0.06em. Prices and dates use tabular figures. with Ysabeau Office 400 and 600 (@fontsource/ysabeau-office, latin 31 KB for both). The letter body is 19px/1.6 on desktop and 17px on mobile; label small print is 14px 600. The cyrillic (9 KB), greek (6 KB), latin-ext (15 KB) and vietnamese (6 KB) slices load through unicode-range only where an endonym needs them., None; no monospace. Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai, Han, kana and Hangul endonyms use the visitor's system faces.
Light
A reader at a kitchen table by a north-facing window in soft morning daylight, opening the day's post over coffee → light.
Signature
'Affix a stamp.' The 33 stamps are <button aria-pressed> elements in a CSS-grid sheet. Activating one runs about 1 KB of vanilla JS that copies its data-endonym, data-code, data-domain and (once gathered) data-articles onto the address label in 'Addressed the way they read it', for example '日本語 · ja.wikipedia.org · JAPANESE'. The violet cancel re-strikes over the chosen stamp (scale 1.06→1, 160ms) and an aria-live line announces the change. German keeps its eight real category names; other editions show their domain and size, never made-up category names. No-JS fallback: the sheet is a static, fully readable list of 33 editions with codes and domains, and the label shows the documented German address. Reduced motion: the label text swaps with no strike.
Remembered as
The pale-blue air-letter page where the 33 Wikipedia languages were a sheet of stamps, and the German one was addressed to Wissenschaft, Physik, Chemie.
Risk
Airmail is a well-worn nostalgia motif and turns twee if the chevrons spread, so they stay on the sheet edge and the sticky strip only. AllPaid's 'Security Tint Envelope' already owns an envelope, a back flap and a postmark ring for release dates, so this style keeps strictly to the pale-blue air letter (no window, no tint lattice, no release-date postmark). The pale ground limits red to type of 24px and up. The stamp read-out stays thin until the 33 article counts are gathered. The H1 'Swipe. Learn. Repeat.' does not say 'Wikipedia', so the tagline directly under it is load-bearing.

App Store route

The official badge is always mounted, unaltered, on label white beside a PAR AVION label, which is the world's sign for 'send this'. It appears in the hero postage block, after the stamp sheet, on the postage tariff and on the back flap. On screens 900px and wider the QR sits in a white franking box ('Scan to deliver it to your iPhone') next to the badge in the same three places. The sticky bar is a 56px airmail-blue label strip with a 4px chevron top edge. It slides up once the hero postage block leaves the viewport and shows 'PAR AVION' caps, 'WanderWiki · Free 3-day trial, then from $1.99/mo' in white, and the badge at 40px. The price statement is price.value restated as postage in the hero. The full tariff is the plans table, with plans_footnote as its small print. Smart App Banner meta goes in the head (app-id=6758459119). There are no ratings or reviews.

Page sequence

  1. Address side (hero): the From line, the PAR AVION label, the icon stamp with its date cancel, the H1 'Swipe. Learn. Repeat.', the tagline, hero.secondary, the German address (proof drawn from features[0] and example_insights[2]), and the postage block (price.value statement, badge, QR).
  2. First inside panel, where the letter opens: quick_answer at 22px as the letter's first paragraph (speakable). Beneath it, the Quick reference <details> styled as a CN 22-type 'Contents declared' form: the summary row is always visible and all the ai-canonical text is in the DOM.
  3. 'The day's post': the three modes as three rows, each marked by its own round cancel (RANDOM / FOR YOU / ON THIS DAY), using features[1–3] and value_points[1]. Real cards from the preview video and screenshots (Crassula arborescens · Species of succulent; Morane-Borel monoplane · French racing aircraft; NASA · 1961) are set as a short stack of air-letter slips. 4.png and 1.png are printed on the sheet as pictorial panels, the way a pictorial aerogramme prints a picture, with corrected alts.
  4. 'Addressed the way they read it': the For You proof. Science is set against the eight real German categories as a full address label, the 10 interests appear as an address book, with '~8–12 native categories per edition'; like/dislike stays on-device (how_it_works[5]).
  5. 'Thirty-three stamps': the 33 editions as one perforated sheet in four panes, following training_vocabulary's groups (Latin-script European 20, non-Latin European 4, Asian 8, Middle Eastern 1). Each stamp shows a code and an endonym. Tapping a stamp re-addresses the label above (the signature interaction). value_points[4] gives the per-edition price, corrected to ≈ $0.76.
  6. 'Postmarked today': Today in History. The five categories form the cancel's legend (Holidays included). Verified 13 May entries replace the faulty example_insights, each under a violet year cancel. The REST path is in small print, and the Home Screen, Lock Screen and StandBy widgets are 'delivered daily' (features[3], how_it_works[6–7]).
  7. 'Poste restante' (held for collection): saved offline articles and folders ('flights', 'before-bed', 'philosophy'; example_insights[3]), the calm reading view, CC BY-SA attribution inline (features[4–5]), and 5.png (Liked/Saved) as a pictorial panel.
  8. 'Tracking': the how_it_works intro and its 8 steps as a numbered tracking history, from 'edition chosen' to 'widgets deliver' (HowTo schema).
  9. 'Postage': the four plans as a tariff table (Service · Rate · Included). Annual is marked as the highlight; Lifetime is 'prepaid once' with Family Sharing. plans_footnote is the tariff's small print, and the badge and QR are repeated on a label-white mount.
  10. 'Secrecy of correspondence': privacy (data collected none, no tracking, no account) and privacy.notes, alongside the transparency record's facts (0 SDKs, 0 tracking domains, network to Wikipedia's public API only, no analytics, the required-reason APIs) linked to /transparency/#wanderwiki. Includes 'not affiliated with the Wikimedia Foundation' and links to the privacy policy and support.
  11. 'Other carriers': comparison_table as a carriers' chart (13 rows × WanderWiki / WikiCards / Wiki Rabbit / Wikipedia official) with its intro and footnote, links to /alternatives/wikipedia-app/ and /alternatives/kiwix/, and an inline badge.
  12. 'Deliver to / Return to sender': who_for (6) as the delivery list. who_not_for (4) and plateau_disclosure (rule, what_it_does_not_do, notes) appear as a violet return-to-sender stamp with ticked reasons, each naming the better carrier.
  13. 'A letter from the sender': the founder story (Lagerland Apps, Finland, heading 'Wikipedia, the way Random Article used to feel.'), the signals as a P.S. list with the live-app count computed rather than hard-coded, the response time, the support email, and a link to /lagerland-apps/.
  14. 'Enquiries': the 13 FAQ as <details> rows (FAQPage schema).
  15. 'Further reading': the journal posts reading-without-a-feed (related_journal) and wikipedia-is-different-in-every-language.

The return address is the maker/freshness line: 'Built by Lagerland Apps, Finland · first released 1 Feb 2026 · last updated 13 May 2026'. 'Also from this sender' lists the other live apps (computed) as small stamps. Then comes the shared Lagerland strip.

Navigation

The top flap is the microsite's whole nav: the wordmark (back to the top of the sheet) and five links (Modes, Editions, Postage, Privacy, Questions). Every fold line names the panel below it, so scrolling reads like unfolding. On mobile, 'Contents' opens a fold-down panel listing every panel of the sheet as links; Esc or a second tap closes it. Focus is a 3px sheet-ink outline offset 3px; stamps also get a red perforation ring.

Motion

Paper-physical and brief. A panel's dashed fold line draws once as it enters (stroke-dashoffset, 300ms). The cancel strikes once when the Today-in-History panel enters (scale 1.04→1, 160ms). The sticky label slides up in 220ms ease-out, and stamps lift 2px on hover. There is no parallax, no floating envelope, no loop and no count-up. With prefers-reduced-motion everything is static and the sticky strip simply appears.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the two alternatives pages are single letters on the same sheet. Each keeps the top flap nav, the chevron edge (sides on desktop, top on mobile) and a short address strip as masthead; on /alternatives/kiwix/ the strip reads 'To: readers comparing Kiwix · WanderWiki vs Kiwix'. The reading column is a label-white letter panel set in Ysabeau 400 at 18px/1.65 with a 68ch measure, and quick_answer opens the letter at 21px. Comparison tables are set as tariff tables. 'Pick WanderWiki if… / Use Kiwix if…' become Deliver-to and Return-to-sender lists. The privacy policy runs under 'Secrecy of correspondence', with the transparency record's facts in a declaration-form box. Support is 'Write to us': the email as an address label, response_time, and what to include.

Materials

Air-letter sheet: flat aerogramme blue, divided into panels by printed 2px dashed fold lines (#7F96B6) captioned in 12px caps 'FOLD HERE · PLIER ICI' plus the name of the panel below · Chevron edge: red and blue parallelograms (24×8px at 45°) separated by sheet-blue gaps, as a 14px edge down the left and right page edges on desktop and along the top on mobile. It is the sheet's own border, never a callout · Perforated stamps: label-white stamp paper with a CSS radial-gradient perforation mask (8px holes, 12px pitch) and a 4px printed inner frame. The sheet margin carries an inscription and a sheet number · PAR AVION label: an airmail-blue rectangle with a 6px radius, 'PAR AVION' over 'BY AIR MAIL' in white. It appears only where the action lives · Round date cancel: inline SVG, a 2px violet ring with arc text and three wavy cancellation bars, struck at 8° · Address label: label white, with four 1px ruled address lines 48px apart; the last line is the 'country' line in caps · Declaration form (CN 22 grammar): a 1px ink grid, 14px checkbox squares and 12px caps field labels · Return-to-sender stamp: a violet rectangular stamp with ticked reason boxes

Colour strategy

Committed. Aerogramme blue is the ground of every surface. Airmail blue and red carry the sheet edge, the labels and the primary action. Cancel violet is used only for dates and cancels. Label white is reserved for stamps, the address label, forms and the badge mount. · light

Type rationale

Bricolage Grotesque comes from the French grotesque line of Antique Olive, and the UPU prints its labels in French. Its optical-size axis gives the tight, characterful cut for 'Par avion' and the H1 and calm small sizes for stamp codes, from one file. Ysabeau Office is a humanist sans built on Garamond bones with real Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese (checked: Č ě ő ș ț ế ệ), so Русский, Українська, Ελληνικά, Čeština and Tiếng Việt sit on the stamp sheet in one design. Leaving the other seven scripts to the system costs 0 bytes and shows each script in the face its own readers' phones already use. Budget: about 108 KB base, about 145 KB with every slice.

New assets needed

No raster art. Built in code: the chevron edge (CSS), the perforation mask (CSS), the cancel (inline SVG with textPath) and the labels (HTML/CSS). Data: approximate article counts for all 33 editions (List of Wikipedias, dated) to complete the stamp read-out (16 of the 33 have no figure in the journal post); a verified 13 May On This Day snapshot to replace example_insights; corrected screenshot alts.

Picked
WanderWikiAlumni Sans

Swipe. Learn. Repeat.

Swipe Wikipedia in 33 languages. Ad-free.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

Today's Leaf

The tear-off day calendar: the Soviet отрывной календарь and the German Abreißkalender, whose leaf backs carried a short article, an anniversary or a recipe and continued long pieces 'on the next leaf'; the Finnish almanac's day rows; and the American Page-A-Day block. Its grammar: a thick block of thin leaves glued under a printed binding strip, on a coloured backing card with a punched hanging hole. Each leaf has a perforation row, a giant condensed date numeral over the month and weekday, Sundays and holidays printed red, and reading on the reverse.

The page is the day's leaf of a tear-off block: the front is a date and what happened on it, from Wikipedia's On This Day feed; the back is a short piece of reading; and every section below is the next leaf. It is a finite block you tear through and put down, not a feed. It refuses the starry 'universe of knowledge' phone page and the infinite card feed.

  • #E8622A
  • #FBFBF8
  • #161616
  • #CC1F1F
  • #5B5A55
  • #B9B6AD
  • #B94A1D
Type
Alumni Sans, variable (@fontsource-variable/alumni-sans, wght 100–900, latin 22 KB). The date numeral is set at 900: 400px on desktop, 210px on mobile. The month is 800 at 52px; the weekday is 700 at 26px. The H1 is 800 at 72px on desktop and 34px on mobile; leaf titles are 800 at 44px and 30px. The card header and binding strip are 600 caps tracked +0.08em. Years and prices use tabular figures. with Piazzolla, variable (@fontsource-variable/piazzolla, wght + opsz file, latin 51 KB). Leaf-back reading is opsz 14 / 420 at 18px/1.55 on desktop and 17px on mobile; small print is opsz 8 / 500 at 13px. Cyrillic and Greek slices load only for the endonyms on the Editions leaf., None; no monospace. Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai, Han, kana and Hangul endonyms use system faces.
Light
Someone at the kitchen counter at 7 a.m. under the ceiling light, kettle on, tearing yesterday off the block hung on its orange backing card → light.
Signature
'Tear to today.' The tab on the hero leaf's perforation is rendered by JS. On tap, about 2 KB of vanilla JS requests en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/feed/onthisday/selected/MM/DD for the visitor's local date. The request is made only on click, with no cookies and nothing sent to Lagerland, and the leaf shows 'fetching' while it waits. The current leaf then tears away (transform-origin at the binding, rotateX to −14deg, translateY −60px, opacity to 0, 450ms), revealing a new leaf with today's numeral and weekday (red on a Sunday) and three real entries. Each entry links to its article with 'From Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0'. No-JS: the verified 13 May leaf stays and the tab never renders. Offline or on error, the leaf stays and small print says it couldn't reach Wikipedia. Reduced motion: the new leaf replaces the old one with no tear.
Remembered as
The orange page with a giant tear-off calendar leaf, Wednesday 13 May, that I tore to today to get real 'on this day' entries from Wikipedia; every section after it was the next leaf.
Risk
This is the most familiar of the seven: 'Today in History → day calendar' is the first association anyone makes. It is the pick because it carries the deck, the date and the finite session without explanation. The calendar must not slide into cream + serif + red; the saturated orange card, the cool white leaves, a condensed grotesque display and red reserved for Sundays and Holidays guard against that. Leaf-sized sections push the 13-row comparison and the 13 FAQs across 'continued' leaves, which means more scrolling. The opt-in live fetch is a third-party request from the site, and the owner may prefer snapshot-only. Scroll-timeline tearing runs in Chromium and Safari only.
Full style card

Left card margin (x 56–300): '33 editions' (Alumni Sans 800, 22px) over the 33 codes in two columns (en de fr es it pt nl pl fi sv da no nb cs sk hu ro hr ca tr ru uk el he ja zh ko hi vi id th ms ar) in Alumni Sans 700 20px/1.45, each linking to the Editions leaf. Centre: the block, a 760×780 leaf at x 340–1100, y 104–884, under a black 40px binding strip ('WANDERWIKI · WIKIPEDIA, ONE DAY AT A TIME', white 15px) with its perforation row; five leaf edges peek out below. On the leaf, 'MAY' (52px) sits over 'Wednesday' (26px), and the numeral '13' fills x 372–650 at 400px. To its right (x 670–1068), the H1 'Swipe. Learn. Repeat.' runs over three lines at 72px, followed by the tagline 'Swipe Wikipedia in 33 languages. Ad-free.' (Piazzolla 600 20px) and hero.secondary (17px). Across y 600–820, below a 1px rule, three On This Day entries sit in two columns, all from the verified 13 May snapshot: the year in Alumni Sans 800 at 30px, a one-line entry in Piazzolla 17px linked to its Wikipedia article, and the category (Births / Events / Selected) at 13px. At the leaf foot are the perforated line, the 'Tear to today' tab and the small print 'One request from your browser to Wikipedia; nothing comes to us.' Right card margin (x 1140–1392): the white imprint mount (252×420), holding the official badge (54px tall), 'Free 3-day trial, then $1.99/mo, $8.99/yr or $24.99 once' (Piazzolla 600 18px), the QR (140px) with 'Scan to put it on your iPhone', and 'iPhone · iOS 18.2+ · No ads · No account' (14px).

The leaf runs the full 366px width from y 56. Under the 32px binding strip comes 'MAY · Wednesday' (22px). The numeral '13' (900, 210px) takes the left 40%, with the H1 'Swipe. Learn. Repeat.' (34px/1.0, three lines) to its right. Then the tagline (17px), hero.secondary (16px, three lines), two On This Day entries (year 22px plus one line each) and the perforated foot with 'Tear to today'.
