App Store route

The badge lives on the card's white imprint mount, never on a leaf: in the hero, beside the Prices leaf and on the closing back of the block. On screens 900px and wider the QR shares the mount ('Scan to put it on your iPhone'). The sticky bar is a 60px strip of the orange backing card. It slides up from the bottom once the hero imprint leaves the viewport, with 'WanderWiki · Free 3-day trial, from $1.99/mo' in black Alumni Sans 700 on the left and a white mini-mount with the badge at 40px on the right. The price statement (price.value) is printed on the imprint. The Prices leaf sets the four plans as a ruled table, with plans_footnote as small print. Smart App Banner meta goes in the head (app-id=6758459119). There are no ratings.

Page sequence

  1. Today's leaf (hero): month, weekday and numeral; the H1, tagline and hero.secondary; three verified On This Day entries; 'Tear to today'. On the card: the 33 edition codes (value_points[0]) and the imprint (badge, QR, price.value).
  2. Leaf back, 'What this is': quick_answer as the leaf's article at 21px (speakable). Under it, the Quick reference <details> as the leaf's boxed calendar notes: the summary is visible and the ai-canonical text is in the DOM.
  3. Leaf, 'Three ways to draw a leaf': Random, For You and Today in History as three ruled rows (features[1–3], value_points[1]). Each row carries a real card from the app: for Random, 'Crassula arborescens · Species of succulent' and 'Morane-Borel monoplane · French racing aircraft' from the preview video; for Today, 'NASA · 1961' from 1.png. 4.png is printed as the leaf's halftone picture.
  4. Leaf, 'German, natively': Science set against the eight real German categories as the leaf's list (Wissenschaft … Medizin), the 10 interests, '~8–12 native categories per edition', and on-device like/dislike (features[0], features[2], example_insights[2] with its headline corrected).
  5. Leaf, 'Thirty-three editions': the endonyms in training_vocabulary's four groups, set like an almanac's name-day list (endonym · code), with the per-edition price line ($24.99 ≈ $0.76, value_points[4]).
  6. Leaf, 'Five kinds of day': Selected, Events, Births, Deaths and Holidays (Holidays printed red), the REST path in small print, and the Home Screen, Lock Screen and StandBy widgets that put out a fresh leaf daily (features[3], how_it_works[6–7]).
  7. Leaf, 'Kept leaves': offline saving and folders ('flights', 'before-bed', 'philosophy'), the calm reading view, CC BY-SA attribution inline, and 5.png (Liked/Saved) as the halftone picture (features[4–5], example_insights[3]).
  8. Two leaves, 'How a session goes': the how_it_works intro and steps 1–4, then 'continued on the next leaf' for steps 5–8 (HowTo schema).
  9. Leaf, 'Prices': Free trial $0 (3 days, no card) · Monthly $1.99 · Annual $8.99 (highlight) · Lifetime $24.99 once ('Best long-term value', Family Sharing), with plans_footnote. The badge and QR sit on a card mount beside the leaf.
  10. Leaf, 'Kept off the block': privacy (data collected none, no tracking, no account) and privacy.notes. The transparency record's facts (0 SDKs, 0 tracking domains, network to Wikipedia's public API only, no analytics, the required-reason APIs) link to /transparency/#wanderwiki. Includes 'not affiliated with the Wikimedia Foundation' and links to the privacy policy and support.
  11. Two leaves, 'Other calendars': comparison_table (13 rows × WanderWiki / WikiCards / Wiki Rabbit / Wikipedia official) continued across both leaves, with its intro and footnote, links to /alternatives/wikipedia-app/ and /alternatives/kiwix/, and an inline badge.
  12. Leaf, 'Whose block this is': who_for (6) and who_not_for (4) as two ruled lists, then plateau_disclosure (rule, what_it_does_not_do, notes) as the leaf's small print.
  13. Leaf, 'From the printer': the founder heading and story (Lagerland Apps, Finland, ending 'The maker uses it every morning.'), the signals as small print with the live-app count computed, the response time, and a link to /lagerland-apps/.
  14. Leaves, 'Questions': the 13 FAQ as <details>, continued across three leaves (FAQPage).
  15. Leaf, 'Further reading': the journal posts reading-without-a-feed (related_journal) and wikipedia-is-different-in-every-language.
  16. The back of the block (closing, on the card): the imprint mount with badge, QR and price; 'Printed by Lagerland Apps, Finland · first released 1 Feb 2026 · last updated 13 May 2026'; the other live apps as 'Also printed by Lagerland' (computed). Then comes the shared strip.

Navigation

The backing card's printed header is the nav: the WANDERWIKI wordmark (back to the top) and Today · Modes · Editions · Prices · Questions. The block's leaf edges are an honest 'leaves left' indicator, one edge per remaining section; they disappear as you pass leaves, so the page visibly ends. On mobile, 'Leaves' opens an index of every leaf title as links (Esc closes). Focus is a 3px black outline offset 3px on leaves; on the orange card it is a 3px black outline with a 2px white inner ring.

Motion

One verb: tear. As a leaf scrolls out past the top, it lifts from its binding and falls away (CSS animation-timeline: view(); rotateX ≤ 12deg, translateY, opacity), and one leaf edge leaves the stack. 'Tear to today' is the same motion at 450ms. Numerals never count up, nothing loops and the card has no parallax. Without scroll-timeline support (Firefox) leaves simply scroll. With prefers-reduced-motion leaves are static panels with perforated tops.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the alternatives pages keep the orange card as a 16px frame with its printed header. The content is one long leaf back: a white sheet under the black binding strip, which carries the page title (e.g. 'WANDERWIKI VS KIWIX'). The reading column is Piazzolla 18px/1.6 at 66ch, and quick_answer is the lead paragraph at 21px. Tables take the leaf's ruled style, and 'Pick WanderWiki if… / Use Kiwix if…' become two ruled lists. Read pages are one long leaf by design, with no 'continued' breaks. The privacy policy keeps its own text, with the transparency facts in a ruled box. Support is a leaf whose single entry is the email, with response_time beneath.

Materials

The block: the current leaf over five visible 1px leaf edges, 3px apart, so the stack's thickness shows. One edge disappears per leaf passed, a true count of what is left · Binding strip: a 40px black glued header across the top of every leaf with white Alumni Sans 600 caps, and a row of 2px perforation dots (6px pitch) under it · Torn stub: a 10px ragged white remnant of yesterday's leaf under the binding (CSS clip-path polygon) · Backing card: a flat orange printed card with a punched 20px hanging hole at top centre. Its printed matter (header, the 33 codes, the imprint) is in black ink · Imprint mount: a white printed rectangle on the card holding the badge, the QR and the price, like the sponsor's imprint on a promotional calendar · Leaf furniture: a 1px rule under the date, entries set as year + line + small-print category, and a 'continued on the next leaf' footer when a section spills

Colour strategy

Drenched. The orange backing card is the ground of every viewport outside the leaves. The leaves are cool newsprint white, one black ink prints everything, and red marks only Sunday numerals and the Holidays category. · light

Type rationale

Calendar leaves are printed in tall, heavy, condensed grotesques, so one day fills a leaf and a month fits a strip. Alumni Sans has the squared rounds of the DIN- and Akzidenz-condensed numerals that German and Soviet blocks used, and its nine weights give the 900 numeral, the 800 month and the 600 header from one 22 KB file. Piazzolla was drawn for newspapers: compact and sturdy at small sizes on thin cheap stock, which is exactly what the back of a calendar leaf is. Together they keep the block a printed object without a bookish serif display. Anybody was dropped because Chessful's 'Key to Symbols' uses it, and Antonio because Millrace's 'Par Is Proven' does. Budget: about 73 KB base, about 100 KB with every slice.

New assets needed

No raster art. Data: a verified On This Day snapshot for 13 May (three to five entries with years, categories, article URLs and CC BY-SA attribution) in a _data file; corrected example_insights and screenshot alts. The halftone on 4.png and 5.png is a CSS treatment, so no new files.

Picked
WanderWikiGentium Book Plus

Swipe. Learn. Repeat.

Swipe Wikipedia in 33 languages. Ad-free.

SECOND ROLL

Thirty-Three Originals

Facing-page dual-language editions: the Loeb Classical Library (since 1912; Greek volumes in green cloth, Latin in red, the original on the left page and English on the right, with running heads and folios), dtv zweisprachig and Penguin Parallel Text. Also the Complutensian Polyglot (Alcalá, 1514–17), which set Hebrew, Latin and Greek in parallel columns, each in its own fount. And the scholarly page's apparatus, which collates other witnesses by siglum at the foot. Grammar only: no publisher name, logo or cover design.

The page is an open facing-page edition whose two pages are honestly not translations of each other. The left page always carries a Wikipedia edition's own words (its endonym, its category tree, its On This Day keys); the right carries WanderWiki's English reading. The form readers expect to be a translation proves the app's real claim: each of the 33 editions is its own encyclopedia, queried in its own words. It refuses the starry 'universe of knowledge' phone page and the white Wikipedia look-alike.

  • #F9FAF8
  • #1B1C1A
  • #23573A
  • #1C4630
  • #5A5E58
  • #E4E7E2
Type
Gentium Book Plus 700 (@fontsource/gentium-book-plus, latin 22 KB). The H1 is 80px on desktop and 44px on mobile; spread titles are 40px and 28px; the eight German categories are 40px. Latin, Greek and Cyrillic endonyms on the frontispiece range from 22 to 76px. with Gentium Book Plus 400 and 400 italic (22 KB + 25 KB). Body text is 19px/1.6 on desktop and 17px on mobile. Italic is used only for Wikipedia article titles, as a citation convention, never as display., Noto Serif Hebrew, Noto Naskh Arabic, Noto Serif Devanagari, Noto Serif Thai, Noto Serif JP, Noto Serif SC and Noto Serif KR (all on Fontsource), each subset once to just the glyphs of its endonym (עברית, العربية, हिन्दी, ไทย, 日本語, 中文, 한국어) at about 2–6 KB each. Gentium's extended Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and Vietnamese glyphs for the endonyms are also subset once (about 10 KB) instead of loading the 58 KB latin-ext slice.
Light
A commuter on a morning train with a dual-language paperback open on their knee, under flat, even carriage daylight → light.
Signature
'Read the frontispiece.' Each of the 33 endonyms is a real link to its row in the Editions table further down (this is the no-JS behaviour). With JS (about 1 KB), a tap instead opens the edition's read-out in place, in the verso's apparatus line (aria-live polite), e.g. 'Deutsch · de · de.wikipedia.org · about 3.0M articles (List of Wikipedias, 2026) · written by its own editors, not a translation of English'. A 'see all 33' link goes to the table. The tapped name is underlined in original green and the others dim to 70% opacity, never below AA. Reduced motion: no fade; the read-out text simply appears.
Remembered as
The page that was an open book: the 33 Wikipedia language names on the left page, each sized by how big that Wikipedia is, facing 'Swipe. Learn. Repeat.'; and further in, 'Wissenschaft, Physik, Chemie' facing 'Science'.
Risk
This is the bookish world the calibration warns about (serif on book pages). It survives only as cool white and green in low-contrast Gentium, with no cream, no italic display and no tracked mono labels. A facing-page form implies translation, and WanderWiki explicitly does not translate, so every spread has to carry its 'not a translation' line or visitors will misread the product. On phones the spread collapses to single pages, losing the facing effect where most visitors are. The frontispiece needs a data pull and seven script subsets. It is the least instantly 'app-like' of the three, since screenshots appear only as plates from the fourth spread on. AppMeta's 'Fifty-Language Leaflet' is also multilingual; this stays a bound facing-page book (spreads, gutter, cloth, Gentium), never a folded leaflet with language tabs.

Page sequence

  1. Frontispiece and title page (hero): the 33 endonyms sized by article count (verso), facing the title page with the H1, tagline, hero.secondary and an imprint of badge, QR and price.value statement (recto). On mobile the title page comes first.
  2. 'Argument & Contents': quick_answer as the 'Argument' on the verso (speakable, 22px). On the recto, the Quick reference <details> as the summary table (summary always visible) and the book's own Contents listing each spread by folio (this doubles as navigation).
  3. 'Science / Wissenschaft': on the verso, in original green, the eight German categories one per line at 40px. On the recto, the English reading: For You's 10 declared interests, '~8–12 native categories per edition', and on-device like/dislike. Caption: 'Pick German + Science and WanderWiki queries these, not a translation' (features[0], features[2], example_insights[2] corrected).
  4. 'Three ways in': Plate I (4.png, Random: John de Grey) and Plate II (1.png, Today: NASA, 1961) tipped in on the verso. On the recto, Random (the whole encyclopedia, ~7M articles in en, against a Good Articles subset), For You and Today in History, followed by five real Random cards from the preview video set as titles with their short descriptions (features[1–3], value_points[1]).
  5. 'On this day': on the verso, the feed's own words, i.e. the path /api/rest_v1/feed/onthisday/{category}/{MM}/{DD} and its five keys (selected, events, births, deaths, holidays). On the recto, the English reading: what each key returns, verified 13 May entries (replacing example_insights), and the widgets that refresh it daily (features[3], how_it_works[6–7]).
  6. 'Editions': the 33-row edition table across the spread in training_vocabulary's four groups (endonym in original green, code, domain, approx. article count). The frontispiece links land here. Also value_points[0] and value_points[4] ($24.99 ≈ $0.76 per edition).
  7. 'Kept for the journey': Plate III (5.png, Profile with Liked/Saved) and Plate IV (3.png, the in-app article view) facing offline saving, folders ('flights', 'before-bed', 'philosophy') and the calm reading view with inline CC BY-SA attribution (features[4–5], example_insights[3]).
  8. 'How a reading goes': the how_it_works intro and its 8 steps, steps 1–4 on the verso and 5–8 on the recto (HowTo schema).
  9. 'Collation': comparison_table across the gutter, with sigla column heads (W WanderWiki, C WikiCards, R Wiki Rabbit, O Wikipedia official) above the full names, 13 rows, and the intro and footnote as apparatus. 'Further collations' links to /alternatives/wikipedia-app/ and /alternatives/kiwix/.
  10. 'Publisher's list': the four plans as a priced list (Free trial · Monthly · Annual, marked as the highlight · Lifetime, 'Best long-term value', with Family Sharing), plans_footnote, and the badge and QR repeated.
  11. 'Copyright page': on the verso, CC BY-SA 4.0 and 'not affiliated with the Wikimedia Foundation'. Facing it, privacy: data collected none, no tracking, no account, privacy.notes, and the transparency record's facts with a link to /transparency/#wanderwiki, plus links to the privacy policy and support.
  12. 'For whom / Not for whom': who_for (6) on the verso facing who_not_for (4) on the recto, then plateau_disclosure (rule, what_it_does_not_do, notes) as an apparatus band across the foot.
  13. 'Editor's preface': the founder heading and story (Lagerland Apps, Finland), the signals as a short list of notes with the live-app count computed, the response time, and a link to /lagerland-apps/.
  14. 'Notes': the 13 FAQ as <details> endnotes (FAQPage).
  15. 'Further reading': the journal posts reading-without-a-feed (related_journal) and wikipedia-is-different-in-every-language.
  16. Colophon on the cloth band (closing): badge, QR and price; 'Set in Gentium Book Plus and Noto Serif. Made by Lagerland Apps, Finland · first released 1 Feb 2026 · last updated 13 May 2026'; the other live apps as 'Also from this press' (computed). Then comes the shared strip.

Navigation

The top cloth band is the nav: the WanderWiki wordmark and Contents · Editions · Prices · Questions. Contents opens the book's contents page, listing every spread by title and folio: a full-height overlay on mobile, a dropdown page on desktop. Running heads link back to Contents. The green ribbon tracks the current spread in the gutter (sticky within each spread), so the reader always sees where in the book they are. Focus is a 3px original-green outline offset 3px; on the cloth band it is page white.

Motion

Book-still. Spreads do not animate in. The ribbon slides between spreads (200ms) as the reader scrolls, the frontispiece read-out fades in over 120ms, and the sticky cloth band slides up in 200ms. There is no page curl, no parallax on plates, and nothing counts up or loops. With prefers-reduced-motion the ribbon jumps and the fades go.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy, support and the two alternatives pages are single pages of the same book: a recto only, no spread. Each has the cloth band and edge, a running head (e.g. 'COLLATION · WANDERWIKI · KIWIX') and a Gentium 19px/1.6 reading column at 66ch, with quick_answer as the 'Argument' paragraph. Comparison tables become collation tables with sigla heads over the full names. 'Pick WanderWiki if… / Use Kiwix if…' become two facing lists on desktop and sequential lists on mobile. The privacy policy is set like a copyright page with its text unchanged, and the transparency record's facts appear as a marginal note on desktop or an inset box on mobile. Support is 'Correspondence': the email, response_time and what to include.

Materials

The open spread: two pages meeting at a 28px gutter band with a 1px darker fold line at its centre; three 1px page edges on each outer side show the book's thickness · Case cloth: a flat green edge (24px on desktop) around the spread, with no weave texture, widening into the top band and the colophon · Running heads and folios: 13px Gentium 700 caps (+0.04em) in original green at the top outer corners, and folios at the bottom outer corners. The verso head names the edition ('de · Deutsch'); the recto head reads 'WanderWiki · in English' · Plates: screenshots tipped in as numbered plates (Plate I–IV), each with a 1px plate mark and a legend in apparatus grey · Apparatus band: a 1px rule across the foot of a page, with 14px grey notes that collate the competitors by siglum · Ribbon: a 6px green silk ribbon marker hanging into the gutter of the current spread

Colour strategy

Restrained. Cool white page stock and black ink carry nearly everything. One green, Loeb's Greek cloth, marks every original-language word plus the running heads, folios and links. The deeper case-cloth green appears only as the edge around the open book, the top band, the sticky band and the colophon. · light

Type rationale

SIL drew Gentium 'for the nations': one design covering Latin with every diacritic, Greek and Cyrillic, made for multilingual scholarly text. That is what a polyglot demands, so the English copy and Čeština, Tiếng Việt, Ελληνικά and Русский share one hand. Its low-contrast, faintly calligraphic roman reads as a book face, neither a news serif nor a fashion Didone, and none of the training-default serifs. Scripts it does not cover are set in matched Noto Serif cuts, as the Complutensian gave each column its own fount. Budget: about 68 KB for Gentium 400, 700 and 400i, plus about 10 KB of extended glyphs and about 25 KB of script subsets, about 103 KB in all.

New assets needed

No raster art. Data: approximate article counts for all 33 editions from Wikimedia's List of Wikipedias, dated (needed to size the frontispiece and fill the Editions table; 16 have no figure in the journal post); a verified 13 May On This Day snapshot; corrected example_insights and screenshot alts. Fonts: one-time custom subsets for the seven Noto Serif scripts and for Gentium's extended glyphs. A native-speaker check of all 33 endonyms.

T

Tare

/apps/tare/ + its privacy and support pages

What the page must prove: In one viewport, with no screenshot to lean on, the page must show a playable mobile that balances by weight × distance, a hidden “?” weight whose beam won't reveal it, and a picture card that lets you deduce it. It must also show that the game is wordless, runs on iPhone and iPad, has 20 levels free and the other 60 for $2.99 once, has no ads and collects no data. The official App Store badge must be in reach.

The default page this refuses: The puzzle-game landing page: full-bleed key art or a pastel ‘zen puzzle’ gradient behind a tilted iPhone; a rounded casual-game face (Fredoka, Baloo); ‘Download now’; a row of icon feature tiles (80 levels · offline · no ads · hints); a screenshot carousel; a star strip; two pricing cards; an FAQ accordion. The incumbent adds a cream ground, Newsreader, a purple accent and the split hero. For Tare it also currently points at an icon and a QR code that do not exist.

Hang the weights. Balance every beam. Deduce the rest.

A wordless balance logic puzzle. Hang the weights, level every beam, deduce the hidden ones.

THE ROLL

The Painted Board

Tare's own ‘Signboard Sky’ art direction, as the front matter and the founder note describe it. Every screen is redrawn as a painted toy on a flat sky-blue board: chalk-white beams with notches 1–4 a side; weights 1–9 painted with a numeral and domino pips; “?” soap bubbles; picture cards pinned above the board; a shelf of pieces below; gold stars and the sun on a solve. The style reads all of this through the single-stroke casual sign painting the direction is named after. No Signboard Sky capture exists in the repo yet, so the page builds the board from those words.

The page is one Tare level at page scale. The headline is the ceiling rail, and a real mobile hangs from it that the visitor can solve before reading a word of copy. Every section below hangs from the same chalk string, forming one balanced cascade. It refuses the game page's key art, tilted phone and row of icon tiles. It also refuses the developer's own discarded museum look of hairline beams on paper.

  • #2172B8
  • #FFFFFF
  • #0B3F6E
  • #FFC94A
  • #0B2A4A
  • #A9D3F2
  • #3C6E57
Type
Recursive, variable: @fontsource-variable/recursive, latin ‘casl’ file (CASL 0–1 × wght 300–1000, 109 KB). It is the page's only font file. Set at CASL 1, wght 850: the H1 is 84px/0.98 on desktop and 34px/1.02 on mobile, centred, in chalk. Section heads are 44/30px. Weight numerals use wght 900 on the painted weights. with The same file at CASL 0.25, wght 420. Body is 19px/1.6 (17px on mobile) at a 62ch measure, chalk on the board or ink on white cards. It also sets FAQ answers and picture-card copy., Recursive at CASL 0, wght 700, with tnum, for real arithmetic and figures: 3 × 2 = 6 = (4 + 2) × 1, the notch numbers 1–4, and $2.99.
Light
A puzzle player on a phone in daylight, on a train or by a window, looking at the same flat cerulean board the game opens on (Morning Sky) → light. One drenched daylight scheme; color-scheme: light.
Signature
Hang it yourself: the hero's playable level, drawn in inline SVG. Input: weights and hooks are real <button>s. Pieces can be dragged (Pointer Events, with a 60px snap like the app), tapped, or moved by keyboard: Enter picks a piece, the arrow keys move between hooks, and Enter hangs it. Physics: beams rotate about their pivot by clamp(net torque × 2.5°, ±9°). Any beam carrying the unsolved “?” sways ±3° on a 3.2s loop instead. While a piece is held, the picture card that mentions it lifts 4px. A full but wrong board shudders once (±4px, 360ms), with no red. The solution: 3 on the left at notch 2; on the right at notch 1, the sub-beam with ? at notch 1 and 2 at notch 2. The sums are 3×2 = 6 = (4+2)×1, and 4×1 = 2×2. The solve: the sway stops and the beams settle with one overshoot. The bubble pops to show 4. Three labelled star grades appear (Hung, Unshaken, Once), scored honestly from the visitor's moves. A flat sun disc rises in the board's top-right corner. An aria-live line narrates each move. No JS: the SVG prints in its solved state, the arithmetic is the caption and the shelf is empty. The pieces UI exists only under html.js. Reduced motion: there is no sway. An unsolved “?” beam stays level, with a dashed chalk outline and the text ‘won't settle until you know the ?’. A wrong board shows the line ‘Full, but not balanced’ instead of shuddering, and reveals are instant.
Remembered as
The puzzle page where the headline was the ceiling and a mobile hung off it. I hung the 3 and the 2, the card said the bubble was two 2s, everything stopped swaying and the sun came out, and the download badge sat on the shelf with the pieces.
Risk
Familiarity: this is the closest of the three to the category canon (a game page in the game's own art). Only the working level and the cascade topology keep it from being key art, so a build that turns the demo into a static picture fails. Colour accuracy: the board is authored from words, so its colours may not match the app until Signboard Sky captures exist. The superseded Quiet Gallery shots must not leak in. Sibling overlap: Soon's First Light also has a sky and a sun. Here the sky is one flat board with no bands and no horizon, and the sun appears only on a solve. Accessibility: a drag-and-drop SVG must be fully operable by keyboard and VoiceOver, with named beams, hooks and pieces that mirror the app's VoiceOver tree. Chalk on #2172B8 is 5.0:1, so no lighter blue may carry text. Stars: on a page with no ratings, the gold stars must stay labelled grades (Hung · Unshaken · Once) and never appear near the badge. Font budget: the 109 KB font file is most of the budget.

App Store route

Badge: Apple's black badge from _includes/appstore-badge.html, unaltered, with its own clear space. It sits on the shelf as the last thing the visitor reaches for. It repeats on the chapter-ledger beam beside the plans and as the bottom weight of the cascade. It always links to app_store_url exactly as the front matter gives it. Price: price.value is painted in chalk on the shelf lip. The plans and plans_footnote sit in the chapter ledger, cta_subline is used verbatim, and the schema stays at 0 / 2.99 / 2 offers. QR: a white picture card pinned at the right end of the shelf, desktop ≥1024px only. The code is black on white inside its quiet zone, captioned ‘Point your iPhone camera here’. Liquid renders it only when assets/qr/tare.svg exists in site.static_files. That file is absent until launch, so before launch the shelf holds the badge alone. Sticky bar: the shelf docks. Once the hero badge leaves the viewport, a 64px #0B3F6E plank with a 6px lip slides up. It holds ‘Tare’ (CASL 1), ‘20 levels free · $2.99 once for 60 more’ and the badge. On mobile it is 56px tall and reads ‘Chapter I free’. Smart App Banner: the existing apple-itunes-app meta (app-id=6806255929). On iOS the native banner sits above the board, and the page adds no competing pill. Status: while status is upcoming, nothing on the page claims ‘available now’ or ‘coming soon’ beyond the front-matter wording.

Page sequence

  1. The board (hero): the wordmark and the pinned-card nav; the H1 as the ceiling rail; the playable demo mobile with its ‘? = 2 2’ card and the demo label; the shelf with the pieces, the badge, price.value and cta_subline. The QR card joins at launch.
  2. Quick Answer: the first thing hanging below the shelf. It is a large white picture card pinned where the string meets it, ink on white at 64ch, marked speakable. Its foot carries the trust line: iPhone & iPad · iOS 26.5+ · no ads · no account · no network code · no data collected.
  3. #how-it-works, One rule: the how_it_works intro in chalk at 28px, then one big chalk beam showing ‘a 2 at the second notch balances a 4 at the first’ (2×2 = 4×1, in tnum). The four steps hang from four hooks of one long beam, numbered 1–4 because the sequence is real (HowTo schema).
  4. #secret, The scale can't be cheated: value point 1 beside two looping beams. One is an honest beam tilting under a 3 and a 2; the other is a “?” beam swaying. Below them, the three picture-card kinds are pinned as the game uses them (equals, heavier, balanced on unequal arms), each drawn in miniature with its one-line meaning from the features text.
  5. Three promises on one beam: value points 2–4 (one answer, no timer, nothing to read). Each hangs at a notch distance inverse to its text length, so the beam visibly balances. This is the page's lever-law layout rule.
  6. The click and the Lantern: the click feature beside a static solved mobile. Then the Lantern's three hint steps in their real order: card, then one hidden value, then a ghost. Then the star grades Hung · Unshaken · Once as three labelled gold stars. Nothing is gated, and no rating stars appear anywhere.
  7. #chapters, Four chapters, one purchase: four hanging canvases on one long beam. They are The Hang · Morning Sky · free; The Secret · Twilight Meadow; The Cascade · Deep Sea; and The Exhibition · Evening Stars. Each has 20 levels and its one-line description from the body. Under them, the two plans hang on either side of the string: Chapter I Free (highlighted) and Chapters II–IV $2.99 once, each with its feature list. Then come the plans_footnote (chapter-order rule, Family Sharing, restore) and the badge.
  8. Built for every player, and quiet by design: one weight drawn large with its numeral and pips. Beside it, the accessibility feature (VoiceOver tree, Dynamic Type, High contrast at 4.5:1, Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency) and the sound, haptics and appearance switches.
  9. Who it's for and who it isn't: the five who_for lines hang on the short arm of one beam, near the string; the four who_not_for lines hang on the long arm. The longer list hangs closer, so the beam balances.
  10. #about: the about_heading H2 and the show_body markdown on a long white card at 64ch. It covers the rule, ‘The rule that makes it a logic puzzle’, the four chapters, and ‘What it does not do’.
  11. The maker's note: the founder bio set large in chalk (‘Tare started as a quiet museum piece…’) under the Lagerland mark. The five signals follow as a plain list, then the response-time line and a mailto link.
  12. #faq: the 13 questions, each opening with a small “?” bubble. Opening the <details> pops the bubble into a filled chalk dot, and the answer hangs below it.
  13. #privacy, Nothing collected: data collection none, tracking false, account false, and the seven privacy notes. Links go to the privacy policy, to support, and to /transparency/ (Tare is not on the record yet; see notes).
  14. Quick reference: the ai-canonical <details> on a white card, open by default and present in the DOM.
  15. The bottom weight: the last and heaviest piece of the cascade is a short shelf with the badge, price.value and cta_label. Below it come other Lagerland apps (computed from site.apps where status is live), the maker and freshness line (Built by Lagerland Apps · version 1.0 · first released · last updated, from release.*), and the shared ‘A Lagerland app’ strip.

Navigation

Desktop: four pinned picture cards at the board's top right, white stock with a yellow pin and ink text. They link to How it plays (#how-it-works), Chapters & price (#chapters), Questions (#faq) and Privacy (#privacy). The card for the current section hangs straight while the others keep their tilt. The ‘Tare’ wordmark returns to the top. Mobile: one ‘Contents’ card opens a <details> sheet in the shelf colour, with the same four links plus Download. Further down the page, the chalk string doubles as a progress cue: the current beam's pivot becomes a filled yellow pin. There is no separate rail. Focus: a 3px #FFC94A outline outside a 2px #0B2A4A ring, visible on the board, the shelf and white cards. DOM order is reading order.

Motion

Pendular only. Anything that moves either rotates about a pivot or drops on a string; nothing slides sideways or fades in from nowhere. Beams settle over 420ms on cubic-bezier(.3,1.35,.5,1), with one overshoot. Under html.js, each section drops 16px and settles from 1° to 0° once (480ms) as it enters. The sticky shelf rises 64px over 260ms. There is no parallax and no scroll-scrubbing. prefers-reduced-motion turns all of it off. All content is in the HTML and visible before any script runs.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy and support share one frame. A 240px board masthead carries the wordmark and the pinned-card nav. The page title hangs from a chalk beam: ‘Privacy Policy’ in CASL 1 at 56px (34px on mobile). The reading column is one long white card pinned under the beam: ink #0B2A4A, Recursive CASL 0.15 at wght 420, 19px/1.65, 66ch. Privacy: the fields (overview, data collection, storage, third parties, sensitive data, children, changes) become H2s. A ‘Data collected: none’ strip opens the card, and a contact line closes it. Support: the email is set large in chalk on the board. The response-time line and the restore steps (from the FAQ) sit on the card, and the page closes on the shelf with the badge and price. Alternatives (future): any /alternatives/<competitor>/ page wears the same masthead. Its comparison table is ruled in 1px #2172B8 on the white card, with Tare's column on a #EAF4FC wash (ink at 13:1), and its verdict hangs from a beam.

Materials

The flat cerulean board #2172B8 as the page ground, edge to edge: painted, with no gradient and no texture. · Chalk-white beams: 10px rounded bars with notch ticks 1–4 a side and a ring pivot. Strings are 2px chalk, including the one string that runs down the whole page. · Painted weights: rounded-square #FFC94A blocks on a hanging loop. Each carries its Recursive numeral and domino pips in ink, as the game does. · “?” soap bubbles: a 2px chalk ring with one highlight arc and #A9D3F2 film at 35%. They are drawn shapes, never a blur or glass effect. · White picture cards held by a yellow pin. They quote pieces in miniature with =, > or a tilted mini-beam, and the same cards serve as nav and as reading cards. · The shelf: a #0B3F6E plank with an 8px lip that carries the pieces, the badge and the price. · Gold five-point grade stars and a flat sun disc, shown only in a solved state.

Colour strategy

Drenched · light

Type rationale

The art direction is named Signboard, and Recursive's Casual axis was drawn from single-stroke casual sign painting. The same brush that paints the weights' numerals can therefore set the headline, and turning the axis down gives a calm reading text from one file. No static Fontsource cut carries the CASL axis, so production and mocks must both serve the variable file.

New assets needed

No raster assets. Beams, weights, bubbles, cards, stars and the sun are all inline SVG/CSS, and the demo level is authored above. Production needs the @fontsource-variable/recursive ‘casl’ latin file (109 KB), because the static Fontsource cuts used by the mock board have no Casual axis. At launch: re-match the board, weight-paint and bubble colours to the Signboard Sky tokens or captures, and add the QR (scripts/generate-qr.py) and the icon.

TareZen Maru Gothic

Hang the weights. Balance every beam. Deduce the rest.

A wordless balance logic puzzle. Hang the weights, level every beam, deduce the hidden ones.

IMPECCABLE’S PICK

Answers Upside Down

Nikoli's pencil-puzzle publishing: Puzzle Communication Nikoli (Tokyo, since 1980; the publisher that named Sudoku) and its pencil-puzzle books. Every puzzle is hand-made by a credited setter and must have one solution reachable by logic. Each puzzle type opens with a framed Rules box and a solved Example, and the answers are at the back. Added to that are the puzzle-digest conventions every solver knows: ‘pencil recommended’, answers printed upside down at the foot of the page, and thumb-index tabs cut into the fore-edge.

The page is Tare's own puzzle-book page: a Rules box, then Puzzle No. 1 to solve in pencil before any feature list, with the answer printed upside down at the foot. It treats the visitor as a solver, the way Tare treats its player. It refuses the game hero (key art, phone, feature tiles). It also refuses the broadsheet puzzle page (hairlines, italic serif, mono labels) by printing in rounded gothic and one lime ink.

  • #FFFFFF
  • #161616
  • #8CC63E
  • #E8F4DA
  • #4A4A4A
Type
Zen Maru Gothic, @fontsource/zen-maru-gothic, about 11 KB per weight in latin. Weight 900 sets the H1 (64px/1.08 on desktop, 32px/1.1 on mobile) and the ‘Rules’, ‘No. 1’ and price-box heads. Weight 700 sets the rule numerals, chapter names, FAQ questions and the 14px tab labels. with Zen Kaku Gothic New 400/500/700, @fontsource/zen-kaku-gothic-new, about 9 KB per weight. Body is 19px/1.65 at 64ch, and never smaller than 19px because of its small x-height. Rules are 18px/1.55; the running head is 15px., Klee One 600 (@fontsource/klee-one, 35 KB), used only for the visitor's pencil: numbers written into hook circles, the pencilled working, and the upside-down answer.
Light
A solver with a pencil on a commuter train or at a café table in daylight, with the book open flat: the same person who plays Tare offline underground → light. Bright white bond printed in black and one lime spot ink, with graphite pencil on top; color-scheme: light.
Signature
Solve it in pencil. Puzzle No. 1 is printed, so its beams never move. Entering a number: tap or focus an empty hook circle, then a piece in the pencil strip. The number writes itself into the circle in Klee One graphite with a 240ms left-to-right clip wipe. Working: pencilled working appears beside each beam, ‘3 × 2 = 6’ on one side and ‘(? + 2) × 1’ on the other. Once the clue card has been read, the working adds ‘? = 2 + 2 = 4’. Checking: when every circle is filled and the puzzle balances, a pencil tick appears with ‘Turn to the answers’ (a link to #answers). If it doesn't balance, the working shows the uneven sides in graphite (‘6 ≠ 5’), with no red and no buzzer, and an eraser clears the entries. The “?” rule: print cannot sway, so the rule is taught in the Rules box and in a small ‘sways’ diagram. No JS: the puzzle prints empty, as in a book. The full answer and working sit upside down at the foot of the page; they are in the DOM, and screen readers read them upright. A CSS-only checkbox (‘Turn the page’) rotates the answer upright. Reduced motion: numbers and working appear instantly, with no wipe.
Remembered as
The puzzle-book one: a green Rules box, a little mobile with empty circles I filled in with pencil numbers, the working written next to it, and the answer printed upside down at the bottom.
Risk
Familiarity: this is the most familiar of the three. ‘Puzzle game → puzzle book’ can be guessed from the category, and many runs would land here. Drift: it slides into the broadsheet puzzle page (rut c) the moment hairlines, an italic serif or mono labels appear. The rounded gothic and the lime discipline are the style. No physics: in print, beams never tilt or sway. Tare's most important rule is therefore told and diagrammed rather than felt, and the page undersells the painted, physical feel the developer rebuilt the game for. Lineage, not costume: no Nikoli name, logo or puzzle-type names appear on the page. Contrast and legibility: lime cannot carry text or lines on white (2.05:1). Zen Kaku's small x-height needs 19px body text. The upside-down answer must stay readable to assistive tech.
Full style card

390×844, on white. • y 0–44: the running head with ‘Tare’ (Zen Maru 900, 20px), the folio ‘1’ and a lime ‘Contents’ tab (72×32) at the right. • y 56–166: the H1 in Zen Maru 900 32px/1.1, three lines. • y 178–330: the lime Rules box with the three rules at 15.5px. • y 344–620: the Puzzle No. 1 frame, with a 300px black-ink mobile, 36px hook circles, the clue card at top right, and the 3 · 2 · ? pencil strip along the frame's foot (44px targets). • y 636–790: the lime price box with price.value (Zen Maru 700, 17px), the badge (44px tall) and ‘No ads · no data collected’ at 14px. • The upside-down answer strip and the Quick Answer follow below the fold. • No QR on mobile.

App Store route

Badge: Apple's black badge, unaltered, on its own white inset inside the lime price box. That box is the magazine's cover-price panel moved onto the page. It repeats on the Price page and at the foot of the Answers page, and always links to app_store_url. Price: price.value is printed in the box. The two plans appear as a printed price list, with the plans_footnote as the fine print. cta_label ‘Play Chapter I free’ heads the box on the Price page. QR: the barcode corner, a 2px black ruled square under the price box (desktop ≥1024px only). It holds assets/qr/tare.svg, black on white inside its quiet zone, captioned ‘Scan with your iPhone camera’. It renders only once the file exists, at launch. Sticky bar: a running foot. When the price box scrolls out of view, a 56px white strip with a 2px black top rule rises. It carries ‘Tare · 20 levels free · $2.99 once for 60 more’ in a mini lime box, plus the badge. Smart App Banner: the native banner sits above the running head, and there is no duplicate pill on iOS.

Page sequence

  1. Page 1 (hero): the running head, thumb tabs and H1; the Rules box with three rules; Puzzle No. 1 to solve in pencil, labelled as a demo printed for this page; the lime price box with price.value, the badge and the privacy line (the barcode-corner QR joins at launch); and the answer, upside down, at the frame's foot.
  2. In one paragraph: the quick_answer in a 2px black rounded box on the lime tint, speakable, at 64ch. Under it, the facts line: iPhone & iPad · iOS 26.5+ · offline · no ads · no account · no data collected.
  3. #how-it-works, How to solve: the how_it_works intro, then the four steps numbered 1–4 (a real sequence, HowTo schema), each with a small ink diagram. Then a worked Example panel on the tint: solved beams showing 2 at notch 2 = 4 at notch 1, and 3 at notch 4 = 6 at notch 2 (both from the FAQ), with the working in pencil.
  4. Key to the clues: the three picture-card kinds as a printed legend (equals, heavier, unequal arms). Alongside: value point 1 (the scale can't be cheated) and a two-panel ‘tilts / sways’ diagram for the “?” rule.
  5. The setter's guarantee: value point 2 and the machine-proof conditions (one balanced arrangement; hidden weights fixed by their cards alone; decoys that fit nowhere), printed like a book's colophon promise. Value points 3 and 4 follow as two short notes.
  6. #chapters, Contents: the four chapters as a contents page with leader dots. I The Hang · Morning Sky · 20 levels · free; II The Secret · Twilight Meadow; III The Cascade · Deep Sea; IV The Exhibition · Evening Stars; each 20 levels. A lime band opens each line. The chapter-opening rule follows: Chapter II opens after 16 of 20, and you can skip up to three ahead.
  7. #price, Price: the two plans as a printed price list: Chapter I Free (highlighted in lime) and Chapters II–IV $2.99 once, each with its feature list. The plans_footnote is the fine print, followed by the price box with the badge.
  8. Hints and grading: the Lantern's three hint steps as a numbered list; the star key Hung · Unshaken · Once as a legend (these are grades, not ratings); and the click.
  9. What's in the book: the remaining features (painted mobiles, four worlds, built for every player, quiet by design) as a two-column run of bold run-in heads, not a card grid.
  10. Recommended for / Not for: who_for ×5 and who_not_for ×4 as two ruled lists.
  11. #about: the about_heading and the show_body markdown, set as an article at 64ch.
  12. From the setter: the founder bio as an editor's note under the Lagerland mark, with the five signals, the response line and a mailto link.
  13. #faq, Readers' questions: the 13 Q&As, questions in Zen Maru 700 and answers in Zen Kaku, all present in the HTML.
  14. #privacy, Nothing collected: a lime box with data collection none and the seven notes, linking to the privacy policy, to support and to /transparency/.
  15. Quick reference: the ai-canonical <details>, kept in the DOM.
  16. #answers, Answers: the answer to No. 1 with its working, upside down, plus the ‘Turn the page’ toggle. Then the closing price box; other Lagerland apps (computed); the colophon maker and freshness line (Built by Lagerland Apps · version 1.0 · first released · last updated); and the Lagerland strip.

Navigation

Desktop (≥1024px): thumb-index tabs on the fore-edge. Six lime tabs run down the right edge, labelled Rules, No. 1, Contents, Price, Q&A and Privacy, each an anchor link. The current section's tab turns black with lime type (8.8:1) and extends 8px into the page. The folio in the running head is a back-to-top link. Mobile: a lime ‘Contents’ tab in the running head opens a <details> contents list with leader dots. Focus: a 2px #161616 outline plus a 4px lime halo. Links are black with a 2px underline.

Motion

Print doesn't move; only the pencil does. Entries and working write in from left to right with 200–300ms clip wipes. The current thumb tab extends 8px over 160ms, and the running foot rises over 200ms. There are no section reveals, no parallax and no hover theatre. Everything is visible on load, and reduced motion removes the wipes.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy and support are pages of the same book. The running head reads ‘Tare · Privacy policy’ with a folio, and the thumb tabs stay. The title is set like a puzzle-type title (Zen Maru 900, 56px), above a lime summary box: ‘Data collected: none · No account · No network code’. The reading column is Zen Kaku Gothic New 400 at 19px/1.7 and 66ch, black on white. H2s are Zen Maru 700, and the storage and third-party items are definition lists. Support becomes ‘Readers' letters’: the email set large, then the response line, then the restore and chapter-unlock answers as numbered rules. It closes on the price box with the badge. Alternatives (future): any /alternatives/<competitor>/ page prints its comparison as an answer grid: a 2px black frame, a lime header row and Tare's column on the #E8F4DA tint, with the verdict in a Rules-style box.

Materials

Bright white bond as the ground, printed flat in two inks: black and a lime spot colour. · Rules boxes: lime panels with a 16px radius, holding numbered rules. · Puzzle frames: 2px black rounded rectangles with a lime ‘No.’ tab. · Black-ink mobile diagrams: 4px beams with notch ticks, pivot triangles, and empty 40px hook circles waiting for a number. · Graphite pencil: Klee One numerals, working lines and a pencil tick. · Thumb-index tabs cut into the right fore-edge. · The answer key printed upside down at the foot of the page.

Colour strategy

Committed · light

Type rationale

Japanese pencil-puzzle books set titles and rule boxes in rounded maru gothic and instructions in square kaku gothic. Yoshimichi Ohira's matched Zen Maru and Zen Kaku are exactly that pair, and their round lining figures sit neatly in a hook circle. Fontworks' Klee is drawn from the pencil handwriting in Japanese school textbooks, so entries read as graphite rather than as a novelty script. About 84 KB in all.

New assets needed

None. Diagrams, frames, tabs and pencil marks are all SVG/CSS, and Klee One supplies the pencil hand. At launch: the QR via scripts/generate-qr.py, plus the icon for the running head if the owner wants it.

Picked
TareTilt Warp

Hang the weights. Balance every beam. Deduce the rest.

A wordless balance logic puzzle. Hang the weights, level every beam, deduce the hidden ones.

SECOND ROLL

Nine Bars, One Chord

The diatonic toy glockenspiel and its play-by-colour songbook. Its rainbow enamel bars are riveted onto two felt rails that converge as the bars shorten, so the longest bar is the lowest note, and each bar is stamped with its number. Songs are written as rows of coloured numbered dots so children who can't read music can play. Also in the lineage: Orff Schulwerk classroom barred instruments and Boomwhackers' tuned-by-length colour tubes. All of it is read through Tare's own rule: every weight has its own note, heavier is lower, and a solved mobile rings out in a single chord.

The page writes Tare in play-by-colour notation. There are nine bars, one per weight, with 9 the longest and lowest. The demo mobile is drawn as coloured note-dots that ring their chord only when every beam balances, and the “?” is the one note that won't sound. Balance becomes something you hear. It refuses the game landing's key art and feature tiles, and the floating pastels of zen-puzzle pages.

  • #34121F
  • #FFF3EA
  • #D9B9C4
  • #24101A
  • #1A0B12
  • #E8452C
  • #5A3443
Type
Tilt Warp 400 (@fontsource/tilt-warp, static, 12 KB; the variable file's 3D-rotation axes are not used). The H1 is 64px/1.04 on desktop and 34px/1.05 on mobile. Section titles are 40/28px. It also sets every numeral stamped on a bar (30px) or in a 44px note-dot (22px). with Andika 400/700 (@fontsource/andika, 18–19 KB each). Body is 19px/1.6 at 62ch in warm white. Nav and price lines use 700; captions are 15–16px in felt dust., No separate utility face. The arithmetic (2 × 2 = 4 × 1) is set in Tilt Warp numerals at 22px.
Light
A player at home after dark with the sound on, earbuds in and the room lights low: the hour Tare's Evening Stars canvas is made for → dark. Claret case felt as the ground, with enamel bars and warm-white type; color-scheme: dark.
Signature
Ring it level. The demo is a real level written in note-dots. Input: tap (or press Enter on) a token, then a hook; dragging works too. Physics: beams tilt honestly by torque (±6°), and any beam carrying the unsolved “?” sways instead. Sound while playing: with sound on, every placed note sounds its pitch. The “?” is silent, so the instrument won't give it away either. The level: 6 on the top beam's left notch 1. On its right notch 1 hangs a sub-beam with 2 at notch 2 and ? at notch 1. The sums are 2×2 = 4×1 and 6×1 = (2+4)×1. The card reads ? = 2 + 2. The solve: the beams settle, and the ? dot takes bar 4's blue and flies onto bar 4. Bars 6, 2 and 4 light and strum from low to high, then sound together: a C-major chord (G3, C4, E4) on the page's illustrative pentatonic mapping, from 9 = C3 up to 1 = G4. The tones are synthesized in Web Audio, with no audio files. A full but wrong board gives one felt thump and a shudder, with no red. Any bar can be tapped to hear it, except the muted one. No JS: the mobile prints in its solved state, with the chord written as three note-dots and the arithmetic in words. The instrument is a static drawing with numerals and pips. Reduced motion: no sway, shudder or strum; bars light in place. Sound still works when switched on, because sound is not motion. Sound is off by default and never autoplays.
Remembered as
The dark red page with the toy glockenspiel along the bottom. I balanced the little mobile and it played a chord, and the question-mark note was the one that wouldn't ring until I'd worked out it was a 4.
Risk
Register: it can read as a preschool toy page. A rainbow xylophone can make a ‘math logic puzzle for adults’ look like a toddler app. Tilt Warp, the claret felt and restraint (colour only where a weight value appears) have to carry the adult register, and the mock has to prove they do. Invented detail: the note-per-weight rule is real, but the page's pitches and its nine colours are invented. The game's weights show a numeral and pips, and its colours are unknown. Both are labelled, and every dot keeps its numeral and pips. Sound: it must stay opt-in, so many visitors will meet the signature silently and only see the bars light. Dark ground: the felt must not slide into near-black-plus-neon. Claret is a colour, the bars are matte and nothing glows. Sibling overlap: LiftLog's ‘Loaded Sleeve’ also colour-codes weights by value. Here it is an instrument and a chord, never plates. Deduction: this is the weakest of the three on deduction.

App Store route

Badge: Apple's black badge sits on the felt ‘maker's plate’ at the instrument's treble end, in the space the shortening bars leave free, where a real instrument carries its maker's plate. It is unaltered, keeps its clear space and links to app_store_url. It repeats beside the plans and in the closing reprise. Price: price.value is set in Andika 700 under the badge. The plans appear as two ‘songs’ with the plans_footnote, headed by cta_label ‘Play Chapter I free’. QR: desktop ≥1024px only. Page sequence

  1. Hero: the notes (the demo mobile hanging from the top edge, with its clue card and demo label); the lyric (the H1 and hero.secondary); and the instrument (nine playable bars) with the maker's plate: badge, price.value and privacy line. The QR joins at launch.
  2. Quick Answer: Andika 21px/1.6 at 62ch in warm white, speakable. Under it, the facts line: iPhone & iPad · iOS 26.5+ · offline · no ads · no account · no data collected.
  3. #how-it-works, One rule: the how_it_works intro, then the rule written as note-dots on a beam (2 at notch 2 = 4 at notch 1; 3 at notch 4 = 6 at notch 2). Then the four steps, numbered 1–4 for the HowTo schema, each with a small notation diagram.
  4. #secret, The note that won't sound: value point 1 and the FAQ answer about the “?”, beside the muted bar, which ignores taps (no sound, no tilt). The three clue-card kinds are written in dots: ? = 2 2; ? > 3; ? at notch 1 balances 2 at notch 2.
  5. Every weight has its own note: the click feature (‘heavier is lower’, one chord) beside the nine bars drawn large with their numerals and pips, so colour is never the only cue. With it come the accessibility feature, ‘quiet by design’ (separate sound and haptics switches), and the founder signal that the game's sounds are its only recorded assets.
  6. Three verses: value points 2–4 (one answer, proven by machine; no timer, no lives; nothing to read, nothing collected) set as lyric stanzas, separated by a single-dot rest.
  7. #chapters, Four songs, one purchase: the four chapters listed like songbook titles: The Hang · Morning Sky, free; The Secret · Twilight Meadow; The Cascade · Deep Sea; The Exhibition · Evening Stars; 20 levels each. Then the plans as two blocks (Chapter I Free, highlighted; Chapters II–IV $2.99 once), the plans_footnote, and the badge on the plate.
  8. The Lantern and the stars: the three Lantern steps, numbered because the sequence is real, and the grades Hung · Unshaken · Once as words with three warm-white dots. There are no gold stars, so nothing can read as a rating.
  9. Who it's for and who it isn't: two lyric lists, five lines and four.
  10. #about: the about_heading and the show_body markdown at 62ch.
  11. The maker: the founder bio as a quoted verse under the Lagerland mark, with the five signals, the response line and a mailto link.
  12. #faq: 13 <details>, each question led by a muted ‘?’ dot that fills with felt dust when opened.
  13. #privacy, Nothing collected: data collection none and the seven notes, including that the motion sensor is read live and never stored. Links go to the privacy policy, to support and to /transparency/.
  14. Quick reference: the ai-canonical <details>, kept in the DOM.
  15. Reprise: the instrument once more at half height; ‘Play Chapter I free’ with the badge and price.value; other Lagerland apps (computed); the maker and freshness line (Built by Lagerland Apps · version 1.0 · release dates); and the Lagerland strip.

Navigation

A song list at the top right in Andika 700 16px: How it plays (#how-it-works), Chapters & price (#chapters), Questions (#faq) and Privacy (#privacy). Each link has a small coloured note-dot that fills when its section is current. The ‘Sound: off/on’ switch sits beside them. It is a real <button aria-pressed>, and its state is kept per viewer in localStorage, guarded with try/catch. Mobile: ‘Contents’ opens a <details> sheet on rail felt with the same links and the Sound switch. Focus: a 3px #FFF3EA outline with a 2px felt gap, on every bar, dot, hook and link.

Motion

Struck, not swung. A sounding bar vibrates ±1.5px for three decaying cycles (240ms), and its light fades over 900ms like a ringing note. Beams tilt fast with a short decay rather than a long swing. Sections enter with no motion at all; the page stays still until it is played. The sticky keyboard rises over 240ms. Reduced motion removes the vibration and the decay animation but keeps the state changes.

Privacy, support and comparison pages

Privacy and support keep the felt. A 200px masthead carries the wordmark and the nine-bar mark, with the title in Tilt Warp 52px (32px on mobile). The reading column is Andika 400 at 19px/1.7 and 64ch, warm white on felt (15.4:1), with H2s in Tilt Warp 28px. Lists are set as lyric stanzas, with a felt-dust note-dot for each item. There is no rainbow in the reading column. Privacy: the page opens with the muted-bar chip ‘Data collected: none’. Support: the email is set large, then the response line, then the restore and unlock steps as numbered lines, closing on the maker's plate with the badge. Alternatives (future): any /alternatives/<competitor>/ page sets its table on rail felt #24101A, ruled in 1px #D9B9C4, with Tare's column marked by a 4px cap in a bar colour.

Materials

Claret case felt #34121F as the page ground, in flat colour. · Nine enamel bars with rounded 8px ends and two felt-dust rivets each, resting on two converging #24101A felt rails and stepping down in length from 9 to 1. · Coloured note-dots: 44px circles in a bar colour, with the Tilt Warp numeral and pips in bar ink. They are used wherever a weight value appears. · The muted “?” token: felt-covered #5A3443 with a dashed felt-dust outline. · Warm-white 3px beams with notch ticks and 1.5px strings, drawn as notation rather than as toys. · The song card: a clue card outlined in 2px warm white that quotes the pieces as mini dots.

Colour strategy

Full palette · dark

Type rationale

Play-by-colour notation depends on round, heavy, monoline lining figures that sit centred in a dot or stamped on a bar. Tilt Warp's soft, sturdy forms give that stamp without a nursery wobble. SIL drew Andika for people learning to read, with an unambiguous a, I, l and 1. The songbook exists so non-readers can play, and Andika keeps the words just as easy. About 49 KB in all.

New assets needed

No raster or audio files. Bars, dots, rails and the mobile are inline SVG/CSS, and the tones are synthesized in Web Audio (illustrative and labelled as such). At launch: the QR via scripts/generate-qr.py. Optionally, real per-weight tones from the app (its sounds are its only recorded assets) can replace the sketch.

Fixes queued before this style is built (7)
  • blockerRe-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.
  • majorrightsplit-c keeps oxblood, the app's own maroon. Re-felt tare-c in a colour no surface uses, e.g. deep olive (~#33361F); Tare's Evening Stars indigo works only if soon-a is not chosen. Remove the hanging mobile from tare-c's hero. The nine bars on their converging rails become the one playable object across the width, and the level is written as a play-by-colour song line on the song card, solved in notation.
  • majorAdd one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).
  • majorMake it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.
  • blockerGate every App Store element on status: wrap the badge, the sticky bar, the QR, cta_label/cta_subline and the apple-itunes-app meta in {% if page.status == 'live' %}. Before launch, render one plain status line in the world's own type, with no Apple artwork and no 'download' verb, e.g. 'Tare is not on the App Store yet. This page holds its rules, privacy and support.' State the price as 'At launch: 20 levels free · $2.99 unlocks 60 more'. Mock the pre-launch state for the owner, and show the live state only as a toggle.
  • majorPrint 'first released' only when status is live. Before launch, print 'Version 1.0 in preparation · page updated {{ release.last_updated }}'.
  • majorBefore build, add a tare row (manifest_source: pending; tracking_domains 0; third_party_sdks 0; network_calls none; data_leaves_device no, all from the front-matter privacy block) and deep-link /transparency/#tare. Until that row exists, the privacy block must say 'Not yet on the transparency record; added at launch' rather than imply a verified entry.

Or the category standard, played straight: a puzzle-game landing page played straight. Full-bleed sky-blue key art behind a tilted iPhone showing a level, with ‘Hang the weights. Balance every beam.’ in a rounded casual face and a big Download button. Below: a row of four icon feature tiles (80 levels · Offline · No ads · Hints), a screenshot carousel (which Tare cannot fill yet), two pricing cards and an FAQ accordion.

Rollout plan: one branch and one PR per phase

23 phases, each with exactly one branch and one PR. Phase 0 changes nothing visible: contract includes, world dispatcher, SEO parity guard, preview and promotion tooling. Phase 1 pilots Observa end to end. Phase 2 ships the studio world. Phases 3–20 ship one app microsite each, reviewed in rounds of three related apps so sister apps are judged side by side. Phase 21 is Tare (upcoming, no images). Phase 22 retires the old stylesheet and writes the design documentation. In every phase you see the three real styles of each page in a private review board, pick one, and only that one is merged. Phases are squash-merged after the SEO parity guard passes. Who writes what: in every phase the code itself (templates, CSS, JS, guard and preview scripts) is written by Sonnet subagents. The lead model owns design decisions, the style cards, reviews, the SEO parity verdicts and the finish review.

  1. P0

    Foundation: contract extraction, world dispatcher, production-engine guard, workflows and preview tooling (no visual change)

    redesign/p00-foundationXL

    Pages

    All 236 built HTML files and every generated file. Nothing may look different.

    Scope

    • Engine and workflows:
    • scripts/redesign/ci/Gemfile and its lockfile (github-pages 232 in :jekyll_plugins), and jekyll.sh.
    • .github/workflows/redesign-guard.yml (PR) and contract-main.yml (push to main, non-blocking, one tracking issue).
    • verify-live.yml (workflow_run of pages-build-deployment, plus workflow_dispatch).
    • indexnow.yml gains the [skip indexnow] guard and the urls dispatch input.
    • Tooling in scripts/redesign/: build-pair.sh, configs (local, parity with pinned time and strict_filters, style-a/b/c, force-legacy, resolver-debug), parity.py with rules, allowlist and baseline, check-contract.py with contract.yml, check-resolver.sh, lint-templates.py, scan-classes.py (writes legacy-classes.txt and legacy-tokens.txt), budget.py, capture.mjs (routes production URLs locally), vitals.mjs, pixel-diff.py, contrast.py, fetch-font.sh with fonts.lock.json, font-metrics.py, make-derivatives.py (with --check), preview-build.sh, preview-assemble.py with the switcher, promote-winner.py, check-clean.py, run-guard.sh, tag-alternatives.py, phases/pN.yml and RUNBOOK.md.
    • Templates (output stays DOM-equivalent):
    • _includes/contract/ (resolver with nested ifs; head with the preview and debug metas; schema includes; quick-answer, ai-canonical, badge, qr, sticky-bar, price, rating, privacy-proof, maker, footer-strip, skip-link, alt-links, related, derivative).
    • _includes/legacy/ (document, assets with today's preloads verbatim, app-body, journal-body, privacy-body, support-body, and pages/* for home and hubs).
    • The dispatcher in default.html; schema emitted through contract includes in the other layouts. In head, page.layout == 'app' becomes page.collection == 'apps' for the Smart App Banner and og:type.
    • The app-card.html and quick-answer.html shims, and the [data-sticky-sentinel] selector in animations.js.
    • Config and data:
    • theme: null in _config.yml (zero diff on the production engine) and _config.preview.yml.
    • _data/worlds/<id>.yml for all 21 worlds, each legacy; an empty _data/derivatives.yml.
    • Content (output identical):
    • The codemod adds app: to the 104 alternatives pages.
    • items: lifted into for/index.html and guides/index.html; faq: into index.html; for_apps: into the 4 audience pages.
    • The /alternatives/ index's numberOfItems computed with its existing where_exp.
    • Assets: Apple's official badge SVG, supplied by the owner, committed unused under assets/badges/. The Mac App Store badge decision is recorded.
    • Docs: a 'Redesign in progress' section in CLAUDE.md:
    • a where-things-moved table: integration point 2 (alt_pairs) moves to contract/alt-links.html; point 4 is unchanged except the computed numberOfItems; the /for/ hub, /guides/ hub and home FAQ are edited through items:/faq:; audience app lists through for_apps:;
    • app: as integration point 5;
    • deploy verification through MCP and verify-live.yml instead of curl;
    • the run-guard.sh command.
    • Baseline: a full-site capture of main plus baseline/incumbent.json, published as a private 'Baseline' Artifact.
    • Smoke test: the whole preview pipeline on a fixture world in a scratch branch (never pushed).
    • Merge: the squash commit carries [skip indexnow].

    How you pick in this phase

    No styles. The owner approves three things: - the zero-diff guard report; - the incumbent baseline, i.e. the existing defects, acknowledged and scheduled rather than fixed here; - the baseline contact sheet.

    The switcher, database pick and promotion are smoke-tested on a fixture world first, so the review flow is known to work before P1.

    Done when

    • Relative rules, main vs branch: 0 FAIL, 0 WARN, empty allowlist. - The generated files, the 5 redirect-from stubs and /apps/thewait/ are byte-identical under the pinned time. - All 236 HTML files are DOM-equivalent once script[type=application/ld+json] is removed and whitespace normalised. - JSON-LD and microdata multisets are identical per URL. - Rendered coverage is identical.
    • The sanity assertions pass on both builds: 225 <loc>, 8 redirects.json keys, all stubs, non-empty generators.
    • pixel-diff.py ≤ 0.1% on every HTML URL at 1440 and 390, in light and dark.
    • A force-legacy build equals the default build byte for byte.
    • CI redesign-guard is green. - actions/jekyll-build-pages builds base and head. - The resolver fixtures assert the expected world for every URL kind under legacy, preview + style, shipped and force_legacy. - lint-templates.py is clean.
    • The local jekyll.sh digest for main equals the CI digest. Adding theme: null changes 0 bytes on the production engine.
    • check-contract.py: - every alternatives page has an app: that matches its body; - the relocated hubs have empty bodies; - legacy-classes.txt, legacy-tokens.txt and baseline/incumbent.json are committed, and the owner has approved the baseline.
    • The preview pipeline smoke test succeeds on the fixture world: 3 builds, assemble, chunked publish, a pick recorded in the database, promote, check-clean.
    • Official badge SVG committed (unused). Mac App Store badge decision recorded.
    • After merge, read through MCP: - the pages-build-deployment run (workflow 227213120) for the merge SHA concluded success; - verify-live.yml fired from workflow_run (or was dispatched) and passed for every sitemap URL; - the IndexNow run was skipped.

    Risks

    • Variables assigned in includes leak into callers (app, parts, price_model). Mitigation: w_ prefixes, and DOM equivalence proves nothing changed.
    • Lifting hand-written hub lists into front matter could change markup subtly. Mitigation: per-item fields cover irregular cards, and DOM equivalence plus JSON-LD multisets prove the output is identical.
    • workflow_run may not fire for the dynamic pages-build-deployment workflow. Mitigation: proven on P0's own merge; the fallback is a dispatch through MCP actions_run_trigger.
    • The 104-file codemod can conflict with concurrent content edits. Mitigation: run it last, right after merging main; contract-main.yml catches any page added afterwards.
    • Byte-identical HTML may be impossible after the include moves. Mitigation: the bar is DOM equivalence (JSON-LD compared separately) plus pixel identity. Generated files stay byte-identical.

    How you pick in this phase

    The 'P1 Observa review' Artifact shows the 11 pages × (A, B, C) live, plus Current as captures, at 390 and 1440, with the JS-off toggle. Each candidate passes tier 1 first.

    The owner picks one style for the Observa world, through the database pick button or in chat. The read variants follow that pick. One revision round on the picked style.

    The pick is confirmed in chat. Then the tag redesign/p1-candidates is pushed, promote-winner.py --world observa --pick <x> runs, and check-clean must pass.

    Done when

    • Standard gate G1–G9 passes (G9 read through MCP).
    • Absolute rules on the app page: - .quick-answer__body equals the front matter, sits before the second h2, and its top is within 1.5 viewports at 390 and 1440 (the baseline was 1.97). - The ai-canonical details block is present. - At least 2 official badges link to https://apps.apple.com/app/id6757438990; the sentinel badge is fully inside the first viewport at 1440×900 and 390×844. - The QR shows at 1440 and is hidden at 390. The sticky bar behaves correctly and never hides focus.
    • Every block key in Observa's front matter renders [data-block], through the world partial or the fallback, with its leaf text rendered-visible at 390 and 1440. That includes 'Free · Pro optional', 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo', all 4 plans, the footnote, 5 release notes, #how-it-works with 6 steps, and 12 FAQs.
    • Founder and maker lines show 2026-07-11 and 2026-01-01. The privacy-proof links and the footer strip are present.
    • JSON-LD is identical on the app page: SoftwareApplication with AggregateOffer (high price 49.99, offer count 4), FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, HowTo, the founder Organization and speakable. Titles, descriptions, canonicals and head-tag counts are identical on all 11 URLs.
    • The 8 alternatives pages: - 100% static and rendered coverage; - comparison-table cells have non-zero padding and visible rules (a computed-style check); - the app-card is in Observa's style.
    • Budgets: lab LCP ≤ 2.0 s, page images ≤ 1.0 MB (from ≈ 12 MB), fonts ≤ 160 KB, every preload used. axe shows 0 serious or critical issues. The VoiceOver pass is done.
    • The owner has approved the aggregated inbound-link table. The tag is pushed and there are no a/b/c leftovers. RUNBOOK.md is updated with timings and guard fixes.

    Risks

    • The contract or dispatcher may prove insufficient. Mitigation: that is this phase's purpose, and nothing else is built on them yet.
    • Shared block partials and read-base could make worlds converge. Mitigation: the partials are semantic only; worlds own order, grouping and form and may override any partial; the finish review compares worlds.
    • The microsite loses the sitewide studio footer links. Mitigation: the strip adds /alternatives/ and the /for/ pages, and the link graph checks orphans and depth relative to base.
    • The owner may not decide. Mitigation: one bounded revision round; otherwise the world is deferred.
    • The testimonial star decision blocks content. Mitigation: ask during P0 (see the open questions).

    Taskful Day microsite

    redesign/p09-taskful-dayL

    Pages

    /apps/taskful-day/ plus privacy and support; alternatives: habitica, habitnow, productive, streaks-app, way-of-life

    Scope

    Review round “calm time” (Taskful Day, Soon., EarnLock): the three apps are shown together in one review board so siblings can't drift into one look, but each ships as its own phase, branch and PR.

    • 9 candidates. This is the /for/calm-productivity cluster.
    • EarnLock: spotlight stats (without the banned hero-metric template, with values server-rendered), release_notes, Apple Watch, and the terms page. The EarnLock world links /apps/earnlock/terms/ from its app page or footer strip and from its support page, which fixes the incumbent orphan.
    • Soon.: roadmap. Soon. and Taskful Day have light app UIs.
    • Why next: 22 alternatives pages (screen-time and countdown comparisons) make it the biggest organic surface left, even though the ratings sum is only 7.

    How you pick in this phase

    The owner picks per app. The Artifact shows the app page, privacy, support and terms, plus the 3 highest-traffic alternatives pages per app (from GSC if available; otherwise the canonical comparison from comparison_slugs plus two more). All 32 URLs pass tier 1; the winners pass tier 2 on all 32.

    Done when

    • Each world PR passes the standard gate G1–G9.
    • Spotlight stat values are in the HTML and identical with JS off. No big-number-plus-small-label template.
    • /apps/earnlock/terms/ now has inbound links and a click depth ≤ 3, which clears its baseline entry. The terms page keeps 100% coverage.
    • EarnLock's hero badge sits fully inside the first viewport at 1440 and 390, and its quick answer within 1.5 viewports (the baseline failed both).
    • All 22 alternatives pages: 0 FAIL; comparison tables keep padding and rules.

    Risks

    • The light UIs of Soon. and Taskful Day push toward the spent cream-and-serif palette. Mitigation: choose light or dark from the use scene.
    • Large read-variant volume. Mitigation: alternatives bodies share one read frame per world plus read-base, and the static guard covers all of them automatically.
