    • WanderWiki: the hero video is transcoded to MP4 and WebM ≤ 1.5 MB with a poster. They are registered in _data/derivatives.yml under the .mov path that hero.video names, never hard-coded in the world. Pause control, and off under reduced motion. WanderWiki also uses plateau_disclosure and training_vocabulary.
    • Millrace: a free game with its own pricing_note. Its badge and quick-answer position are fixed.
    • GSC data may move this batch earlier: MediaKit's 14 converter comparisons could be the biggest organic surface in the catalogue.

    How you pick in this phase

    The owner picks per app. MediaKit's Artifact sample is the app page plus 3 of its 14 alternatives pages; all 14 pass tier 1, and the winner passes tier 2 on all 14.

    Done when

    • Each world PR passes the standard gate G1–G9.
    • The video meets its budget, resolves through derivatives.yml, and behaves correctly under reduced motion and pause. The poster is the LCP.
    • Millrace's pricing_note and plans_footnote are visible, and the 'free' price statement is correct. Millrace's badge is inside the first viewport, and its quick answer within 1.5 viewports.
    • MediaKit: no horizontal overflow at 390 or 320.
    • The redirect stubs are byte-identical.

    Risks

    • Three unrelated apps make for a weakly coherent review. Mitigation: present them as three separate worlds; nothing is shared.
    • The video re-encode is an asset task that needs the owner's approval.
  22. P21

    Tare (upcoming and unlisted; works without images)

    redesign/p21-tareS

    Pages

    3 URLs: /apps/tare/, /apps/tare/privacy/, /apps/tare/support/. Status stays upcoming and sitemap: false; the page is not listed anywhere.

    Scope

    • Three styles whose material is type, colour and structure only: no icon, no screenshots, no QR file, no OG card.
    • The QR and icon includes render nothing when their files are missing. That removes today's broken images (allowlisted).
    • privacy-proof shows the privacy and support links only. Tare has no _data/transparency.yml row; one is added with the owner at launch.
    • The badge still links to app_store_url.
    • The page keeps working unchanged when the launch adds an icon and screenshots, because the world declares where they slot in.
    • Can run in parallel with any phase after P1; its files are all per-world.

    How you pick in this phase

    The owner picks one of three. Recommend timing it so the pick happens before launch day.

    Done when

    • Standard gate G1–G9 passes.
    • No broken images. Status and sitemap settings unchanged. Not linked from any listing (inbound from listings stays 0, as today).
    • No /transparency/#tare link is emitted (no broken fragment). The privacy and support links are present.
    • The privacy URL that the app hard-codes still serves with all its policy fields.

    Risks

    • Designing before the Signboard Sky screenshots exist. Mitigation: the world declares the slots, and the launch adds images without a redesign.
  23. P22

    Hardening: retire legacy, studio fallback, finish reviews, DESIGN.md and CLAUDE.md

    redesign/p22-hardening-docsL

    Pages

    All URLs. Content changes only from finish-review fixes.

    Scope

    • Cumulative parity first: a force-legacy build against the shipped build with the same content, over the whole site (relative rules plus rendered coverage). The report goes to the owner as an Artifact before anything is deleted.
    • Retire legacy:
    • delete assets/css/style.css, assets/js/animations.js, assets/fonts/{inter-var,newsreader-roman,newsreader-italic}.woff2 and _includes/legacy/*;
    • delete the frozen legacy includes once they have zero references (hero, pricing, screenshots, who-its-for, how-it-works, insight-gallery, jump-nav, testimonials-ticker, you-might-like, alternatives, faq, header, footer);
    • remove the legacy branches and force-legacy handling. theme: null (P0) keeps Primer from serving its own style.css at the freed URL.
    • Untagged alternatives pages now resolve to the studio read frame, and contract-main.yml opens an issue for them.
    • Keep the preview mechanism for future redesigns.
    • Future apps: worlds/studio/app-fallback/ (complete contract, studio style, contract blocks) with a fixture test.
    • Finish review: impeccable-finish-reviewer on each of the 21 worlds; apply its fixes.
    • DESIGN.md: impeccable-documenter writes it as an index (shared contract, read-base tokens, block partials, budgets, how worlds resolve) with one section per world, plus .impeccable/design.json.
    • CLAUDE.md: replace 'Design system v3 Paper & Ink' with the worlds system: contract includes, _data/worlds/<id>.yml, adding an app or world, the hub items:/faq:/for_apps: sources, alternatives integration point 5 (app:), derivatives, the guard commands, contract-main and verify-live, budgets and the allowed class/token vocabulary. Fix the stale 96 count; counts are computed.
    • Owner sign-off: a final contact sheet of every URL at 1440 and 390.
    • Timing: start only after the last app phase has been live for at least 14 days with no rollback.

    How you pick in this phase

    No new styles. The owner signs off on the cumulative report, the finish-review fixes and the final contact sheet.

    Done when

    • Standard gate G1–G9 passes.
    • Zero references to retired files in the built site and source. The production-engine build serves no /assets/css/style.css. The URL set is unchanged except for allowlisted asset removals.
    • Cumulative parity against force-legacy: 0 FAIL on every indexable URL (the 225 sitemap entries) plus Tare, across titles, descriptions, canonicals, head-tag counts, JSON-LD, h1, quick answer and static and rendered coverage. Every baseline defect is cleared or acknowledged as by design (Tare and 404).
    • A fixture app with no world entry renders with a complete contract and every block through the studio fallback.
    • contract-main.yml is green on main with no legacy renderer left: every live URL passes the absolute rules, and there are no stale derivatives.
    • DESIGN.md and CLAUDE.md are updated (both stay excluded from the build). Every finish-review must-fix is closed.
    • The 28-day GSC review plan is agreed: clicks, impressions, CTR, position and CWV for each world's URLs against out-of-scope controls.

    Risks

    • After this phase, per-world rollback is no longer one line. Mitigation: wait 14 days or more; git revert of a world's squash commit stays available.
    • Hidden references to style.css or animations.js in content bodies. Mitigation: grep the built site and source before deleting; verify-live checks every referenced asset returns 200.
Architecture

Model split (owner instruction): all implementation code — Liquid templates, world CSS, vanilla JS, the scripts under scripts/redesign/ — is written by Sonnet subagents, one world or one tool per agent. The lead model writes the briefs and style contracts they build from, reviews every diff and capture, runs the parity guard verdicts and the finish review, and owns every merge decision.

1. Rules the architecture keeps

  • No changes to URLs or front-matter meaning. Permalinks, layout names (default, app, journal, privacy, support) and every existing key keep their meaning.
  • P0 adds only keys lifted from each page's own body, and the rendered output stays identical:
    • app: <slug> on the 104 alternatives pages;
    • items: on for/index.html and guides/index.html;
    • faq: on index.html;
    • for_apps: on the 4 audience pages.
  • The redesign never edits _apps/*.md (the ratings bot owns those files), the _journal/*.md bodies (they feed feed.xml), or _data/{transparency,testimonials,app_enrichment}.yml.
  • It adds _data/worlds/<id>.yml and _data/derivatives.yml. No generator template reads them.
  • It adds theme: null to _config.yml. Without it, deleting style.css in P22 would let Primer's style.scss take over the same URL.
  • Machine-facing output comes only from layouts and contract includes, never from a world. That covers <head>, every JSON-LD block, microdata, speakable targets and the generated files.
  • A lint stops any world head.html from emitting title, description, robots, canonical, OG, Twitter or apple-itunes-app tags, or ld+json.
  • Every front-matter block renders. Section order, grouping and form belong to the world, but every block present in front matter must appear.
  • The world renders a block either with its own partial or with the shared contract/blocks/<key>.html, and the element always carries data-block="<key>".
  • Each contract include marks its root with data-contract="<name>".
  • Content stays where authors edit it. Hand-written bodies are not rewritten: the 104 alternatives pages, the /alternatives/ index, 5 guides, 4 audience pages, about, /support/, the app sub-pages and the journal markdown.
  • Only bodies that are really layouts move into templates: home, /apps/, /journal/, the /for/ and /guides/ hubs, and transparency.
  • Their lists render from front matter (items:, faq:) or from collections, so an author still edits one place.
  • check-contract.py fails a PR, and contract-main.yml flags a push, if any of these pages gains body content again.
  • One file per world. _data/worlds/<id>.yml holds status: legacy | preview | shipped, plus handles: (the block keys the world designed itself) and contrast_pairs:. Separate files mean per-world PRs never conflict, and the status field doubles as the rollback switch.

2. World resolution: _includes/contract/resolve-world.html

The resolver assigns only w_-prefixed variables, because include assigns leak into the caller. It uses nested ifs, with no not, no parentheses and one and/or per condition, since Liquid evaluates and/or right to left and silently mis-parses parentheses.

{%- assign w_id = 'studio' -%}{%- assign w_mode = 'read' -%}
{%- if page.collection == 'apps' -%}
  {%- assign w_id = page.slug -%}{%- assign w_mode = 'persuade' -%}
{%- elsif page.app -%}
  {%- assign w_id = page.app -%}
{%- else -%}
  {%- assign w_parts = page.url | split: '/' -%}
  {%- if w_parts[1] == 'apps' and w_parts.size > 3 -%}
    {%- assign w_id = w_parts[2] -%}
  {%- elsif w_parts[1] == 'alternatives' and w_parts.size > 2 -%}
    {%- assign w_id = '' -%}
  {%- elsif page.url == '/' -%}
    {%- assign w_mode = 'persuade' -%}
  {%- endif -%}
{%- endif -%}
{%- assign w_conf = site.data.worlds[w_id] -%}
{%- assign w_live = false -%}
{%- unless site.force_legacy -%}
  {%- if w_conf.status == 'shipped' -%}
    {%- assign w_live = true -%}
  {%- elsif w_conf.status == 'preview' -%}
    {%- if site.preview_style -%}{%- assign w_live = true -%}{%- endif -%}
  {%- endif -%}
{%- endunless -%}
  • What the branches cover:
  • /apps/<slug>/<sub>/ covers privacy, support, methodology, coaches, terms and api-access.
  • An alternatives page with no app: resolves to '', which means legacy until P22. From P22 on it uses the studio read frame, and contract-main.yml opens an issue.
  • Template choice. w_tpl is assigned the same way (page, privacy, support, read, home, hub-apps, hub-journal, hub-for, hub-guides, post, article, transparency).
  • Paths.
  • Shipped: w_dir = worlds/<id> and w_asset = /assets/worlds/<id>/<id>.
  • Candidate: w_dir = worlds/<id>/<site.preview_style> and w_asset = /assets/worlds/<id>/<site.preview_style>.
  • Which config sets what.
  • site.preview_style is set only by scripts/redesign/config/style-{a,b,c}.yml.
  • site.force_legacy is set only by config/force-legacy.yml.
  • site.resolver_debug is set only by config/resolver-debug.yml. It makes the contract head emit <meta name="lagerland-world" content="id|mode|tpl|dir"> for the fixture tests.
  • Safety. GitHub Pages builds with plain _config.yml, so a branch that carries candidates still renders legacy there, and an unselected style cannot reach production by mistake.

3. Layouts

  • _layouts/default.html becomes the dispatcher.
  • Live world: <html class="w-{{w_id}}">, then contract/head.html, then {% include {{ w_dir }}/head.html %}. The world head holds theme-color, color-scheme, at most 2 font preloads, the stylesheets, its own LCP image preload, and its JS with defer. Then contract/skip-link.html, then {% include {{ w_dir }}/{{ w_tpl }}.html body=content %}, then contract/footer-strip.html (app worlds only), then /assets/js/contract.js with defer.
  • Otherwise: {% include legacy/document.html body=content %}, which is today's markup verbatim.
  • _layouts/app.html keeps its name.
  • It always includes contract/app-schema.html first. That file holds SoftwareApplication with Offer/AggregateOffer, aggregateRating only when count ≥ 25, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, HowTo, CreativeWork and the founder Person/Organization, all moved verbatim from today's app.html.
  • Then it renders either {{ w_dir }}/page.html, followed by contract/blocks/rest.html and contract/sticky-bar.html, or legacy/app-body.html.
  • journal.html, privacy.html and support.html work the same way, with contract/journal-schema.html (Article, FAQPage and Breadcrumb, with speakable .quick-answer__body and .faq-a).
  • Head conditions.
  • In contract/head.html, the Smart App Banner and og:type tests become page.collection == "apps", which matches exactly the same pages.
  • Both image preloads (the per-app first screenshot, and /assets/screenshots/observa/1.png on /) leave the contract.
  • legacy/assets.html keeps them byte for byte with today's tests. Each world head preloads only its own derivative, using imagesrcset/imagesizes.
  • Never create _layouts/redirect.html. jekyll-redirect-from would start using it for its stubs.

4. Contract includes (_includes/contract/)

Each is listed with its marker and what it emits or computes. - head.html emits: - title (seo.title or title), meta description, author, publisher, robots, keywords, icons, canonical and hreflang; - the alternate links to the feed, ai-index.json, llms, llms-full and the sitemaps, plus rel=me; - all OG and Twitter tags, the Organization and WebSite JSON-LD with computed counts, the Smart App Banner, the inline html.js line, and GoatCounter.

Preview builds (site.preview) instead emit noindex,nofollow and <meta name="lagerland-preview">, and leave out GoatCounter. - Schema includes: app-schema.html, journal-schema.html and schema/{home,apps,for,guides,journal}.html. - Hub ItemLists and the home FAQPage render from collections or from the page's own items:/faq:, so JSON-LD and visible lists share one source. - The /alternatives/ index keeps its JSON-LD and cards in its body. Its numberOfItems is computed with the where_exp the page already uses for its visible count. - quick-answer.html (quick-answer): .quick-answer__body (itemprop=text) plus the speakable WebPage JSON-LD. The label text is a parameter. - ai-canonical.html (ai-canonical): the "Quick reference" <details> block, verbatim. It may be restyled or moved, never hidden. - badge.html (badge): Apple's official artwork (/assets/badges/app-store-badge-en-black.svg, img 120×40 or larger, alt "Download on the App Store"), inside an <a> to app_store_url with an aria-label. Size is a parameter. It carries data-sticky-sentinel when used as the hero action. - qr.html (qr) renders only when two things are true: - platforms includes an iPhone or iPad platform (iOS, iPadOS, iPhone or iPad; Tare uses the last two); - /assets/qr/<slug>.svg exists in site.static_files.

It shows at a minimum of 96 px and is never inverted or filtered. Mac-only AppMeta and Mockly get no QR, because scanning would land an iPhone on a listing it cannot install. - sticky-bar.html (sticky-bar), price.html (price) and rating.html (rating): as before. The rating stays silent until ratings.count ≥ 25, then matches the schema. - privacy-proof.html (privacy-proof) shows the privacy.* fields and links to /apps/<slug>/privacy/ and /apps/<slug>/support/. The _data/transparency.yml row data and the /transparency/#<slug> link render only when a row for the slug exists. Tare has none. - maker.html (maker): "Built by Lagerland Apps" with Organization microdata, last updated, first released, version, the backstory link and the email. - footer-strip.html (footer-strip) is the only element shared across microsites. "A Lagerland app" links to: - home, all apps, /alternatives/; - the app's audience page(s) under /for/, computed from the for_apps: lists; - transparency, and the app's privacy policy and support.

It reads the host world's --strip-* tokens and body face, plus the Lagerland mark derivative. It has no studio-specific styling, so the pilot needs no retrofit. - Blocks. blocks/<key>.html is a shared semantic renderer for every known front-matter block key: faq, how_it_works (with #how-it-works and step ids), comparison_table, plans/pricing, release_notes, roadmap, spotlight, value_points, features, who_for, testimonials, plateau_disclosure, training_vocabulary, coach_cta, insight_gallery, example_insights, value_math, related_journal, alternatives_to, screenshots, founder and show_body. - A world styles these or overrides them with its own partial, which keeps data-block. - blocks/rest.html renders, before the maker line, every known key present in front matter but missing from the world's handles:. A block added on main later therefore always renders. - Resolvers assign variables and emit nothing: - resolve-world.html; - alt-links.html: w_alt_links and w_alt_primary, with the alt_pairs and comparison_slugs maps moved verbatim from _includes/alternatives.html; - related.html; - derivative.html: looks up site.data.derivatives[src] and falls back to the original src. - The two body-called includes stay as shims. _includes/app-card.html and _includes/quick-answer.html keep their paths. Each renders the world version when the page's world is live, and today's markup verbatim otherwise. - Required IDs. #how-it-works must exist whenever how_it_works.steps does. #faq, #pricing and #features are required whenever a link or JSON-LD URL targets them.

5. File layout

Phase time (candidates):

_data/worlds/observa.yml     {status: preview, scheme: dark, handles: [...], contrast_pairs: [...], candidates: {a: {label, kicker}, b: …, c: …}}
_includes/worlds/observa/{a,b,c}/   head.html page.html read.html privacy.html support.html app-card.html _*.html
assets/worlds/observa/{a,b,c}.css  (+ a.js only for a signature interaction)
assets/fonts/<fontsource-id>/…woff2 + LICENSE        (shared pool, fonts.lock.json)
assets/img/d/<sha8>-{360,720,1080}.webp, assets/img/d/<sha8>-{64,128,256}.webp   (content-hashed derivatives)
_data/derivatives.yml        '/assets/screenshots/observa/1.png': {sha256, w: [360,720,1080], base: /assets/img/d/<sha8>}

Shipped (after promote-winner.py):

_includes/worlds/observa/*.html   assets/worlds/observa/observa.css (+ observa.js)
_data/worlds/observa.yml  {status: shipped, scheme, handles, contrast_pairs, label, picked: 2026-11-03}
  • Partials are included through {{ w_dir }} and assets through {{ w_asset }}, so promotion is a move plus deletions, with no rewriting.
  • The studio uses _includes/worlds/studio/ (head, persuade, read, home, hub-apps, hub-journal, hub-for, hub-guides, post, article, transparency, app-card) and assets/worlds/studio/studio.css.

6. CSS

  • assets/css/contract.css (≤ 1.5 KB gz) holds mechanics only:
  • badge sizes;
  • the QR media rule (min-width:900px) and (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine);
  • the sticky bar (hidden without html.js, transform toggle, no transition under reduced motion);
  • html.js [data-reveal], .visually-hidden, the skip link, and scroll-padding fed by --sticky-h.

It sets no colour and no font. - assets/css/read-base.css (≤ 3.5 KB gz, loaded on read pages of live worlds only) is token-only structure for the legacy body vocabulary and for the shared block partials. It contains no colour or font values, only var() references to world semantic tokens. - It covers every class in legacy-classes.txt (about 100: hero, overline, lead, gradient-text, section*, grid-*, card*, faq*, btn*, compare-*, kv*, pill, prose, privacy-block, …). - It defines every inline token in legacy-tokens.txt (--s-2 to --s-5, --border-1, --border-2, --text-sm, …) mapped onto world tokens. Inline style= attributes in comparison tables therefore keep their padding and rules in every world. - Banned forms are restyled, never deleted: gradient-text becomes plain ink, and overline becomes inline meta text. - An accessibility fix to body vocabulary is one edit, not 21. - One world stylesheet per page: assets/worlds/<w>/<w>.css. It covers persuade and read, holds the tokens on .w-<id>, and follows the world's scene: a single scheme sets color-scheme, a pair is designed in both. - Vocabulary changes. scan-classes.py writes legacy-classes.txt and legacy-tokens.txt from bodies and inline styles. - A listed class or token missing from read-base is a FAIL. - A class or token that newly appears in a body (for example, from another session's page) is a WARN that the owner resolves: style it in read-base or rewrite the body. It is never a 21-world failure. - assets/css/style.css is frozen from P0. Only legacy/assets.html loads it, and P22 deletes it.

7. Fonts

  • scripts/redesign/fetch-font.sh <fontsource-id> <weights> [italic] [--variable] runs npm pack in scratch. It copies the latin woff2 files and the LICENSE into assets/fonts/<id>/, and records version, files and sha256 in fonts.lock.json.
  • Each world declares its @font-face rules (font-display: swap, latin unicode-range) and a metric-matched fallback face (computed by font-metrics.py, using fontTools). It preloads at most 2 files.
  • Budget: 160 KB of woff2 per page at most. Shared families share one cached file. Inter and Newsreader stay for legacy pages until P22.

8. JS

  • assets/js/contract.js (≤ 1.5 KB gz) does three things:
  • toggles the sticky bar from [data-sticky-sentinel];
  • sets --sticky-h;
  • runs the [data-reveal] observer with the 2.5 s force-visible safety net.
  • A world may add <w>.js (≤ 5 KB gz, defer) for its signature interaction. The server-rendered state is the fallback, and the script is inert under reduced motion.
  • animations.js stays for legacy pages. P0 gives it the [data-sticky-sentinel] selector, with .hero .actions as the fallback.

9. Images and video

  • Derivatives. make-derivatives.py (uv + Pillow) writes WebP derivatives with content-hashed names:
  • screenshots at 360, 720 and 1080 widths;
  • icons at 64, 128 and 256 px;
  • the Lagerland mark at 64 and 128 px.

It records _data/derivatives.yml, keyed by the source path and holding the source's sha256. - Lookup. Templates resolve each src through contract/derivative.html. A source with no entry (a new or renamed screenshot) falls back to the original PNG, so it is never wrong, only heavier. - Staleness. A file replaced in place cannot be detected at build time (Liquid cannot hash files). contract-main.yml runs make-derivatives.py --check on every push and reports stale or missing entries. - Video. WanderWiki's video derivatives (MP4, WebM, poster) are entries keyed by the .mov path in hero.video, never hard-coded in a world. - Markup. Images use srcset/sizes, width and height, and fetchpriority=high on the LCP image only. JSON-LD screenshot/image and og:image keep the original URLs.

10. Read variants

  • Privacy, support and the app-owned sub-pages (aftershift/methodology, gymlogger-x/coaches, earnlock/terms, appmeta-pulse/api-access) get their world from the URL.
  • Alternatives pages get it from app:, which P0's codemod tag-alternatives.py adds from each body's where: "slug". An untagged page stays legacy (until P22) rather than wearing the wrong world.
  • The world's read.html owns the frame. The reading column stays calm.

11. Generated files and redirects

  • llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai-index.json, ai-sitemap.xml, feed.xml, sitemap.xml, sitemap_index.xml, robots.txt, humans.txt, .well-known/* and redirects.json are layout: none templates or plugin output, so the redesign cannot change them. The guard requires them byte-identical under the pinned time:.
  • Redirect stubs:
  • 5 come from jekyll-redirect-from: /apps/calm-2048/ and /apps/zen-2048/ (from _apps/millrace.md), and /apps/screenflow-studio/ with its privacy/ and support/ (from Mockly's pages). redirects.json lists 8 keys because it also includes the index.html variants.
  • /apps/thewait/ is a hand-written layout: null stub.
  • All 6 must stay byte-identical, and no redirect_from key is touched.

12. Engines

  • Local builds all run through scripts/redesign/jekyll.sh:
  • the github-pages 232 bundle from scripts/redesign/ci/Gemfile (gem 'github-pages', group: :jekyll_plugins, lockfile committed);
  • run with that folder as the working directory and -s <src> -d <out> --safe;
  • BUNDLE_PATH in scratch (never under the repo, since exclude: replaces Jekyll's defaults);
  • LANG=C.UTF-8 (Primer's Sass fails under a POSIX locale) and JEKYLL_ENV=production;
  • overlays config/local.yml (baseurl: "", which stops github-metadata's blocked API call) and config/parity.yml (time: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", liquid: {strict_filters: true}).
  • CI uses actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1, the real Pages builder, with GITHUB_TOKEN. A CI-only step appends the parity keys to each checkout's _config.yml; nothing is committed.
  • Template lint rejects find, find_exp, {% render %}, not, and parentheses or mixed and/or in conditions.

13. Drift after shipping (.github/workflows/contract-main.yml)

It runs on: push to main, is non-blocking, and keeps one tracking issue up to date. It runs: - pages-compat; - check-contract.py absolute rules on every live-world URL (every block key present renders data-block with its leaf text visible; markers; required ids); - the app: check on alternatives pages; - the check that relocated hubs have empty bodies; - the derivative staleness check; - an unknown-block-key report for _apps/*.md.

This covers launches and edits that go straight to main under CLAUDE.md, and the ratings bot's commits.

14. Rollback and future apps

  • Until P22, setting status: legacy in one world file is a one-line revert. After P22, use git revert of the world's squash commit (a new commit, never a history rewrite).
  • P22 adds _includes/worlds/studio/app-fallback/: a full-contract page in the studio's style for any future app that has no world yet.
Previewing and picking the three real styles

Previews are not Jekyll pages

Rendering /preview/<slug>/<a|b|c>/ inside a Jekyll build has three problems: - the llms and sitemap lists and the hub counts would pick up the preview copies; - safe mode allows no generator plugin, so it would mean committing stub files; - the copies would carry wrong canonicals.

Instead, every candidate renders at its real URL in its own full-site build, and the review pages are assembled outside Jekyll. /preview/ paths exist only inside the private Artifact.

Candidate builds (scripts/redesign/preview-build.sh pN)

  • phases/pN.yml lists the phase's world branches and representative URLs.
  • For each world branch and each style x: jekyll.sh <worktree> build-<world>-<x> _config.preview.yml config/style-<x>.yml.
  • build-current comes from a worktree of origin/main.
  • _config.preview.yml sits at the repo root. Its leading underscore means Jekyll never serves it, and GitHub Pages reads only _config.yml. It contains only preview: true.
  • Every build uses the production engine (section 12 of the architecture), so the owner approves exactly what Pages will render.

Two-tier gating

  • Tier 1, every candidate before the owner sees it (cheap, fully automated):
  • static rules on all in-scope URLs: parity.py relative rules, check-contract.py markers and blocks, budget.py, template and CSS lint, contrast tokens;
  • a quick capture of the representative pages at 390 and 1440 in the world's scheme, JS on and off: badge in the first viewport, quick answer within 1.5 viewports, no overflow, rendered coverage, no console errors.
  • Tier 2, the promoted winner only:
  • the full capture matrix, vitals and axe on every in-scope URL;
  • the VoiceOver pass.

Losing styles are never polished past tier 1.

Assembly (scripts/redesign/preview-assemble.py --phase pN)

Output in $SCRATCH/preview/pN/:

index.html  switcher.css  switcher.js  manifest.json
preview/<page-id>/{a,b,c}.html                 (e.g. preview/observa--app/b.html)
current/<page-id>-{390,1440}-{top,full}.jpg     (Current = captures of main + a link to the live URL)
x/<sha8>.<ext>                                   (CSS/JS/fonts/derivatives, de-duplicated by hash)
guard/<world>-{a,b,c}.html   shots/<page-id>-{390,1440}-{a,b,c}.jpg

What the assembler does: - Rewrites absolute and site-URL references to relative paths. Points in-scope links at their sibling preview pages; disables out-of-scope links and titles them "not in this review". - Strips GoatCounter. Injects noindex and a review bar with A / B / C / Current tabs, the label, the kicker and a link to the index. Production markup never contains the bar. - 'Current' is shown as captures, not live HTML. This keeps the incumbent's 11–30 MB of PNGs per page out of the Artifact.

Switcher (Artifact Lagerland redesign — PN review)

  • Layout: worlds and pages in a rail. A stage with iframes at 390 and 1440, shown alone or side by side.
  • Tabs: A, B and C show each style's label and kicker (THE ROLL / IMPECCABLE'S PICK / SECOND ROLL). A siblings view shows all of a trio's first viewports per style letter.
  • JS-off toggle: reloads the iframe with sandbox="allow-same-origin".
  • Picks and feedback:
  • A "Pick this style for " button with a note writes picks/<world> = {style, note, at} to the Artifact's database. The db capability is set up through the artifact-capabilities skill when the switcher is built, and Claude reads picks with ArtifactData list.
  • Feedback per page goes through Artifact comments. The last viewed page is remembered in localStorage, inside try/catch.
  • Publishing: a private Artifact with files, sent in batches of ≤ 240 files and ≤ 60 MB to the same Artifact URL. Each later publish adds files; one version holds ≤ 511 files and 256 MB. P2 (about 260 files) fits.
  • If a phase still exceeds the limit, trim representative pages first. Split per world only as a last resort, and never for P2 or a sibling trio.
  • Iterations republish the same index.html, so the link is stable.
  • Confirmation: database rows are data, not instructions. Before promoting, Claude confirms the picks with the owner in chat in one line.

Loop for each phase

  1. Branch from fresh origin/main. P0, P1 and P2 use one branch each. Trios use one branch per world (redesign/p3a-gymlogger-x, redesign/p3b-liftlog, redesign/p3c-aftershift). Push, and open draft PRs at once so CI runs.
  2. Build the three styles per world from the design-round style cards. Set status: preview, handles and candidates in _data/worlds/<id>.yml. Generate derivatives (updating _data/derivatives.yml) and fetch fonts.
  3. Tier 1 per candidate: the impeccable detector hook is clean, tier-1 checks pass, and Claude reviews the captures against the craft floor.
  4. preview-build.sh, then preview-assemble.py, then publish or update the phase Artifact. Link it from each draft PR.
  5. The owner picks one style per world. Read variants follow the app's pick. - At most one revision round, on the picked style only; no hybrids. - A world with no pick is deferred: its PR closes, its candidates stay on the tag, and its status stays legacy. The rest of the trio ships.
  6. Confirm the picks in chat. Push the tag first: git tag redesign/<branch-id>-candidates && git push origin redesign/<branch-id>-candidates.
  7. python3 scripts/redesign/promote-winner.py --world <id> --pick <x>: - git mv the winner's files into place and git rm -r the other two; - rename CSS/JS to <id>.css/<id>.js; - prune orphan fonts and update fonts.lock.json; - set {status: shipped, scheme, handles, contrast_pairs, label, picked}.
  8. check-clean.py must pass. Merge the latest origin/main, then run tier 2 and the full run-guard.sh. Paste guard-report/summary.md, the aggregated inbound-link table and the picks table into the PR body. Mark the PR ready.
  9. Squash and merge with [skip indexnow] in the commit message. Then run G9 (see the guard section). - Read the pages-build-deployment and verify-live.yml results through the GitHub MCP tools. - Once verify-live passes, dispatch indexnow.yml with the in-scope URLs.

Branch and merge conventions

  • Keeping up with main. The ratings bot pushes to main daily at 06:07 UTC and touches only rating fields in _apps/*.md, which the redesign never edits. Use git fetch origin && git merge --no-edit origin/main. Never rebase or force-push a pushed branch, and never rewrite main. If a conflict in _apps/*.md ever appears, take origin/main's version.
  • Merging. CI runs on the PR's merge ref. Squash merge keeps one commit per world on main, and losing styles never enter its history.
  • Independence. Per-world files (_data/worlds/<id>.yml, _includes/worlds/<id>/, assets/worlds/<id>/) let a trio's three PRs, and P21, merge in any order without conflicts. _data/derivatives.yml is append-only: on a conflict, keep both sides' entries.
  • Commits end with the session attribution lines.
SEO parity guard

Engines and deterministic builds

  • Local builds use jekyll.sh (github-pages 232 in the :jekyll_plugins group, safe mode, LANG=C.UTF-8, JEKYLL_ENV=production, overlays local.yml + parity.yml). parity.yml sets time: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" and liquid: {strict_filters: true}. That pins site.time everywhere (feed, ai-sitemap, ai-index, llms-full, sitemap lastmod) and makes Jekyll-4-only filters fail loudly.
  • CI builds base (the PR base SHA) and head (the merge ref) with actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1 and GITHUB_TOKEN, after appending the same keys to each checkout's _config.yml.
  • Digest: both engines print a site digest (sha256 over the sorted per-file sha256 values) to the job summary. P0 requires that the local and CI digests for main match.
  • Sanity runs before any comparison, so a vacuous pass is impossible. In both builds:
  • sitemap.xml exists with ≥ 225 <loc>;
  • redirects.json has its 8 keys;
  • the 5 redirect-from stubs and /apps/thewait/ exist;
  • llms.txt, llms-full.txt, ai-index.json, ai-sitemap.xml, feed.xml, robots.txt and the IndexNow key are non-empty.

A file missing from both builds is a FAIL, never "identical". - Scope: the guard compares the union of every file in both builds. - P22: config/force-legacy.yml gives the cumulative comparison against the pre-redesign rendering.

Scripts (all in scripts/redesign/, which the build excludes)

script inputs outputs
run-guard.sh --phase pN [--style x] [--tier 1\|2] phases/pN.yml guard-report/ and summary.md; exit 0 = pass, 1 = fail
jekyll.sh <src> <out> [overlays…] source tree build, digest
parity.py --base B --head H --src . --allow parity-allow.yml --baseline baseline/incumbent.json two builds plus source front matter parity.json/.md, linkgraph.csv, inbound.md (aggregated)
check-contract.py --site H --contract contract.yml build, _data/worlds/*, legacy-*.txt contract.json/.md
check-resolver.sh fixture configs the expected lagerland-world meta per URL kind and status
lint-templates.py _includes, _layouts, world CSS forbidden Liquid, world-head tags, CSS lint
budget.py --site H build budget.json (bytes raw/gz, unused preloads)
capture.mjs --site DIR --urls F --matrix quick\|full --out shots/<label> [--compare shots/<base>] build, served locally with gzip PNGs, capture.json, contact.html
vitals.mjs, pixel-diff.py, contrast.py, scan-classes.py, make-derivatives.py --check as named as named

Relative rules: every URL, head compared with base (parity.py and capture.mjs)

FAIL blocks the PR. WARN is listed for the owner. INFO is reported only. 1. URL set and generated files - FAIL: any HTML URL missing or added; any sitemap <loc> changed. - FAIL: any byte difference in the generated files, the IndexNow key, the Google verification file, the 5 redirect-from stubs or /apps/thewait/. - FAIL: any noindex added or removed. - FAIL: any preview leak marker in production: data-review-bar, an href or src starting with /preview/, <meta name="lagerland-preview">, or <meta name="lagerland-world">. Plain words such as max-image-preview, "Previewed" or wanderwiki_preview.mov are not markers. - WARN: new static files outside assets/{worlds,fonts,img,badges}/, contract.css, read-base.css and contract.js. Removals only via the allowlist. 2. Head - FAIL: any value change in <title>, meta description, canonical, robots, hreflang, keywords, every og:* and twitter:* tag, apple-itunes-app, rel=me, the feed and sitemap links, or html[lang]. - FAIL: the count of any of these tags differs from base (this catches duplicates emitted by a world head). - FAIL: any new external origin in script, link, img, iframe or source. Only GoatCounter is allowed, as today. - INFO: theme-color, color-scheme, stylesheets, preloads, scripts. 3. JSON-LD: every block is parsed and normalised; the per-URL multiset must be identical. A parse error is a FAIL. 4. Microdata: the itemscope/itemtype/itemprop triples must be identical. 5. H1: the count and the normalised text equal base. The verification file keeps its 0. 6. Quick answer and speakable - If the front matter has quick_answer or base had .quick-answer__body, head has exactly one, with identical text. - Every speakable cssSelector matches at least one element, and the text it matches is identical to base (for example .faq-a, and .about-strip p on the home FAQ). 7. ai-canonical: <details class="ai-canonical__details"> is present, with identical text and no hidden. 8. Front-matter coverage (app, privacy, support and journal pages): every YAML string leaf visible in base's static text must be visible in head's, reported by key path. 9. Block coverage: every base text block of 3 or more words must be found in head. FAIL when it was inside main; WARN for header, nav, footer and chrome strings. 10. Rendered coverage (capture.mjs, at 390 and 1440, with every <details> opened): every coverage string that is rendered-visible in base must be rendered-visible in head. - Visible means it is in innerText, has a non-zero box inside the document, and is not clipped or inside .visually-hidden. - Also FAIL when JS-off innerText lacks text that JS-on has. - This catches content that a world hides with CSS, for example mobile-only display:none. 11. Links and anchors - FAIL: an internal target in base's main is missing from head's main; a broken internal link; a missing fragment that an internal link or JSON-LD URL references. - FAIL: /transparency/#<slug> ids or hub anchor ids removed. - WARN: any other id removed from main, such as #roadmap, #algorithm-disclosure or #spotlight-*. - FAIL: an internal rel=nofollow. - FAIL: a URL that is indexable (listed in sitemap.xml and not noindex) becomes orphaned, or its click depth from / rises above max(base depth, 3). Existing orphans in the baseline are reported, not failed. - WARN: anchor-text changes on links to /apps/, /alternatives/, /for/ and /guides/, chrome links removed, and URLs losing more than 50% of their inbound links. These are aggregated into one inbound.md table that the owner approves once per PR. 12. Images: FAIL on any new img without alt. WARN on any image without width and height. 13. Pixels: ≤ 0.1% difference on every URL whose world is not live in head (the whole bar in P0), at 1440 and 390, in light and dark.

Absolute rules: only URLs whose world is live in head (check-contract.py, capture.mjs, budget.py)

  • A1 Markers.
  • App persuade pages need quick-answer, ai-canonical, badge (2 or more), exactly one [data-sticky-sentinel], sticky-bar, price, privacy-proof, maker, footer-strip and the skip link. They also need qr when an iPhone/iPad platform is listed and the QR file exists.
  • App read pages need the footer strip, plus a badge on alternatives pages. Privacy pages need every policy field visible.
  • Studio pages need the quick answer where one exists and the hub ItemLists, and templates must not hard-code counts (regex \b(19|20|96|104)\s+(apps|comparisons) and numberOfItems": [0-9]).
  • A2 Blocks. Every known block key present in front matter renders [data-block=<key>] with its leaf text visible. The required ids exist.
  • A3 Conversion.
  • The price-model phrase and price.value are visible.
  • privacy-proof has the privacy and support links, plus the transparency link when a row exists.
  • maker shows last_updated, first_release and version when the front matter has them.
  • aggregateRating appears if and only if a visible rating does. No star glyphs (this enforces "no stars").
  • A4 Lint.
  • World heads emit no contract-owned tags.
  • CSS: no outline:none without a :focus-visible replacement; no @import or external url(); nothing targets badge or QR pixels; a reduced-motion block whenever motion exists; every font in fonts.lock.json; read-base covers legacy-classes.txt and legacy-tokens.txt.
  • Templates: no forbidden Liquid.
  • A5 Capture FAILs.
  • Horizontal overflow at 390 or 320.
  • The badge is not fully inside the first viewport at 1440 and at 390.
  • The quick answer's top is beyond 1.5 viewport heights.
  • The QR is not visible at 1440 when required, or is visible at 390.
  • The sticky bar is wrong: visible while the sentinel is visible, or hidden after scrolling 2 viewports.
  • Focus is obscured, or has no visible change.
  • Any axe-core serious or critical violation.
  • A non-essential animation runs under reduced motion.
  • Same-origin console errors or 4xx/5xx responses.
  • A preload is not used by the first render.
  • A6 Budgets (see the budget section).

Incumbent baseline (scripts/redesign/baseline/incumbent.json, committed in P0)

P0 runs the absolute rules against main and records the results. The owner acknowledges them; they are not fixed in P0. Later phases fix them as each world goes live, and new regressions still FAIL. The list: - /guides/ has no inbound link, and /guides/best-xiangqi-apps-iphone/ is linked only from that hub; P2 fixes both. - /apps/earnlock/terms/ has no inbound link; P9–P11 fixes it. - Tare's pages and 404.html are orphaned by design. - Star glyphs appear on 94 pages with no aggregateRating. - The quick answer sits at 1.97–2.26 viewports at 390 on Observa, GymLogger X, Millrace and EarnLock. - The badge is outside the first viewport on Millrace and EarnLock. - Horizontal overflow on MediaKit at 390, and on 4 apps at 320. - Legacy markup has no contract markers.

Visual capture (capture.mjs, Playwright 1.56 from /opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright)

  • Request routing.
  • page.route('https://lagerland-apps.github.io/**') is served from the local build, because 229 pages load the mark and favicons through site.url.
  • gc.zgo.at is aborted.
  • Only same-origin errors and failed requests count. Blocked third-party requests are INFO.
  • Quick matrix (tier 1): representative pages at 390×844 and 1440×900, in the world's scheme, JS on and off.
  • Full matrix (tier 2 and P0): adds the 320×640 reflow, both colour schemes (single-scheme worlds must match within 0.5%), reduced motion on and off, and forcedColors at 390.
  • Shots: the first viewport always; the full page for the light JS-on run.
  • axe is injected from a scratch node_modules; nothing is added to the repo.

Allowlist (scripts/redesign/parity-allow.yml)

Each entry has phase, url_glob, check, match, reason and decided_by: owner|brief. Entries known in advance: - app-card star pills and the testimonial stars and average (if the owner confirms); - chrome links on microsites; - Tare's broken icon and QR img; - the QR removed from AppMeta and Mockly (if the owner confirms); - legacy chrome strings; - the P22 asset removals.

Every entry used is listed in the PR body.

CI and workflows

  • .github/workflows/redesign-guard.yml runs on pull_request to main.
  • Job pages-compat: actions/jekyll-build-pages@v1 on the merge ref, the sanity assertions, lint-templates.py, and check-resolver.sh.
    • The resolver check builds a fixture copy under legacy, preview + style, shipped, and force_legacy.
    • It asserts w_id, w_mode, w_tpl and w_dir for /, a hub, a post, an app page, a privacy page, /apps/aftershift/methodology/, and an alternatives page with and without app:.
  • Job parity: base and head built with the same action; then parity.py, check-contract.py and budget.py. Uploads guard-report, and writes the summary and digest to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.
  • .github/workflows/contract-main.yml runs on: push to main and is non-blocking. It runs pages-compat plus the absolute rules on live worlds, the app: check, the relocated-hub body check, the derivative staleness check and the unknown-block-key report. It updates one tracking issue.
  • .github/workflows/verify-live.yml runs on: workflow_run of pages-build-deployment (types: [completed]), plus workflow_dispatch with a sha input.
  • It checks out that SHA, builds it with jekyll-build-pages, and fetches every sitemap URL plus Tare, 404 and the redirect stubs from production with ?v=<sha>. It retries for up to 10 minutes for CDN propagation.
  • It compares <title>, the meta description, canonical, robots and apple-itunes-app per URL. It requires 200 for every CSS, font, JS and image URL the build references.
  • It uploads a report and writes the job summary.
  • indexnow.yml (edited in P0): its if: also skips commits whose message contains [skip indexnow]. workflow_dispatch gains a urls input, passed through an env var to indexnow-ping.py's positional-URL mode.
  • Captures, vitals and the owner's preview run locally in the session.

Standard gate, required for every PR

  • G1 CI pages-compat passes: the real Pages builder, sanity checks, template lint and resolver fixtures.
  • G2 The relative rules report 0 FAIL, and every WARN (including the aggregated inbound table) is acknowledged.
  • G3 The absolute rules A1 to A4 report 0 FAIL on live-world URLs.
  • G4 Budgets and vitals pass on live-world URLs.
  • G5 Tier-2 capture reports 0 FAIL on live-world URLs, and pixels are ≤ 0.1% on all other URLs.
  • G6 check-clean.py passes: no _includes/worlds/*/[abc]/, no assets/worlds/*/[abc].(css|js), no status: preview, no orphan fonts.
  • G7 Picks are recorded in _data/worlds/<id>.yml and the PR body, and confirmed in chat.
  • G8 The branch contains the latest origin/main, merged rather than rebased.
  • G9 (after merge, read through the GitHub MCP tools; this session cannot reach the live site or the Pages API):
  • actions_list list_workflow_runs on workflow 227213120 (pages-build-deployment) shows a run for the merge SHA with conclusion success. Poll for up to 10 minutes. A failure means a revert PR.
  • The verify-live.yml run for that SHA is green. If workflow_run did not fire, dispatch it with actions_run_trigger. Read failures with get_job_logs.
  • indexnow.yml is dispatched with the in-scope URLs and is green. P0 dispatches nothing.
  • CLAUDE.md's "curl the live URL" step is replaced by this procedure in P0.
Performance and accessibility budget

Baseline (today's build, site-before)

  • style.css is 66 KB raw (13 KB gz) and loads on every page.
  • Fonts: 106 KB preloaded (Inter variable 48 KB, Newsreader 58 KB), plus a 26 KB italic.
  • animations.js is 10 KB.
  • The header mark lagerland-mark.png is 1.96 MB and is shown at 30 px on 229 pages.
  • App icons are 0.56–3.96 MB PNGs shown at 40–64 px. The homepage references 25 images, about 26 MB if all of them load. The Observa page is about 12 MB of images.
  • The app hero LCP image is the first screenshot PNG, about 0.9 MB, preloaded at high priority.
  • App page HTML is 52–101 KB raw.

Budgets for each live-world page

budget.py checks static bytes. vitals.mjs measures lab vitals on a Moto G Power profile (412×823, DPR 1.75, 4× CPU, 150 ms RTT, 1.6 Mbps, median of 3 runs). Field data comes from CrUX and the GSC Core Web Vitals report. - LCP: lab ≤ 2.0 s on app microsites and the homepage, ≤ 1.6 s on read pages. Field p75 ≤ 2.5 s. - CLS: lab ≤ 0.02. Field p75 ≤ 0.05, hard limit 0.1. Font swap contributes ≤ 0.01. - INP: field p75 ≤ 200 ms. Lab: TBT ≤ 100 ms, no long task over 50 ms after load, and the signature interaction ≤ 100 ms. - Fonts: ≤ 160 KB of woff2 per page, counting every file the page's CSS references. At most 2 preloads and 4 files, latin subset only, font-display: swap, self-hosted. - CSS: - Render-blocking CSS ≤ 12.5 KB gz on persuade pages (contract.css ≤ 1.5 plus world CSS ≤ 11). - ≤ 16 KB gz on read pages, which add read-base.css ≤ 3.5. Read-base carries the legacy vocabulary, so world CSS does not. - World CSS ≤ 60 KB raw. No @import, no external url(), exactly one world stylesheet. - JS: contract.js ≤ 1.5 KB gz; world JS ≤ 5 KB gz, defer. Content needs no JS. The only inline script is the html.js line. The only third-party script is GoatCounter, unchanged. - HTML: at most the baseline +10% raw, and ≤ 30 KB gz. - Preloads: every preload must be used by the first render. - budget.py matches preload URLs against the image, srcset, font and CSS URLs the page actually uses. - vitals.mjs confirms Chrome reports no unused preload. - The app LCP preload uses the derivative's imagesrcset/imagesizes. The legacy PNG preloads never appear on live-world pages. - Images: - LCP image ≤ 100 KB on mobile and ≤ 180 KB on desktop, a WebP derivative with fetchpriority=high, never lazy. - Above the fold ≤ 200 KB on mobile and ≤ 400 KB on desktop. - Whole page after a full scroll at 390 and DPR 2: ≤ 1.0 MB for app pages, ≤ 600 KB for the homepage and read pages. - Icons ≤ 15 KB at displayed size; brand mark ≤ 8 KB. - Every img has width, height and alt. Nothing below the fold loads eagerly. No images of text. - A source without a derivative falls back to the original. contract-main.yml reports it so it is regenerated. - Requests: ≤ 8 before LCP, ≤ 40 in total. - Video (WanderWiki hero, a 13 MB .mov): poster first, preload="none" on mobile, MP4 plus WebM ≤ 1.5 MB resolved through _data/derivatives.yml, a visible pause control, and no autoplay under reduced motion.

Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA, every world and every style)

  • Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1, large text ≥ 3:1, non-text UI ≥ 3:1. contrast.py checks each world's declared pairs, including the footer-strip tokens and the read-base mappings. axe checks the rendered pages, including text over screenshots.
  • Focus:
  • A themed :focus-visible ring of 2 px or more, at ≥ 3:1 against both adjacent colours. For the badge, the ring is drawn on the <a>.
  • Focus is never hidden behind fixed elements (2.4.11): scroll-padding comes from the nav height and --sticky-h, checked by tabbing.
  • Targets: ≥ 24×24 CSS px. The badge is ≥ 40 px tall and ≥ 120 px wide.
  • Keyboard: the skip link is first; navigation works without JS; carousels are tabindex=0 regions with an aria-label and a visible scroll cue; Escape closes JS menus.
  • Structure: landmarks; one h1 and no skipped heading levels; lang=en (quotes keep their own lang); <th scope> in tables (the shared comparison_table block emits it); FAQ entries as <details>/<summary>; meaningful QR alt text.
  • Motion: under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, no non-essential animation or transition, no parallax, no scroll-jacking and no autoplay. Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second.
  • No JS: 100% of content is visible. Reveal effects are hidden only under html.js, with the 2.5 s safety net. Animated numbers are server-rendered with real values. Rendered coverage proves both no-JS completeness and that no CSS hides content.
  • Resilience: reflow at 320 px; 200% text zoom; overridden text spacing (1.4.12) without clipping; forced colours keep the badge, focus rings and borders; single-scheme worlds set color-scheme, and pair worlds are tested in both.

Enforcement

  • Tier 1 (static rules, contrast tokens and the quick capture on representative pages) applies to every candidate before the owner sees it.
  • Tier 2 (the full matrix, vitals and axe on every in-scope URL, with 0 serious or critical issues) applies to the promoted winner before the PR is marked ready.
  • One manual VoiceOver pass on iOS per shipped world, on its app page and one read page. P1 covers every Observa page.
  • After shipping, contract-main.yml re-checks the static budgets on every push to main.
Risks and mitigations

A microsite leaves out a contract element or a front-matter block, or moves the quick answer down the page.

Layouts emit all schema and head output. blocks/rest.html renders every known block a world did not handle. check-contract.py requires the markers and data-block elements. The capture checks fail when the quick answer sits below 1.5 viewports or the badge is outside the first viewport.

Content is silently dropped or hidden by CSS when a world reorganises a page, especially on the mobile render Google indexes.

Coverage is checked three ways against base: front-matter leaves by key path, text blocks, and rendered visibility at 390 and 1440 with details opened. The rendered check also fails on clipped and visually-hidden text, and the JS-off text must equal the JS-on text.

The guard passes vacuously because CI used a different engine or skipped plugins (no sitemap, no redirects on either side).

CI builds with actions/jekyll-build-pages. Local builds use the github-pages bundle in the :jekyll_plugins group. Sanity assertions require every generated file and stub, and a file missing from both builds is a FAIL. P0 requires the local and CI digests to match.

Local and production engines diverge (a Jekyll 4 filter that silently misbehaves on 3.10).

Every build runs on github-pages 232 with liquid strict_filters, and lint-templates.py rejects find, find_exp, render, not and parenthesised conditions. The owner approves exactly what Pages renders.

Rules that the current site already breaks make every gate unpassable, or get waved through.

Every URL is compared with base. Absolute rules apply only where a world is live. The current site's defects are committed in baseline/incumbent.json, approved once, and each is scheduled for a fix (Guides in P2, EarnLock terms in P9–P11, Millrace and MediaKit in P18–P20).

Edits pushed straight to main after a world ships (new blocks, new alternatives pages, new screenshots, new body classes) bypass the PR guard and drift silently.

contract-main.yml runs on every push to main (non-blocking, one tracking issue). It checks block rendering, app: tags, relocated-hub bodies, derivative staleness and vocabulary. Block fallbacks render new keys, untagged alternatives stay legacy, and derivative lookups fall back to originals.

Hand-written hub lists end up in several copies (contract schema, legacy body, studio template, a/b/c candidates), and launches update only one.

The /for/ and /guides/ hubs and the home FAQ render from one front-matter list. The /alternatives/ index keeps its body and computes numberOfItems. CLAUDE.md gets a where-things-moved table in P0, and relocated pages that regain body content are flagged.

Post-deploy verification cannot run from the session (the proxy blocks the live site and the Pages API).

verify-live.yml runs in GitHub Actions after pages-build-deployment. Claude reads both runs through the GitHub MCP tools and dispatches verify-live if workflow_run does not fire.

Microsites lose the sitewide studio footer links, which weakens internal linking.

The footer strip links /alternatives/ and the app's /for/ pages, and the studio footer links every live app. The link graph fails new orphans and depth increases relative to base. Inbound changes come as one aggregated table per PR.

A preview or candidate style leaks into production, or into the llms and sitemap lists.

Previews are separate builds assembled outside Jekyll. Candidates need site.preview_style, which only local configs set. The leak check looks for dedicated markers (data-review-bar, /preview/ paths, lagerland-preview and lagerland-world metas). check-clean.py runs before the PR is ready, and squash merges keep losing styles out of main's history.

The ratings-sync bot pushes daily, so branches go stale.

The redesign never edits _apps/*.md. Branches merge origin/main and are never rebased or force-pushed. CI builds the merge ref, so diffs isolate the branch's own changes.

Each world's fonts, screenshots and preloads push performance below the current site's.

Hard budgets per page. Derivatives replace the 1–4 MB PNGs. Image preloads moved out of the contract head, so no world preloads the unused legacy PNG, and unused preloads fail.

Sameness: 20 microsites become one template in different costumes, made more likely by the shared block partials and read-base.

The partials are semantic only, and worlds own order, grouping, form and overrides. Dice-protocol style cards, sibling trios decided together in the siblings view, and a finish review comparing section order, navigation, type and signature interaction.

Candidate gating cost: 63 world implementations, 42 discarded, each through an ~18-render matrix.

Two tiers: candidates pass cheap static rules plus a quick capture of representative pages; the full matrix, vitals, axe on every URL and VoiceOver run only on winners. Trios split into per-world PRs.

Owner decisions are slow or absent.

One bounded revision round. A world without a pick is deferred while the rest of the trio ships. Picks are recorded in the Artifact database and confirmed in chat.

Rankings or CTR drop after a world ships.

GSC review at 7 and 28 days against out-of-scope control pages. Before P22 the rollback is one line (status: legacy); after it, git revert of the world's squash commit.

Inline styles in 104 alternatives bodies depend on style.css tokens, so tables lose padding and rules in new worlds.

scan-classes.py emits legacy-tokens.txt. read-base.css defines every token mapped onto world tokens, check-contract enforces it, and a computed-style check confirms it on comparison tables. An optional content pass to replace inline styles is left to the owner.

Artifact limits break the review.

Chunked publishes to one Artifact URL (≤ 255 files and 64 MB per publish, ≤ 511 files and 256 MB per version). Current is shown as captures, assets are de-duplicated by hash, and derivatives are used.

Committed derivatives and fonts grow the repo.

Derivatives only for in-scope apps (WebP, 3 widths, content-hashed). Shared fonts, with orphans pruned on promotion. Expected growth is about 20–30 MB against roughly 250 MB of assets today.

IndexNow resubmits the whole sitemap on every phase merge (_includes, _layouts and _data are global triggers), which IndexNow discourages.

Squash commits carry [skip indexnow]. After verify-live passes, indexnow.yml is dispatched with only the in-scope URLs. P0 submits nothing.

The current App Store badge is an approximation drawn with system fonts, which is arguably a redraw of Apple artwork.

Apple's official SVG is a P0 exit criterion (committed unused) and goes live in P1 through contract/badge.html. CSS lint forbids altering it.

Open questions
  • Does the repository allow 'Squash and merge'? The plan assumes it, so losing styles never enter main's history. Otherwise use a merge commit; the losers are already deleted from the branch tip and kept on the tag.
  • Can we get a Google Search Console export: Pages and Queries for the last 3 months, plus the Core Web Vitals report? It would: - refine the order of P3–P20 (ratings.count is a weak proxy, and MediaKit's 14 converter comparisons may outrank its zero ratings); - choose the alternatives pages shown in the review Artifacts; - serve as the 28-day monitoring baseline.
  • Official App Store badge (now a P0 exit criterion): will you download Apple's official 'Download on the App Store' SVG (black, US English) from Apple Marketing Tools? And should Mac-only apps (AppMeta, Mockly) use Apple's 'Download on the Mac App Store' badge instead?
  • QR on Mac-only apps: the plan stops rendering the QR for AppMeta and Mockly, because scanning lands an iPhone on a listing it cannot install. The brief only says the QR is 'less central' for them. Confirm removal, or keep it with Mac-specific copy.
  • Studio pick granularity: one studio style for every studio template (recommended), or separate picks per template family (home vs read vs hubs)?
  • Testimonials (GymLogger X, Observa, Soon., Chessful): the brief says no star ratings anywhere. Should we keep the real quotes but drop the per-quote stars and the computed '4.x · N rated reviews' average, which today has no schema behind it?
  • App cards show a star pill when ratings.count is 3 or more. Confirm it goes away everywhere in P2, as the 'no star ratings' rule implies.
  • Should the Smart App Banner (apple-itunes-app meta) also be added to each app's read variants (support and alternatives pages)? It is a likely conversion gain and an intentional head addition that would be allowlisted.
  • Microsite pages drop the studio header and footer links (Journal, About, every app by category). They keep the 'A Lagerland app' strip, which now also links /alternatives/ and the app's /for/ pages, plus you-might-like. Is that acceptable? Each PR shows the inbound-link changes as one table for you to approve.
  • The 300 .overline kickers in hand-written alternatives, guides and for/ bodies: restyle them as inline meta text (the default, no content change), or remove them in a separate content pass? Separately, should a later content pass replace the inline style= attributes in comparison tables with a compare-* class?
  • Tare: design its world now without images, as the brief decided, or schedule P21 for when the icon and Signboard Sky screenshots exist?
  • WanderWiki's 13 MB .mov hero: approve re-encoding it to MP4 and WebM at 1.5 MB or less, with a poster image?
  • Workflows: is it OK to add these? - redesign-guard.yml (PRs only); - contract-main.yml (non-blocking on every push to main; keeps one tracking issue); - verify-live.yml (after each Pages deploy). Is it also OK to edit indexnow.yml with a [skip indexnow] guard and a urls input for manual dispatch? None of them deploys anything. The Gemfile lives only under scripts/redesign/ci/.
  • OK to add `theme: null` to _config.yml in P0? It changes 0 bytes today (verified on the production engine). Without it, once P22 deletes style.css, GitHub Pages' default Primer theme would serve its own CSS at /assets/css/style.css.
  • GoatCounter stays exactly as it is today on production pages; it is stripped only from the private previews. Confirm that no change is wanted as part of the redesign.
  • Should the OG share cards (assets/og/*.png) be regenerated in each world's style after its phase? URLs and tags stay the same, so parity is unaffected, but it is extra asset work.
  • Rejected (in part): the issue on image derivatives asked templates to fall back to the original when the source's hash differs. Liquid cannot hash a file at build time, and site.static_files modification times are checkout times on GitHub Pages, so a build cannot detect a screenshot replaced in place. Adopted instead: - derivatives are content-hashed and looked up by source path in _data/derivatives.yml; - a new or renamed source falls back to the original; - contract-main.yml runs make-derivatives.py --check on every push and reports stale entries.
